Detailed Itinerary of Everest Base Camp Trek in September

Day 01: Arrival at Kathmandu Airport

We will meet you at Kathmandu Airport for a warm reception. From there, we will drive towards your hotel. You will settle there for refreshment and rest. Later in the evening, we will meet up once again for an introduction meeting. You will get to know about your team and its members. Overnight back in the hotel.

Day 02: Fy from Kathmandu to Lukla(2,860 m) and trek to Phakding(2,600 m) | 3-4hrs trek

We will now set up for a flight to Lukla and ultimately begin the trip. Some 40 minutes in the air and enjoying the flight views, we will make a safe landing in Lukla.

Then, We will commence our trek to Phakding as we finish breakfast in Lukla. It will begin with a descending hike before joining the banks of the Dudhkoshi River. Then, walking side by side of the river, we will make it to Phakding. Overnight in a Teahouse of the village.

Day 03: Trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar(3,450 m) | 6-7hrs

Without much delay in the morning, we will join the trail that ends up in Namche Bazaar. The walk will be along the river and peaceful forested area. We will cross several high suspension bridges dotted with prayer flags.

Likewise, at Monjo, we will run into Sagarmatha National Park. We will reach Namche by spending half of the day on this serene trail full of bridges and trees. Overnight in the town.

Day 04: Acclimatization Day in Namche Bazaar

We will have a rest day in Namche Bazaar to do some hikes to the nearby places. It will help us to become familiar with the heights before we start to gain more highs.

Then, along with a detailed exploration of Namche Bazaar, we will set out for Everest View Hotel and Khunde Hospital, the two must-visit places nearby. Later, we will revert to our hotel in Namche Bazaar for the night.

Day 05: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Tengboche(3,865 m) | 5-6hrs

Now we shall leave Namche to progress on the trek. Beginning with an uphill climb from Namche, we will trek along the valley. That is when we will start seeing majestic glimpses of Mt Everest, Ama Dablam, and several other peaks.

There will be some chortens and lots of woods along the trail today. The beautiful trek will slow down as we find ourselves in Tengboche by the monastery here. Overnight in the village.

Day 06: Trek from Tengboche to Dingboche(4,410 m) | 5-6hrs

Waking up to breathtaking mountain views, we will prepare to leave the place for Dingboche. Firstly, we will descend from Tengboche to the sounding Imja Khola(River). Then we will trek upwards to and through Pangboche Village.

All this time, we will be blessed with the exquisite close views of Mt Ama Dablam. Besides, we will cross many beautiful forested sections, gompas, and mani walls. Finally, by dusk, we will reach Dingboche to settle for the night.

Day 07: Acclimatization Day in Dingboche

Just like the other day in Namche, you’ll have a rest day in Dingboche to acclimatize properly. We will spend this day hiking up to Nakartsang Gompa that lies nearby. From there, we will capture the unreal sights of the majority of the Everest Region’s peaks. After all of that, we will trace back to the hotel.

Day 08: Trek from Dingboche to Lobuche(4,940 m) | 5-6hrs

Joining the treeless landscapes, we will begin moving out from Dingboche. As we walk on, we will trek on a sandy and dusty trail surrounded by giant mountains. We will also come across the memorial stop where there are memorials of multiple mountain souls.

Crossing all of the glacier moraine and rough trail, we end up in Lobuche. From the place, we will be able to see creamy mountains. Overnight in a teahouse in the village.

Day 09: Trek from Lobuche to Everest Base Camp through Gorakshep(5,140 m) | 3-4hrs

With a push to a ridge from Lobuche, we will begin the Everest Base Camp Day. The track is rough and half-deserted due to the terminal moraines. Finally, we will trek across Gorakshep to reach the legendary base camp area.

From Base Camp(5,364 m), we will catch breathtaking scenes of Everest and other mountains along with the glaciers and rough landscapes. After the view, we will head back to Gorak Shep for the night.

Day 10: Trek from Gorakshep to Kala Patthar(5,545 m) and then descend to Pheriche

Now we will hike in the direction of Kala Patthar, where the best views of Mt Everest will await us. It will be an early morning walk over a steep trail. We will get mountain views along the trek, but the best views will be only from Kala Patthar. As we reach, we will relate the breathtaking views in Kalapatthar before descending to Pheriche. It will be a comfortable hike down to Pheriche for the night.

Day 11: Trek from Pheriche to Namche Bazaar | 7-8hrs

From Pheriche, we will join a retracing trek back to Namche Bazaar. The trek will be through the beautiful vegetation and away from the mountains. Eventually, we will slowly leave the mountains back as we reach Namche through Tengboche by descending the same trail.

Day 12: Trek from Namche To Lukla | 6- 8hrs

We will continue retracing the trail as we leave Namche Bazaar. The already been places will come along once again; we will recall them too. In this way, we will reach Lukla by the evening after trekking for 7 to 8 hrs. And this is where our trek will get concluded.

Day 13: Fly back to Kathmandu from Lukla | 40 minutes

With an early morning scenic flight, we will make it back to Kathmandu. The rest of the day, we will walk around the UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Kathmandu. The night’s rest back in the hotel.

Day 14: Departure from Nepal

The adventure of the trek will come to finish as you will prepare for your departure. Ultimately, we will arrange a transfer for you to the airport.

Reasons to do Everest Base Camp Trek in September

There are some top reasons to choose September for Everest Base Camp Trek. We’ll describe all of them here:

Transition Month

September is a transition month when Autumn substitutes Monsoon. During the month, a lot of changes happen in the environment, and you’ll experience that. You’ll live through that in one of the best treks in the world. You’ll be there when the clouds finally leave the skies and mountains start to open freely. And ultimately, you’ll experience the region in two seasons on a trip.

Picturesque Views

Everest Region, which is never too dull but ever beautiful, looks unique in September. Wherever you point your head, it will only bring picturesque views for your eyes. The thanks go to Monsoon and its heavy rainfall.

As of the earlier wettest three months, the region gets a new look. And the dusty views get washed by the rain, and there you receive the exquisite views. Mountains, deep valleys, villages, or a simple suspension bridge, everything turns magical.

Less Crowded Trail

Usually, Autumn is the busiest time on the Everest Base Camp’s trail. People know it is an excellent season, and as a result, everyone is there on the trail. But, thankfully, the number of trekkers is relatively low during September. Most of them plan for the later months, October and November. If you cannot help crowds during a trip, September is your time for the trek.

Scenic Flight

Everest Base Camp Trek commences with a scenic flight to Lukla from Kathmandu. But if you plan for September, the view is unreal and breathtaking. As the flight touches the clouds, you will be able to see a crystal clear view of the entire Himalayas, including several of the world’s tallest peaks. Not only that but the terrains of the country will also impress you. So for a scenic mountain flight only, you should choose September.

Some Festivals

Along with the trek, you will observe and be part of some of the festivals of Nepalese. The much-celebrated carnivals like Indra Jatra and Teej fall in September. You’ll get invites from the lovely people to enjoy the food and be part of the celebration. Therefore, the trek is a perfect time for this specific reason too.

Tips for those doing Everest Base Camp Trek in September

Choose the Right Agency

If you are not a solo trekker, it is better to go through local agencies. The local trekking agencies arrange everything from tickets to accommodation. But make sure you are picking the right and experienced one. The expert group of the team will only provide you the best and safe deal.

We at Base Camp Adventure provide organized trekking activities in Nepal. Our team is highly experienced, one from a trekking guide to the driver. You’ll have a good trek with us.

Get Yourself Insured

You should possess travel insurance when you are trekking in the mountains. The situation can turn against you anytime from anywhere. When everything is uncertain, you can stay safe by having insurance. The insurance will cover the cost of emergencies like helicopter rescues, injury treatment, and more. That is why you should get yourself insured while you come for the trek.

Right sort of Packing

What you have in your backpack is more important than anything during the trek. The reason is it’s September, and there will be little rainfall. Likewise, the temperature is also chilly during the night hours. If you do not have clothes and gear to keep you safe in those conditions, you are finished. Thus, make sure you have the correct packing before you join the tour.

Trek Slowly

Rushing on the trail is not a good thing, especially when you are in the mountains. It may take you to your destination quickly, but it may take you to the doors of altitude sickness. Not taking rest and trekking continuously is a significant factor of altitude sickness. So a better decision is to walk slowly and calmly. Make sure you do the same.

Water saves life

We all know what the importance of water in our life is. Well, it helps you trek safely on a high-altitude trek. If your body is hydrated, you will not be affected by the mountain sickness. In case if you are not drinking enough water, your body is more prone to disease. That is why you should fill your stomach with water on the trek.

Other Routes in the Everest Region

Classic or Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek

If you seek a more extended Everest Base Camp Trek version, this classic option will complete you. It is called classic for some reason; this is the actual trail to the foothills of Mt Everest before the establishment of Lukla Airport.

Trekkers, including the early climbers of the mountain, walked the same trail. You will retrace the footprints of those legends and have a widened trekking experience of the trek.

As its path tells, the trek starts from Jiri and moves towards the base camp. It is a 21 days long package with the team of Base Camp Adventure. With the added distance and days, you will experience the legendary trail and its offerings as the legends.

So, it can be a great alternative to Everest Base Camp Trek in September.

Everest Three Pass Trek

Everest Three Pass Trek is an 18 days long journey to the three highest passes in the Everest Region. It will be a quest to find Kongma La(5,535 m), Renjo La(5,360 m), and Cho La(5,420 m).

Each of the passes is unparalleled when it is about mountain views. You’ll have some climbs to scale every one of them; it is even more adventurous than Everest Base Camp Trek.

It can be a great alternative who loves more and more thrills every day. Along with those mountain passes, the trek goes through Base Camp and Kala Patthar also. So this trekking option is an exclusive deal for the tour of the Everest Region.

Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return

Or you can simply choose this itinerary which ends with a helicopter return. You’ll trek all the way to Base Camp, but you will not walk a step while returning; the helicopter will bring you back. That means you will trek half of the trek. In the timeline of 9 days, you’ll dare to reach the base camp of the world’s highest peak.

This program aims to reduce the trekking days by half to save energy and time. If you also have the same desires, take this plan over Everest Base Camp Trek in September.

Find more details here.

Everest View Trek

Everest Base Camp Trek and other challenging treks are not everyone’s cup of tea. But, luckily, people can still explore the Everest Region without taking the difficult road. This Everest View Trek is the option for such avid trekkers. On the nine days of the trek, trekkers will reach Tengboche Monastery(3,860 m), the trip’s highest point. From Tengboche, they will scrutinize the beautiful edges of Mt Everest and other peaks.

Without taking much risk, you will traverse and know what it is like to be in the Everest Region with this option. If you are also looking for an easy and less demanding option to trek in September, this can be your apple to pick up.

Gokyo Valley Trek

Last but not least, Gokyo Valley Trek is one fine alternative to Everest Base Camp Trek. This trek is more about the beautiful Gokyo valley and the lakes there. On this trek, you’ll trek a little away from the base camp on the sides of the valley.

You will view Mt Everest, Cho Oyu, Ama Dablam too on this trek but from a distance only. This trek will be solely about exploring the picturesque valley and seven pristine Gokyo Lakes.

Base Camp Adventure has a 13 days long Gokyo Valley Trek for you if you do not want to do Everest Base Camp Trek. Choose this option and see the less popular side of the Everest Region.

The Bottom Line

Everest Base Camp Trek in September is a promising plan to make it happen. As you already know, you will have nothing but a memorable experience in the foothills of Mt Everest during this month. Therefore, You should perform Everest Base Camp Trek in the month.

The best in the business, Base Camp Adventure, is always there to organize your adventure. The team will look after everything to make sure you have a safe and comfortable travel time.

title: Everest Base Camp Trek in October
excerpt: Everest Base Camp Trek in October is a combination of the best trek and month. The ideal weather, rich forests, clear mountain view, and beautiful terrain are a few offerings of the Everest region in…
html:
Everest Base Camp Trek in October is a combination of the best trek and month. The ideal weather, rich forests, clear mountain view, and beautiful terrain are a few offerings of the Everest region in October.

October is a month in the autumn season. This season comes right after the monsoon, so the forests seem lively and greener with no air pollution. The rain washes away the dirt and dust surrounding the region.

October is a peak hiking and trekking season in Nepal. The weather is favorable with clear skies, bright sun, and unobstructed views. In addition, this month lets you be part of major festivals and enjoy the special delicacies.

To learn more about Everest Base Camp Trek in October, you can read further:

About Everest Base Camp

Everest Base Camp lies on the two sides of Mount Everest, the south base in Nepal and the north base in China. Among these bases, the South Everest Base Camp is a famous trekking destination.

Everest Base Camp Trek is the major trekking destination of Nepal that attracts trekkers. Peop

le globally visit Nepal to walk in these trails to get a glimpse of Mount Everest.

This famous trek route goes through Sagarmatha National Park, so you get to walk fabulous forest trails. While entering the jungles, you get to see many unique species of animals, plants, flowers, and birds.

The forests are their home, where they have been living for more than a century. Some of the animals and birds found here are red panda, bearded vulture, pheasant, snowcock, snow leopard, red panda, musk deer, etc.

Not only the views and vegetation, but Everest Base Camp Trek lets you be a part of the Himalayan people and learn about their lifestyle. During this trip, you also get to enjoy different delicacies that might be new to your taste.

The people living in the Everest areas are mostly from the Sherpa Community. They follow Tibetan Buddhist culture and tradition, so you get to learn about the religions as well.

Everest Base Camp Trek Route

After arriving at Kathmandu, you begin your Everest Base camp trek in October the following day. You start the trip with a scenic flight to Lukla, viewing various peaks and landscapes.

Then arriving at the airport, you trek to Phakding the same day and stay there for the night. The next day, you head towards Namche Bazaar, the sherpa town and hub of the Everest region.

The first acclimatization of the EBC trek is here in Namche. Then, during the rest day, you visit nearby places and explore the town. Then you move towards Tengboche the next morning after a hefty breakfast.

Tengboche has an ancient monastery that is famous around the Everest region. From there, you trek to Dingboche, where is your second acclimatization. Similar to the first rest day, you explore and go on to hike during the stay.

From Dingboche, you trek to Lobuche taking zigzag paths through rocky glacial moraines. Finally, the day you have been waiting for is here. You trek towards Everest Base Camp via Gorak Shep.

Then after taking some pictures and enjoying the views, you head back to Gorak Shep for the night. The next morning, you wake up early and hike to Kala Patthar for a sunrise view and trek down to Pheriche.

From Pheriche, you trek to Namche, then to Lukla, and fly back to Kathmandu. After returning, you end your Everest Base Camp Trek in October.

Reasons to visit Everest Base Camp Trek in October

Everest Base camp trek is possible throughout the year, but each month shows you a different side of this region. Here, we have mentioned a few of the reasons to visit Everest Base Camp Trek in October:

Perfect Climate

Everest Base Camp Trek in October has ideal climatic conditions. The days are pleasant with walking under the clear blue skies and warm climate. Compared to winters, the nights are bearable during October in the Everest region.

The perfect climate is the best part for trekking to Everest Base Camp in October. The climate and weather are travel-friendly with no worry of cold, snowfall, or rainfall.

Another best thing is that you don’t need to carry thick, heavy clothes or rain, snow gear. The bag is not heavy, giving ease to your shoulders. The climatic conditions in October are perfect for trekking to Everest Base Camp.

Festive time

October is also a festive season/ month in Nepal when the two main festivals Dashain and Tihar, fall under here. This is the time of the year when happiness flows all around the country as families meet, have fun and celebrate this occasion together.

People share love, blessing, and happiness, making the destinations vibrant during this festive month. You can feel the festival in the air as you also are a part of this unknowingly.

Everest Base Camp Trek in October is ideal for exploring the Nepalese culture and traditions. You also get to taste many special dishes prepared for the festival.

Wonderful Vegetation

During October, the vegetation around the Everest region looks extraordinarily beautiful. Maybe because the monsoon rain has just finished and the warmth of the Autumn sun is on arrival. But this month is best to observe the flora on these trails.

The wonderful vegetation comes to life with new beauty and charm. The trails of Everest Base Camp Trek in October are green, colorful, and lively, with unique species of plants and flowers.

The main highlight is walking through the alpine forest of Sagarmatha National Park. This national park is full of diversified floras and faunas. In the lower regions, you can see the farming of paddy and millets.

The observation of the beautiful natural vegetation is the best part for most trekkers. You trek through lush forests filled with pines, oaks, and colorful rhododendrons.

Scenic flight

The best reason to visit Everest Base Camp Trek in October is the scenic flight from Kathmandu to Lukla and vice versa. As the October weather is just perfect, the flights are also the best at this time.

As you take off, the clear sky is the first nice thing, then the views of mountains, valleys, and landscapes under them are what mesmerizes you the most. The magnificent mountains stand tall, dominating the jungles below.

The flight is comfortable, reliable, fast, and exciting, along with unique views of your surroundings. This is another reason not to miss out on trekking to Everest base camp in October.

Picturesque views

Picturesque views are the main reason many trekkers visit Everest Base Camp in October. The surroundings are scenic everywhere in the Everest region, with a stunning view of snowy peaks, bumpy terrains, and green hills.

The beauty of the Everest region will never be enough for your camera and eyes. This region looks like a nymph bride to astound you with its beauty. The mountains and terrains are not the only views, but the ancient monasteries, rich traditional villages also add flavor to its beauty.

You also get to observe the animals grazing and grasslands near the villages. But most people visit with a wish to get even a glimpse of the great Mount Everest.

Weather conditions during Everest Base Camp Trek in October

Before beginning your Everest Base Camp Trek in October, learn about its weather. Without proper climatic conditions, trekking can be a bit harsh and challenging.

Weather-wise, you don’t need to worry about trekking in October because it is one of the great months for trekking to Everest Base Camp. The warm and sunny blue sky offers a clear view of peaks during this time.

October is a dry month, so there is no rainfall or snowfall to make your trek difficult. The weather conditions are stable with less humidity compared to other months.

Due to low humidity, the chances of fog covering the view is pretty low. Therefore, you can enjoy your trek to the fullest without any worries. Due to the stable climatic conditions trekking to EBC in October without any hassle is possible.

Read more on: Everest Base Camp Weather in Autumn

The temperature during Everest Base Camp Trek in October

As the weather condition is stable, so is the temperature, but there rises or drops according to the elevation. Thus, the lower places can be hot and sweaty, while the upper region can have a mild climate.

With each elevation, the temperature drops, but as October falls under autumn, it is not too high. It will be warm, bright, and sunny in higher elevations, unlike in monsoon or winter seasons. Also, the night and day temperature varies drastically.

In Lukla, the temperature ranges from 9 ℃ to 20 ℃ during the daytime, likewise it drops between -3 ℃ to 20 ℃. In Namche, it ranges between 7 ℃ to 18 ℃ in the daytime and drops from 2 ℃ to 12 ℃ a night.

Similarly, in Dingboche, the max temperature ranges about 5 ℃ to 15 ℃ during the day and -7 ℃ to 6 ℃. In Lobuche, it ranges between 4 ℃ to 12 ℃ during the day and at night drops to -4 ℃ to 7 ℃.

Like on, the temperature rises slowly with each climb. So, usually, the temperature ranges between the above numbers during October.

Outline Itinerary- Everest Base Camp trek in October

Day 1: Arrive at Kathmandu

Day 2: Flight from Kathmandu to Lukla (2,860 m) (25 min) then walk to Phakding (2,600 m) (3 to 4 hours)

Day 3: Phakding to Namche Bazaar (3,450 m) (6 to 7 hours)

Day 4: acclimatize day

Day 5: Namche to Tengboche (3,865 m) (5 to 6 hours)

Day 6: Tengboche to Dingboche (4,410 m) (6 hours)

Day 7: Second acclimatization

Day 8: Dingboche to Lobuche (4,940 m) (7 to 8 hours)

Day 9: Lobuche to Everest Base Camp (5,364 m) and back to Gorakshep (5,140 m) (total duration: 6 to 7 hours)

Day 10: Hike to Kala Patthar (5,545 m) (2 hours) then to Pheriche ( 6 hours)

Day 11: Pheriche to Namche Bazaar (7 to 8 hours)

Day 12: Namche to Lukla (7 hours)

Day 13: Fly back to Kathmandu (1,400 m)

Day 14: Departure

Food and Accommodation in October

Everest Base Camp Trek is mainly a tea house trek that offers basic food and accommodation services. The lodging is mostly average and provides necessities like blankets, pillows, hot water, etc.

However, the lodges in the upper region use solar energy to produce electricity, so they charge you extra for its usage. You will also be paying additional costs for hot showers and water.

Other than that, they also offer a variety of clean and healthy meals on the trails. Each day, you eat bread, jam, scrambled eggs, boiled eggs, paratha, and more for breakfast.

For lunch and dinner, you will have authentic Nepali cuisine for the entire trekking trip. They offer you Dal, Bhat, curry, pickle, and side dishes like meat, paneer, spinach, etc.

For drinks, you have limited options like coffee, tea, coke, etc. The food you eat on the trails helps you fuel enough energy to continue the trek every day.

Difficulties Faced during Everest Base Camp Trek in October

As you know from above, October is the best month for Everest Trek, so many trekkers choose to travel during this time. However, along with the fun, there also comes different challenges, and they are:

Finding accommodation

The main difficulty you face during the Everest Base Camp Trek in October is finding accommodation. However, there are several teahouses and lodges to accommodate.

October is the peak season, so finding a place to stay overnight is quite difficult as most of the lodges and teahouses are already tenanted. It will also be hard to find a room of your choice as you may have to adjust to what you get.

In most cases, trekkers have to share their room with fellow companions and stand in long queues to use the bathroom.

Altitude Sickness

Traveling to Everest Base camp is a high-altitude trek as most of the trails are above 4,000 m elevation. The highest point you reach is at an altitude of 5,643 m above sea level.

So, the chances of catching altitude sickness are high during the trek. Some people even suffer from Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS) when crossing the 3,500 m altitude.

Altitude sickness is usually due to a lack of preparation and acclimatization. The symptoms you suffer from are headache, shortness of breath, vomiting, lack of sleep, etc.

If you feel any of the symptoms, you should inform your guide or descend down to the lower parts. In case of emergencies, you have helicopter rescue options as well.

Route Difficulty

Unlike winter and monsoon, the routes are less slippery and snow-covered. The chances of snowfall and rainfall are also low, making the walks less difficult. But walking under the sunny temperature through rugged terrains can create route difficulty.

Also, the mountain trails are not straight or pitched, so walking the zigzag paths is tiring for new beginners. The Route difficulty mostly depends upon the individual as well.

If you are new to the trekking trails, then a few hour’s walks can easily take you out of breath. You can also find it difficult to catch up to other trekkers if you are not well-trained.

No privacy

Having no privacy can be a difficulty if you are an introvert. October is the peak month, so the trails are swarming with people visiting the Everest region. It will be hard to find even a moment of peace on these trails.

Trekking in October can be suffocating if you don’t like traveling with crowds. In every nook and turn, you will find a fellow companion, so having the trail to yourself can be hard.

Also, you will have to wait for the crowd to clear if you want to click a clear view picture. Thus, if you are not fond of crowds and do not like traveling in a herd, then Everest Base Camp Trek in October is not a great choice.

sometimes for Everest Base Camp Trek in October

Pre-book flights and rooms

Since many travelers choose October Everest Base Camp Trek, it might be hard for you to find rooms and flights on the spot. So, we recommend you to pre-book your accommodation and flights.

Also, the price of rooms and flights increases during peak time, so you might pay more than the advance bookers. If you do not book beforehand, you might have to share rooms with other trekkers.

In the worst scenarios, you might have to sleep in the lobby or kitchen and even camp outside sometimes. Also, you will have to wait in line for food in the restaurants.

Carry warm clothes

October might be one of the hot months, but it is only during the daytime. On the other hand, the higher places tend to get chilly by night, so carrying warm clothes like a sweater shawl might come in handy.

You do not need to pack thick or heavy jackets, just light ones that do not take much space. You can either carry a fleece jacket, light sweaters, thin inners, etc. But do not bring along many warm clothes as it is still hot during October.

Hiring proper guide and porter

If you are traveling through an agency, then you won’t need to worry about it. But if you are a solo traveler, then hiring a guide and porter will be advantageous for you.

Guide and porter have worked in these trails for years, so they are well-informed about the region. They can take you through shortcuts and help you communicate with the locals.

While selecting a guide, know whether they can speak multiple languages or not to make communication easier. Of course, it is better to select even just one of them as your companion for your safety too.

Start the Trek Early

Starting the trek early means beginning your walk first thing in the morning. The trails each day are about 5 to 7 hours far, so if you move early in the morning, you have much time to rest and explore the destinations.

Also, you get to leave the crowd behind as many travelers start late in the morning. The weather is unpredictable, so early trekking is a great choice to avoid bad weather.

Travel Insurance

Travel insurance is compulsory if you are traveling at a high altitude. This insurance covers all uncertainties you might face when going on a trek. In addition, it covers the costs of mishap and misfortunes occurred in the trek.

Most agencies do not provide insurance above a certain altitude, so make sure your insurance covers the trails of Everest Base Camp.

Packing List

Before starting the Everest Base Camp trek, you need to choose the right wears and gears. The correct choice of clothing can help you bear the Everest region cold.

So, we have prepared a packing list to give you ideas on what you can bring along in this trek.

For head

  • Sun caps/ hats
  • Scarf
  • UV protected Sunglasses
  • Buffs

For upper body

  • Lightweight but warm mid, base, and shell layer cloths
  • Hiking t-shirt
  • Down jackets
  • Water and windproof jackets
  • Warm tops
  • Sports bra

For hand

  • Inner gloves
  • Outer gloves

For lower body

  • Breathable undergarments
  • Hiking shorts
  • Trekking pants
  • Inner trouser
  • Waterproof pants

Footwear

  • Inner socks
  • Trekking socks
  • Gaiters
  • Hiking boots

For Toiletries

  • Quick-drying towel
  • Soap
  • Nail cutter
  • Toothbrush and paste
  • Moisturizer
  • Body lotion
  • Sunscreen

Personal hygiene

  • Toilet paper
  • Sanitizer
  • Wet tissues

Accessories

  • Water purification tablets
  • Torch
  • Trekking maps
  • Sleeping bags
  • Plastic bags
  • Water bottle
  • Extra batteries
  • Power banks
  • Personal first aid kit

Final Say

October Everest Base Camp Trek is full of festivals, clear views, and walks in marvelous terrain. So, this October, why not spend your time trekking in the Everest region and reaching Mount Everest base?

title: Everest Base Camp Trek in November
excerpt: Fall is the most incredible time of the year to be anywhere in Nepal. Its freezy weather with colorful autumn leaves, crisp air, and bright days make any place look fabulous. To make it even better…
html:
Fall is the most incredible time of the year to be anywhere in Nepal. Its freezy weather with colorful autumn leaves, crisp air, and bright days make any place look fabulous. To make it even better, November offers spectacular views to all its visitors, wishing for a delightful trip.

Autumn’s allure doesn’t spare the Himalayas either, causing it to captivate trekkers. With a picturesque backdrop, glistening mountains, and charming villages, it stands out from the rest. That speaks volumes for the madness and fascination of hikers for Everest Base Camp Trek.

Most travelers visiting Nepal prefer trekking Base Camp in November for its impressive view, mild weather, and easy walking trails. Whether it’s the deep valley, hilltops, or flat terrains, the region doesn’t leave a bit to impress visitors.

Trekkers can spot the change in the color of leaves while walking through the forest and valleys. As autumn prepares to take time off and winter, ready to make its way, trekkers can sense the iciness in the air.

It’s still fine at the lower hills with beautiful sunny days. But the higher they climb, the colder it gets with the temperature falling below 0 Degree Celsius. However, in general, the weather is cooler and dryer during the month.

Mornings and nights are pretty cold in November, while days, bright and sunny. By the end of the month, visitors can even witness light snowfall at the campsite. Cooler temperature provides relief to hikers while ascending steep hills and rugged terrains.

How is the weather like at Everest Base Camp in November?

Everest Base Camp Trek has always astounded visitors with its magnificent vista, breathtaking landscapes, and unique topography. It brings out the best from each season that travelers can’t help but fall for the beauty of base camp.

Autumn being no exception, offers astonishing scenery to its guests especially, in November. The month provides moderate weather with splendid mountain views and landscapes for a pleasant trip. But that’s not all; it even brings fall colors to life with tinted red, orange, and yellow leaves all around the woods.

November is a magical season with a mix of fall and winter colors. The crispness in the air with the subtlety of warm sunshine is what makes it so appealing. Trekkers can experience a hot climate at the beginning of the month, but it gets bitter cold in and around the base camp as the day passes.

The weather is nice and lovely till early November, but by mid, it gets frosty with the temperature dropping below -11 Degree Celsius. Trekkers can expect light snowfall at the end of the month as the winter finally arrives in the valley.

Highlights of Everest Base Camp Trek in November

  • A pristine view of Mt. Everest alongside Ama Dablam, Nuptse, and Cho Oyu
  • A quick visit to ancient Tibetan monastery in Khumbu Valley
  • Snap of stunning fall foliage with lush green terrains
  • Breathtaking sunrise view from Kala Patthar at 18,500 ft
  • Exploring the rich culture and lifestyle of people in the Himalayas
  • Walking through the subalpine forest of Sagarmatha National Park

Why trek Everest Base Camp in November?

With mild weather, marvelous sceneries, and fewer crowds, November may be one of the best times for a trip to Everest Base Camp. It offers terrific scenes with beautiful fall foliage, clear sky, and warm sunshine before the winter looms.

Although the weather cools down in the month, it’s still incredible walking the trails of base camp. Trekkers will get an excellent chance to snap unique flora and fauna before they go into hibernation.

Also, since the weather is crisp and clear, it’s easy for them to catch a glimpse of dazzling snow peaks in November. Here are some other reasons to trek Everest Base Camp in the month.

1. Fewer Crowds

Compared to the earlier months, November has fewer visitors arriving at the base camp due to unforeseeable climatic conditions. As the winter is close to arrival in the region, many trekkers avoid hiking the campsite in the month.

Following that, the trail remains empty for most of the days in November. As a result, trekkers to base camp can explore more hidden places and relish sweeping views without being disrupted.

Even getting the flights to Lukla won’t be that tough in the month as not many hikers flock to the region. The trails are quieter in November, which means visitors don’t have to compromise with their privacy.

2. Scenic View

The astounding view of Everest Base Camp in November has a stronger pull. It draws visitors from wide across with picturesque scenes of rolling hills, diverse landscapes, and vibrant valleys. The fresh wind with clear blue sky enables the trekker to catch a glimpse of snow-capped mountains from miles away in November.

Unlike in winter, trekkers won’t have to brave the stormy winds or fight against the fog and mist to sight the breathtaking view of Everest. In addition, wandering through the forest provides them glimpses of wild species and birds.

As far as escaping chilly wind and snowfall is concerned, November is the perfect time to visit the campsite. The month offers its visitor an overflowing charm of villages with vibrant valleys and picturesque meadows.

3. Availability of Accommodation

In November, Trekkers of Everest Base Camp won’t have problems finding accommodation as much as that in October. There’ll be plenty of lodges and guest houses willing to serve the guests as not many travelers visit the region in the month.

Even if the trekkers haven’t booked the room in advance, they can easily find lodging in tea houses. In addition, the visitor won’t have to line up or rush in the trail to avoid running out of accommodation and food.

4. Sharp Visibility

One of the perks of trekking Everest Base Camp in November is the easily visible snow peaks, sheer glaciers, and rock hills. Whether they’re miles away or near to the camp, trekkers can swiftly snap the glistening mountains, which otherwise they would be struggling to sight. In the absence of fog and mist, visitors can discover the surrounding mountains, glacial lakes, and icefall at the base camp.

5. Holiday Season

With Tihar just around the corner, November is a festive time in the Everest region. Trekkers can find the locals preparing to celebrate the festival of lights all around the villages. They can even partake in the celebrations and perform rituals. Religious gathering, dancing, and playing songs are the major highlights of Everest Base Camp Trek in November.

Outline Itinerary

Day 01: Flight to Lukla (30 mins), Trek to Phakding (2,610 m), 2-3 hrs

Day 02: Trek to Namche Bazaar (3,450 m)

Day 03: Rest day at Namche

Day 04: Trek to Tengboche (3,865 m), 5-6 hrs

Day 05: Trek to Dingboche (4,410 m), 6hrs

Day 06: Trek to Lobuche (4,940 m), 7-8 hrs

Day 07: Hike to Everest Base Camp (5,364 m), Return to Gorak Shep (5,140 m), 7-8 hrs

Day 08: Trek to Kala Patthar (5,643 m), 2-3 hrs Hike to Pheriche, 6 hrs

Day 09: Trek to Namche Bazaar, 7-8 hrs

Day 10: Trek to Lukla, 7 hrs

Day 11: Fly back to Kathmandu, 1,400 m

Difficulties of Everest Base Camp Trek in November

Hiking Everest Base Camp is so demanding that even trekkers in November get quickly exhausted and annoyed. Whether it’s the long winding trails or steep climbs and temperatures, visitors are always challenged to extremes to get to the top.

They’ll even have to deal with the rugged terrains filled with rocks and boulders to arrive at the base camp, which is strenuous. Some other trek difficulties that hikers have to face while climbing Everest Base Camp in November are as follows.

1. Severe Weather

November indicates the start of the winter season, following which trekkers may have to endure cold weather. But, of course, with autumn still lasting in the month, they won’t have difficulty climbing the trails at lower elevations.

But at an altitude of 4,310 m, the climate appears to tear down the hikers. It makes them combat bitter weather with icy wind and snowstorms. As the temperature falls rapidly, trekkers might even have to defy snow-covered trails that cause frostbite.

2. Altitude Sickness

Altitude sickness has always been a matter of concern for hikers climbing Everest Base Camp. But, in November, it gets intense, with most of the trekkers struggling from insomnia, dizziness, headache, and fatigue.

Due to the unstable weather and continuously rising elevation, visitors often find it difficult to breathe after climbing high mountain terrains. With the decreased air pressure and rapid exposure at higher altitudes, they also struggle from acute illnesses like fatigue, loss of appetite, and dizziness.

Hence, to minimize this effect, trekkers are recommended to acclimatize before going to higher elevations. They are also suggested not to climb more than 500 m and rest after reaching 900 m and above.

3. Long Trails

November does offer pleasant weather and lovely views for multi-day trips like Everest Base Camp. But, it won’t take away the fact that the trek is still strenuous, with a long and bumpy trail ending at 17,598 ft.

Starting from Lukla, the trail runs more than 40 miles and back, tiring for any hiker. On top of that, they’re jagged and run through alpine forest. Most of the sections have steep hills with loose rocks, making it difficult for hikers to ascend.

Therefore, hikers of the Everest Base Camp trek must come prepared to defy rocky trails. They must fully train themselves to stand the rugged terrains and steep slopes.

Read more on: How difficult is Everest Base Camp Trekking?

Food and Accommodations at Everest Base Camp Trek in November

The accommodation choice during Everest Base Camp Trek in November is mostly tea houses. These lodgings are comfortable but basic, with only necessary facilities like a pillow, blanket, and hot shower available for use.

Most tea houses have a range of rooms, from single to ensuite, which trekkers can book according to their needs. Lodges at places in higher elevations use solar energy to provide electricity and hot showers.

Therefore, they charge an extra amount to the trekkers willing to use the service. Other than that, visitors will have to pay for the meals provided in the guesthouses and lodges. At lower altitudes, they charge only US$1.50 for breakfast, but at higher altitudes, it costs relatively more.

Even the meals and snacks are a bit pricey in the upper region due to the unavailability of transportation. Foods served to guests are usually traditional Nepali dishes, consisting of rice, pulses, vegetables, and pickles. Seasonal ingredients and spices are used to make the dish for a delicious taste.

Some tea houses also offer various dishes and cuisines to guests, including stir-fried noodles, muesli, spring rolls, and spaghetti. Although these foods don’t look as fancy as in the restaurant, they still taste pretty good.

Equipment for Everest Base Camp Trek in November

Trekking a fine spot like Everest Base Camp is always fun, but it’s more remarkable in November. The month doesn’t disappoint its visitors with the sheer beauty, wonderful backdrop, and epic landscapes.

But, despite the splendid scenery and fine weather, trekkers still have to brace themselves for a challenging hike like Everest Base Camp. First, they’ll have to ensure that they have the right equipment and gear required for the trip; otherwise, it’ll be tough to make it to the top.

Having the right tools and apparatus makes the journey to the camp easy and comfortable. So, here are a few of the trekking checklists that’ll help you overcome the challenges during Everest Base Camp Trek in November.

Clothing

  • Windproof and puffy jacket
  • Long sleeves shirt and trouser
  • Lightweight fleece pants
  • Synthetic or woolen t-shirt
  • Convertible hiking pants
  • Woolen scarf and midweight fleece/winter hat

Footwear

  • Sturdy climbing shoes
  • Insulated mountaineering boots
  • Pairs of synthetic and moisture wicking socks

Other Miscellaneous

  • First-aid kit
  • Personal toiletries and sanitizer
  • Spare batteries, charger, and flashlight
  • Water bottle and purifier
  • Insect repellent
  • Journals and pen

Read more on Packing List for Everest Base Camp Trek

Preparation for Everest Base Camp Trek in November

Since it’s a moderate hike with no technical difficulties, trekkers won’t have to overwork themselves. They can go easy on their workout routine and don’t rush things. That said, trekkers will still have to work on their physical fitness to withstand the rough terrains with steep hills and boulders.

Physical Preparation

It may be an easy walk for mountaineers, but Everest Base Camp Trek is demanding for beginners. Even the average walking course can be incredibly difficult for them in lack of physical stamina and endurance.

Therefore, trekkers of Everest Base Camp have to prepare themselves ahead of the trek. They’ll have to stay fit and regularly exercise for the long-distance walk. Before heading out on the trail, they’ll have to improve their physical strength and stability.

It doesn’t mean they have to follow an intense workout regimen and strict diet. Even regular exercise like jogging, cycling, and running can be of great help to beat the rough terrain of Everest Base Camp. Besides, both long and short-distance walks are pretty beneficial for the Preparation of the trek.

Mental Preparation

Mental Preparation is as important as physical to prevent the stress of walking steep trails. Hikers can get easily intimidated by the long-distance walk like Everest Base Camp. Therefore, they’ll have to keep their mind stable to avoid anxiety and additional pressure.

If the travelers are new to hiking, they better start with a day trip and small hikes to boost confidence. Studying the weather and itinerary of the base camp trek also helps the climber to avoid extra pressure.

title: Everest Base Camp Trek in June
excerpt: Wondering What Everest Base Camp Trek in June is like? Our article solely helps you know about the weather, temperature, difficulties and many more about this month. Firstly, let me ask you how many…
html:
Wondering What Everest Base Camp Trek in June is like? Our article solely helps you know about the weather, temperature, difficulties and many more about this month.

Firstly, let me ask you how many of you have reached the Everest Base Camp or visited the Everest region in June? Well, if you have prior experience, you know how adventurous the journey is at this time.

June is the month when monsoon and summer coincide with each other. So, you might question how wise the Everest Base Camp Trek in June is? The answer is with the proper plan, and gear trekking in June is delightful for all trekkers.

Trek to Everest Base Camp is a lifetime experience, but traveling during June can make it tricky with the monsoon rain. But what is a journey without any adventure and thrill, right?

June is Grishma Ritu (meaning summer) in Nepal, but the monsoon also begins mid-month. So, you should prepare well and choose good reliable agencies for a safe, comfortable trek.

Reasons to Do Everest Base Camp Trek in June

Many travelers avoid visiting Everest base camp in June, but they don’t realize they miss many things. So, we have some reasons written below:

Low crowds

Everest Base Camp Trek in June falls during the off-season time. There are a low no. of trekkers and climbers during this time, giving you as much privacy as you want.

Many travelers and visitors end their trip during this time, making the routes less crowded and perfect for peace lovers. If you love walking in silence, then trekking to Everest Base Camp in June is an ideal month for you.

Discount and offers

Another best reason for EBC Trek in June is the discounts and offers. As it is the off time for travelers, many agencies, lodges, and flights provide discount and combo package offers for travelers.

Usually, the prices are fixed for the accommodation, but you can lower the cost with your bargaining skills as there are fewer visitors in June. Also, you get to enjoy the full hospitality without delays or long waiting.

Unique Vegetation

Unlike other months, you might find it hard to get a clear view of your surroundings by mid-June. But the unique vegetation makes up for this disadvantage.

With continuous rainfall, new species of plants and flowers grow in the trails. The forest paths are colorfully covered in beautiful wildflowers adding flavor to them.

Adventure

Everest Base Camp in June is an adventure itself. The main reason is the harsh and challenging trials. Only those traveling during June can tell about the interesting episodes that happen when walking on these routes. It is quite a journey you will remember for a lifetime.

Rice Planting Festival

The National Paddy Day usually falls during late June or early July so that you can catch this festival during your trek. The farmers plant rice after enough rain has fallen. The people eat Dahi Chiura (flattened rice with yogurt) and sing folk songs. If you are interested, you can take part by offering them your help with planting.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Major Attractions

As you know, June falls in summer with a slight touch of rainfall, making the month beautiful for travel. Some major attractions to travel to EBC during June are:

  • The walks are comfortable with the warm temperature and pleasant wind at a high altitude.
  • The light rain showers during the evening and nighttime make the following day beautiful and fresh.
  • This month offers the rice planting festival, so you can try it out and help the locals as well.
  • The environment looks fresh and luscious after the rain clears.
  • With non-stop rainfall, the valleys and jungles look greenery.

Weather and Temperature of During the Trek

June is a combination of summer and monsoon, so it goes through different climatic changes. The weather is sunny, hot, and bright in the earlier weeks; slight rainfall occurs during the midweeks and dark clouds with heavy rain by the end of the month.

One good thing about the June monsoon is that it usually occurs in the late evening or early morning. Thus the daytime is primarily bright with slight rays of the sun.

The first half of June is suitable for trekking, so the earlier weeks are best to avoid the rain if you are traveling this month. During the mid-week, there is occasional rainfall but not a heavy downpour.

The final weeks have heavy rainfall with occasional thunderstorms, but the higher you climb, the less the downpour. The temperature ranges from 18 ℃ /64 ℉ to -3 ℃ /27 ℉.

Each destination has a different temperature, and it drops with every ascent. Like the max temperature in Lukla is 18 ℃ while it is 8 ℃ in Namche. Similarly, the max temp in Lobuche is 12 ℃ while it is 10 ℃ in Gorak Shep.

The max wind speed is 9.4 mph in Namche Bazaar, while the average wind speed in Base Camp is 5.4 mph. The days are brighter and warmer compared to the night. The weather gets chilly and cold by nighttime.

Difficulties During Everest Base Camp Trek in June

The trekking difficulty in June is challenging yet amazing. You experience different challenges according to other times. Some of them are:

Landslide

Landslide is a major difficulty faced during the Everest base camp trek in June. It might be summer for earlier weeks, but the monsoon begins by the mid of the month. So, there is continuous rainfall in the lower areas, which increases the risk of landslides and avalanches.

Landslides don’t occur in every place, but there are some points in the trails exposed to them. During June, the chances of landslides are high in these areas, so you need to be extra careful while passing these points.

Also, in some parts of the trails, excessive water flows from the waterfalls requiring you to take off your shoes.

Slippery and muddy road

By now, June is a monsoon month, so the trials being slippery and muddy is not a new thing. The roads get wet even with slight rainfall making them muddy.

Trekkers should not underestimate the trails, mostly during monsoon months. The routes have steep ascend, descend and the slippery, muddy road adds extra challenge and pressure to the visitor.

So, If you do not bring the right shoes, you might slip and injure yourself. Thus always be cautious and careful during the walks.

Bugs and leeches

If you are not a fan of bugs and insects, traveling to EBC will be a disaster during June. Whether it be during the earlier week or later, you will have to deal with bugs and insects.

During the summer weeks, you come across bugs like mosquitoes, grasshoppers, centipedes, spiders, etc. And as the monsoon begins, you will deal with leeches in the trails as well.

Dealing with leeches is very tiring during wet weather. You come across them in every twist and turn of the forest trails; they will be crawling on the way, trees, and plants.

Unstable weather condition

Usually, the weather is unpredictable, and it gets more uncertain during June. The temperature and climatic conditions can change anytime in the Everest region.

You might see a clear blue sky one minute, and the next minute, dark clouds are hovering over them. During monsoon, it can rain anytime without any notice making the walks difficult.

Sometimes, it even rains continuously for days which can be a problem when catching the flight from Kathmandu to Lukla or vice versa. The flights are often canceled or delayed due to bad weather.

Altitude sickness

Altitude sickness is a difficulty faced any time or month of the year. It can happen while you’re hiking or climbing to higher altitudes and your body could not adjust to the new environment.

Not everyone but a few suffers from altitude sickness, so it is nothing to panic about. However, if you do not treat the illness in time, it will put your life in danger.

A few symptoms of the AMS are headache, nausea, vomiting, sleeping difficulty, breathing difficulty, and many more. If you feel sick, then immediately inform the guide or nearest person.

Lighting and Thunderstorms

Lighting and thunderstorms are typical during the monsoon season. The sound of thunder and lighting is both beautiful and terrifying. They come unexpectedly so that you might get caught in the middle of it.

Lighting and thunderstorms are fascinating when staying at home but can be scary when going on treks. It is because there are no proper places on the trails to shelter you.

So, in case of heavy lightning and thunderstorms, the trek will come to a halt and make you stop on the way for safety purposes.

Tips to Overcome the Difficulties

You can’t change the difficulties, but you can overcome them for a better and memorable trek. So, we have pointed out a few ways to make your tour easier.

Keep the weather forecast updated.

The first standard tip you will hear is to keep yourself updated with the weather forecast. As you know from above, weather is quite tricky in the Himalayan region and especially during June. So, always listen to the weather report and make plans accordingly.

Carry Bug spray and salt

You might be wondering why salt? It is because if you have made up your mind to travel in June, then it is indispensable. The trials are filled with leeches during this time, so salt helps to pull them out.

You can expect leeches, insects, and bugs at every point of your way. As it is the rainy season, you can see earthworms in the trails as well. So, Bug spray and salt help you keep them away.

You can also wear long sleeve t-shirts and leech socks to protect yourself from leeches. It is better not to wear loose or short clothes during the rainy season.

Start the trek early.

We recommend trekkers start the trek early in the monsoon season to avoid rain showers. Wake up early and check if it is raining or not. If it is raining, you can rest and check the time and again for the rain to stop.

But if it is not raining, then carry your bag and begin the journey. The rain mostly starts during the late evening, so days are usually dry.

Add extra days to your trip.

Always add extra holiday time to your trip when traveling in June. These days are for in case of flight cancellation and delays due to bad weather conditions. It will be a problem if you have an international flight right the next day as your trek ends. Thus, we advise you to add the extra time at the end of your itinerary to be on the safe side.

Hire Guide or Porter

You can trek solo for EBC trek, and we know you might be excited to walk in privacy. But we recommend you not travel solo and hire a guide or porter during June. Having a companion along can be beneficial if you injure yourself or are lost.

Itinerary for Everest Base Camp Trek in June

Day 1: Welcome to Kathmandu

You begin by landing at the Tribhuvan International Airport, where you meet our officials. They will wait for you at the terminal to pick you up and drop you off at the hotel. The representative will help you check-in and later introduce you to the tour guide.

Day 2: Preparation and city tour day

Today you will roam around Kathmandu city and visit the UNESCO heritage sites. You see many famous places like Pashupatinath, Swayambhunath, Basantapur Durbar Square, Boudhanath, and Patan Durbar Square.

After finishing the tour, you return to the hotel, where the guide will explain to you about the Everest Base Camp Trek. Later, you will join us for dinner organized by our company. The next is going to be hectic, so get some rest.

Day 3: Fly to Lukla (2,860 m) then Trek to Phakding (2,610 m)- 3 to 4 hours

The Everest Base Camp Trek in June begins with a scenic flight from Kathmandu to Lukla. It is a short 25 to 30 min ride over the hills with mesmerizing views of peaks around you.

After the short flight, you now begin your trek by heading to Phakding. You climb the trails from the left bank of Dudh Koshi river, then descend and join the Everest route to arrive at Phakding.

Day 4: Trek to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m)- 6 to 7 hours

The trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar is quite adventurous today. You cross several suspension bridges and enter the Sagarmatha National Park.

After heading out of the village, you cross a high suspension bridge over the Dudh Koshi river. Walking for about an hour, you reach Monjo and enter the national park. Then moving further ahead, you get to Jorsalle and ascend a steep route to arrive at Namche Bazaar.

Day 5: Acclimatization day

Namche is the main stop for trekkers and climbers visiting the Everest region. People spend an extra day here before climbing to higher altitudes. They acclimatize in Namche to adjust their body to the current environment. During your stay here, you can visit nearby attractions like the Everest view hotel, Khunde hospital, museum, etc.

Day 6: Trek to Tengboche (3,860 m)- 5 to 6 hours

Your trek to Tengboche begins after having a warm breakfast. You start by walking on the trails above the Dudh Koshi river. Continuing the trip, you cross several beautiful settlements and tea shops before making a steep descent.

Then you cross a bridge over the Dudh Koshi river and gradually climb to reach Tengboche, a beautiful Sherpa village. This place offers an ancient Buddist monastery.

Day 7: Trek to Dingboche (4,410 m)- 6 to 7 hours

You begin by descending the trails then crossing over the Imja Khola. After that, you climb to Pangboche village that lies opposite the great Ama Dablam (6,856 m). From there, you make a gradual ascend through the lush forest of juniper oaks before arriving at Dingboche.

Day 8: Acclimatize at Dingboche

The second acclimatization is here at Dingboche. You can explore the surroundings or climb to close-by viewpoints. You can also add a small side trip to Chhukung valley for some delicious food.

Day 9: Trek to Lobuche (4,940 m)- 4 to 5 hours

The trek starts by following the trails through Dugla, seeing the panoramic view of several mountains. Then climbing the routes, you walk a zigzag path through the rocky moraines. On your way, you will see many Mani walls, Chortens, and prayer flags. Continuing the ascend along the glacier, you reach Lobuche.

Day 10: Hike to Everest Base Camp (5,364 m) and back to Gorak Shep (5,164 m) 5 to 6 hours

From Lobuche, you head to Gorak Shep, where you have your lunch and take a rest for some time. The hike to EBC is about 2 hours long; it is pretty short but challenging with steep gradual climbs. After reaching the base camp, you explore the area, spend some time and return to Gorak Shep for the night.

Day 11: Hike to Kala Patthar (5,643 m), then trek to Pheriche (4,371 m)- 7 to 8 hours.

You wake early in the morning to hike to Kala Patthar to view the sunrise. This place is a viewpoint that offers the breathtaking sights of several peaks. Some are Everest, Khumbutse, Lhotse, Nuptse, Lingtren, Pumori, etc. After a beautiful time, you descend to Pheriche.

Day 12: Trek to Namche Bazaar- 7 hours

Today you cover the walk through the hillside covered in juniper, oaks, and rhododendron. The trail is colorfully filled with flowers of pink, red, and white. Making a descent in the tracks, you reach Tengboche, where you have your lunch. Then retracing the steps, you continue to head towards Namche Bazaar.

Day 13: Trek to Lukla- 6 to 7 hours

You carefully and slowly descend the steep trails through the rocky terrain to reach Lukla on this day. Cross over the river through a suspension bridge and follow the same path; you continue the walk. After walking through jungles, streams, rivers, and settlements, you make a final ascend in the trail to reach Lukla.

Day 14: Flight to Kathmandu- 25 to 30 minutes

In June, your Everest Base Camp Trek comes to a halt as you fly back to Kathmandu from Lukla. Viewing the same beautiful scenarios, you land at the airport. The guide will then drop you at your hotel ending the trip.

Day 15: Departure

The final time to say our goodbyes has arrived. The official will transfer you to the airport according to your flight schedule. We hope the journey was exciting for you.

Packing list

Advice for all trekkers is to pack wisely and lightly. You should include all the essential gears needed for Everest Base Camp Trek in July. So, make a list in advance to help remember the things. We have also recommended a few items below:

  • Sleeping bag
  • Waterproof backpack and cover
  • Rain jacket
  • Rain trouser
  • Waterproof shoes
  • Down and fleece jacket
  • Light, breathable t-shirts
  • Windcheater
  • Gloves
  • Socks
  • Warm cap for nights
  • Sun hat
  • Moisturizer
  • Waterproof sunscreen
  • Lip balm
  • Body lotion
  • Water bottle
  • Purification tablets
  • Personal hygiene kit (toothpaste, toothbrush, etc.)
  • Quick-drying towels
  • Trash bag
  • Salt and bug spray
  • Camera, extra batteries, and other miscellaneous items

P.S. The above items are samples, so you can add or subtract things according to your needs.

Final Say

We hope our article Everest Base Camp Trek in June was helpful for you. Traveling in June is exciting but be prepared to overcome all the difficulties that come along with it.
