title: Everest Base Camp Trek in February
excerpt: Aren’t you here to alleviate your doubts about the Everest Base Camp Trek in February? We guess you are! Well, you are at the right place to clear all of your concerns. By the end of this blog, you…
html:
Aren’t you here to alleviate your doubts about the Everest Base Camp Trek in February? We guess you are!

Well, you are at the right place to clear all of your concerns. By the end of this blog, you will be so sure and clear about everything related to February’s exploration of Everest Base Camp Trek. And then you can make a precise decision on whether to do the trek in February or not.

As you may have a hint, February is one of the peaceful times for rambling on the trails of Nepal. Do you know why it is so? Well, the month is the final month of the Winter season in Nepal. Many people think that it is still so cold in the mountains and too risky as well. That’s why most of them do not plan for Everest Base Camp visit in February.

Yet, the circumstances are different during the month. With peaceful surroundings, the Everest Region’s higher hills and mountains remain mantled by snow. Likewise, the clear skies tend to last longer than usual, resulting in mountain views all day.

Still, people will say the month is chilly and hence tricky, don’t go!

But remember that it is mainly when February is compared to the Autumn and Spring months, the two most crowded times of the year in Nepal. February, in reality, is the warmest month of Winter, and there is no severe problem in bearing the adventure with the proper clothing.

You might still be confused about what to do! Just read the whole article, and your mind shall come across a rightful decision.

Everest Base Camp Trek Weather in February

The month you are considering, February, is a month that comes at the very end of Winter in Nepal. It concludes the effects of the chilly and snowy Winter. The high temperature, which has been freezing the mountains for some months, starts to warm them slowly by this month.

Looking at a thermometer throughout this month, you will find the average temperature around the Everest Region from 4.3°C to -15°C, which is a little chilly as expected. The morning and night parts are cold and windy. But the temperature gets a little warmer as we go to the second half of the month.

Besides, the weather also varies with the altitudes. If you are in the higher region already, make sure you wear good clothes. You can guess the higher parts of the trek like Kala Patthar, Everest Base Camp, and Gorakh Shep to be colder than other places.

On the other hand, you can be part of a beautiful adventure during the month. The mountains are transparent and visible throughout the month. However, there can be occasional snowfall in February. You have to be aware of that and follow the instructions of your trekking guide. And everything will go as planned.

In a nutshell, February is not a bad month for doing Everest Base Camp Trekking. If you have the right kind of clothes and gear, you will witness Everest’s face, which the rest of the people miss. Most importantly, with not so many people’s crowd around the trail, you will enjoy the serenity like no other month.

Similar articles you may like:

  • 7 day Everest Base Camp Trek
  • Packing List for Everest Base Camp Trek
  • Everest Base Camp Trek Map

Why Everest Base Camp Trek in February?

February in Nepal has something in the box for its visitors. To know what the offerings are, you need to do the trek. But still, we are going to present what is so special about February’s Everest Base Camp Trekking:

Lesser Crowd

You should explore Everest in February to experience and enjoy the less crowded conditions. The trails are not as congested as they are in the autumn and spring months.

That means there will not be many people on the track during the month, which is unusual for a trail like Everest Base Camp. You will feel the quietness all over the path, even inside the teahouses(lodges). Therefore, February is just a perfect time for those who prefer a peaceful time for treks.

Breathtaking Views

Winter is a sublime time for breathtaking views in Nepal. As you know, snowfall occurs during this season. The snowfall makes the effortlessly picturesque place even more alluring.

In that case, February is the suitable month to observe the fresh snow decoration in the hills and peaks of the Khumbu Region. Mt Everest, the showstopper of the trek, looks ethereal during the month. You should not miss that one!

Lots of Discounts

February can be a suitable month for the wise spenders. As February is not as busy as April or October, the tour planners display heavy discounts to attract more trekkers. As a result, it becomes less costly to do Everest Base Camp Trek in February than in October and March, the two peak months for the trek.

Moreover, the flight and accommodation costs are also relatively low during the month. Thus, it is a month to save some bucks for you.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

How to Prepare for Everest Base Camp Trek in February?

Proper Cardio Training

First and foremost, you will need a good cardio level for Everest Base Camp Trek. The trek is a longer and more challenging one for beginners than the experienced ones. If you are one of them, then training is hugely important for you. Start the cardio training program as soon as possible.

You can participate in swimming, cycling, day hiking, running, and others as well. Stick to the training, and you shall be ready for the trek in February. Well, exercise is crucial for every month’s Everest Base Camp Excursions, not only February. So immediately after finishing this blog, make a strict cardio training plan and start working on it.

Right sort of Packing

Just getting a good body shape will not do things in February. You will need something warm and thick to cover your body throughout the trek. Plus, you will need a few extra snow gear like gaiters and crampons. If you miss any of these packings, you will face the worst side of February’s Everest Base Camp visit.

You can check out our full blog dedicated to Packing List for Everest Base Camp Trek for the packing reference. Check that out and begin arranging the items without omitting any.

Altitude Education

The altitude of the trek is worrying you, right? Do not be! It is obvious, and everyone experiences it while they plan the trek. Who in the world would not worry about heights when choosing none other than Everest Base Camp Trek. Thus, accept the fact and start planning on how you are going to face it.

Well, the first step to face the high altitudes of any trek is to know more about altitude. You have to be aware of everything related to mountain sickness. That will make you literate about the illness and its do’s and don’ts. And you will be able to avoid it on the trek quite easily.

If you don’t know about altitude sickness yet, go and look all over Google about it, just go. Wait, finish the article first!

Mental Readiness

Everest Base Camp Trek may look like an impossible hill to some of you. With so much to trek on such rugged terrain, the hike will not be easy at all. But thinking only about the hurdles of the tour will not perform wonders for you.

Instead, you should be mentally ready to face anything that February’s Everest Base Camp Trek has for you. Do not seed even a negative thought in your head, and you shall become mentally prepared for the fantastic adventure. This way, you will perform great during the trek unknowingly, and you’ll thank yourself for it later on.

Essential Tips for Everest Base Camp Trek in February

Get Yourself Going in the Morning

Start the day’s trek as early as possible. The days in February went by quite quickly and are shorter than usual. You may have to trek in the dark. So be careful about that and aim to get going early in the morning.

Bring all of the Vital Winter Gear and Clothes

Buy all of the necessary Winter gear and clothing. And then take a thorough check of your kits and clothing before starting the trek. Possibly, you might leave crucial gear and apparel at your home or in the places you go during the journey. So make sure you check your things every day from the first to the last.

Pass Your Loads to the Man

If you have a heavy backpack and other things for the trek, hiring a porter is a game-changer decision. You will have someone to carry your belongings with you all the time, and you can enjoy the walk thoroughly.

Hire an Expert Local Guide

Winter solo treks in Nepal are high risk. The risk is still prevalent during February as well. Therefore, you should hire an experienced local guide for yourself and the team to guide you through various possible situations.

Keep the Water Going In

When you are trekking in the mountains, you have to drink water time and time again. Your body gets easily dehydrated up there, and you might catch mountain sickness for that reason. Hence, keep your body hydrated.

Slow Trek Wins the Race

Trek calmly without hurrying much. The quicker you walk, the closer to the mountain sickness you will get. A tired body needs some time to acclimate the altitudes. So slow walking will help you a lot. However, do not walk too slow though; you might stay far behind.

Outlined Itinerary for Everest Base Camp Trek

Day 01: Arrival in Kathmandu

Your journey will be ours once you land in Kathmandu at Kathmandu Airport. The team will be there at the airport to receive you and your belongings. Following that, you will trace the way to your hotel in Kathmandu. Later in the evening, you will meet the entire Everest Base Camp Trek team for dinner together. And overnight in Kathmandu.

Day 02: Fly to Lukla(2,860 m) and Trek from Lukla to Phakding(2,610 m) | 40 minutes Flight, 3 to 4 hours Trek

The next day, you will fly to Lukla from Kathmandu, a 40 minutes scenic flight. It will be the day when you will start tracing the Everest Region for the first time. You will get a warm welcome at Lukla after your landing. The day will begin to get better as you will leave Lukla following a downhill trail to Phakding.

Along the route, you will walk through traditional villages, Dudh Koshi River’s riverbank, suspension bridges, and lush woods too. It will be a pleasing and easy trekking day which will end at Phakding. Overnight in Phakding.

Day 03: Trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar(3,450 m) | 6 to 7 hours Trek

From Phakding, the way will wind up towards Namche Bazaar, the Himalayan Town of the mighty Sherpas. You will walk through the gate of Sagarmatha National Park at Monjo by showing your permits.

Also, you will cross the whitish Dudh Koshi River several times through swinging suspension bridges. Likewise, you will reach Jorsalle just before climbing to Namche Bazaar through a steep hill. As you step into Namche Bazaar, you will know why the town is so famous.

Day 04: Acclimatization Day in Namche Bazaar

The fourth day will be around Namche Bazaar with no altitude gain for the day. Your body needs some time to get along with nature. That’s why this day will be on the itinerary to make you friendly with the altitudes. You will spend the whole day being busy hiking around Namche Bazaar. Overnight in Namche.

Day 05: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Tengboche(3,865 m) | 5 to 6 hours

Now, you shall move towards Tengboche after a rest day in Namche. It will be a busy trek day as you will see peaks of the region transparently through the day. Moving over a stone patched trail, via several villages and forests, you will end up in Tengboche, a village of Tengboche Monastery, and a great mountain panorama.

Day 06: Trek from Tengboche to Dingboche(4,410 m) | 5 to 6 hours

It will be another trekking day where you will get to see lots of mountains. More specifically, Ama Dablam will be more apparent than others. Trekking over a scenic trail through a pine forest area, you will reach Dingboche. Overnight in the lapses of Mt Ama Dablam in Dingboche.

Day 07: Acclimatization day in Dingboche

Luckily, you will spend an entire day in Dingboche by rambling around the villages, looking at the breathtaking mountains and landscapes. While you stay busy exploring the place, your body will acclimate to new heights—yet another overnight in Dingboche.

Day 08: Trek from Dingboche to Lobuche(4,940 m) | 5 to 6 hours

Lobuche will be the trek destination for the day. You will start with a climb of a rounding trail made of glacier terminal moraine. And en route, you will also come across the memorial place of stones and chortens dedicated to the lost souls in the mountains. This way, you will reach Lobuche, a small village right near the Lobuche Peak.

Day 09: Trek from Lobuche to Everest Base Camp(5,364 m) via Gorak Shep(5,140 m) |7 to 8 hours

And this will be the day when you will finally step on the Everest Base Camp(5,364 m). To do this feat, you’ll trek a long distance from Lobuche to the base camp via Gorak Shep. Crossing all the odds and hard parts, you will reach the legendary place to adore the mountain show of various peaks, including Mt Everest. Once you have enough time at the base camp, you will get back to Gorak Shep for the night.

Day 10: Trek to Kala Patthar(5,5545m) and descend to Pheriche(4,243 m) | 6 to 7 hours

After being in the base camp, it is time to reach Kala Patthar, the best place in the Everest Region to watch mountains. The trail goes straight upwards from Gorak Shep through the terminal moraine. As soon as you get there, you will get to see the so-called best mountain panorama in the world. After that, you will descend toward Pheriche, where you will end up at a teahouse for the night.

Day 11: Trek back from Pheriche to Namche Bazaar | 7 to 8 hours

As the job of the trek is already done, you are now on the retracing part of the trek. On this day, you will descend through the same way via Tengboche to reach Namche Bazaar in the evening. The trek is entirely downhill and dropping; you will love it. Overnight in Namche Bazaar.

Day 12: Trek back from Namche Bazaar to Lukla | 6 to 8 hours

This day will be the last trekking day of Everest Base Camp Trek when you trek back to Lukla from Namche. Along the way, you will pass via the same settlements like Monjo, Phakding, and more. Once in Lukla, you will call it a day.

Day 13: Fly back to Kathmandu from Lukla | 40 minutes Flight

In the same way, you will join the flight, which will take you back to Kathmandu. The flight duration will be 40 minutes long, and along the time, you will see the same bird’s eye view again. After the safe landing in Kathmandu, you will go to the hotel for refreshment and later to the happening places of the city for hangouts. Overnight in Kathmandu.

Day 14: Departure

And this day will bring an end to your Everest Base Camp Trek and the time with the team of Base Camp Adventure. The team will give you a hotel transfer to the Kathmandu Airport for your departure.

You may also like:

  • Everest Three Pass Trek
  • Luxury Lodge Trek to Everest Base Camp
  • Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return

Alternatives to Everest Base Camp Trek in February

Everest Panorama Trek

Everest Panorama Trek, the shortest trek of the region, is an excellent alternative to Everest Base Camp Trek in February. The nine days long itinerary, whose highest point is Tengboche(3,860 m), is specially designed for beginners who cannot go all the way to Everest Base Camp.

This trek involves fewer trekking days, and altitude sickness is also less prone during it. For someone looking to avoid the strenuous trail of the Everest Base Camp Trek but still wants to view the Everest Region, this trek works excellent. Plus, you will not experience the chilly weather of the high area during February as you will return from Tengboche only. That’s why we do not see a better option than this for the starters who like to play it safe.

Everest Gokyo Trek

With some added adventure, Everest Gokyo Trek is another option to do in February. Gokyo Valley, the heartthrob of the Everest Region, is a valley known for its pristine lakes and unique landscapes. If someone wants to see the other side of the Everest Region, Gokyo Valley Trek is the choice.

The region where Gokyo Valley resides is not as famous as the Everest Base Camp Area. But, Gokyo Valley is equally rewarding as the Everest Base Camp area or maybe more than that. The trek’s highest point is Gokyo Ri(5,357 m) and the place provides you with the best views of the mountains and the Gokyo Lakes. Along with mountains, you will explore the fresh lakes in the high hills of Nepal during this trek. Thus, this trek becomes an easy choice for those who like to see lakes and mountains in one trip.

Other Notable Mentions

There are plenty more trekking options in the Everest Region that you can consider. Some of them are: Everest Base Camp Trek with Island Peak Climbing, Rolwaling Trek, Gokyo Valley and Renjo La Pass Trek, Everest Three Pass Trek, and more.

To know more on all of the Everest Region Treks, visit this page, Everest Region.

Conclusion

Life without dares and adventures is merely a life without great experiences. If you want to experience something special, you should do the things that others are not doing. One of those sorts of experiences can be Everest Base Camp Trek in February. So, nothing should stop you from doing this adventure, not even the chilly weather of the month.

Base Camp Adventure will help you do that safely. Just book the trek with us, and the rest will be some serious fun.

title: Manaslu Tsum Valley Trek Map
excerpt: A trekking map is an essential part of any trekking journey in the remote terrains of Nepal. This Manaslu Tsum Valley Trek map is an easy-to-read document that provides you with accurate information…
html:
A trekking map is an essential part of any trekking journey in the remote terrains of Nepal. This Manaslu Tsum Valley Trek map is an easy-to-read document that provides you with accurate information regarding this trek. They also denote the trekking route of this journey in great detail.

Moreover, the new Manaslu trek map also includes the possible side trips during this journey. This accurate map provides all the details about motor roads and trekking paths. You will have an overall idea of the distance you need to cover to arrive at your destination.

Furthermore, this map allows you to plan your logistics to avoid any hassles. Travelers can maintain a steady pace and tackle fatigue-related issues during this journey. Besides that, you can also set up acclimatization points and take shortcuts if necessary. Since the mountainous region has a poor network connection, these maps work as ideal reference points.

Therefore, trekkers should take this map with them all along the trek. Read on to know more about the Manaslu Tsum valley trek map and other related information in detail.

Check our package: Manaslu and Tsum Valley Trek and Manaslu Circuit Trek

About the Route

Our journey starts with a Kathmandu to Soti Khola scenic drive, passing through Dhading and Arkhet bazaar. Moreover, you will start your journey from Soti Khola as we continue our trek to Machha Khola. The trail then leads you to Jagat from Machha Khola.

You will pass through various Gurung villages with incredible views of snow-capped mountains. We will pass through Philim, Chumling, and finally arrive at Chhokang Paro, with Tibetan Buddhist monasteries like Tanju, Rainjam, and Gho. The beautiful Ganesh Himal range and the Tibetan Himalayan range look incredible along the trail.

The trail then leads you to the Nile via Milarepa cave, a sacred meditation cave used by the revered Yogi Milarepa. You will then start your journey from the Nile to Bajyo, passing through Tibetan settlements near the border. The Mu Gompa trail provides you with many cultural insights as you pass through the Dhephu Doma Nunnery Gompa.

Trail then passes through Yangdol Khola to arrive at Rachen Gompa, passing a beautiful waterfall. Rachen Gompa leads back to Chhokang Paro through Domje. The beautiful snow-capped mountains in the region include the Ganesh Himal range.

Domje to Bihi passes through Rachen and descends to Lokpa.

The trail then passes through various suspension bridges and passes through Nyak, Rana, Deng, and others. Travelers will then trek to Namrung on a plain terrain and then move uphill through the alpine forests. Namrung to Sama Gaon trail passes through the frozen lake of Birendra Tal.

It will then lead you to Samdo village, from where you will trek to Dharamsala/Larkya Phedi on a steep trail. The Dharamsala – Bimthang trail passes through the lateral moraine of Larkya Glacier, the frozen pass of Larkya La (5,160 m). The Manaslu and Annapurna massifs and the various glaciers look incredible while traveling to Bimthang.

Bimthang to Dharapani through alpine forests lead you to Gho. Travelers will pass alongside the beautiful Dudh Khola. Besisahar is another four hours off-road jeep drive from Dharapani. Finally, you will take another drive back to Kathmandu. You can enjoy fabulous landscapes filled with lush hills during your journey from Besisahar. It takes around 5-6 hours to arrive at the capital city on a scenic highway path.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Manaslu Tsum Valley Trek Map Description

Kathmandu – Soti Khola

Drive duration: 7-8 hours

Maximum altitude: 700 m

Kathmandu to Soti Khola is the starting journey of the Manaslu Tsum Valley Trek. Moreover, the trip also passes through scenic and diverse landscapes of the hilly region. There are many rice fields, terrace farmed hills, and serene waterfalls in the area.

Arkhet bazaar is the significant point of this journey. You can observe the beautiful Arkhet Khola as well, with many lodges along the trail. There are various means of transportation to arrive at this destination, including jeeps and local buses. Soti Khola is a beautiful settlement with greenery all around. It is also the starting point of the Manaslu Tsum Valley trek.

Sotikhola – Machha Khola

Trek duration: 6-7 hours

Maximum altitude: 863 m

The Soti Khola to Macha Khola trail starts on a bumpy journey in the Budhi Gandaki basin. You can find various serene waterfalls and other natural wonders before arriving at Liding. It is a beautiful village with a camping site, and Lapubesi village near a green hill.

The peaceful and scenic town will provide you incredible adventure. Later, you will pass through the slippery trails and thrilling suspension bridges to arrive at Machha Khola. There are different accommodation facilities and medical clinics in the village located on a hilly slope.

Machha Khola – Jagat

Trek duration: 7-8 hours

Maximum altitude: 1,350 m

This section of the trek trails passes through narrow paths between a cliff and the Budhi Gandaki river. After trekking for some time, you will pass through Dobhan, Shyaule Bhatti, and finally arrive at Yaru.

The beautiful views of scenic Budhi Gandaki will enchant you, and you can observe lovely cascades. After trekking incredible landscapes for a few hours, you will arrive at Jagat, which has stone-paved streets. There are basic accommodation facilities and a campsite too.

Jagat – Film

Trek duration: 3-4 hours

Maximum altitude: 1,570 m

The trail from Jagat to Philim passes through rugged terrain alongside the Budhi Gandaki River. You will pass through various scenic landscapes while en route to Philim. The magical views of snow-capped mountains, including Shringi Himal (7,161 m), will enchant you along the trail. Finally, after a trek of a few hours, you will arrive at Philim, which is a large Gurung village where you can find many corn and millet fields.

Philim – Chumling

Trek duration: 6-7 hours

Maximum altitude: 2,386 m

Philim to Chumling trail starts with a steep ascent as it travels high up to Budhi Gandaki River. It then passes through the beautiful serene waterfall Lokpa. Travelers will pass through small streams and Siyar Khola observing majestic views of snow-capped mountains, including Ganesh Himal and Shringi Himal (7,161 m).

Chumling – Chhokang Paro

Trek duration: 5-6 hours

Maximum altitude: 3,031 m

The trail from Chumling to Chokkhang Paro traverses through Siyar Khola. The Chokkhang Paro is a Tibetan-Buddhist settlement home to various monasteries like Rainjam, Gho, and Tanju. There is also a Dzong in Chhokang Paro. The Ganesh Himal range and Tibetan Himalayan range look spectacular from the village viewpoint.

Chumling – Gumba Lungdang

Trek duration: 6-7 hours

Maximum altitude: 3,200 m

The trail from Chulming to Gumba Lundang passes through steep paths along the foothills of the Himalayas. Various scenic landmarks in the region provide trekkers with an incredible adventure. Trekkers will also pass through multiple routes that can lead to Ganesh Himal. Therefore, numerous mountaineers take this route to reach the base camp for their expedition.

Chhokang Paro – Mu Gompa

Trek duration: 5-6 hours

Maximum altitude: 3,031 m

Choking Paro is a beautiful village settlement that passes through the Milarepa Cave, a sacred meditation cave dedicated to Yogi Milarepa. You can also visit the beautiful Chi Phu Gompa before finally ascending to Siyar Khola to arrive at the Nile. You can cross the river and also visit Gongye Gompa. After arriving at the Nile, you can also extend to Mu Gompa, which lies near the Tibetan border.

Rachen Gompa – Domje

Trek duration: 5-6 hours

Maximum altitude: 2,460 m

The trail from Rachen Gompa to Domje starts with a crossing in a bridge that leads to Choking Paro. After descending to Siyar Khola, we will arrive at Gompa in Gho. Then we will drop along the river to reach Domje. There are various viewpoints along the trail that provide incredible views of snow-capped mountains, including the Ganesh Himal range.

Domje – Bihi

Trek duration: 5-6 hours

Maximum altitude: 2,130 m

Domje to Bihi is the next section of this trek as we continue our journey, descending towards lower Tsum valley. You will then pass through various settlements of Rachen before arriving at Lokpa. You will cross over a suspension bridge to enter the Manaslu Circuit Trail over the Budhi Gandaki River. Following the river will take you through Nyak, Deng, and Rana before finally arriving at Bihi.

Bihi – Namrung

Trek duration: 6-7 hours

Maximum altitude: 2,630 m

The trail from Bihi to Namrung passes through various settlements along a plain terrain. Then the path moves uphill through an alpine forest with green vegetation. A serene waterfall and Buddhist monasteries in Ghap will enchant any traveler before you arrive at Namrung. The Nam Gumba, in Namrung, is a beautiful attraction point along a trail. From this viewpoint, you can also observe Ngadi Chuli (7,871 m), Boudha Himal (6,672 m), Himal Chuli (7,893 m), and others.

Namrung – Sama Gaon

Trek duration: 7-8 hours

Maximum altitude: 3,520 m

The Namrung to Sama Gaon trail goes through a winding path on the Budhi Gandaki River above a ridge. The Lama and Sho settlements along the route provide you with incredible views of snow-capped mountains. After arriving at Lho, you can explore Ribung Gompa. A steep uphill climb later, we will come to Shyala along an easy and comfortable trail. We will arrive at Sama Gaon and explore the region, including the sacred Pema Chyoling Lhakhang.

Sama Gaon – Samdo

Trek duration: 4-5 hours

Maximum altitude: 3,875 m

The trail from Sama Gaon to Samdo provides you with incredible views of snow-capped mountains, including Manaslu (8,163 m). The ascending path takes you to frozen lake Birendra Tal and as we climb gently to Samdo along a quiet trail. A stunning Mani wall crossing will lead you to the Taka Choling Gompa in Samdo.

Samdo – Dharamsala/Larkya Phedi

Trek duration: 5-6 hours

Maximum altitude: 4,460 m

A beautiful trail from Samdo to Dharamsala passes through beautiful streams to arrive at Larkya Bazaar. The steep trail then passes through Mani walls before reaching the base of Larkya La (5,160 m). A path then steadily climbs Larkya Bazaar and leads you to Larke Phedi.

Dharamsala – Bimthang

Trek duration: 7-8 hours

Maximum altitude: 3,590 m

The trail from Dharamsala to Bimthang passes through the Larkya Glacier before arriving at Larkya La (5,160 m). The Manaslu and Annapurna massifs look incredibly beautiful from these mountain passes. The descending trail then passes through an icy path that provides majestic views of the glacier to arrive at Bimthang.

Bimthang – Dharapani

Trek duration: 7-8 hours

Maximum altitude: 1,963 m

The trail from Bimthang to Dharapani leads you to beautiful settlements and alpine forests to arrive at the Gho. Trekking along, you will pass through small settlements, including Tilje. The trail from Tilje to Dharapani is descending. You will continue the suspension bridge over Dudh Khola to arrive at this beautiful settlement.

Dharapani – Besisahar

Drive duration: 4-5 hours

Maximum altitude: 1,963 m

The trail from Dharapani to Besisahar starts on an off-road route. You can take a jeep which takes you around four hours to arrive at Besisahar. You will go on a descending trail to arrive at Syange village. This trail further ascends to Gharmu Phant before finally descending to Besisahar.

Besisahar – Kathmandu

Drive duration: 6-7 hours

Maximum altitude: 1,300 m

Besisahar to Kathmandu’s journey is a short scenic drive of around 6-7 hours. Beautiful landscapes with lush green hills and other rivers will enthrall all travelers. This scenic drive passes through Dumre, a point from where you can take an alternative trip to Pokhara.

Why is Manaslu Tsum Valley Trek Map Essential?

Manaslu Tsum Valley Trek map is an ideal piece of information that helps you navigate the region’s rugged and remote terrains. The map provides trekkers with all information regarding the maximum elevation, time duration, trekking distance, etc. The essential factors of this map are as follows:

Planning in advance

Ideal for side trips

There are various acclimatization points that you can select through these maps to avoid altitude sickness in high-altitude regions. Furthermore, the map also provides the lesser-known routes in the Tsum valley Manaslu region.

Ideal for remote treks

The Manaslu trek map is ideal for remote and rugged terrains with connection problems. Trekkers who cannot get a proper connection can use this map to navigate along the trail. Furthermore, they can also learn about restricted areas and no entry zones so that you can be safe from any hassles along the route. Besides that, maps protect trekkers from getting lost and keep them safe along trails.

The Final Say

The Manaslu Tsum Valley trek is an off-the-beaten adventure in incredible Himalayan landscapes. Moreover, trails of this trek pass through the foothills of the Himalayas. The Manaslu Tsum valley trek map is essential information during your trekking adventure.

Trekkers can use this map to navigate through various landscapes of the region. Moreover, maximum altitude, time duration, trekking distance are significant factors that you can observe in this map. Overall, the Manaslu Tsum valley trek map is ideal for all trekkers on this journey.

title: Mustang Trek vs Annapurna Trek
excerpt: It may be diminutive in size, but Nepal within itself has unique geographical features and diverse landscapes. The landforms vary here, from deep canyons to towering rock cliffs, glacial giants, and…
html:
It may be diminutive in size, but Nepal within itself has unique geographical features and diverse landscapes. The landforms vary here, from deep canyons to towering rock cliffs, glacial giants, and staggering mountains.

Each place in Nepal has its own rustic charm with spectacular views of vibrant valleys, steep slopes, surrounding terrains, and plateaus. As for trekking, the combat is usually between Manaslu and Annapurna, as both trekking spots are incredibly popular and astounding.

Trekkers always find it tough to choose between Mustang Trek vs Annapurna Trek as they are extraordinary on their own. Both Mustang and Annapurna are the epitome of exotic beauty in their own right.

While Mustang has historical landmarks, cultural spots, and religious pilgrimage, Annapurna has a dazzling view of snow-capped mountains, hanging glaciers, and beautiful terrain. Travelers can visit Muktinath Temple and also explore royal palaces in Lo Manthang during the trek.

There are many hidden natural beauties and picturesque spots in the kingdom where travelers can escape. They can explore the ancient royal palace, walled cities, and sky cave during the trip to Mustang.

Annapurna trek comes with the splendid view of the shimmering Annapurna massif, Gangapurna, Tilicho Peak, and Paungda Danda. It also offers trekkers many religious sites with ancient Tibetan monasteries to explore. Visitors of the Annapurna trek will be able to get an insight into the culture and lifestyle of people in the region.

Weather at Mustang Trek vs Annapurna Trek

It’s no secret that many trekkers consider the weather at Mustang Trek vs Annapurna Trek to decide which of them makes a better place to visit. Their decision has to do with the atmospheric condition and climate of the sites, which can make or break the trek.

The weather in Mustang is unlike the one in Annapurna, given trans-Himalayan climate conditions. It’s probably the reason that most trekkers tend to visit the region in Autumn, which offers lovely weather and mind-blowing views.

The season puts on an incredible sight for visitors with peak fall foliage, wild landscape, and vivid valleys. Travelers can catch a glimpse of shimmering Dhaulagiri and Nilgiri mountains in the north face along with Tibetan plateaus.

Summer in Mustang is warm and dry with good old sunny days. Temperature scales from 30 to 20 Degree Celsius in Summer, making trekkers sweat. Abruptly, nights are colder in the region with low precipitation and high winds.

Spring makes the perfect time to visit Mustang as it experiences typical weather that’s neither too hot nor cold. As the icy winter fades, the climate becomes lovely and satisfying. Trekkers will have an easy time navigating the trail, especially with the fabulous view of lofty mountain ranges, colorful plateaus, and deep river gorge.

Winter is frigid at Mustang, with the temperature dropping below -25 Degree Celsius. Heavy snowfall and tropical cyclones make the expedition impossible at times. The cold wave and fog so often cause flight cancellations and delays.

It’s why trekkers are advised to keep up-to-date on the weather forecast and make plans accordingly. For the Monsoon, trekkers can expect light rain showers. But, since Mustang is a rain shadow area, hiking is possible during the season.

Meanwhile, on the other end of Annapurna, the weather varies depending on the season. In spring, it’s pleasantly warm, while Autumn has a moderate climate with brisk air. On the whole, trekkers would be pleased to hike Annapurna in any of the seasons as both of them offer delightful weather with panoramic views.

In summer, trekkers have to combat scorching heat during the daytime, but at night, it’s cold, with the temperature falling up to -6 Degree Celsius. Unlike Mustang, Monsoon witnesses heavy downpours in Annapurna, with trails getting filthy and slippery. Climbing the route gets super intimidating due to continuous rainfall.

Winters can be harsh in Annapurna, depending on the altitude and time. Since it’s still warm in December, hikers wouldn’t have trouble trekking the circuit or base camp. By early January, the weather becomes worse, with the region facing extreme snowfall.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Difficulties between Mustang Trek vs Annapurna Trek

Since Mustang and Annapurna have varied geography and climatic conditions, trekking Annapurna is utterly different from Mustang. Hikers will experience varied challenges in both the hike. With that, they’ll get to enjoy the magnificent view and explore the major attraction of each trek.

Since Mustang lies at 13,200 ft. high, only a few trekkers deal with acute mountain sickness. Instead, they have to fight the dry and rugged trails filled with boulders to arrive at Upper Mustang.

The trail from Jomsom to Mustang is over 11 miles running beside rock cliffs and steep-sided valleys. It passes through several villages including, Jomsom, Muktinath, Kagbeni, and Lo Manthang, making trekkers weary.

Another challenge for trekkers of Mustang is to tackle the ever-changing weather that sometimes impedes the trip. The weather differs from season to season, so those who travel in winter will even have to resist a harsh climate.

With heavy snowfall and a bitterly cold atmosphere, trekkers will have a hard time walking the trail. Following poor weather, it gets tough to find accommodation during the season. Thus, many hikers make the booking of tea houses and lodges in advance to prevent such unfortunate situations.

Trek to Annapurna is relatively more complex than Mustang, with long winding trails, unforeseeable weather, and crowded trails. The classic route walks through peaks and valleys, which causes trekkers to fatigue quickly.

It has the world’s two most popular trek destinations, Annapurna Circuit and Base Camp. But sadly, each of them has their fair share of difficulties as trekkers struggle to climb the trail. They’ll have to go through dense forest, climb steep hills and valleys to reach the final destination, and savor marvelous views of towering snow peaks.

Hikers of Annapurna are more susceptible to altitude sickness than those traversing Mustang. As the trail gains an elevation of 17,800 ft, trekkers will likely suffer from shortness of breath due to low barometric pressure.

Hence, many hikers take their time to adapt to the temperature before going high. Another obstacle that may occur during the Annapurna trek is accommodation. Spring and autumn witness excessive tourist inflows in the region, prompting an inadequate dwelling.

Accessibility of Mustang Trek vs Annapurna Trek

Compared to most trekking routes in the Himalaya, both Annapurna and Mustang trek have an easy access route. Both the hikes are moderately challenging, with just a few difficulties that even beginners can pull off the expedition.

Although the Mustang trek vs Annapurna Trek route appears similar in so many ways, travelers can pretty quickly figure out the differences between the two hikes. As for Mustang, climbers have to encounter unpaved trails full of rocks and boulders.

The trek kicks off with a scenic flight from Kathmandu to Jomsom that lasts almost 30 minutes. The trail stretching 30 miles from the village passes through Kagbeni and Chele and Charang before ending up in Lo Manthang.

Most of the sections en route are explored but least visited. The trails paved their way through remote villages and abandoned valleys, which can be nerve-wracking. Yet, the breathtaking views along the way keep the travelers occupied throughout the course.

In the meantime, the Annapurna Circuit trek begins with a long drive from Kathmandu to Bandipur via Besisahar. From there, the trail moves to Jagat Lamjung and Daharapani, scrambling steep hills and Marsyangdi River Valley.

The trail makes its way through Lower Pisang and Manang, which provides mesmeric views of vertical rock cliffs and glacial lakes. Out of here, the path ascends to Thorong La Pass via Yak Kharka and Phedi. Most trekkers spend a day in Manang to rest and prevent the extreme effect of altitude sickness.

With every climb to the circuit, the scenery ahead changes and gets more and more impressive. Trekkers will get to glance at the sweeping hills, steep-sided valleys, and stunning terrains on the way up.

The multi-day trek to Annapurna Base Camp starts with a 7-8 hour drive from Kathmandu to Pokhara, followed by Ghandruk. The trail heads to Chomrong and Bamboo from the Gurung village, climbing the steep slopes and winding through the remote settlements.

Leaving the beautiful village of Deurali behind, the trail runs over rocks and stone stairs to the Annapurna Base Camp. At base camp, trekkers will get to snap the Annapurna range along with Dhaulagiri, Machhapuchhre, and Manaslu.

Acclimatization at Mustang Trek vs Annapurna Trek

With merely a 3,600 ft rise in altitude, hikers are not required to acclimatize during Mustang Trek. They can easily finish climbing the trail without taking a day off. However, they must have to prepare for the trek in advance.

Since the average trekking hours of Mustang trek is merely 5-6 hours, trekkers don’t have to follow a strict fitness regimen. They can rely on cardio exercises like jogging, cycling, and brisk walking to prepare for the hike.

For the Annapurna Circuit trek, trekkers stop at Manang for a day to ease off before climbing the hill. They even train themself ahead of the expedition and plan hardcore workouts, including jump squats and step-up exercises.

It doesn’t go the same for visitors of the Annapurna trek as they have to rest at least two days before ascending the trail. Hikers can feel a gradual decrease in air pressure which triggers acute mountain sickness. As a result, most of them show symptoms like headache, dizziness, and fever, while only a few have extreme effects like hypoxemia.

In case of Annapurna Base Camp, trekkers acclimatize based on the itinerary. If the expedition is more than a week-long, they’ll halt the trip and stay at the village to adapt to the change in weather. Most hikers don’t prefer to acclimatize and finish the trek as early as possible.

Cost of Mustang Trek vs Annapurna Trek

Whether they acknowledge it or not, travelers keep their eyes peeled on the cost of Mustang Trek vs Annapurna trek to figure out which one’s more affordable. A lot of them even compare the price of the hike and make the decision based on it.

Trek for Annapurna usually cost between US$700 to US$1000 depending on the itinerary and services. Hikers traveling in a group will incur lower costs than the solo traveler. The cost also differs due to the transportation fare as the private jeep charges more price.

Hikers need a TIMS card for the Annapurna trek, which costs approximately US$30. They’ll also have to pay for the transportation, food, and dwelling, whose average price is US$40-US$50 per day.

Tea houses are more popular at Annapurna trek as they are less expensive with all the needed facilities. Options for single and double bedrooms come with a difference in prices. If you need hot showers or electricity to charge batteries, be prepared to pay an extra amount.

If you trek the circuit with a travel agency, they’ll take care of all the essentials. They will make the booking for you and even provide you a three-time meal each day throughout the trek. However, personal expenses, including trekking equipment, clothing, and souvenir, have to be made by the trekker.

Trekkers visiting Mustang trek need to plan a budget of around US$1,500. The price may vary, subject to the length of stay in the region. The expenses include accommodation, food, and a return flight to Jomsom.

The flight from Kathmandu to the Thakali village of Jomsom cost about US$200. However, if trekkers want to minimize the cost, then it’s better to fly to the town from Pokhara. Hiring a guide and porter can cost trekkers anywhere from US$20 to US$25.

Many companies offer direct heli flights to Lo Manthang. Trekkers can take the flight and escape the rugged trail that takes more than a week to finish. Nonetheless, they’ll have to pay a hefty price for it.

Preparation for Mustang Trek vs Annapurna Trek

Trekkers can somewhat relate with the preparation for Mustang Trek vs Annapurna Trek as both steers off-the-beaten-path. No matter which trek they choose to go with, trekkers must come well-prepared to traverse the meandering trail.

Hikers of the Annapurna trek have to follow a steep trail that ascends 5,416 m They’ll have to traverse a zigzagged path, running up and down to reach the hilltop, which requires a lot of physical strength.

Without physical stability and improved stamina, trekkers won’t be able to beat the trails of Annapurna. Therefore, they have to spend plenty of time on their fitness before starting the trek to either circuit or base camp.

They’ll have to up the ante and improve their physical stamina in order to beat the meandering terrain. Trekkers have to start training at least two weeks before the trek. Apart from the fitness routine, they must also take a few short walks to the hillside to withstand the trail.

When it comes to Mustang trek, hikers won’t have to keep up with the intense training. Since the hike is also for beginners, almost everyone can complete the trip on time. However, if they want to have an easy time climbing the rocky trail, it’s better to strengthen their physical stamina.

They can stick to their regular exercise or make a new workout plan to build endurance and improve balance. In addition, trekkers can meditate and follow a strict diet regimen to boost stamina.

Mustang Trek vs Annapurna Trek crowd

Since both Mustang and Annapurna are prime trek destinations, travelers often flock to these regions to explore stunning landscapes, religious places, and historical monuments. A lot of them even take the strenuous jagged trail to enjoy the breathtaking sights.

It’s the Annapurna trek that’s often crowded as compared to Mustang. Trekkers from all around the world travel north-central Nepal to explore the significant landmarks and sight glistening mountains.

Winter and Monsoon have the least number of visitors at Annapurna due to poor weather. As the trail gets drenched in the rain most of the time, it becomes slippery and difficult to travel. As a result, most trekkers avoid the Annapurna trek during Monsoon.

Mustang too sees a large number of visitors during Autumn and spring as the season offers breathtaking views. Trekkers get strong visibility during the time of the year. They can sneak peek at the shimmering mountains of Dhaulagiri and Nilgiri from miles away.

title: Manaslu Circuit Trek Without a Guide
excerpt: Are you planning to do the Manaslu trek without a guide? Well, there is something you need to know if you are thinking so. Have a nice read! The Earth is full of beautiful places. You need not go any…
html:
Are you planning to do the Manaslu trek without a guide? Well, there is something you need to know if you are thinking so. Have a nice read!

The Earth is full of beautiful places. You need not go any further than Nepal to find beautiful places. I mean, just consider Manaslu Region, one of the major tourist destinations of Nepal.

Manaslu Region is a concealed gem in the Himalayas of Nepal. And Manaslu Circuit Trek is one trek that takes you through the rugged roads of the Manaslu Region. From lush forests to snow-white mountains, lovely people to the sounding rivers, and more, the trek has everything. Yet, you have to be with a licensed guide to explore the beauty. In simpler words, Manaslu Trek without Guide is not allowed by the government of Nepal.

Opened only after 1991 for foreign trekkers, Manaslu Trek and Manaslu Region is a protected and restricted area of Nepal. The region is home to lush vegetation, diverse wildlife, legendary mountains, unique Tibetan Influenced Culture. In a moto of preserving and maintaining those region’s natural and cultural wealth, the Government announced it as a restricted region. That is why you cannot explore this region on your own.

But what you can do is Manaslu Circuit Trek with an experienced and licensed guide of ours. Trekking in the Manaslu Region with a guide is not as dull as you think. As you may know, Manaslu Region is an off-the-beaten path, and trekking in such a region alone is quite challenging. For such places, the guides are nothing less than saviors. Those escorts are used to the area so much that no one can lead as they do. And they are so friendly, humble, and full of humor too. Hence, doing a Manaslu Trek with a guide is not a boring plan.

This blog will tell you everything about why you need to do the Trek with a guide and why not. Moreover, you will also read some important information about the trek.

Can you do Manaslu Trek without Guide?

Well, we are afraid that the answer is a resounding no.

The answer may sound sad to those who are planning to explore the Manaslu area without a guide. That dream of yours will not come true as Nepal’s Government has restricted it to do so. Well, this initiation of the government is actually for good causes. You have to understand why the Manaslu Region is limited to solo traveling.

Manaslu Region is one of the most rural regions of Nepal. As of its ruralness, the region is not explored by many. And it is pretty risky to walk through the roads solo that are less frequently less traveled. Secondly, the natural attraction of the region is still to be seen by many. To preserve the beauty and livings of the beauty, Manaslu Conservation Area always looks after the area. Solo travelers can enter this protected area unless a licensed guide accompanies them. Otherwise, there is no chance.

Moreover, the region homes around six settlements that display a Tibetan-influenced culture and lifestyle. All of those villages give you a good look into the inspiring lifestyle. To preserve the unique culture, the government has labeled them as the restricted villages. That means you cannot explore these settlements on your own; you will need a licensed guide.

So, it is pretty clear that you cannot be on Manaslu Trek Without Guide. The only way to explore this scenic region is trekking with a guide. However, make sure you are in a group of at least two trekkers(excluding guides and porters). That is the first and foremost requirement for Manaslu Circuit Trek.

Reasons to Hire an experienced cum licensed Guide

As you have known that Manaslu Trek without Guide is a never happening dream, the only option is to hire one. Well, there are some excellent reasons to hire a guide for the trek. Let’s find them out:

  • Manaslu Trek is not allowed to do if you do not have a licensed guide or porter.
  • Manaslu Region is not so populated and developed as other trekking trails. The difficulties come pretty quickly at any point in time in such areas. You will need an experienced guide for tackling such times.
  • There will be no worry to get lost along the trail as a guide will lead you the right way.
  • The licensed guides are well experienced in dealing with emergencies.
  • The guide will take you through the wilderness of the region without any hassles.
  • A Himalayan guide knows everything about altitude sickness. He will help you to deal with the altitudes on the trek.
  • In case of any injuries, a guide will come in handy with his treatment kit and curing ability.
  • He/She will manage almost everything along the journey; you do not have to worry about anything other than exploring and trekking.
  • The guide knows well about the culture, tradition, language of the region. He will help you to connect with those things.
  • A guide will manage hygienic food and comfortable accommodation for you throughout the trek.

Difficulties of Manaslu Trek without Guide

Manaslu Circuit Trek is among the strenuous treks to do in Nepal. Be it altitude-wise or the trail’s nature, the walk is a challenging one. What makes it even extra tricky is the ruralness and less explored trails. Trekkers can easily be in problems during the trek if they are doing it without guides. Let’s find out what sorts of difficulties do the trekkers have to face if they are doing Manaslu Trek without Guide:

Odds of Getting Lost

Manaslu Circuit Trek’s trails are not that easy to navigate as trekkers less frequent them. The region is also equally remote and rural as well. That is how there are high chances of getting out of the track on the trek. And there is no way you kind find the way on your mobile as the region doesn’t have access to such facilities yet. If you are not with anyone used to this region, you are sure to get lost. And to stay lost between the wild side is not that appealing.

Injuries and Emergencies

If you are injured amid the trek and want someone’s help, you may not get any in this trek. There are no hospitals or doctors to treat you around the trial in case of emergencies. Likewise, if situations turn worse and you need emergency rescues, there will be no one to call for the rescues. You have to deal with emergencies on your own.

To Communicate

The people of the Manaslu Region are not literate enough to understand foreign languages. You will hardly meet someone who can communicate with you in English during the trek. Hence, you will experience it difficult to communicate with people along the trail if not with a local guide.

Dealing with Altitude Sickness

A professional guide can do wonders when it is about dealing with mountain sickness. Manaslu Trek is a high-altitude trek, and risks of mountain illness are always there. If not taken seriously, anything can happen during the trek. The chances of getting sick of mountains are lower when you are with an experienced guide. He suggests you in every next step on how to avoid the sickness. If you are not so aware of mountain sickness, this can be your problem if not with a trekking guide.

Read more on – Manaslu Circuit Trek Difficulty

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

A Guide, A Porter or Both

A Licensed Guide

As said before, A licensed guide is a must for Manaslu Circuit Trek. A licensed guide is the first thing that will be required while applying for the permit to the Manaslu Region. There is no more reliable person than a licensed one for doing Manaslu Region. A licensed guide has enough experience and expertise to lead you through the extreme lands of Nepal. They are pretty good at multiple languages like English, Germany, etc.

These guides know everything about the region, climate, weather, culture, and conditions. And they are also trained to deal with difficult situations like altitude sickness, injuries, and more. Hence, that is how they become the right fit to help you find the way. A licensed guide can cost up to 30 USD per day. The fee will cover expenses of the guide’s food, lodging, and insurance charges.

A Porter

A porter is someone who will carry your heavy belongings during the trek. It is challenging and not suggested to carry bulky backpacks while trekking in the mountains. That can stimulate chances of altitude sickness as you will get quickly tired while ascending. If you have a big backpack to carry, it is better to hire a porter. The porter will take good care of your backpack by taking it wherever you go. A porter carries up to 25 kgs of luggage during a trek and charges around 25 to 30 USD per day. The salary will cover his expenses, including meals, accommodation, and insurance.

A Guide Cum Porter

You can get both porter and guide services from one person, and such a person is called a guide cum porter. It is a good deal, especially for the limited budget trekkers. They get both of the services by paying a single salary. A guide cum porter can charge around 30 to 35 USD per day, covering all expenses. However, these sorts of the workforce are a little hard to get.

Whom to hire?

As you came across three types of guides, you might get confused when choosing one for your expedition. The licensed guide has to be with you while on the trek. What if you also have a huge load to carry? You can go for both a licensed guide and porter or just a guide cum porter in such a situation. However, you can do the trek with a porter only, but typically porters are less skillful than the guides. Thus, we suggest you to hire an experienced licensed guide and a porter only if you have a loaded backpack.

How to Hire a Guide for Manaslu Trek

After knowing the value of having a licensed guide in Manaslu Circuit Trek, you should also learn how to hire one. The simplest way to get an experienced guide is to contact us, Base Camp Adventure. We are a professional team that has been helping people across the world to do expeditions in Nepal. Our tour and trekking packages are among the most selling in Nepal.

If you reach us for the trek, we will arrange everything for you. From the start to the very end of Manaslu Trek, our team will accompany you. We are best at organizing trips in Nepal, so many of our previous clients have excellently reviewed us.

As you know, Manaslu Trek without Guide is not possible. But it is possible with the Base Camp Adventure Team. We will assign a highly experienced guide and porter for your Manaslu Circuit Trek.

Must-know information about Manaslu Trek

Significant Highlights of Manaslu Circuit Trek

  • Walk and explore the off-the-beaten trails of the Manaslu Region.
  • Experience the eighth tallest peak in the World, Mt Manaslu, and other peaks teasing you.
  • Meet and learn more about the settlements and people of the region influenced by the Tibetan culture.
  • Reach Larkya La Pass(5,153 m)-one of the picturesque passes in Nepal.
  • Explore the wild side of Manaslu Conservation Area.
  • Trek via amazing landscapes and valleys.
  • Pay visits to some of the oldest Buddhist monasteries, gompas, chortens.

Outline Itinerary for Manaslu Circuit Trek

Day 01: Arrival in Kathmandu and Hotel Transfer

Altitude Gain: 1,400 m(Kathmandu)

Day 02: Kathmandu Sightseeing and Trek Preparation

Day 03: Drive from Kathmandu to Soti Khola

Drive Hours: 7 to 8 hours

Altitude Loss: 700 m(Sotikhola)

Day 04: Trek from Sotikhola to Machha Khola

Trek Hours: 6 to 7 hours

Altitude Gain: 863 m(Machha Khola)

Day 05: Trek from Machha Khola to Jagat

Trek Hours: 7 to 8 hours

Altitude Gain: 1,340 m(Jagat)

Day 06: Trek from Jagat to Deng

Trek Hours: 6 to 7 hours

Altitude Gain: 1,860 m(Deng)

Day 07: Trek from Deng to Namrung

Trek Hours: 6 to 7 hours

Altitude Gain: 2,630 m(Namrung)

Day 08: Trek from Namrung to Samagaun

Trek Hours: 7 to 8 hours

Altitude Gain: 3,520 m(Samagaun)

Day 09: Rest and Acclimatization day in Samagaun

Day 10: Trek from Samagaun to Samdo

Trek hours: 3 to 4 hours

Altitude Gain: 3,690 m(Samdo)

Day 11: Trek from Samdo to Dharamsala

Trek hours: 4 to 5 hours

Altitude Gain: 4,460 m(Dharamsala)

Day 12: Trek from Dharamsala to Larkya La Pass and then back to Bimthang

Trek hours: 8 to 9 hours

Altitude Gain: 5,160 m(Larkya La Pass)

Altitude Loss: 3,890 m(Bimthang)

Day 13: Trek from Bimthang to Dharapani

Trek hours: 7 to 8 hours

Altitude Loss: 1,860 m(Dharapani)

Day 14: Jeep drive from Dharapani to Beshisahar

Drive hours: 3 to 4 hours

Altitude Gain: 760 m(Samdo)

Day 15: Drive from Besisahar to Kathmandu

Trek hours: 6 to 7 hours

Altitude Gain: 1,300 m(Kathmandu)

Day 16: Departure from Kathmandu

Best Time for Manaslu Trek

Autumn and Spring are the two correct times for Manaslu Circuit Trek. To start with Autumn, September to November are Autumn’s and eventually suitable months to do Manaslu Circuit Trek. The weather during these months remains stable thoroughly, and you will have easy trekking days.

Likewise, the visibility of the region is also quite evident with the bright sun. Mountains like Manaslu, HImlung Himal, Annapurna II, etc., are seen all day long. The season is also a season of festivals in Nepal, making it an even best season to visit the country.

After Autumn, Spring is known as the most suitable time to do Manaslu exploration. March, April, and May are the months of the season when you should plan the trek. These months provide you a clear and stable trekking day every other day. Clean mountain views, fine weather, and warm temperature are the perks of the Spring season. However, the best part about Spring is the blooming flowers across the trails of Nepal.

When compared to Monsoon and Winter, Autumn and Spring are suitable times by far. The Monsoon and Winter are the low times to do any outing in Nepal. That is the time when conditions are not stable at all. There is high snowfall in the higher areas in the Winter season. Likewise, there is massive rainfall around the country during Monsoon. That is why Autumn and Spring become the best time for Manaslu Trek.

Read more on: When is the Best Time To Trek Manaslu?

What to Pack for Manaslu Trek?

“What to pack for Manaslu Trek” is a general question of everyone preparing for Manaslu Trek sooner or later. To help those souls, we have listed the list of the essential items for Manaslu Circuit Trek. The list is workable for the Autumn and Spring seasons.

(Note: If you are embarking on the expedition during Monsoon and Winter, you have to add some extra specific gears.)

Clothing:

  • Down Jacket
  • Insulated Jacket
  • Waterproof/Windproof Jacket
  • Thermal Layers
  • Trekking Shirts
  • Waterproof Trousers
  • Trekking shorts
  • Breathable underwears
  • Rain gears(for monsoon trek)

Headwear and Handwear:

  • Scarf
  • Woolen hat
  • Sun hat
  • UV Sunglasses
  • Inner and Outer Gloves
  • Headlamp and extra batteries
  • Buff

Footwear

  • Hiking socks
  • Gaiters(for monsoon and winter treks)
  • Sandals
  • Sturdy trekking Boots

Personal Hygiene

  • Quick Drying Towel
  • Sanitizers/Hand wash
  • Sunscreen
  • Moisturizer
  • Lip Balm
  • Cold Cream
  • Wet Tissues
  • Toilet Paper
  • Tooth Brushing Set
  • Soap

Miscellaneous

  • Trekking Poles
  • Sleeping Bag
  • Day Backpack
  • Water Bottle
  • Books
  • Playing Cards

Permits required for Manaslu Trek

There are several permits that you should have to do Manaslu Trek. Without those permits, you cannot do the trek. Some of them are to enter the protected areas, and the rest are to enter the restricted places. Let’s dig each of them below:

Restricted Area Permit(RAP)

As Manaslu Region is a restricted area, you will need the Restricted Area Permit to enter this area. The cost of getting this permit does not remain the same always. If you are traveling between September to November, the pass costs 70 USD for the initial seven days and 10 USD per day afterward. Likewise, for December to August trekking, 50 USD will work for the first seven days and thereafter 7 USD per day.

Manaslu Conservation Area Permit(MCAP)

Manaslu Conservation Area is a protected site established to protect the wildlife and vegetation of the region. It is a site loaded with a wide range of plants and wildlife. You have to pay a certain amount as a permit fee to enter this site. The cost of MCAP for SAARC Nationals is 2 USD and 30 USD for Non-SAARC Nationals.

Annapurna Conservation Area Permit(ACAP)

You will pass through another protected area during this trek, Annapurna Conservation Area. This protected area is also enriched with loads of natural resources and lives. This permit’s cost is the same as the Manaslu Conservation Area Permit, 2 USD for SAARC and 30 USD for Non-SAARC Nationals).

Tsum Valley Restricted Permit

This permit is only required if you are traveling through Tsum Valley. The valley is a restricted area, and you have to pay 35 USD as a permit fee for this valley.

How and Where to get Permits?

You have to visit the tourist office with all the necessary documents in Kathmandu to get all of those permits. If you go through us, Base Camp Adventure, we will manage everything related to permits pretty quickly for you.

At Last

Manaslu Trek Without Guide is not a doable plan. As you grasp by now, the government has restricted solo trekking in the remote region by considering the difficulties of solo trekking there. That is why a licensed guide or porter is a must to do this remote but beautiful trek. The guide leads trekkers through the Manaslu Region safely and soundly.

Manaslu Circuit Trek is all about unturning the unturned stones of the region. Everything in this region is so new and pure that the trek will be a memory for a lifetime. If you want to do Manaslu Trek sooner or later, remember us, Base Camp Adventure, to organize your visit.
