Why Take The Annapurna Base Camp Trek In June?

June is an off-season for trekking in the Annapurna region. However, there are various reasons that you should trek this month. Some of them are as follows:

Quiet and peaceful trails

The offseason means that there are few number trekkers. The quiet, less crowded trails provide you with a peaceful adventure in a tranquil atmosphere. If you love to trek without any disturbance, this Annapurna Base Camp trek in June is ideal.

The magnificent views of the Himalayan vista are one of the highlights of this trek. You will get to hear natural sounds like water flowing and birds chirping in the region.

Magical views of the snow-capped mountains

After heavy rainfall, the sky clears, and you will get majestic views of the mountains. You can also observe the green environment all-around in its glory. The clear blue skies and unobstructed views of Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and others will enchant you along the trail.

Gorgeous Sunrise vista

The evenings and nights are overcast with heavy rainfall throughout. However, the skies remain clean early morning, providing you with magnificent views of the mountain peaks. The golden sunrise over silver mountains and turning them golden is a once in a lifetime experience. The green hills, vast meadows, and water streams look beautiful in the region.

Discount and bargain offers

Backpackers can take advantage of the off-season. The accommodation and transportation costs will reduce significantly in off-seasons. Trekkers will get special discounts offered during this season.

The fewer crowds mean that you will get to pick your accommodation and meal facilities. If you can bargain, you will get additional discounts as well. Some tea houses also offer free accommodations in the condition that you will eat your meals in the same teahouses.

Variety of food and accommodation

The tea houses and lodges remain empty in most parts of the trail. You can choose your desired room with the facility at a fair price. Trekkers will get blankets, electronic charging, hot water, and other facilities.

You don’t have to share your rooms. You also don’t have to queue in long lines to enjoy solo rooms with attached bathrooms. However, the higher elevation settlements will cost you more as there are no transportation facilities. Food ingredients need to get carried by a porter or a yak.

You will get served Nepalese “Dal Bhat” which is a healthy meal that will keep you charged. Hydration with fluids is essential to tackle altitude sickness and you should drink at least 2-3 liters of water. You can carry water purifying tablets and mix them with water you get at teahouses.

Difficulties of Annapurna Base Camp Trek in June

Annapurna Base Camp trek is a challenging trek for all age and skill levels. If you have not trekked at high altitude before, you will find these trekking routes strenuous. Trekkers need to trek for around 6-7 hours a day. The monsoon season provides you with extra challenges of heavy rainfall and slippery trails.

There are leech-infested trails, which is another added challenge. Physical strength, stamina, and a basic level of fitness is another essential part of this trek. Proper training is hence an integral part of your preparation. This trekking trail moves above an altitude of 5,000 m and above, so altitude sickness is a considerable risk among trekkers.

You should check for any underlying heart condition before starting your trek. Acclimatization at regular settlements and hydration is essential. Dehydration can cause altitude sickness in the high altitude region. Hence, these are some of the difficulties of the Annapurna base camp trek in June.

Food and Accommodation Along the Trek

The Annapurna Base Camp is a beautiful trek that takes you through beautiful landscapes. Meal and accommodation facilities like the room of your choice are available at bargain costs. You can also enjoy various facilities like an attached bathroom, Hot showers, warm heaters, Wi-Fi, charging, etc.

“Dal Bhat” is a typical Nepalese cuisine that gets served twice a day for lunch and dinner. The high-calorie dish is ideal as they provide energy for the taxing trek. Hydrating is essential and you can use purification tablets or chlorine solutions to purify water. Hot beverages, including tea, garlic soup, coffee, rhododendron tea, mint tea, and others, are also available.

You can also get these facilities of accommodation at bargain prices in the offseason. Some tea houses also offer free accommodation, but you have to have your meals in the same teahouses. Besides that, you can also carry protein bars, granola bars, Chocolate bars, and others to get energy for trekking.

Trekking Itinerary – Annapurna Base Camp Trek in June

Day 1: Fly from Kathmandu to Pokhara, drive to Nayapul, and trek to Ulleri.

Trekking duration: 6-7 hours

Maximum Altitude: 1,960 m

Our representative will pick you up from a hotel in Kathmandu (1,400 m). You will get transferred to Tribhuvan International Airport, from where you can fly to Pokhara (1,400 m). You will arrive at Pokhara airport after around 25 minutes of flight. Besides, you can observe snow-capped mountains and green hills of the region.

Nayapul is our next destination where you will after a short 2-hour drive from Pokhara. We will trek through various settlements after arriving at Nayapul from Pokhara. From Nayapul, we will start our Annapurna Base Camp trekking journey. There are various settlements and steep ascent along the trail from where we arrive at Birethanti (1,100 m).

This beautiful village settlement lies near Modi and Burundi Khola. From Birethanti, we will continue our trek through steep uphills to arrive at Tikhedhunga (1,520 m). After a hike of around 5 hours via the Sudame route, we will reach Tikhedhunga. From Tikhedhunga, we will hike uphill for 2 hours to arrive at Ulleri.

The spectacular views of snow-capped mountains are incredible from various viewpoints along the trail. We will stop our trek after arriving at Ulleri (1,960 m), which is our destination for the day. After arriving at Ulleri, we will rest and stay overnight at the teahouse.

Day 2: Trek from Ulleri to Ghorepani

Trekking duration: 5-6 hours

Maximum Altitude: 2,850 m

After having breakfast in Ulleri, we will hike uphill to Ghorepani (2,874 m). Ghorepani, located at the top of a hill, is a beautiful settlement. The trail starts with a hike through forests of rhododendron and oak trees.

We will arrive at Banthanti (2,200 m), a beautiful Gurung settlement, after a trek of around 2 hours. After a further 2 hours, we arrive at Nang Thanthi (2,500 m). We can observe beautiful views of snow-capped mountains, including Annapurna I, Hiunchuli, Annapurna South, and others.

After Ghorepani, we will pass through various settlements of the region. Different snow-capped mountains, including Annapurna South, Dhaulagiri, and Machhapuchhre are an attraction along the trail. There are various tea houses along the trail where you can stay overnight in Ghorepani.

Day 3: Trek from Ghorepani to Poon Hill and Trek to Tadapani

Trekking duration: 5-6 hours

Maximum Altitude: 2,630 m

We will trek to Poon Hill early before dawn. After ascending for 45 minutes, we will arrive at Poon Hill viewpoint. You can observe one of the best sunrises overlooking snow-capped mountain vista. After observing the Himalayan sunrise, we trek back to Ghorepani.

We descend to Tadapani (2,630 m), enjoying the views of sun-kissed mountains like Annapurna South, Manaslu, Annapurna I, and more. We will trek around 5-6 hours to arrive at Tadapani, passing through beautiful forests. You will pass through beautiful suspension bridges, streams, and cascades.

There are various birds and orange orchards that you can find on your route to Tadapani. Tadapani provides you majestic views of Manaslu, Machhapuchhre, Annapurna I, and Hiunchuli. We will rest and spend the night at a teahouse in Tadapani.

Day 4: Trek from Tadapani to Sinuwa

Trekking duration: 5-6 hours

Maximum Altitude: 2,360 m

We will start our trek after having a sumptuous breakfast early in the morning. We will continue our tour to Sinuwa, passing through an easy downhill trail to Sinuwa (2,360 m). Sinuwa provides an incredible view of Modi and Chhomrong Khola. There are tea houses in the region with beautiful architecture that attract many trekkers in Sinuwa.

After downhill trekking, we will reach a crossing with a suspension bridge over the Modi River for some time. We will finally arrive at Chhomrong, a village settlement just below Annapurna I. We will trek for around 2 hours from Chhomrong to reach Sinuwa. After arriving at the village, we can observe the beautiful scenery of snow-capped mountains north to Sinuwa. We will stay in a local teahouse in Sinuwa.

Day 5: Trek from Sinuwa to Deurali

Trekking duration: 5-6 hours

Maximum Altitude: 3,230 m

We observe the beautiful Himalayan sunrise from Sinuwa and its beautiful surroundings. Thereafter, we will have our breakfast in Sinuwa and continue our trek.

We will begin our trekking journey from Sinuwa to Deurali (3,230 m). After hiking for around 45 minutes, we will arrive at Bamboo.

We further pass through rhododendron and dense bamboo forest with many wildlife and birds. Deurali is a beautiful settlement where we will arrive after crossing Hinku cave. You can observe various glacier rivers, streams, and suspension bridges, on your trekking route to Deurali. After arriving at Deurali, you will stay overnight at a tea house.

Day 6: Trek from Deurali to Annapurna Base Camp

Trekking duration: 5-6 hours

Maximum Altitude: 4,130 m

We will start our trek to Annapurna Base Camp early in the morning. After having breakfast, we continue our walk on the Modi Khola bank to arrive at Machhapuchhre Base Camp. There are beautiful mountains all over in this Base Camp area that will spellbind any trekker.

After taking pictures and exploring Machhapuchhre Base Camp (3,700 m), we make our way to Annapurna Base Camp. The spectacular views of Annapurna I, Mardi Himal, Dhaulagiri, and others, will enchant you. Avalanches are quite common in the region. Hence, you should stay cautious in avalanche-prone areas.

After hiking for around 7 hours, we will arrive at Annapurna Base Camp (4,031 m). The trek provides you with an incredible mountain vista, including massif Annapurna. The view of the gorgeous sunset from Annapurna Base Camp is magical. We will explore the area and stay overnight at a teahouse in Annapurna Base Camp.

Day 7: Trek from Annapurna Base Camp down to Sinuwa

Trekking duration: 7-8 hours

Maximum Altitude: 2,360 m

We will enjoy the majestic golden sunrise overlooking the surrounding vista from Annapurna Base Camp. After breakfast, we will trek down to Sinuwa (2,360 m), passing through sparse forest and stony trails. We will trek downhill and pass through various settlements.

The descending trail is relatively more comfortable than other routes in the region. The view of the Annapurna Range of mountains is another exciting aspect of this trek. After arriving at Deurali, we will then pass through various settlements via Hinku Cave and Bamboo. We will stay in Sinuwa.

Day 8: Trek from Sinuwa to Siwai and drive to Pokhara

Trekking duration: 3 hours

Maximum Altitude: 1,250 m

We will start our trek from Sinuwa for around 2 hours to arrive at Siwai (1,250 m). The breathtaking views of snow-capped mountains, scenic farmlands, cascades, welcome you to Chhomrong.

From Chhomrong, we will start our trip to Jhinu Danda after having lunch. We will cross Kimrong Khola to arrive at Siwai. Our trek comes to an end in Siwai, and we will drive to Pokhara via Nayapul. We will take a further 2-hour scenic drive from Nayapul to Pokhara from where you can drive to your destination.

Things To Consider For Annapurna Base Camp Trek In June

Acclimatize and hydrate

Adapting to a higher altitude trail is essential to tackle altitude sickness along trails. Acclimatization is a process of adjusting to high altitude conditions with lesser oxygen levels. Acclimatization helps your body adjust to the current environment. Therefore, you should take proper rest, acclimatize and hydrate regularly.

Hire a guide

Annapurna Base Camp is an excellent region for trekking. But solo trekking is not favorable in the monsoon season. The unpredictable weather means that there are higher chances of injuries and accidents. Hence, it might be hard to find help in emergencies.

Hence, you should consider either trekking in a group or hire a professional guide. These locals guides are also handy when it comes to navigating along trails. It can get quite confusing at times and interaction with locals also gets easy with them.

Train properly

Annapurna Base Camp trek can get quite challenging at times. You can trek this route even as a beginner. But you must undergo a rigorous training regime to build stamina and gain fitness levels. Strength and endurance training and cardiovascular activities are essential. You can perform activities like swimming, hiking, cycling, jogging, and others at least 2-3 weeks before the trek.

Pack well with essential items

The weather can frequently change in high altitude regions as it can get both hot and cold. The heavy rainfall brings damp and humid conditions. The night time remains colder in the area.

Raincoats and waterproof jackets are essential to pack during the trek. You need to pack clothes that are easy to wear and take off based on weather conditions.

Get a Travel insurance

Travel insurance is another important factor when it comes to high altitude trekking. You must ensure that it covers injuries, flight delays, thefts, and others. You might also require emergency evacuation. Make sure your travel insurance covers altitude over 6,000 m

Training For Annapurna Base Camp Trek In June

Annapurna Base Camp Trek is a lovely trek in the foothills of Annapurna massif. A basic level of fitness is essential to complete this trek. Therefore, strength and endurance training and mental preparation will help you immensely.

Strength and endurance training

Training including strength and endurance exercises is essential for trekking in the Annapurna region. These exercises will provide you incredible stamina and fitness levels. Cardiovascular activities, including jogging, hiking, swimming, cycling, hiking, and others, provide you with energy and breathing ability in high altitude conditions.

Mental preparation

Mental preparation is a significant part of the trek in the Annapurna region. A positive attitude through motivational exercise will help you in this trek. You can also go on researching about this trek by asking veteran trekkers or on the internet. A practice hike with backpacks will give you an overall idea of this trek.

Some Essential Tips for Annapurna Base Camp Trek in June

  • Acclimatize well during the trip and hydrate with water and other liquid drinks.
  • Sleeping bags are essential as teahouses do not have enough blankets
  • Check weather forecasts before you start on this trek.
  • Carry cash in Nepali rupees and beware of pickpockets
  • Renting trekking gears is quite efficient.
  • Carry water purifying tablets to purify water along with tea houses
  • Training routine is essential to gain stamina and fitness levels.
  • Booking in advance allows you to trek without any hassle.
  • Carry granola bars, protein bars, chocolate bars, and others during your trek

Annapurna Base Camp trek in June is a challenging adventure but doable with proper packing and preparation. Heavy rainfalls in the lower region provide major threats to trekkers with landslides and slippery trails. You should trek with appropriate caution and be wary of the leech-infested trails.

Also, there is cheaper food, accommodation, and transportation with discounts. You will get the room of your choice. The trails of this trek are peaceful, with fewer trekkers. html:
Annapurna Base Camp Trek in August is the real thing to do for every enthusiastic trekker from all around the world.

August is an off-season for trekking and traveling in the Annapurna region. The monsoon season in August brings heavy rainfalls, especially in lower areas. Most trekkers stay away from this month due to weather-related challenges. However, if you are a rain lover and botany enthusiast, this monsoon season Annapurna Base Camp trek is ideal for you.

Annapurna Base Camp region is unique because it receives less rainfall even in peak monsoon. Trekkers can experience two different geographical conditions of lush green vegetation in the lower and high altitude regions’ barren landscapes. Hence, it is ideal for all seasons, given that you pack well for the trip.

Moreover, there are diverse landscapes with beautiful snow-capped mountains, including Annapurna I, Mt. Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre, and others. This rich biodiversity and wildlife of the region is a significant highlight of this trek. Besides that, you will also explore the culture, tradition, and heritage of ethnic Gurung, Magar, and Tamang communities.

Furthermore, this unique trek offers crowd fewer trails and exciting adventures. A peaceful, tranquil environment makes this trek quite attractive. Likewise, it is ideal for budget trekkers, and backpackers as the cost of food and accommodation is almost half. Besides, you can enjoy this spectacular trek if you remain cautious and prepare well in advance.

Read further for a detailed description of Annapurna Base Camp Trek in August and other relevant information in detail.

Highlights of the Trip

  • Less crowded trail and tranquil environment.
  • Astonishing views of snow-capped mountains, including Annapurna I, Hiunchuli, Annapurna South, Mardi Himal, Nilgiri, and others.
  • Magical sunrise and sunset view from Poon Hill viewpoint.
  • Warm welcome and hospitality of local people.
  • A cultural exploration of Gurung, Tamang, and Magar community.
  • Dipping in Jhinu Danda hot water spring.
  • Discount on meal, accommodation, flight, and others.
  • Exploring lush green vegetation along trails.

Weather during Annapurna Base Camp Trek in August

Weather in high altitude regions is unpredictable. The climatic conditions of the region impact weather significantly. Moreover, the Summer-Monsoon season in the Annapurna region has sunny days and rainy evenings and nights. Therefore, you need to pack well with proper rain gear, including raincoats and waterproof trekking gear.

August is the final month of the summer monsoon season. It rains frequently, and you can feel slight coldness due to it. Similarly, you should be careful as slippery trails and the risk of landslides and avalanches are relatively high. Also, the temperature along trails remains between 6°C to 18°C.

Moreover, the rain clears the environment and provides you with incredible views of snow-capped mountains. Also, you can observe the entire mountain vista in all its glory. The days are warm and humid, with high amounts of water vapor in the air. Hence, you should drink water regularly to protect yourself from dehydration.

Furthermore, you should check the weather forecast before you start on your trek. Besides that, you should try to trek in the latter parts of August as far as possible. In fact, the rain reduces significantly after mid-August, so you will not face any significant difficulty. Overall, with proper packing and preparation, you can complete this trek with ease.

Difficulties of Annapurna Base Camp Trek in August

Annapurna Base Camp Trek is quite challenging. You will need to trek for around 6-7 hours daily with rests in the middle. The rainy weather and wet trails create difficulties for trekkers in August. A proper raincoat and waterproof trekking gear are essential. Likewise, you will have to trek high-altitude regions that move up and down a lot.

Hence, you should train well for the trek with physical training for strength and endurance. You also require mental preparation for completing this trek with ease. You should take proper preparation as many travelers suffer from altitude sickness. Furthermore, there is a lesser amount of oxygen and air pressure, making breathing difficult in high altitude regions.

Trails are well marked, and you will not have any difficulty navigating along the trail. Also, you should not climb more than 600 m on a trekking day. Overall, this Annapurna base camp trek is moderately challenging. Hence, you should acclimatize well with hydration to tackle altitude sickness in these high altitude conditions.

Why Go On Annapurna Base Camp Trek in August?

August has many unique features that will attract you to trek Annapurna Base Camp. Some of the reasons to go on the ABC trek in August are as follows:

Quiet and peaceful trails

There are fewer trekkers in August as it is off-season. Also, you can trek in a quiet atmosphere and explore the tranquil region in all its glory. You can travel with friends and family or even go trekking solo.

The quiet trail allows you to capture incredible pictures of the region. Annapurna Base Camp remains jam-packed in the peak season, with few opportunities for you to capture the region’s real beauty. Hence, if you want to trek in peace, you should take this ABC trek in August.

Clear blue skies

The sky remains clear after heavy rainfall in August. The days are quite warmer and the nights are cooler in higher altitudes. Likewise, there is a higher amount of rain in lower regions. The upper Annapurna region is quite dry as it receives less rainfall. Hence, you can observe beautiful mountains from various points along the trail.

The blue sky clears after heavy rainfall, and you can observe Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Hiunculi, and other mountains of the region. Green vegetation gets a chance to grow lush that makes trails quite beautiful.

Discounts offers and bargain price

There are various off-season discounts and offers packages available along the trail. Similarly, you can get cheaper flights and meal and accommodation facilities during August. ABC Trek in August is ideal for a budget traveler.

The food and accommodation in tea houses are almost empty, so almost prices get reduced to half. You will get the best rooms, and you can get more discounts if you bargain. In fact, you can also get accommodation facilities for free if you eat at the same teahouses.

Food and Accommodation in Annapurna Base Camp Trek in August

There Tea houses and lodges along the trail provide basic food and accommodation services. You can get your preferred choice of room and meal in the offseason as there are fewer trekkers. You will get a basic room with twin beds, warm blankets, a pillow, and a warm blanket.

Offseason treks mean that you can have your room for yourself and don’t have to share rooms. You can get your private toilets as well. Hot showers, charging facilities, and warm heaters are also available at some tea houses for an added cost. You will get served “Dal Bhat,” twice a day, which is a staple Nepalese diet.

It provides you with the nutrition and energy required for the trek in high-altitude regions. Also, you should also drink water regularly to tackle altitude sickness, as dehydration is one of the major causes. You must carry water purification tablets and a water bottle. Overall, you can get beverages like tea, coffee, hot lemon, garlic soup along the trail.

Some tea houses also offer momo, noodles, pizza, burgers, and another cuisine. Chocolate bars, protein bars, and granola bars will help you by providing energy during the trek. Hence, you should carry them along with water. You should also increase your food intake as you will lose a lot of calories during your tour.

Factors You Should Consider for Annapurna Base Camp Trek in August

Hire a professional guide/porters

You should not travel alone in August, even though it is a mainstream trek with well-marked paths. There are empty trails, and you might want to travel independently, but it is not safe to trek solo. You may experience some kind of emergency, and you need someone to help you in such cases.

Hiring a professional guide is essential as it will help you navigate and keep you safe throughout the journey. Empty trails mean that there are various routes, and you might get lost. A porter will help you carry luggage as it is a long trekking route and you have to trek with heavy bags. You can also hire a porter guide who works both as a porter as well as a guide.

Get the necessary permits.

Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP) and Trekkers’ Information Management System (TIMS) are two travel permits essential for ABC Trek in August. You can get these permits at Nepal Tourism Board’s office in Kathmandu. If you trek through an agency, you will not have to worry about these logistics, as they will manage everything in advance.

Acclimatize and hydrate

Altitude sickness is one of the problematic aspects of this high-altitude trek in the Annapurna region. The walk is not possible without adapting to high altitude conditions through acclimatization.

ABC Trek in August passes through high altitude conditions. Minimal oxygen levels and air pressure will create difficulty in breathing. Similarly, this monsoon season in August adds to the difficulty. Besides that, you should also hydrate regularly to tackle altitude sickness along the trail.

Pack well with the necessary gears.

Since this is a monsoon season trek, you will need to pack well with proper trekking gear. Waterproof jackets, rain covers, and hiking boots are essential. There are sunny days and colder nights with heavy rainfall in the lower region and low rainfall in the upper region.

You should pack layers of clothes as it is comfortable to wear and remove based on weather conditions. You can also pack jackets, trekking boots, and trekking sticks as trails can get slippery. First aid kits, toiletries, and other important documents are also essential.

Get a Travel Insurance

Travel insurance is another essential part of this high-altitude trek. Annapurna Base Camp Trek in August is challenging and comes with various risks. The unpredictable weather is another challenging aspect of this trek.

There might be various medical emergencies along the trail that might even require Evacuation by helicopter, which costs you $5000 to $10000. If you get proper travel insurance, it will cover injuries, thefts, flight delays, helicopter evacuation, and others. This monsoon season has a high risk of injuries and flight delays; hence travel insurance is essential.

Annapurna Base Camp Trek – Detailed Itinerary

Day 01: Drive from Kathmandu to Pokhara and then to Nayapul, Trek from Nayapul to Ghandruk.

Drive duration: 6-7 hours

Trek duration: 1 hour

Maximum altitude: Ghandruk (2,020 m)

We take a scenic flight early in the morning to arrive at a Pokhara from Kathmandu. You can also take a scenic 6-7 hours drive along Prithvi Highway. After arriving at Pokhara, we will take another short drive to Nayapul, which is also the starting point of our Annapurna Base Camp trek.

From Nayapul, you can start trekking to Ghandruk, which is a beautiful Gurung village. The Ghandruk hike takes around one hour as we pass through forested trails with rhododendron and oak trees. We will spend the night at Ghandruk village homestay.

Day 02: Trek from Ghandruk to Sinuwa via Chhomrong

Trek duration: 5-6 hours

Maximum altitude: Sinuwa (2,340 m)

We will have breakfast, start our trek from Ghandruk to Sinuwa via Chomrong. We are going to pass through lush alpine forests along the trail. The Gurung tradition and lifestyle will enchant you. You will get to observe various local people busy in their daily lifestyle of agriculture and animal rearing.

You can interact with villagers and try to learn about their culture and heritage. We will trek through the forested landscapes of Sinuwa on rugged terrains. After arriving at Sinuwa, we will stay overnight at a teahouse.

Day 03: Trek from Sinuwa to Deurali

Trek duration: 6-7 hours

Maximum altitude: Deurali (3,200 m)

After breakfast through various settlements of Bamboo, Dovan, Himalaya, we will continue our trek to Deurali. We can observe beautiful green valleys, vast meadows, snow-capped mountains as we pass through the trails of this exciting trek.

After arriving at Bamboo, we will have our lunch and trek for around 6 to 7 hours to Deurali. The trekkers can also observe and spot diverse flora and fauna of the region. Afterward, we will arrive at Deurali and spend the night at a teahouse.

Day 04: Trek from Deurali to Annapurna Base Camp via Machhapuchhre Base Camp

Trek duration: 5-6 hours

Maximum altitude: ABC (4,130 m)

After quick morning breakfast, we are going to continue our trek to Annapurna Base Camp, our prime destination. It will take an arduous hike in rugged terrain and remote trails to arrive at ABC. We can observe magnificent views of snow-capped mountains, including Machhapuchhre, Annapurna III, Annapurna South, Gangapurna, Himchuli, Glacier Dom, Gandharva Chuli, and others.

Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) is a scenic viewpoint where you can pass through trails and observe beautiful snow-capped mountains. We can explore the base camp area and take beautiful pictures of surrounding areas after arriving at the ABC. Finally, you will spend the night near Base Camp.

Day 05: Trek from Annapurna Base Camp to Bamboo

Trek duration: 5-6 hours

Maximum altitude: ABC (4,130 m)

We will wake up early to observe the Himalayan sunrise overlooking snow-capped mountains, including Barahi Shikhar, Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Tent Peak, Gandharvachuli, and Himchuli.

After breakfast at teahouses, we will continue on our journey to the Machhapuchhre Base Camp. We will then pass through various settlements of Himalayan, Deurali, Dovan to arrive at Bamboo after a trek of around 5-6 hours. We will spend the night in Bamboo.

Day 06: Trek from Bamboo to Kyumi

Trek duration: 5-6 hours

Maximum altitude: Bamboo (2,340 m)

We will trek through the beautiful landscapes of forested bamboo trails after having breakfast. Likewise, we will then continue our trek passing through Jhinu, Sinuwa, and Chhomrong. We will have lunch after arriving at Jhinu (1,690 m) and rest.

Jhinu danda hot water springs are one of the significant highlights of the journey. Besides, we relax at this hot water spring after a taxing trekking adventure and then continue our trek to Kyumi. Finally, we will arrive at Kyumi after a hike of around 5-6 hours and then stay overnight at a teahouse in Kumi.

Day 07: Trek from Nayapul via Siwai, Drive to Pokhara or Kathmandu

Trek duration: 5-6 hours

Drive duration: 2 hours from Pokhara, 6-7 hours from Kathmandu

Maximum altitude: Kyumi (1,690 m)

After breakfast, we will trek from Kyumi to Nayapul via Siwai. You will pass through diverse landscapes with green vegetation and colorful trails. Thereafter, we will arrive at Nayapul after a trek of around 5-6 hours. You can then drive back to Pokhara and stay at a hotel. In fact, you can also drive back to Kathmandu on Prithvi Highway.

Training And Preparation For Annapurna Base Camp Trek In August

Annapurna Base Camp Trek is a challenging adventure in remote and rugged parts of the country. In fact, various unpredictable factors make trekking difficult. Therefore, a proper training routine is essential to complete this trek with ease.

Strength and endurance training

Annapurna base camp trek requires a basic level of fitness and stamina. Therefore, trekkers must take part in strength and endurance training. Hence, you should do weight training and trek with a backpack to practice at high altitudes of the region.

Practice hikes also help you immensely during your trek. You should also perform various cardiovascular activities like squats, push-ups, hiking, jogging, cycling, hiking, and others that will help you build physical strength and endurance. Moreover, yoga will help you with breathing in high altitude conditions and also with flexibility.

Mental preparation

Mental preparation is another essential aspect of this trek. You should have a positive attitude to complete this challenging trek with ease. Therefore, you can perform various mental exercises and motivational therapy to help you with this trek.

  • Acclimatization well and hydrate regularly.
  • Get a proper Training regime to gain basic fitness levels and stamina.

Final Say

August is a challenging off-season for ABC trek, but it is doable with proper packing and preparation. The Upper Annapurna region receives minimal rainfall. The meal and accommodation costs are almost half in these seasons. Overall, the quiet trails provide you magnificent trekking experience in a peaceful adventure.

title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek in May
excerpt: Annapurna Base Camp trek is an incredible trekking adventure in the beautiful foothills of the Annapurna massif. May in the Spring season and is one of the best times to trek in the region. This…
html:
Annapurna Base Camp trek is an incredible trekking adventure in the beautiful foothills of the Annapurna massif. May in the Spring season and is one of the best times to trek in the region. This exciting adventure provides you with a perfect trekking atmosphere and breathtaking views of the snow-capped mountains.

May is a peak season for trekking in Nepal and hundreds of trekkers flock in this region to trek magnificent Himalayan landscapes. The daytime weather is favorable and temperatures are moderate which makes it ideal for trekking. You can observe the awe-inspiring snow-capped mountain views of Annapurna I, Manaslu, Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre, Mt. Dhaulagiri, and others.

Moreover, this incredible trek passes through the Annapurna Conservation Area (ACA) and its diverse flora and fauna. You can explore the rare and endangered animals of the Annapurna region including Snow Leopard, Himalayan Tahr, Danphe, and others. This trek also takes you on a cultural exploration of the Gurung, Tamang, and Magar community settlements.

Furthermore, trekkers will stay at the local tea houses and lodges. The warm welcome and hospitality of the local people will make you fall in love with the place. We are offering this spectacular trek at a reasonable price. Read on to know more about the Annapurna Base Camp trek in May and other related information in detail.

Highlights of the Trek

  • Awe-inspiring Himalayan sunrise views from the Poon Hill viewpoint
  • Breathtaking views of snow-capped mountains including Annapurna I, Machhapuchhare, Annapurna South, Dhaulagiri, Himchhuli, Manaslu, and others
  • Walking through diverse landscapes of Annapurna Sanctuary
  • Spotting rare and endangered animals of the region
  • Exploring the culture, heritage, and lifestyle of the local ethnic community
  • Hot water bathing at Jhinu danda hot springs
  • Incredible welcome and hospitality of the local people

Trekking Route

After an early morning flight from Kathmandu to Pokhara, we will take a short drive to Syauli Bazar. The trekking journey starts with a hike from Syauli Bazar to Ghandruk. Thereafter, we will stay overnight at a community-run homestay in Ghandruk and trek to Sinuwa Danda via Chomrong the next day.

Furthermore, we trek to Deurali from Sinuwa Danda, passing through bamboo forests. We will start our ultimate trek to Annapurna Base Camp passing through the Machhapuchhre Base Camp. After exploring the area and taking beautiful pictures, we will rest in the evening and spend the night at ABC.

Finally, we will start our return trek from ABC to Bamboo. We will pass through various settlements to arrive at Jhinu from Bamboo passing through the various settlements. We will take a scenic drive back to Pokhara and stay at a hotel or return to Kathmandu on another 6-7 hour drive along Prithvi Highway.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Why Go On Annapurna Base Camp Trek in May?

Annapurna Base Camp Trek in May has many exciting aspects. Some of the major reasons to go on this trek are as follows:

Minimal precipitation and snowfall

May has stable weather conditions and fewer chances of rainfall or snowfall as it is a post-winter and pre-monsoon period. The dry trails allow trekkers to explore the region in all its glory.

Besides that, flight cancellations or delays are not common in this season. The green valleys and mountains landscapes look incredibly beautiful in May as well.

Breathtaking mountain views on clear skies

This incredible trek in May provides you with incredible views of snow-capped mountains and other natural beauties in a clear blue sky. The sharp views of peaks and surrounding vista will make you fall in love with the place.

May is also the peak spring season so the peaks look majestic. The golden sun rays falling over silver mountains are spectacular. The picturesque surroundings like green meadows, valleys, and water streams are the highlight of the Annapurna Base Camp trek.

Visit Annapurna sanctuary

You will trek through the beautiful landscapes of the Annapurna sanctuary. The rare and endangered animals of the Annapurna region and unique vegetation are highlights of this trek.

Some of the animals you can spot in this trek are Pandas, Foxes, Snow leopards, the Himalayan bear, Musk deer, and others. The animals also start to remain active in May.

Bustling Trails

It is also the peak season for trekking and traveling in the Annapurna region. The routes are bustling with trekkers from all around the world in May. The wildflowers blooming all over hills including Rhododendron will spellbind you.

The trek also provides you with an opportunity to go on a group trekking with fellow family and friends. Even if you trek solo, fellow trekkers will keep you company throughout. So, this is another excellent aspect of this trek.

How is the Weather Condition of Annapurna Base Camp Trek in May?

May lies at the end of the Spring season in Nepal. The stable weather conditions with minimal precipitation are the highlight of the trek in May. A favorable trekking environment in May makes hundreds of trekkers flock to the Annapurna region.

May ranges around 20-degree Celsius in temperature at lower altitudes whereas higher altitudes are significantly lower. The temperatures in the mornings and nights drop around 5 degrees Celsius. Hence, you should pack well for a trek with warm clothes and proper trekking gear.

Moreover, the ABC trek is also known for harsh winds of around 10km/hr in higher elevations. There is minimal precipitation in the early parts of May in the Annapurna region but there are some occasional rainfalls in the latter parts of May. Hence, you should trek in early May as far as possible.

Food And Accommodation During Annapurna Base Camp Trek In May

The Annapurna Base Camp Trek trail includes many tea houses and lodges. You can find many of these accommodations along the trail where you can stay overnight. They provide basic facilities for food and accommodation. Most of the rooms in these tea houses have two separate beds, a warm blanket, a mattress, a pillow, and a clean sheet.

They also provide hot water, charging, and Wi-Fi facilities in lower regions at an added cost. As you move along trails, you will find these facilities to decline gradually in higher elevations. The food facilities are quite basic with the local Nepali cuisine of Dal Bhat being most common.

The dish contains Dal, Bhat, vegetables, lentils, pickles, Gundruk, meat, and others. You will get served this dish twice a day for lunch and dinner. For breakfast, you will get bread toast, porridge, and eggs. And for drinks, tea, coffee, garlic soup are quite common. Some tea houses also provide momo, Chowmein, pizza, pasta, burger, and others in lower regions.

How Difficult is Annapurna Base Camp Trek in May?

May is the peak season for trekking and traveling in the Annapurna region. However, there are some difficulties that you might have to face during the ABC trek in May. Some of them are as follows:

Altitude Sickness

Altitude sickness is one of the major difficulties of the trek. There is a lesser amount of oxygen and air pressure in high elevations which makes breathing difficult. Headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, difficulty in breathing, etc are some of the symptoms of altitude sickness.

If you can feel any of the symptoms you should stop your trek and descend at a lower altitude immediately. You should also inform your guide so that they can help you with the emergency evacuation if necessary. They will provide you with immediate first aid help as well.

Duration and Distance

The ABC Trek is generally 11 to 15 days long. Trekking for a long duration in remote regions is quite challenging. The itinerary can get changed based on your preference. A longer itinerary with proper acclimatization days is generally recommended for beginners.

A shorter itinerary means that you will have to work for a long duration and not get time for acclimatization and rest. Usually, a trek of around 5 to 6 hours with breaks in the middle is comfortable.

A short itinerary means that you will have to trek for 7 to 9 hours each day covering a 20 to 25 km distance. This can make your trekking journey harsh especially with no acclimatization.

Lack of Privacy

The route of this ABC trek in May will remain crowded as it is a peak season for trekking in Nepal. So, you might find it difficult to adjust if you love trekking in a quiet peaceful atmosphere. You will find fellow trekkers in every corner along the trail.

Annapurna Base Camp Trek in May can be quite challenging for these reasons. You will have to queue up for everything including toilet and meal facilities and cannot get a clear view without obstruction. The noise created by fellow trekkers along the trail is disturbing as well.

Packed Accommodation

There are a limited number of tea houses and lodges in the Annapurna region. So, they remain crowded and if you do not book in advance you will not find the best accommodation facilities.

May is a peak season and you might have to share rooms or even sleep in the dining hall due to the unavailability of rooms. Also, rooms will cost you more in these seasons.

Detailed Itinerary – Annapurna Base Camp Trek

Day 01: Fly to Pokhara and drive to Syauli Bazar (1,100 m), walk to Ghandruk village (1,930 m).

Flight duration: 35 minutes

Maximum altitude: 1,930 m

Trekking hours: 06 hrs

After breakfast, we will start our journey with a scenic flight from Kathmandu to Pokhara. You can also drive to Pokhara which takes around 6-7 hours. Pokhara is a beautiful lake city with many pristine lakes and provides magical views of snow-capped mountains including Annapurna and Machhapuchhre Himal.

You can go on a short sightseeing tour of Pokhara and then drive to Syauli Bazar from where you will start a short hike of around 2 hours to arrive at Ghandruk. Ghandruk is a famous Gurung village from where you can observe majestic views of snow-capped mountain peaks including Annapurna. You will spend the night at a community homestay in Ghandruk.

Day 02: Trek from Ghandruk to Sinwa Danda (2,355 m) via Chomrong (2,170 m).

Trek duration: 06 hrs

Maximum altitude: 2,355 m

After having breakfast, we will trek from Ghandruk passing through a stone-paved trail to arrive at the village of Sinuwa Danda. A trek of around two hours will take you to Chomrong Danda ridge. We will gradually descend downhill to arrive at the Chomrong River valley passing through a deep forest.

Terraced farmed hills and vast green fields along the trail will enchant you. After climbing a steep hill, we will arrive at Chomrong which is a scenic village settlement. From Chomrong, we will take downhill descent and continue trekking alongside the Chomrong river, before taking another sharp uphill to Sinuwa.

Sinuwa village on top of a hill provides you with awe-inspiring views of the snow-capped mountains of the Annapurna region. After exploring around the area and observing this incredible mountain vista we will rest and stay overnight at a teahouse in Sinuwa.

Day 03: Trek from Sinuwa Danda to Deurali (3,235 m).

Maximum altitude: 3,235 m

Trek duration: 06 hrs

We will start trekking from Sinuwa to Deurali after having breakfast early in the morning. Trekkers will pass through the forest trail with dense wood and bamboo trees to arrive at Bamboo. Bamboo is a small temporary settlement where you can find many tea houses and lodges.

This trail then continues on a river gorge with many rhododendrons, bamboo, and pine trees. From Bamboo, we will descend gradually alongside the Modi River gorge to arrive at Dovan. You will arrive at the Himalaya Hotel after passing through many winding roads.

You can find a large Hinko cave along the trail beneath the mountain peaks of Annapurna South and Himchuli. We will trek downhill passing through the Modi River to arrive at Deurali where you can find many Alpine bushes along the trail. We will spend the night at a teahouse in Deurali.

Day 04: Trek from Deurali to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) (4,130 m).

Maximum altitude: 4,130 m

Trek duration: 06 hrs

After breakfast, we will start our trek steeply alongside the Modi Khola and continue through forested trails. The trail then leads us to Machhapuchhre Base Camp located in the north face of the Machhapuchhre.

We will explore around Machhapuchhre Base Camp and take pictures before continuing our journey to the Annapurna Base Camp. We will pass through the Annapurna Sanctuary region that works in the conservation of flora and fauna of the region. Many up and down paths within the sanctuary will challenge all trekkers to their core.

After trekking for a few hours, we will arrive at the Base Camp. The Annapurna Base Camp located at an altitude of 4,130 m is also the highest point of the trek. The magical vista of Gangapurna, Vara-Shikhar, Annapurna South, and others will spellbind you. You can explore the ABC area and then stay overnight at the local teahouse in the Base Camp.

Day 05: Trek from Annapurna Base Camp to Bamboo (2,345 m)

Maximum altitude: 2,345 m

Trek duration: 06 hrs

We will wake up early in the morning to enjoy the glorious Himalayan sunrise overlooking the Annapurna range of mountains from the Base Camp. We will then have our breakfast, and continue our downhill trek of bamboo. The trail then takes us through tree lines and forested areas. We will spend the night at a local teahouse after arriving in Bamboo.

Day 06: Trek from Bamboo to Kyumi via Jhinu village (1,780 m) and drive to Pokhara.

Maximum altitude: 1,780 m

Trek duration: 07 hrs

We will have our breakfast early in the morning and then continue our trek to Chomrong. We arrive at Chomrong hilltop after trekking for a few hours and then continue to Jhinu village. Jhinu hot water springs are a prime attraction of this trek where many trekkers relax their muscles by dipping in hot water after trekking.

We then descend downhill for half an hour alongside the Modi-River, to arrive at Jhinu hot water springs. Thereafter, we arrive at Kyumi village after a trek of a few hours where you can find many green farms. Furthermore, we will then drive to Pokhara which takes around 2 hours, and then spend the night at a hotel.

Day 07: Drive or Fly back to Kathmandu and transfer to the hotel.

We will drive back to Kathmandu after having breakfast. You can also take a scenic flight back to Kathmandu. You can go on a sightseeing tour of the city or observe the bustling atmosphere of the Thamel area. Thereafter, you will stay overnight at a hotel in Kathmandu.

Factors to consider for Annapurna Base Camp Trek in May

Some of the essential factors to consider for the ABC trek in May are as follows:

Advance Booking

Booking is essential, especially in peak season. You might have to sleep in the dining hall or camp outside in case the rooms get packed. If you travel with a trekking agency you don’t have to worry about these logistics. They will help you with accommodation booking and your behalf as most of the tea houses remain packed for the whole season.

Gradual walk

Walking gradually at a gentle pace is the most important tip while trekking in the foothills of the Himalayas. You should not take this trek as a race and trek in a slow manner. So, you should trek slowly exploring around the region, and taking your time to enjoy the moments during your trek.

Magnificent mountain peaks and colorful forests are highlights of this trek. You can also learn about the tradition, culture, and heritage of the people. Hence, you should trek gradually along the trail.

Hire a Guide or Porter

Hiring a professional trekking guide and porter is essential especially if you have not trekked in high altitude conditions. Trekking for a long duration carrying heavy backpacks is not a walk in the park.

The guide helps you with navigation along the trail as there are many many routes to Annapurna Base Camp. They also know all their shortcuts. They will also help you translate and learn about local culture.

Regular Hydration

Annapurna Base Camp Trek in May requires regular hydration. Dehydration leads to altitude sickness and hence carrying a water bottle is essential as you can refill them in tea houses.

The bottled water costs are high in higher elevations and thus you should carry water purification tablets and purify them. However, boiled water may cost you extra along the trail. You should fill all your water bottles at the beginning of your trek as water resources are scarce.

Physical Training

Physical training will help you gain a basic level of fitness and stamina for the Base Camp. The moderate-level trek then leads you to remote and rugged terrains. However, you must remain physically and mentally fit, so that you can go on this incredible adventure with ease.

So, physical training is essential for this trek. The physical training exercise will build your strength and endurance. Running, swimming, cycling, hiking, and others are some of the cardiovascular activities that you can perform in your training regime. These exercises along with mental preparation at least two weeks before your trek will help you immensely during the trek.

Some Essential Tips For Trek

  • Proper acclimatization will help you tackle altitude sickness in high altitude conditions.
  • Check the weather forecast to plan for the trek.
  • Hydration at regular intervals is essential to tackle altitude sickness along trails.
  • Carry cash in Nepali money and beware of pickpockets.
  • Pack lightly with only those items that are essential during the trek.
  • Walk at a gentle pace with proper rest in the middle.
  • Hire professional trekking guides and porters.

Annapurna Base Camp trek is an exciting trek in the beautiful landscapes of the Annapurna region. This trek passes through incredible mountain foothills and other natural landscapes. May is one of the best times to trek this outstanding region.

This magical view of snow-capped mountains and green valleys is highlighted in May. Overall, the Annapurna Base Camp trek in May is one of the best trekking adventures in Nepal. We hope you learned about this ABC trek in May in detail. Contact us for more information and book your trip now!

title: Everest Base Camp Trek 8 Days
excerpt: Everest Base Camp Trek 8 Days is one of the most suitable treks for those who are in short of time. For many adventure seekers, Nepal embodies thrill and agitation with stunning landscapes, hidden…
html:
Everest Base Camp Trek 8 Days is one of the most suitable treks for those who are in short of time.

For many adventure seekers, Nepal embodies thrill and agitation with stunning landscapes, hidden valleys, deep fjords, and towering cliffs. Its unique geographical features alongside staggering rock formations, terrace farm, and exotic village have people lose their head

Regardless of that, nothing seems to transcend the charm and unequivocal effect that Everest Base Camp holds. Its unprecedented beauty attracts travelers from around the world and makes them visit the place. This explains why Everest Base Camp Trek 8 days has so many visitors all year long.

Everest Base Camp Trek pre-defines nature’s grandeur with fascinating hills, sweeping meadows, and glaciers before climbing off Gorak Shep. It boasts a mind-boggling vista along the winding lanes teemed with primeval villages, old monasteries, and chortens.

Perched at 17,598 ft. elevation, Everest Base Camp is in the seam of lofty mountains, glacial moraines, crags, and boulders. It sits right on the Khumbu Glacier, providing a seamless view of Everest along with Nuptse and Cho Oyu.

8 days Everest Base Camp Trek begins with an early flight to Lukla and presumably a short-haul to Phakding. The trial paves its way through wild forests and over the valley to wind up at Namche Bazaar.

As the lane keeps stretching distant, we’ll pass legions of charming Sherpa villages including Tengboche and Lobuche. Getting out of here, the trail gets harsh with steep ascents and rocks all the way up to Everest Base Camp.

In between the time, we’ll have a few more breaks for stretching out the leg, having lunch, and exploring the places around. The sightseeing from the base camp is unreal with a closer look at Everest and its dramatic landforms.

Highlights of Everest Base Camp Trek 8 days

  • Aerial view of sky-high mountains, soaring cliffs, and vast meadows
  • Exploring picturesque destinations including Syangboche
  • A close snap of Mt. Everest and its nearby mountains
  • Cultural tour of Namche Bazaar and Tengboche
  • A visit to quaint villages of Himalaya and interaction with locals
  • Peek at wildlife and birds in Sagarmatha National Park

When is the Best Time for 8 Days Everest Base Camp Trek 8 days

The invincible beauty of Everest Base Camp Trek may trick people with the wrong impression that it can be done any day now. While it’s fair that the base camp is always up to host travelers from around, the weather doesn’t favor most days.

Oftentimes it becomes hard to finish the Everest Base Camp trek in 8 days due to bad weather and sudden climate changes. Trekkers must therefore don’t take any chance and do the trip in either spring or autumn.

Both these seasons put up with the loveliest weather and scenic views, making it a perfect time to do the hike. Starting from mid-March, spring embarks in Nepal, shoving off the long blistering winter. Furthermore, the climate is a bit frosty in the early days but in the long run, it gets so much better with a cool breeze and sublimity.

Days get longer during spring with a warm and cozy atmosphere all over. With temperatures ranging from 0 to 15 Degree Celsius, it’s less stressful, navigating the incessant trails. The season is satisfying in all respects as they put up a wonderful atmosphere with breathtaking views.

Spring is also the only occasion for trekkers to enjoy blooming rhododendron and wildflowers throughout the hills and forest. There’s green verdure everywhere along with glimpses of various wildlife and birds.

Autumn is the most delightful of all seasons and also the right moment to be outside. The weather is splendidly unreal for as long with a mild temperature, warm sunshine, and spectacular scenes. Overall, temperatures are normally between 6 to 22 Degree Celsius in the months which makes it perfect for hiking.

The views look breathtaking during the entire time with colorful autumn leaves in hills and inside woods. Autumn treats its guests with picturesque landscapes, glistening snow peaks, and highlands that can be seen from miles.

Although not so terrific, 8 days Everest Base Camp Trek can also be done in winter and monsoon. That said, hiking will not be easy during the season following continuous rainfall and storms. In fact, trails are usually muddy and drenched in rain during the monsoon, causing the hikers to slip off.

With the dark clouds looming in the sky all day, it’s hard to get a clear view during the season. Meanwhile, trekkers in winter will have to dodge frigid weather with extreme snowfall in order to reach the base camp. Temperatures are normally measured in minus Degree Celsius during winter so without insulated clothes and boots, it’ll be hard to do the trek.

Everest Base Camp Trek 8 Days Detailed Itinerary:

Day 01: Flight to Lukla, trek to Phakding

Maximum Altitude: 2,610 m

Flight Duration: 40 minutes

Trek Duration: 2-3 hours

Flight Distance: 138 km

Trek Distance: 6.2 km

Early in the morning, we’ll catch the flight to Lukla at Tribhuvan airport. We’ll be picking you up from the hotel and driving on the way to the airfield. The trip will last for about 40 minutes, offering us an eye-candy vista of staggering cliffs, fascinating waterfalls, and landscapes.

Since the weather is quite subtle and crystalline clear at the crack of dawn, we’re likely to spot a few mountains and narrow valleys. At Lukla, we’ll swing by a local teahouse, grab lunch, and head to Phakding.

The trek starts with a gentle ascent uphill on the left bank of Dudh Koshi River which comes with a great view. We’ll get our way through the forested area and beautiful mani walls leading up to Ghat. Likewise, the trail to Phakding ends up with a series of uphill and descents that’ll take no time.

Day 02: Trek to Namche Bazaar

Maximum Altitude: 3,440 m

Trek Distance: 7.4 km

Trek Duration: 5 to 6 hours

After breakfast, we’ll head on to the trail that gets underway crossing a creek and over the terraced hill. After reaching Bengar, we’ll turn up to a zigzagged trail that has several ups and downs. Before access to the sanctuary, we’ll make a stop at Sagarmatha national park and get the permit.

As the trek gets ahead, we’ll walk past a few more villages including Jorsale, and cross the suspension bridge. The walk to Namche is continuously upward over a steep hill which lasts almost 2 to 3 hours.

The journey from Phakding to Namche will take approximately 6 hours based on the pace of a trekker. After arriving at the village, we get a quite astonishing view of towering hills, picturesque forests, and patchwork fields. Overnight stay in a lodge at Namche.

Day 03: Acclimatization at Namche Bazaar

Contemplating the severe and tough voyage to Namche, a day off is well worth it. Hence, we’ll use a break and instead use the time to explore the village. After having a delicious meal for breakfast, we’re on for a trip to Syangboche.

The trail is mostly uphill with a rough course that takes between 1 to 2 hours. The excursion has some charming sceneries to offer its visitors along with nice weather. During the trip, we’ll stop by Everest view hotel to get a glimpse of Mt. Everest and its nearby Kangtega and Thamserku.

After traversing the hilltop, we’ll take an easy walk on the way back to Namche. The path is mostly downhill so it’ll take less time than previous. Finally, those who want to escape the trip can instead visit the national museum or stroll the town and markets.

Day 04: Trek to Tengboche

Maximum Altitude: 3,860 m

Trek Distance: 9.2 km

Trek Duration: 5-6 hours

After a full-day outing, we’re now ready to retrieve the hike to Tengboche which takes around 5-6 hours. The trek starts off with a gentle descend beneath the hill and through a small settlement of Trashinga. From there, we’ll follow the long steep trail that passes lush-green forests and mani stone.

After coming off the level ground, we’ll walk a few more miles and finally stand before the gigantic stone gate of Tengboche. Upon arrival, we can witness the glistening Ama Dablam and sweeping hills. Tonight, we’ll stay in a tea house at Tengboche.

Day 05: Trek to Dingboche

Maximum Altitude: 4,410 m

Trek Distance: 9 km

Trek Duration: 5-6 hours

Today we’ll pay a visit to the Tengboche monastery in the early morning hours and join the devotees for morning prayers. Shortly afterward, we’ll head on our way to Dingboche by climbing up the mountainside besides Ama Dablam and Kantega.

The trek follows an endless path above the river valley that passes several chortens and rocky hills. Thereafter, leaving behind the lovely village of Pangboche, we’ll head towards a Tibetan-styled mani stupa.

From here, the trek gets slightly easier with a short walk. Eventually, after hiking for an entire 6 hours, we’ll wind up at Dingboche. As it’s inconceivable to continue the journey ahead, we’ll stop at Dingboche for the night.

Day 06: Trek to Lobuche

Maximum Altitude: 5,180 m

Trek Distance:

Trek Duration: 6-7 hours

From Tengboche, we’ll start our expedition with a downhill walk to Pheriche. Also, the trek follows a lane from the edge of the hill which provides a marvelous view of Chukhung valley and the surrounding snow peaks.

The trek maintains its course and takes a steep climb for quite a while before moving quickly to the plains. From here on, the hike becomes slightly more relaxing. As of right now, the settlements are sparse with only a few tea houses and lodges for travelers.

Provided the steep trail ahead, we’ll have a little break at Dugla for lunch prior to continuing the trek. After filling up, we’ll continue with the rest of the trek and ascend sloppy hills for about an hour. Along the way, we’ll be provided with an impressive view of hillocks and snow peaks including Mt. Pumori and Everest. At Lobuche, we’ll spend the night in a tea house.

Day 07: Trek to Gorak Shep and hike to Everest Base Camp. Return to Gorak Shep

Maximum Altitude: 5,364 m

Trek Distance: 14.5 km

Trek Duration: 6-7hours

The trek to Everest Base Camp is a long and tiring journey through the brink of a frozen lake bed and moraine. The entire walk to the base camp takes around 6-7 hours which is why we’ll start early.

Tracking the path through a rocky moraine below Khumbu Glacier, we’ll head to Gorak Shep, a small hamlet sitting at an elevation of 5,164 m We’ll stop here for a short while and have lunch before resuming the hike.

From here onwards, the trek gets quite tough with rugged trails full of stones and cobblers. Hence, the trail has to be carefully steered with enough precautions. After reaching the base camp, we’ll be taking a tour of the site and clap eyes on the world’s tallest mountain. When done with exploring the campsite, we’ll head back to the village and rest the night there.

Day 08: Trek to Kala Patthar and pick up by helicopter

Maximum Altitude: 5,643 m

Trek Distance: 1.2 km

Flight Distance: 152 km

Trek Duration: 2-3 hours

Flight Duration: 1 hour

Since it’s the last day of Everest Base Camp Trek 8 days, we’ll wake up by dawn and start climbing the trail to Kala Patthar. During the whole time, we’ll be scaling up a rocky terrain crammed with boulders.

After walking steadily for 2 to 3 hours depending on the traveling speed, we’ll get to the landmark at 5,643 m As soon as we’re done with scouting the mountain and topography, our aircraft will pick us and fly back to the city.

The flight will last almost an hour feeding us with some magnificent scenery of cascading waterfalls, green hills, and forest. After taking down the airport half an hour later, our staff will drive you back to the hotel where you can rest off.

Preparation for Everest Base Camp Trek 8 days

With merely 8 days of trek schedule, it may seem that the trip to Everest Base Camp doesn’t need a lot of preparation. But, that’s just a fallacy as trekkers have to come fully prepared for the hike otherwise, they’ll have a tough time doing the trip. Hikers have to get ready for both physical and mental challenges that come on the way to Everest Base Camp trek 8 days.

Physical preparation

At the height of intense trails and unpredictable weather, Everest Base Camp Trek 8 days requires a lot of physical stamina and endurance. Without sufficient energy, it’s hard to pull off a hike as formidable as Everest Base Camp.

Therefore, trekkers who’re planning to do the trip must level up their fitness training and get in good shape. It’s always a great idea to start with regular exercises like jogging and cycling to improve the current fitness level. These workouts will help you stay fit and also release the stress before switching to a hardcore fitness regimen.

Aerobic exercise like planks and squats are highly recommended for Everest Base Camp trek as it strengthens the physical resistance. A few short hikes and camping before the actual trek will be nice to combat the difficulties that might occur on the way.

Mental Preparation

With endless steep terrains and wilderness, Everest Base Camp Trek 8 days can make any hikers anxious and startled. This is why trekkers expected to arrive at the camp should be mentally prepared to withstand the difficulties that might arouse en route.

The hiker must always keep a positive attitude throughout the ride and don’t let fear control their mind. Staying calm and cool is the best way to avoid emotional strain and distress while on the trek. Know your abilities and closely monitor your health while going to higher elevations to avoid acute mountain sickness.

It’s quite common for trekkers to get dehydrated while traversing the lanes so drink as much water as possible. Get yourself ready for basic living standards and take proper care of your hygiene. It’s crucial for travelers to retrieve the energy, so carrying enough nutritious food and snacks would be a wise move.

Essentials Packing list for 8 Days EBC Trek

Trekking Everest Base Camp for a whole 8 days is a mammoth task and you need to be a lot prepared for it. From physical fitness to backpacking, everything has to be sorted out ahead of time. You need to make necessary purchases before the trek and make sure that nothing is left out.

Carrying way more weight affects the walking speed of trekkers and even prevents them from enjoying the trip. Thus, you need to be really careful about what you pick for hiking and scrap unwanted items.

Keep the backpack as light as possible but without missing significant gears like trekking poles and tents. Listed below are some of the essentials that you must bring during 8 days Everest Base Camp Trek.

Clothing

  • Windproof or fleece jacket to prevent storms and rain
  • Long sleeve warm t-shirts for winter
  • Lightweight pants and trousers
  • Breathable rain pants to avoid getting soaked
  • Quick-drying shorts

Footwear

  • High-quality hiking boots to resist snow
  • Sturdy mountaineering shoes
  • A few pair of synthetic or woolen socks

Miscellaneous

  • First-aid supplies with some prescribed medicines
  • Extra batteries, power bank, and charger
  • Reusable water bottles and purifier
  • Sun protection glasses and hat
  • Gloves or mittens

Difficulties of Everest Base Camp Trek 8 days

As might be expected, Everest Base Camp is a moderate trek with no technical challenges and undefeated trails. The course could be long and strenuous but not transcendent with hundreds and thousands of hikers already climbing the base camp.

Despite that, there are times when the trails of Everest Base Camp get harsh to excursionists. It throws quite a lot of difficulties on their way to camp and makes it nearly impossible to reach the height. Here are those challenges that hikers of Everest Base Camp trek 8 days have to overcome to reach the ultimate destination.

1. Altitude Sickness

Trekkers of Everest Base Camp Trek 8 days often suffer from altitude sickness due to steep trails that never seem to end. Likewise, the low atmospheric pressure noticeable from Namche Bazaar seems to strike travelers and make it hard to breathe.

Early symptoms like headache, dizziness, and muscle aches are evident while going to higher places. Similarly, indications like these should not be overlooked, and take medications on time. In case of emergency, one should descend the trail and return back to Kathmandu.

There’s no better way than altitude acclimatization to prevent the adverse effect of acute mountain sickness. Therefore, if you’re suffering from low-oxygen in the air, take a time off from the walk and have proper rest.

2. Long and Steep Trail

The trail of Everest Base Camp from Lukla is 40 miles long with most of the sections steep and narrow. Moreover, the walk is mostly uphill over the edge of cliffs and valleys which is nerve-wracking even for professionals.

Therefore, trekkers who’re supposed to visit the camp must be physically and mentally resolute. While they must be in good shape, climbers also need to have a positive mindset in order to tackle the rugged trail of Base Camp.

3. Weather

The unforeseeable weather of Everest Base Camp Trek is another challenge for hikers. Besides, it presents uncertainties to the hike and occasionally causes the climber to abandon the trip. The reduced air resistance with sudden rainstorms, fog, and snow makes the Everest Base Camp Trek 8 days quite difficult. Moreover, the climate in Khumbu Valley can often be different from Lukla with high wind and cold. In such circumstances, you need to be extremely cautious and keep track of the weather forecast report.

8 days Everest Base Camp Trek is an everlasting experience of great pleasure and thrill ride to Himalaya’s epic places. The trip is filled with long walks, cultural exploration, watching mesmeric sceneries, and wildlife. Also, it has trekkers visit some of the quintessential villages in Nepal, meet mountain tribes, and get a sneak peek of unique cultures.

The journey to base camp is no doubt tough with continuous steep trails and unstable weather but it’s also rewarding, given the amazing view of Mt. Everest, glacial lakes, and diverse landforms. title: 10 Days Everest Base Camp Trekking – Detailed Guide
excerpt: It may sound a bit odd, but a trekker can do Everest Base Camp Trek in 10 days. Yes, Everest Base Camp Trekking 10 Days is a short itinerary that takes you on the Everest region’s walk and ultimately…
html:
It may sound a bit odd, but a trekker can do Everest Base Camp Trek in 10 days. Yes, Everest Base Camp Trekking 10 Days is a short itinerary that takes you on the Everest region’s walk and ultimately to the base camp of the world’s tallest mountain.

This, 10 Days Everest Base Camp Trekking, is a trek for experienced trekkers. Without a single acclimatization day, you’ll be doing this trek just to reach the base camp. Usually, the length of Everest Base Camp Trek is around 14 to 16 days. Those itineraries have enough rest and acclimatization days. But the trek we are talking about does not have one also. It is just a straightforward approach to one of the highest places in the world.

With the days reduced, the difficulty level of Everest Base Camp Trek does increase. The same will happen on this trek. Yeah, you’ll run across many beautiful views and things on this trek. But for making that happen, you’ll have to give something extra.

Specially designed for experienced adventurers, the trek is also recognized as the short Everest Base Camp Trekking. If you are an accomplished trekker, why don’t you do this short version of the hike? You’ll save some days and will have loads of adventures there on the trek.

To tell it in a few words, in a matter of 10 days, you will trek down one of the challenging treks in the world. It will surely be the best moment of your life to do an expedition like this in fewer days.

This blog is all about the Everest Base Camp Trekking 10 Days. If you are in for this adventure, this blog will be beneficial to you. Read it all.

Significant Highlights of 10 Days Everest Base Camp Trekking

  • Dare a trek in 10 days that takes 14 to 16 days to do in normal.
  • Start the trip with a morning mountain flight that is scenic to Lukla.
  • Commence the trek from Lukla and move through picturesque villages and landscapes.
  • Explore the natural richness of Sagarmatha National Park, UNESCO listed world heritage site.
  • Run to the popular stops like Namche Bazaar- the Himalayan Town and Tengboche-the village with the region’s most important monastery.
  • Get to know the Sherpas, their lifestyle, and culture.
  • Get to glance at the mountains of the region every day through the trek.
  • Reach Everest Base Camp through a not-so-easy trail and celebrate the struggle there with the view.
  • Hike up to Kala Patthar for the best mountain panorama of Everest and adjoining peaks.
  • Descend back to Lukla by trekking and witnessing the same beauty once more.

Best Time for Short Everest Base Camp Trekking

For Everest Base Camp Trekking or any other treks, Autumn and Spring are the right times for adventure in Nepal. Looking at the weather conditions, those two are the times that you have to choose one from. However, you can also pick the two others for Everest Base Camp Trek: Summer and Winter. It is just a little bit difficult to do the trek in these times.

But if you choose between Autumn and Spring, you’ll get favorable conditions for trekking. You do not have to face any irregularities like rainfall and snowfall in these so-called best times. And it is excitingly comfortable and easy to do a trek in Autumn and Spring compared to the other two. Let’s discuss each of them more concisely.

Autumn

September to November is the time of the Autumn season in Nepal. During this period, the conditions are all in favor of trekkers. Days are with more sunny hours, cloudless skies, warm temperature, and clear visibility are some of the Autumn season’s happenings. Just imagine doing Everest Base Camp Trek under such conditions, isn’t it exciting? You’ll have enough mountain views in a crystal-clear way each day.

It is not only weather-wise, but the season is worth doing cultural-wise because some of the biggest festivals of Nepalese lie in the season only. For example, Dashain and Tihar, the most widely celebrated festivals, fall in October. If you go trekking at this very time, you’ll see the country in a happy and celebrating mood.

The weather of the Everest Region in Autumn is as follow:

Places: Lukla, Namche, and Tengboche
Elevation(m) : 3,000 m to 4,000 m
Max Temperature(°C) : 16°C
Min Temperature(°C): 2°C
Sunny hours: 9 hours

Places: Dingboche, EBC, and Kala Patthar
Elevation(m) :4,000 m to 5,500 m
Max Temperature(°C) : 10°C
Min Temperature(°C): -7°C
Sunny hours: 9 hours

Spring

As Autumn, Spring is another best time for doing Everest Base Camp Trek. The conditions in Spring are more or less similar to in Autumn. From March until May, you’ll get conditions like warm and sunny days to trek, clean and unobstructed mountains to look at, and more. Likewise, the weather is too stable through this season, with no odds at all. Above all the facts, this season is not as crowded as Autumn. Therefore, for those who love less overcrowded trails, this can be the right time.

Plus, this season is a time when flowers start blooming. This means the landscapes and terrain look more beautiful in this season than usual. It will be another critical reason that you should pick this season. If you think of doing 10 days Everest Base Camp Trekking this season, you’ll enjoy it thoroughly.

The weather of the Everest Region in Spring is as follows:

Places: Lukla, Namche, and Tengboche
Elevation(m) : 3,000 m to 4,000 m
Max Temperature(°C) : 17°C
Min Temperature(°C): 2°C
Sunny hours: 9 hours

Places: Dingboche, EBC, and Kala Patthar
Elevation(m) :4,000 m to 5,500 m
Max Temperature(°C) : 10°C
Min Temperature(°C): -2°C
Sunny hours: 9 hours
