How Difficult is it to do Everest Base Camp Trekking 10 Days?

Well, the straight answer to this question would be, “it is challenging.” When you are doing a long trek in a shorter duration, then it becomes difficult eventually. The Everest Base Camp Trekking 10 days major difficulties are as below:

Altitude

First thing first, the main challenge on Short Everest Base Camp Trek will be altitudes. The trek achieves new and high altitudes daily and drastically. For example, you will start the trek from 2,860 m(Lukla), and the next day you will be at a height of 3,440 m(Namche). So these changes in altitudes will happen every day, and you’ll not spend any day as a rest or acclimatization day in this short Everest Base Camp Trek.

Noticeably, the highest point of the trek is Kala Patthar(5,500 m+). It will be a trek that starts from 2,860 m to 5,500 m and then back to 2,860 m Clearly, over 10 days, you will handle some problems to acclimate to the altitudes. A high-altitude trek without acclimatization days is always difficult to do. Through the process, you always have odds of getting found by mountain sickness.

Distance

130 KM is the total distance of Everest Base Camp Trek. You’ll trek the distance in just 10 days. That is around 10 KM of distance per day. To walk 10 KM on a hilly trail daily is clearly a difficult one. You’ll require to be consistently active on the trail for around 6 to 7 hours on the trek. These numbers can be okay for highly skilled trekkers. To others, it is just a difficult dream to dare.

Trail Nature

Looking at the trail structure of Everest Base Camp Trekking, it is pretty mixed up. There are steep ups and rolling downs at various parts of the trail. You have to traverse through this mixed trail. As you gain heights, the trail then turns rough due to the glacier moraines. This sort of trail can never be easy for any sort of trekkers. It is just that the trained trekkers are very used to them, and the rest do not.

Extreme Weather

The weather does not bother you much if you are trekking in Autumn and Spring. But, if you are picking times like Monsoon and Winter, you have to face serious circumstances. These times are not highly suggested for trekking in Nepal, and thus they are known as the low times. As you know, Monsoon is the time of rainfall, and Winter the time of snowfall and extreme cold. The Everest Base Camp Trekking 10 Days is even more difficult if you are traveling at these off-seasons’. You have to deal with problems like slippery trails, Snowfall, rainfall, landslides, and more.

Detailed Itinerary of Everest Base Camp Trekking 10 Days

Day 01: Flight from Kathmandu to Lukla and Trek to Phakding from Lukla

Flight Duration: 40 minutes

Trek Duration: 3 hours

Trek Distance: 6.2 KM

Highest Altitude: 2,850 m

The first day of the Short Everest Base Camp Trek starts with a breathtaking mountain flight to Lukla, the place where your trek commences. It will take not more than 40m to reach Lukla. Once you arrive in Lukla, you will begin to get set and ready for the trek.

As you leave Lukla behind, you will be already en route to Everest Base Camp. Phakding will be waiting ahead to welcome you for the night stay. It will be a short trekking day of 3 hours from Lukla to Phakding. Along the trail, you’ll see the Dudh Koshi River. Following the river, you’ll reach Phakding(2,650 m), the first stop of almost all Everest region treks. Overnight in Phakding.

Day 02: Trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar

Trek Duration: 6 hours

Trek Distance: 7.4 KM

Highest Altitude: 3,440 m

With the early rays of the morning, you’ll join the trail to move ahead. As you get past Phakding, the Dudh Koshi River will guide you ahead. You’ll cross several suspension bridges today to get across the river. The serpentine trail will then lead to the woods of Sagarmatha National Park. You’ll enjoy the walk pretty much as you’ll see lush greenery and a peaceful environment.

Today, the trail will be moderately steeper than the first day. But the views of the mountains will keep you moving. Take rests and enjoy the view whenever you feel tired. Moving along the trail, you’ll see Namche Bazaar coming. Namche Bazaar(3,440 m) is a nice-looking Himalayan Town. The place is the trade hub of the Everest region. The town has almost all things from shopping to good restaurants. A comfortable overnight in Namche.

Day 03: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Tengboche

Trek Duration: 5 hours

Trek Distance: 9.2 KM

Highest Altitude: 3,855 m

From Namche Bazaar, you’ll now turn towards Tengboche. You’ll start the day with an uphill trek that takes you out of Namche Bazaar. At the end of every ascend, you’ll come across the striking visions of Lhotse, Everest, Ama Dablam, and more. This is when you’ll feel the trek is not just a trek but something else. You’ll see the traditional villages while you move ahead.

After trekking for a whole day through woods, hills, and riverbeds, you’ll reach Tengboche before nightfall. Tengboche, a small but picturesque village in the Khumbu region. The Tengboche Monastery is the best part of this village. And you can gaze at the snow-clad mountains from this village. Your beautiful evening will be around the monastery before you finally take a rest in Tenboche’s teahouse.

Day 04: Trek from Tengboche to Dingboche

Trek Duration: 6 hours

Trek Distance: 12 KM

Highest Altitude: 4,360 m

You will wake up to the pleasing sounds of morning prayers from Tengboche Monastery. Receiving blessings from the monastery and having breakfast, you’ll forbid a goodbye to Tengboche to join the trail again. The trek will start with a gradual descent through a forest full of Rhododendron to Debuche village. You will see houses made of scattered stones, Buddhist Chortens, and long Mani walls in the village.

Crossing the Imja Khola and passing by several scenic villages, you’ll find your way to Dingboche. You’ll now be very close to the mountains, and the views of them get even clear. Keeping your body moving, you’ll reach Dingboche(4,360 m), a village by the mountains and hills. Ama Dablam looks so surreal from Dingboche. You’ll take a much-deserved rest at Dingboche by looking at Ama Dablam Peak. Overnight in Dingboche.

Day 05: Trek from Dingboche to Lobuche

Trek Duration: 5 hours

Trek Distance: 8.5 KM

Highest Altitude: 4,930 m

Your beautiful morning at Dingboche will end as it becomes time to leave it. It is always better to start the trek early; you’ll get extra time to trek slowly by enjoying the scenario. From Dingboche, you will head in the direction of mountains to Lobuche. The day will be pretty scenic as you will get to see the mountains all the time. Plus, the landscapes will also keep you busy throughout the day.

Now the trail is a bit rough as you move closer and closer to the Everest Base Camp. You’ll ascend the Khumbu Glacier’s moraine to reach Lobuche. There on the way, you’ll come across the memorial sites where you’ll find many memorial stones of the lost souls in the Everest Climb. Trek for some more time, and you’ll reach Lobuche, a village that lies just below Mt Lobuche. Overnight in Lobuche.

Day 06: Trek from Lobuche to Everest Base Camp and return to Gorak Shep

Trek Duration: 6 to 8 hours

Trek Distance: 15 KM

Highest Altitude: 5,364 m

Now comes the most important day of Everest Base Camp Trekking 10 Days. It is important because you’ll ascend Everest Base Camp today. Take a tight breakfast as you have a lot of distance to walk. The trail is not easy as before, plus the oxygen level is shallow around 5,000 m altitude. From Lobuche, you’ll approach Everest Base Camp via the lateral moraine of the world’s highest glacier, Khumbu Glacier.

As you will be walking on the moraine part, the trail will be rough and difficult to walk upon. Crossing several steep parts, you’ll reach Gorak Shep. And after a short rest there, you’ll head out for moving closer to the base camp. Once you reach Everest Base Camp(5,364 m), the level of excitement will burst out as you see Mt Everest just in front of you. Taking this moment enough into the photos, you’ll fall back to Gorak Shep for night rest. Overnight in Gorak Shep.

Day 07: Early morning Hike to Kala Patthar and trek to Pheriche

Trek Duration: 6 to 7 hours

Trek Distance: 14.3 KM

Highest Altitude: 5,555 m

As you have achieved Everest Base Camp already, now you will do a morning hike to Kala Patthar before ascending back. Kala Patthar is the best place to look at Mt Everest; you can get clear views of it from here. For that reason, you’ll do an ascend to Kala Patthar(5,555 m) from Gorak Shep. It can take around 2 hours to ascend Kala Patthar from Gorak Shep. If possible, do the hike before sunrise because the sun rising looks so surreal from Kala Patthar.

After enjoying the mountains sufficiently, you will then start descending back to Gorak Shep. From there, you’ll leave for Pheriche village(4,250 m), where you’ll spend the night. It will be easy peasy descending to Pheriche but make sure you watch the slippery stones. Overnight in Pheriche.

Day 08: Trek from Pheriche to Namche Bazaar

Trek Duration: 6 to 7 hours

Trek Distance: 14.3 KM

Highest Altitude: 4,250 m

From Pheriche(4,250 m), it is time to trek back to Namche Bazaar(3,440 m). The trek will be mostly downhill and easy as you will be descending this time. The same places and views will come along for the second time, don’t forget to explore. Moving through Rhododendron forest and crossing the Dudh Koshi River via suspension bridges, you’ll be back at Namche Bazaar. While you descend, do not forget to look back at the mountains, saying bye to you, overnight in Namche Bazaar.

Day 09: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Lukla

Trek Duration: 6 to 7 hours

Trek Distance: 13.5 KM

Highest Altitude: 3,440 m

After spending another night in Namche Bazaar, you’ll leave the place to trace back to Lukla. To do that, you’ll join the riverbed of Dudh Koshi River. Crossing those same prayer flags decorated suspension bridges and traversing through the vegetation of the national park, you’ll finally step in Lukla. As this will be the last trekking day of Everest Base Camp Trekking 10 Days, explore and enjoy as much as you can. Overnight in Lukla.

Day 10: Fly back to Kathmandu

Flight Duration: 6 hours

Here arrives the time when you’ll leave the Everest Region by completing the Everest Base Camp Trek. You’ll join the 40 minutes flight to Kathmandu. Through the moment, you’ll recall all of the adventures and memories from the 10 days trek. Once you reach Kathmandu, you will get back to your hotel for a rest and refreshment. So this is how the 10 Days Everest adventure will end.

Packing list for 10 Days Everest Base Camp Trekking

To decide things to pack for Everest Base Camp Trek can be confusing. And not having packed the necessary items will cause problems later during the trek. Therefore, it is an important decision to pack everything wisely.

Well, the packing list for Everest Base Camp Trek is respective to each season. If you are trekking in either Autumn or Spring, the list we will present below will be enough for the trek.

Footwear

Additional Accessories

Toiletries and Medication

title: Annapurna Base Camp 6 Days Itinerary
excerpt: Annapurna Base Camp is widely known as one of the best trekking destinations in the world. This outstanding trek passes through the Himalayan foothills of the Annapurna region. In sum, the Annapurna…
html:
Annapurna Base Camp is widely known as one of the best trekking destinations in the world. This outstanding trek passes through the Himalayan foothills of the Annapurna region. In sum, the Annapurna Base Camp trek 6 days is a short duration trek that provides you with an incredible exploration opportunity of the region.

This adventure is ideal for those who want a quick trekking adventure or have a short time on their schedule. The short itinerary starts and ends in Pokhara. Similarly, this high altitude trek is challenging as it is compact and has fewer days for acclimatization. Hence, you should rest well after each trekking day and get charged for the next adventure.

Moreover, first-time beginner trekkers find this trek challenging as it passes through the remote parts of the country. Therefore, you should have a basic level of fitness and stamina to complete this exciting trek in the Annapurna region. Proper training before the start of the trek is essential.

Furthermore, this Annapurna Base Camp trek 6 days passes through the magnificent landscapes of Annapurna Sanctuary. Also, there are forested trails of rhododendron trees, Himalayan rivers, and serene waterfalls. There is also an opportunity to go on a cultural exploration of ethnic Tamang and Gurung communities.

Additionally, the breathtaking views of snow-capped mountains including Mt. Annapurna, Dhaulagiri, Mardi Himal, Gangapurna, Machhapuchhre, and others are spellbinding. Trekkers require ACAP (Annapurna Conservation Area Project Permit) and TIMS (Trekkers Information Management System) for this trek.

Annapurna Base Camp 6 days trek is available at a reasonable cost. Read on to know more about the trek and other related information in detail. Book your trip now!

Significant Highlights of the Trip

  • Breathtaking views of the snow-capped mountains of the Annapurna region
  • Gorgeous Sunrise overlooking the snow-capped mountains
  • A cultural exploration of the ancient ethnic settlements of Gurung and Tamang community
  • Incredible hospitality of local people and their delicious food
  • Passing through the scenic landscapes of the Annapurna sanctuary
  • Dipping in Jhinu Danda hot water springs
  • Spotting and exploring the rare and endangered wildlife of the Annapurna region

About the Route

In particular, we will start our journey with the scenic drive from Pokhara to Nayapul. This two-hour drive passes to the scenic settlements in remote landscapes. From Nayapul, we start our trekking journey as we trek to Jhinu Danda. Thereafter, from Jhinu Danda, we pass through a dense bamboo forest to arrive at the settlement of Bamboo.

Furthermore, from bamboo, we continue our journey through a bamboo forest to arrive at Deurali. Likewise, as we move along the trail the vegetation starts to decline. Also, the route starts to get challenging as there are tough and rugged terrains. From Deurali, we will trek to our ultimate destination of Annapurna base camp via Machhapuchhre base camp.

Furthermore, the view of the entire range of mountains will make you fall in love with the place. Similarly, you can take as many pictures as you like and explore around the base camp area. You will spend the night at the ABC and then return to Sinuwa Danda the next day. Finally, we will then trek back to Nayapul and drive back to Pokhara as our trek comes to an end.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

When Is The Best Time For Annapurna Base Camp 6 Days Trek?

The best time to Annapurna base camp trek 6 days is Spring and autumn. These are the best peak seasons for trekking and traveling in the country. There are a pleasant climate and moderate temperatures these seasons.

Autumn (September-November)

September to November is the post-monsoon season in Nepal. There are dry weather conditions with minimum rainfall and warm temperatures. The breathtaking views of the snow-capped mountains in clear blue skies highlight trekking in autumn. Autumn is also the month for many festivals in the country including Dashain, Tihar, and Holi. You will have a great time trekking the beautiful Annapurna region in autumn.

Spring (March-May)

March to May is a beautiful time to trek in the Annapurna region. Wildflowers like rhododendron bloom all over the hills making the journey colorful and pleasant. There is less precipitation in Spring with stable climate and weather conditions. You can observe the snow-capped mountains in all their glory on a clear sky.

Moreover, you can take the offseason treks in the winter and monsoon as well. These treks are quite challenging as there are heavy rainfalls and snowfalls. The extremely cold trails in the winters with temperatures below zero degrees celsius.

Moreover, there are slippery trails with the risk of avalanches and landslides in the monsoon. However with proper packing in preparation you can take this Annapurna base camp 6 days trek any time of the year.

How Difficult Is The Annapurna Base Camp 6 Days Trek?

The Annapurna Base Camp trek 6 days is a moderately challenging Trek. Difficulties of the trek include altitude sickness. At high altitude conditions, there is less amount of oxygen in the air and even less air pressure. Hence, these factors make breathing difficult and altitude sickness quite common.

Proper acclimatization and regular hydration is the key to tackle altitude sickness in high altitude conditions. You can rest until you feel better and descend to a lower altitude if necessary. You might also have to abandon the trip if the symptom persists. Another important thing is that you should trek at a gradual pace.

Trekkers will have to cover approximately 115 kilometers in 6 days. For this, you will need to trek for around 6 to 7 hours daily which makes the trek quite taxing. Thus, trekkers should have incredible stamina and a basic level of fitness to complete the trek with ease.

Besides that, you should have a good training routine at least two weeks before the start of the trek. This exciting trek in the Annapurna region also goes up and down the route and stony paths which can turn out to be quite difficult for first-time trekkers. Overall, this Annapurna Base Camp Trek 6 days moderately challenging.

Food And Accommodation During The Annapurna Base Camp 6 Days Trek

The food and Accommodation facilities are quite basic along the trails of the Annapurna base camp. You will stay in tea houses and lodges that provide standard facilities like beds, clean sheets, a mattress, and a warm blanket. Toilets are generally squat style located out of the main house and you have to carry your toiletries.

You will get “Dal Bhat” which is the traditional Nepalese dish twice a day. For breakfast, you will get porridge, bread toast, and boiled eggs. Some houses also provide Chinese and continental cuisine like noodles, momo, burgers, bread, pasta, and others. Tea, coffee, Rhododendron tea, lemon tea, mint tea, garlic soup, and other hot beverages are quite common along the trails.

You should avoid alcoholic beverages as it can cause dehydration which can lead to altitude sickness. Besides that, you can carry snacks like snickers, chocolate bars, granola bars, protein bars, and others along the trail to munch on during the trek.

Why To Go For Annapurna Base Camp 6 Days Trek?

Scenic mountain vista

Annapurna region is one of the most beautiful trekking destinations in the world. There are various viewpoints along the trail that provide incredible mountain vista. You can observe the snow-capped mountains of the Annapurna mountain range including Mt. Annapurna I, Machhapuchhre, Annapurna South, and others along the trail.

Cultural diversity

Cultural diversity is another incredible aspect of this Annapurna base camp trek 6 days. You will pass through cultural settlements of Gurung, Magar, and Tamang community. There are architectural settlements and religious landmarks in the region. You can also observe local people involved in traditional activities like farming and animal rearing.

Short duration

The short duration of this trek is another great aspect of this trek. This short duration trek is ideal for those individuals who would like to trek in a short amount of time and have a compact schedule. You can go on a completely natural and cultural exploration in just 6 days.

Natural diversity

The natural diversity of the Annapurna region makes trekkers flock to this beautiful region. There are incredibly rare and endangered flora and fauna that you can observe along trails. This trek also passes through the landscapes of Annapurna sanctuary that works in the conservation of local wildlife and plants.

Detailed Itinerary – Annapurna Base Camp 6 Days Trek

Day 01: Drive from Pokhara to Nayapul and Trek to Jhinu Danda

Maximum altitude: 1,780 m

Drive duration: 1 hour 30 minutes

Trekking duration: 5 hours

Annapurna Base Camp Trek 6 days starts with a scenic drive from Pokhara to Nayapul. We will arrive at Nayapul after driving for around 2 hours. The trail passes through scenic settlements of the highway and hilly landscapes.

The beautiful views of snow-capped mountains along the journey will enchant you before arriving at your destination of Nayapul. Nayapul is the starting point of our journey. We will trek through the beautiful Annapurna region. We will pass through the settlements of Birethanti, Kyumi, Siwai, along the forested trails before arriving at Jhinu.

You can observe ancient settlements of various ethnic communities including Gurungs, Magars, Tamangs, and others. We will arrive at the destination of Jhinu Danda after trekking for around 5 hours. Jhinu danda hot spring is a famous site where you can relax and take a hot bath. We will explore the region and spend the night at a teahouse in Jhinu Danda.

Day 02: Trek from Jhinu Danda to Bamboo

Maximum altitude: 2,310 m (Bamboo)

Trekking duration: 6 hours

Early morning breakfast later we will start our journey from Jhinu Danda towards Bamboo. There are stone trails that make the trekking journey quite challenging. You will pass through scenic waterfalls and beautiful villages and bamboo forests along the journey.

There are large settlements of Sinuwa and Choomrong between Jhinu Danda and Bamboo. In these villages, you can find local people busy in their daily activities like farming and animal rearing, and other agricultural activities. You can observe the traditional attire along with their rural lifestyle.

Furthermore, the unique culture and incredible hospitality will enchant you. There are beautiful bamboo forests and natural trails in this peaceful journey. After a trek of around five hours, we will arrive at bamboo where you can find many lodges and tea houses. We will rest in the evening and spend the night at a teahouse in Bamboo.

Day 03: Trek from Bamboo to Deurali

Maximum Altitude: 3,230 m (Deurali)

Trekking duration: 4 to 5 hours

We will start our journey from Bamboo to Deurali early in the morning after having breakfast. Our trail passes through a dense bamboo forest. You can feel certain dampness and coolness along the trail. We will then ascend green hills as the forest gets sparse and opens up gradually. After arriving at Himalaya, we can observe a glacial river down below.

The trail gets challenging as there get rugged and tough terrains. We will continue our journey from Himalaya to Hinku cave along a difficult trail that climbs steeply through a forest Hill. There is another bamboo forest that is much dryer on our way to Hinku Cave. There is a river that you need to cross on a suspended bridge.

After the final ascent along a scenic and peaceful route, we will arrive at Deurali. You can find the vegetation around the region depleting as we move up in the high altitude region. There are various small Rocky clips from where you can observe serene waterfalls.

This journey takes around 5 to 6 hours. Deurali is a beautiful settlement in the Annapurna region where you can find many tea houses and lodges for trekkers. We rest in the evening and spend the night at a teahouse in Deurali.

Day 04: Trek from Deurali to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) via Machhapuchhre Base Camp

Maximum Altitude: 4,130 m (ABC)

Trekking duration: 5 to 6 hours

After having early morning breakfast we will start our journey from Deurali to Annapurna base camp which is our ultimate destination. The uphill climb on tough landscapes will take you past the avalanche site. The inspiring 360-degree views of snow-capped mountains is one of the highlights of our journey.

Trekkers need to be careful in higher altitudes rocky and slippery terrain. We will first arrive at Machhapuchhre Base Camp after working for a few hours. We will rest and explore around the base camp. Hence, this will help you with acclimatization as you will need to spend the night at ABC.

In addition, trekkers can get breathtaking views of the Annapurna range of mountains including Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre Himal, Annapurna III, Mt. Hiunchuli, Gangapurna, Annapurna I, Gandharvachuli, and others. Also, we will further explore the area and take incredible pictures. After that, we will continue our journey to the famous ABC.

Finally, we will arrive at ABC after walking for around 2 hours from MBC. You can also observe various snow-clad mountain peaks from ABC. In fact, these mountain peaks include Annapurna III, Mardi Himal, Machhapuchhre, Mt. Gangapurna, Singu Chuli, Khangsar Kang, Hiunchuli, Annapurna South, Annapurna I, and others.

Day 05: Trek from Annapurna Base Camp to Sinuwa Danda

We will spend the night at camp in ABC observing the beautiful night sky. Also, we will observe a beautiful sunrise early in the morning looking at the snow-clad mountain peaks of the Annapurna region. Similarly, the base camp provides us with incredible views of the golden sun rays falling upon glistening to snowy mountain peaks.

The breathtaking views of the entire Annapurna range of mountains are the highlight of the place. Besides, after taking some stunning pictures while exploring around the basecamp area, we trek back to Sinuwa. Along the way back, we can observe a different perspective of the mountains along the same trail.

Furthermore, we will pass through the settlements of the Machhapuchhre Base Camp, Himalaya, Dobhan, Deurali, and Bamboo to arrive at Sinuwa. You can trek comfortably as the route is mostly descending and less challenging. Besides, you can also go on a cultural exploration of the local community and learn about the lifestyle. Thereafter, we will arrive at Sinuwa after 5 to 6 hours where we will rest and spend the night.

Day 06: Trek from Sinuwa Danda to New Bridge and Drive to Pokhara

Will have an early morning breakfast in the cinema before continuing the trek back to Nayapul. Besides, we will pass through the forest trails back to the Chhomrong village. From Chhomrong village, you can either take the right to Ghandruk or left towards Jhinu Danda.

It will take you along the same path that you took earlier to arrive at Jhinu Danda. Chhomrong to Ghandruk pass through Kimche and finally meet Siwal at the old trail. In fact, this is a new route and will provide you with a new perspective of the Annapurna region.

From Siwal, we pass Birethanti along the bamboo forest to arrive at Nayapul. Thereafter, the Annapurna base camp 6 days trek comes to an end in a pool as we take a scenic bus drive to the lake city of Pokhara. Finally, you can rest in the hotel or explore around the city and its sightseeing points and spend the night at a hotel in Pokhara.

Factors To Consider For The Trek

Acclimatization and hydration

Acclimatization and hydration are essential as they help you tackle altitude sickness which is one of the major difficulties along the trail. Moreover, trekkers must not hike more than 600 m in altitude gain and sleep at a lower point than the maximum point along the trail.

In short, drinking water is also quite essential as dehydration is the primary cause of altitude sickness. Likewise, you can carry water purifying tablets so that you can fill water at teahouses and purify it to drink along the trail.

Guides and porters

Guides are essential parts of your trekking journey. A local professional guide will provide you with local insights along with navigation along the trail. Porters help you carry luggage along the trail. However, you can also get a porter-guide that will provide you services of both porters and guides at a lesser cost.

Time of trek

Generally, weather conditions are another aspect that you should consider before starting a trek. Spring and autumn are the best time to trek in the Annapurna region. Also, you can trek in stable weather conditions and mild temperatures. Besides that, you can also trek in the off-seasons with proper packing and preparation.

Training

Having a proper training regime is essential so that you can trek the rugged landscapes of the region. Overall, trekkers should start their training regime for two months or at least two weeks before starting this trek.

There are various activities like hiking, jogging, swimming, cycling, and other cardiovascular activities that you can perform. Besides, you should focus on your physical stamina and mental stability. In conclusion, a basic level of fitness will help you to tackle any challenges along the trail.

Travel insurance

Travel insurance is necessary as well during high altitude Annapurna base camp trek 6 days. In addition, there are various challenges along the trail that increase the risk of avalanches and landslides along trails. Similarly, these travel insurance will provide you coverage from theft, accidents, medical emergencies, flight cancellations, helicopter evacuation, and others. Hence, it is essential to have travel insurance along the trail.

Some Essential Tips For Trek

  • You should pack according to season and keep only those items that are necessary.
  • You should carry cash in Nepali Rupees. Also, be aware of pickpockets and divide your money and keep your money in separate pockets.
  • Always walk at a gradual pace and rest well.
  • Hire professional guides and porters along trails.
  • Always check weather conditions before starting on this trek.
  • Regular acclimatization is essential to complete this trek.
  • Always manage your wastage along the trail

Packing List For Annapurna Base Camp 6 Days Trek

  • Trekking shirts

Important documents

Annapurna Base Camp Trek 6 days is a beautiful trek in the Annapurna region. Also, trekkers can take this outstanding adventure if they want to explore nature in a short amount of time. title: Packing List for Everest Base Camp
excerpt: Wondering what are the essentials to be included on your Packing List for Everest Base Camp Trek? This article is gonna be of some help to you. Packing is the last thing a wanderer has to do before…
html:
Wondering what are the essentials to be included on your Packing List for Everest Base Camp Trek? This article is gonna be of some help to you.

Packing is the last thing a wanderer has to do before heading out to the destination. Last but not least, packing is one of the things to look at while traveling. Also, it is even more important when you are doing Everest Base Camp Trek.

In particular, the Packing List for Everest Base Camp Trek has to be on your sight. Besides, the trek is a time-taking journey and you need various things on your back to endure this trek. Therefore, you’ll need good clothes for the body, a sturdy shoe for your feet, a good pair of gloves for your hand, and so on.

Especially, not having the required items in your Everest Base Camp Trek’s backpack can make you see problems. Besides, if your wish is not to experience any of the problems, you have to pack wisely for the trek. Yet, the packing process for the trek may seem very easy but in the real world, it is too confusing. Overall, it is even difficult when you are not so much used to Himalayan Trekking.

Furthermore, the temperature is cold up there, so are the conditions: different and unpredictable. In fact, you’ll require to use some of those things on the trek that you have never seen also. Saying it yet again, the packing list for Everest Base Camp has to be suitable enough to help you do this adventurous trek.

You probably have come to the best place for the guide on the packing list for Everest Base Camp Trek. Down further, we are going to inform you about all the things you’ll require for the trek. Overall, a complete backpacking list for the trek is displayed. Likewise, you’ll also read things to consider while packing for Everest Base Camp Trek and some of the important Everest Base Camp Trek guides like Itinerary, the best time for the trek, and difficulties of the trek.

This guide will help you to figure out what items to pack and why you need them for the trek.

A Complete Packing List for Everest Base Camp Trek

Here is a complete list of the things that you surely require and may require in Everest Base Camp Trek. However, you can pack something that is not on the list also but that does not mean you can just pack everything. Be wise while filling the limited space backpack.

Clothing

Generally, your body will be in extreme temperature conditions on the trek. That is why you have to start packing by selecting good clothing. Moreover, this includes everything you will wear to keep your body warm and cozy. Here, the list goes as below:

  • Inner Layer Thermals.
  • Middle Layer(Fleece).
  • Water/Windproof jacket.
  • Down Jacket.
  • Fleece Pants.
  • Trekking Trousers.
  • Hiking Shirts.
  • Breathable Underwears.
  • Buff(especially for neck).
  • Trekking socks(Thick Woolen).
  • Gloves
  • Woolen Cap.
  • Sun Hat(for sunny hours)

Footwear

In sum, Everest Base Camp Trek is all about walking so you obviously need something good for your feet. Similarly, this list highlights all of the footwear you must pack for the trek.

  • Trekking Boots.
  • Gaiters(For Snowy season only).
  • Sandals/Flip Flops(For non-trekking hours).

Toiletries

This heading enlists all of the toiletries things to carry for the trek. Most of the trekkers get confused when it is about packing toiletries for the trek. So here is the list.

  • Sunscreen(SPF 30-50).
  • Lip Balm.
  • Toilet Paper(Not more than 2 rolls).
  • Toothbrush.
  • Toothpaste.
  • Shower Gel.
  • Shampoo
  • Quick Drying Towel.
  • Hand Towel.
  • Moisturizing Cream and Face Wash.
  • Hand sanitizer.
  • Sanitary Napkins(For Women).
  • Plastic Bags(For dirt collection)

Medication

Medication packing is a must for solo travelers. Generally, if you go with a trekking expedition team like us, Base Camp Adventure, you do not need to pack any medics. Our guide takes care of most of the medical necessities. In fact, it is not that you have to use medics but they all are for emergencies. Overall,  the complete list of medication is as below:

  • Povidone-Iodine Cream(1 tube).
  • Cotton roll.
  • Dressing Gauze.
  • Bandage
  • Paracetamol(for general headaches).
  • Ibuprofen
  • Decongestant(For congestion).
  • Antiemetic
  • Diamox
  • Water Purification Tablet.
  • Loperamide

(Note: If you are using prescription medicines, pack sufficient of them from your country only. You cannot get everything anywhere in Nepal.)

Electronics and Gadgets

In this age of electronics, you surely cannot move without having electronics in your pockets. Below is the list that denotes all of the electronic requirements for the trek:

  • Mobile Phone and its charger.
  • Universal socket adapter.
  • Camera with extra batteries.
  • Power Bank.
  • Binoculars.
  • Bluetooth speaker.

Others

  • Sunglasses(UV protected).
  • Trekking poles.
  • Raincoat(For the rainy season)
  • Diary and pen.
  • Playing cards.
  • Day backpack.
  • Sleeping bag.
  • Head Torch.
  • Dry fruits and snacks.

Necessary Documents

  • A valid Passport.
  • Enough cash.
  • Credit Card.
  • Tickets
  • Passport Sized Photos.
  • Travel Insurance Documents.

Things to Consider while packing for Everest Base Camp Trek

This part of the article is going to be very helpful for you while packing for the EBC Trek. In sum, that is because we are going to list down some of the things to consider while filling your backpack for the trek. Therefore, go through all of them and be on the safer side.

Pack Timely

In particular, time is a very important thing and more important while packing. Therefore, arrange some free and enough time for packing. Do not ever pack rashly. That way, you’re going to either miss out on something or may pack unnecessary things. Instead, get yourself a certain time for packing. Besides, our tip for you is that, start packing some days prior to the departure date. By doing this, you will have enough time to figure out your packing.

Pack wisely

Do your packing for the trek wisely taking all of the things into consideration. Don’t go for everything that is in your mind. Check whether the things you are packing are suitable or necessary or not for the trek. In addition, this way you will save some valuable space in your backpack. And you can also have a light and easy backpack to carry.

Go for thick but light clothes

Everest Base Camp Trek sees a chilly temperature no matter which season you trek in. But you don’t need heavy clothes to wear, the thick and light clothes can do good for the trek. Therefore, prefer thick but light clothes over heavy and space-consuming clothes.

Know everything about the trek

Knowing what it is like to do Everest Base Camp Trek will help you pick the right items for the trek. Here, check info like how long is the trek, difficulty of the trek, detailed itinerary, accommodation, and other facilities in the trek. Similarly, if you have known every corner of the trek then you can do suitable packing for the trek easily. Here, we mentioned most of the trek info down below, don’t forget to check those.

Know the season you are traveling in

This is the most important thing to look at, the season you are traveling in. Out of Winter, Monsoon, Spring, and Autumn, which season you are picking for the trek. As you may know, the conditions are different in each season. Find the right time and know about the stats of temperature and conditions and then start packing accordingly. Likewise, if you see, the packing for the Winter season is not the same for seasons like Spring and Autumn.

Talk with the experienced ones

If you have some experienced Everest Base Camp Trekkers in your reach then reach them. Besides, they can tell you the dos and don’ts for packing lists for the trek. It is a blessing to have someone like that in your circle.

Buying or Hiring the gear

Generally, you will have options to buy or hire the basic trekking gear in Nepal. However, you cannot rent everything, just a few of the gears like a Sleeping bag, hiking boots, and down jackets. Also, the gears are charged around USD 1 per day and they are of good quality, clean and wearable. Otherwise, you always have a choice to buy gears yourself. Besides, there are shops around Kathmandu and Namche Bazaar selling a variety of trekking gears.

Hire a Porter

This can be the most helpful thing if you hate carrying loads on your back. Hiring a porter for carrying your loaded backpack is highly suggested for the trek like Everest Base Camp Trek. Also, the trek is long and you have to walk for a long distance. If your bag is too heavy to carry then it can slow your speed. Thus, in such situations, you can hire a porter for the whole trek.

The porters in EBC trek generally charge around USD 16 to 20 per day. That cost will cover all of the salaries and other costs of a porter. Also, if you have already thought of hiring a porter for yourself then you can pack freely. Moreover, you don’t have to make the backpack light now, you’ll get plenty of porter services. Overall, you just have to pay them their salary, they are so used to carrying loads in the Himalayas.

Outlined Itinerary for Everest Base Camp Trek

The only reason to mention the outlined itinerary of the trek here is to make you aware of the trekking plan. It takes around 13 to 16 days to do Everest Base Camp Trek in a normal manner. However, there are other shorter and longer itineraries designed for all ranges of trekkers. The most popular one is the 15 days long Everest Base Camp Trekking from Base Camp Adventure Team which goes as below:

Day 01: Arrival in Kathmandu and Hotel Transfer.

Overnight in: Kathmandu’s hotel.

Day 02: Fly to Lukla from Kathmandu and then trek from Lukla to Phakding.

Flight Duration: 40 minutes.

Trek Duration: 4 to 5 hours.

Altitude Gain: Lukla(2,845 m), Phakding(2,610 m)

Overnight in: Phakding’s Teahouse.

Day 03: Trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar.

Trek Duration: 6 to 7 hours.

Altitude Gain: Namche Bazaar(3,450 m)

Overnight in: Namche Bazaar’s Tea House.

Day 04: Acclimatization Day in Namche Bazaar.

Overnight in: Namche Bazaar’s Tea House.

Day 05: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Tengboche.

Trek Duration: 5 to 6 hours.

Altitude Gain: Tengboche(3,865 m).

Overnight in: Tengboche’s Teahouse.

Day 06: Trek from Tengboche to Dingboche.

Trek Duration: 5 to 6 hours.

Altitude Gain: Dingboche(4,410 m).

Overnight in: Dingboche’s Teahouse.

Day 07: Acclimatization Day in Dingboche.

Overnight in: Dingboche’s Teahouse.

Day 08: Trek from Dingboche to Lobuche.

Trek Duration: 5 to 6 hours.

Altitude Gain: Lobuche(4,940 m).

Overnight in: Lobuche’s Teahouse.

Day 09: Trek from Lobuche to Everest Base Camp and return to Gorak Shep.

Trek Duration: 6 to 7 hours.

Altitude Gain: Everest Base Camp(5,364 m), Gorak Shep(5,140 m)

Overnight in: Gorak Shep’s Teahouse.

Day 10: Trek from Gorak Shep to Kala Patthar and return to Pheriche.

Trek Duration: 6 to 7 hours.

Altitude Gain: Kala Patthar(5,545 m), Pheriche(4,243 m).

Overnight in: Pheriche’s Teahouse.

Day 11: Trek from Pheriche to Namche Bazaar

Trek Duration: 7 to 8 hours.

Altitude Loss: Namche Bazaar(3,450 m)

Overnight in: Namche Bazaar’s Teahouse/lodge.

Day 12: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Lukla.

Trek Duration: 6 to 8 hours.

Altitude Loss: Lukla(2,860 m)

Overnight in: Lukla’s Teahouse.

Day 13: Fly back to Kathmandu from Lukla.

Flight Duration: 40 minutes.

Altitude Loss: Kathmandu(1,400 m)

Overnight in: Kathmandu’s hotel.

Day 14: Departure from Kathmandu.

After going through the above given outlined itinerary, you certainly have understood somewhat about Everest Base Camp Trek. It is pretty clear now that the trek is a 14 days long plan to explore the Everest region and ultimately Everest Base Camp. This information will help you somehow to prepare the backpack surely.

Best Time for Everest Base Camp Trek

The best time is supposed to be a time that is just perfect for trekking in every means. Such time has to be good weather and temperature-wise especially when you are trekking on one of the challenging trails. If that is the case then there are two such times whom you can call the best times: Autumn and Spring. Trekking during these seasons is very much easy and convenient as compared to the Winter and Monsoon which are also known as the low times for any trek in Nepal.

Now, let’s know-how are the best times and low times like:

Autumn | September to November

From September to November, it is Autumn season in Nepal and Everest region. The season is considered the best time for trekking in Nepal including Everest Base Camp Trek. Therefore, if you travel in this season, you are sure to get clear mountain views, sunny trekking days, and a warm temperature to trek under. Also, the temperature of most of the parts of Nepal in this season is around 15°C to 25°C, which is a pleasant condition to trek amid. In fact, this means you don’t have to pack extra heavy and warm clothes, a few pairs will work nicely. No need for snow gears at all.

The weather chart of the Everest region in Autumn is as below:

Place Altitude Max Temp Min Temp Sunshine
Lukla, Namche Bazaar, Tengboche 3,000 m to 4,000 m 16°C 2°C 9 hours
Dingboche, Everest Base Camp, Kala Patthar 4,000 m to 5,500 m 10°C -7°C 9 hours

Spring | March to May

The season of flowers, Spring, is another right time for Everest Base Camp Trek. Also, the temperature is bearable enough, not too cold and not too warm. With the right kind of clothing, you can do the trek this season. Likewise, you’ll experience mountains clear and nonstop all day long. Plus, the blooming flowers do make the trail more scenic in Spring. There is no chance of overcast nor snowfall throughout Spring. In sum, this means some thick warm clothes can complete the trek, no need for gaiters, and heavy down jackets.

The weather chart of the Everest region in Spring is as below:

Place Altitude Max Temp Min Temp Sunshine
Lukla, Namche Bazaar, Tengboche 3,000 m to 4,000 m 17°C 2°C 9 hours
Dingboche, Everest Base Camp, Kala Patthar 4,000 m to 5,500 m 10°C -2°C 9 hours

Read more: Everest Base Camp Weather

Low times for Everest Base Camp Trekking

Monsoon and Winter are the low times for Everest Base Camp Trek. The times that are very difficult to endure. Not many people pick these times for trekking in Nepal, that is why they are called low times.

However, some people like to dare adventure in Winter and Autumn. Trekking in Nepal is possible in these seasons if you go when the seasons are not at their best, like early or late Winter. But when the seasons are at their top, the conditions become very unfriendly and challenging. Moreover, you have to face the challenges of these seasons and also have to carry extra winter and monsoon gear. Therefore, that ultimately weights your backpack.

Winter | December to February

Winter which runs through December to February is a difficult time to trek. It is very harsh and chilly up in the mountains during this season. You’ll need loads of warm and thick clothes to keep yourself warm.

The weather chart of the Everest region in Winter:

Place Altitude Max Temp Min Temp Sunshine
Lukla, Namche Bazaar, Tengboche 3,000 m to 4,000 m 12°C -5°C 7 hours
Dingboche, Everest Base Camp, Kala Patthar 4,000 m to 5,500 m 8°C -15°C 7 hours

Monsoon| June to August

This is the season of rainfall when mountains are mostly behind the dark clouds. Similarly, rainfall can occur anytime and any longer in these months. In particular, there are high chances of rainfall, snowfall, and landslides in this season, which is why people do not like to trek in it. However, you can trek in the times when Monsoon is not so active. But you need to pack rain gears to avoid possible problems.

The weather chart of the Everest region in Monsoon:

Place Altitude Max Temp Min Temp Sunshine
Lukla, Namche Bazaar, Tengboche 3,000 m to 4,000 m 18°C -2°C 8 hours
Dingboche, Everest Base Camp, Kala Patthar 4,000 m to 5,500 m 10°C -2°C 8 hours

Difficulties of Everest Base Camp Trek

Trekking Distance

Everest Base Camp Trek is a trek of a total of 130KM from Lukla to Lukla. Besides, the distance is supposed to be covered within 14 days. If this sounds impossible to you then you have a thing to worry about. Also, you should be in a good condition to cover the distance in the scheduled time. Otherwise, you are sure to face difficulties on the trek.

Trekking Duration

Every day you will be walking for around 6 to 7 hours in Everest Base Camp Trek. Similarly, on some day even more than that. If you don’t seem like a guy who can walk for such a duration then here is another problem for you. Besides, those 6 to 7 hours are to be walked on a trail which is very steep at some parts. Overall, the trail is demanding and if you cannot give the 6 to 7 hours daily, do not do this trek.

High Altitude

In particular, it is oblivious that you have to reach some height to see the tallest peak of the world. But that height can cause you some problems if you are not so used to such height. Everest Base Camp Trek gains around 500 m daily and the highest point you reach is the 5,545 m(Kala Patthar. Also, this altitude gain always brings the risk of altitude sickness among the trekkers. In fact, if no precautions are taken, the trekker may have to cancel the trek due to sickness.

Trekking With the Backpack on the back

Usually, trekking with a backpack on the back is a difficult thing to do if your backpack is a little too heavy. Also, this will slow your speed down and can also bring mountain sickness closer. Furthermore, the experienced trekkers are so good at this but the novice cannot do this right. Similarly, that is why novice trekkers are not suggested to carry a heavy backpack for the trek. Actually, it is better to switch your load to a porter in challenging treks like this. In fact, you just imagine walking the whole 130 KM with a heavy backpack on your shoulder, how difficult it sounds.

Limited available services

Generally, this trek can be a huge blunder for those who love trekking in developed areas. On the Everest Base Camp trek, you have to compromise with limited services most of the time. Besides, you cannot seek luxury and comfort everywhere you go on the trek.

Read more on: How difficult is Everest Base Camp Trekking?

Here, we reach the end of this article. In short, we believe that this article has turned very helpful for you to provide enough information about the Packing list for Everest Base Camp Trek. Additionally, our motive in this blog is to make you aware of other information than just the Packing list for Everest Base Camp Trek. Therefore, it is why we have added the headings like outlined itinerary, best time, and difficulties along with the full item list for the trek. Moreover, we believe that you have taken more than we expected from this blog.

title: Manaslu Circuit Trek Cost
excerpt: In this article, we are going to discuss the Manaslu Trek Cost and other informational details of the trek. Circumnavigating the eighth-highest peak in the world, Mt. Manaslu(8163 m), the Manaslu…
html:
In this article, we are going to discuss the Manaslu Trek Cost and other informational details of the trek.

Circumnavigating the eighth-highest peak in the world, Mt. Manaslu(8,163 m), the Manaslu Circuit trek beckons all the trekkers and adventurous alike to take the off-the-beaten-path for unfolding the splendor of natural wonders and cultural encounters. You will unravel the winding paths passing through the dense forest and verdant meadows of the Manaslu Conservation Area.

Meandering the quaint villages under the dominance of snow-glistening Ganesh Himal, Shringi Himal, Hiunchuli Peak, and other surrounding peaks, you will discover the cultural and religious essence of the isolated region. Reaching the top of Larke La Pass will offer you a profound sense of accomplishment as you stand beneath the blue sky, contrasting with snow-capped Larke Peak and Cho Peak.

While planning to bask in the adventurous journey, it is necessary to consider the overall cost that will ensure a memorable Manaslu Circuit Trek. However, there are various factors, such as highlights, itinerary, logistics, facilities, and amenities, that will determine the Manaslu Circuit Trek Cost. Usually, the cost for this thrilling journey will range between USD 1200 to USD 1600.

If you are planning to embark on the foothills of the Himalayas with Base Camp Adventure, then it will only cost you USD 1440 for 16 days to make a seamless experience. In case you are not satisfied with the available itinerary packages or you want a different highlights exploration, then we are more than ready to make your custom-tailed Manaslu Circuit Trek.

Why is a Comprehensive Cost Breakdown Necessary for Manaslu Circuit Trek?

People may take trekking as carrying luggage on the back and walking on the trails. However, a lot of meticulous planning must be done beforehand to actually hit the trails. Among such planning, cost management remains at the top. A comprehensive breakdown of the Manaslu circuit trek cost allows you to know about the expense for each overhead. This will ensure smooth and economical budget planning.

Additionally, you can be well-informed about the level of comfort and service that you want throughout the trek. You can choose the accommodations and transportation as per the budget you have decided, whether you want to stay strict on the budget or go overboard.

What Are the Costs Included in the Manaslu Circuit Cost Trek Package?

Our team has decided on specific factors that will be included in the cost. Most of the variables during the trek remain inclusive, but some factors that are out of our hands are not included in the cost.

Manaslu Circuit Permits Cost

Permits are the legal documents that will give you authorization to have access to certain trekking trails. If you embark on the Manaslu Circuit Trek without permits, then it can be considered illegal trekking. You will have to face legal consequences such as fines, deportation, banning from trek, etc. So, acquiring permits is a crucial aspect of your voyage. You will have to acquire two permits. One is a Restricted area permit, while the other is a Manaslu Conservation Area permit.

Restricted Area Permit

The government of Nepal has declared the area between Jagat and Dharapani as a restricted area. Since those areas are close to the border of Tibet and the inflow of tourists shall be maintained in those areas, you will have to acquire a restricted area permit to enter those regions.

The cost of this permit during the autumn season from September to November will be around USD 100 per person/week. If you exceed the duration of one week, then you will have to pay an additional USD 15 for each day you spend in the restricted area. Likewise, from December to August, the cost of the restricted area permit will be USD 75 per person/week. If you have to spend additional days in the restricted areas beyond one week, then you will have to pay an extra USD 10 per day.

Manaslu Conservation Area Permit

Since the Manaslu Conservation Area Project covers the region beyond Philim, your Manaslu conservation area permit will be checked by authorities at different checkpoints, including Philim. The cost for this permit is given below:

For foreign nationals other than SAARC Nationals: Nrs 3000( around USD 30)

For SAARC nationals: Nrs. 1000(around USD 10)

Annapurna Conservation Area Permit

The area from Dharapani to Besisahar falls under the care of the Annapurna Conservation Area Project. Therefore, you will need to acquire an Annapurna Conservation Area Permit to have access to those regions. Like other national park and conservation area permit costs, this permit will also cost you Nrs. 3000 or around USD 30 if you are a foreign national other than SAARC nationals. In case you are SAARC nationals then it will cost you about Nrs. 1000 or about USD 10.

Cost of Meals

It is important to have nutritious meals during your Manaslu Circuit trek. You will have to traverse through the rugged terrains and walk back and forth on the steep uphill and downhill, so it is natural that your body will consume a lot of energy.

In order to replenish your energy for hiking for about 6 to 8 hours, you should eat nutritious foods without skipping meals. Additionally, we recommend you to skip on hard drinks and excessive consumption of tea and coffee since they can obstruct your acclimatization process and will cost you more money.

As the teahouses and lodges on the trekking trails want to accommodate trekkers worldwide, they will offer you an extensive menu, including traditional Nepalese foods, regional foods, Indian and Tibetan cuisines, and even some Western specialties.

Usually, the food in teahouses and lodges is affordable and reasonably priced, so it will cost you, on average, around $8 to $12 per day for meals. However, altitude plays a vital role in determining the price of the meal. The Manaslu region is an isolated and secluded region with no proper infrastructure development. So, difficulty in food transportation can somehow increase the food cost.

The package cost will include all 3 time meals ( Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner) on the trekking trails however, the cost will only include breakfast while you stay at the hotel in Kathmandu. Hence, you will have to be responsible for lunch and dinner during your stay in hotels in Kathmandu. It will cost approximately you around $20 to $30 per meal.

Accommodation Cost

Teahouses and lodges are the common modes of accommodation alongside the trails of Manaslu Circuit Trek. After the long, tiring day of trekking, an overnight stay in the teahouses gives rest to your body and allows your body to reduce all fatigue and exhaustion of the day. Teahouses offer you twin-sharing rooms with well-equipped beds. The beds will be equipped with mattresses, blankets, and pillows. Moreover, they will provide you with common toilets and a bathroom with communal-style dining spaces.

The accommodation cost in the teahouse can range between $7 to $10 per person, but if you do not want to share the room with others, then you can book a room for yourself, which will be comparatively expensive. Likewise, the accommodation cost for staying at the tourist-oriented hotels will cost you approximately $25 to $45 per night. However, the accommodation cost for the whole trek will be included in the package if you opt for our Manaslu Circuit Trek.

Similarly, another mode of accommodation during the trek can be camping. If you want a different experience and to connect with nature more, then this option might be appropriate for you. You can either decide to rent or buy the camping tools such as sleeping bags, tents, etc. However, managing all the camping equipment, along with carrying those things to higher elevations with porters and mules, can be quite expensive.

Cost of the Trekking Staff

Having guides and porters in your Manaslu circuit trek enhances your journey with their expertise and guidance, Since you are going to an unfamiliar place, the guide will navigate the rugged terrain along with providing you with necessary information about the region.

Moreover, they can be a mediator when you are having trouble communicating with the locals. Additionally, they are well trained in basic first aid, so in case of any accidents and mishaps, they will give you an immediate response either by taking you to health centers or evacuating you to a safe place.

Hiring a guide can cost you an average of $25 to $35 per day. If you hire a more experienced and professional guide, then it can cost you around $50 per day.

Like guides, porters are also an integral part of the Manaslu Circuit Trek. They will carry the weight of your luggage and equipment, allowing you to enjoy the trek with more ease. Hiring a porter will cost you anywhere from around $20 to $30 per day. But this price will depend on the distance and difficulty of the trek.

With our package, we will provide you with a government-licensed English-speaking guide and one porter who will carry the luggage of two trekkers.

Transportation Cost

You will start and end your thrilling Manaslu Circuit Trek with a drive from Kathmandu. You will have a scenic drive to Soti Khola by heading north on Prithvi Highway. At the end of your journey, you will have a ride from Dharapani to Kathmandu via Besisahar.

There are different modes of transportation. You can either choose from a bus drive or a jeep ride. It will cost about USD 15 -20 if you choose a local bus from Kathmandu to Soti Khola. The cost might slightly increase by a few dollars if you choose a tourist bus. Similarly, the jeep ride from Kathmandu to Soti Khola will cost you around USD 205.

While deciding on the return transportation, the jeep drive from Dharapani to Besisahar will cost you approximately USD 150. From Besisahar to Kathmandu, the jeep ride will cost you around USD 200. If you want to start your trek from Maccha Khola, which is a few miles forward from Soti Khola, then the cost of a jeep drive from Kathmandu to Maccha Khola will cost you around USD 225.

Expenses That Exclude from the Manaslu Circuit Trek Cost

Tips for Trekking Staff

Tipping culture has been recently introduced in Nepal. Even though tipping is not mandatory and is just a way to show gratitude, tipping guides and porters are usually expected in the tourism business. Usually, it is said that you should tip the amount they deserve, but estimating such an amount can be quite confusing.

Most people follow the general theory of tipping 10% to 15% of the total trekking cost. Some even tips guides and porters with 15% of their salary. You can take the following chart as a reference for tipping guides and porters.

Trekking Guide- USD $10 to $20 per day

Tour guides- USD $10 to $20 per day

Porters- USD $10 to $15 per day

Flight Cost

As you will be traveling to Nepal from other different countries, the only medium to arrive at Nepal is by airways. This package does not include your incoming and outgoing international flight fare, along with any airport departure taxes. Therefore, you will have to manage these costs on your own. An air ticket can cost you between USD 700 and USD 1000. This may vary on various factors like countries, airplanes, agencies etc.

Travel Insurance

Insurance is mandatory while traveling with Base Camp Adventure. Travel insurance helps you to mitigate the risks and share the financial burden with the insurer. Moreover, you will be spending more than two weeks amidst the Himalayas, so carrying travel insurance is like taking precautions before embarking on the journey.

Your travel insurance shall cover all your medical expenses, hospital bills, air ambulance, and evacuation costs. Moreover, we recommend you take cancellation insurance in case you will have to cancel or postpone your trek due to any reason. This will cover your money in case you have pre-paid any expenses like accommodations, flight fare, etc. The overall travel insurance will cost you around USD 150 to USD 200.

Drinks Expenses

Staying hydrated throughout the trek is very essential to avoid altitude sickness. For that you will need to intake enough water and fluids. The teahouses and lodges along the trail will offer you freshly squeezed juices, water, soft drinks, hot drinks, and even hard drinks.

However, the package cost does not include bottled and bar drinks. You will have to pay out of your own pocket if you want to have access to these drinks. While you have to pay around $2 to $ for a cup of tea, you will need to pay anywhere between $3 to $7 for a cup of coffee. Teahouses can charge you $2 to $7 for bottled water and soft drinks.

Similarly, they will charge you $8 to $10 for hard drinks. This cost may vary depending on what kind of hard drinks you have chosen, Branded wine can cost a lot more than this.

Other Personal Expenses

Other personal-level expenses that you make on the trek will not be included in this package. Renting or buying trekking equipment, personal accessories, toiletries, and snacks shall be borne by you. How much you want to spend on these personal expenses depends upon your requirements and luxury. You can allocate around USD 500 to USD 1000 for these personal expenses.

Trekking equipment like a down jacket, sleeping bag, and duffle bag will be included in the package. However, you will have to return these things back to the company after the completion of the trek.

Some Tips for Reducing Your Manaslu Circuit Trek Cost

Bring Enough Cash

You will not find ATMs on the trails of Manaslu Circuit. However, most teahouses and lodges deal on a cash basis rather than using visas and master cards. In case they accept those cards, it will take a 3% or 4% charge for each transaction. So, it is better to encash Nepalese currency when you have easy access to banks and ATMs in Kathmandu. In case you do not have Neplasese currency, then easily convertible currency like US dollars, Pounds, Australian Dollars, Singaporean Dollars, Malaysian rings, and Euros can come in handy.

Use Data Than Wifi

The teahouses will charge you $3 to $5 for access to WiFi facilities. Instead of that, you can buy NTC or Ncell sims. If you don’t want to use Wifi, you can use data to stay connected with teh world while you are trekking. However, the network reception might not be stable as you trek deep into the Manaslu region.

Buy Snacks From Kathmandu

Buying toiletries, snacks, and medicines on the trail might be expensive. Moreover, you cannot have a large variety of things you want to buy. So, if you want to save some dollars, then you can purchase those things in Kathmandu, where department stores and other shops provide a variety of options.

Use Purification Tablets

Usually, the water in the Manaslu region is fresh and pure. However, if you do not want to drink that water, then you will have to buy bottled water, which will cost you $2 to $7. Additionally, you will have to intake about 3 to 4 liters of water daily in the trek. It might cost you a lot of money in the bottled water. So, what you can do is buy water purification tablets or filters and use them to filter your water.

Bring Power Banks or Solar Chargers

Usually, the teahouse will charge you USD 2 to USD 3 per hour to recharge your electrical devices. Instead of spending a few dollars on recharging, you can bring solar power banks or solar batteries.
