title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek in February
excerpt: Annapurna Base Camp Trek in February: February is the last month of the winter season. Winter is the coldest time of the year when there is an occurrence of snowfall in high altitudes. People usually…
html:
Annapurna Base Camp Trek in February: February is the last month of the winter season. Winter is the coldest time of the year when there is an occurrence of snowfall in high altitudes. People usually think trekking is impossible during February which is a misconception.

Because it is possible, so if you are interested in the Annapurna Base Camp trek in February. You can look forward to having an exciting time on this trek. Annapurna Base Camp is one of the popular trekking routes of the Annapurna Region.

You will trek to the base of the world’s tenth highest peak on this trip. Annapurna Base Camp lies at an altitude of 4,130 m above sea level. To reach this base you will be crossing Machhapuchhre Base Camp.

Walking through lush green forests and landscapes while exploring the flora and fauna in the sanctuary is a dream come true. Also, the snowy peaks look breathtakingly beautiful during this time.

The temperature and weather are also stable during this month. It will be a bit chilly during earlier weeks but by the end, it gets warmer. You should not miss out on this exciting trip to the Himalayas.

This trek gives you a once in a lifetime experience. You get to pass through many traditional villages while learning about their culture and lifestyle. One of the plus points will be privacy and peace throughout the trek.

You get to enjoy the trek at its fullest without any disturbance. With proper planning and preparation, you can complete this trek with ease. So, don’t think twice and join this adventurous Annapurna Base Camp Trek in February.

To know more about the benefits, difficulties and related matters of this trek read further below.

Highlights of Annapurna Base Camp Trek in February

  • Explore the beautiful and traditional villages inhabited by Gurung Community
  • Walking through lush forests of oaks, pines, and rhododendron
  • Crossing several enduring rivers and suspension bridges
  • Glimpse on the lifestyle of rural Nepalese people
  • Tasty and flavourful local dishes
  • Clear and unobstructed view of various peak
  • Mountains in this trek Annapurna Massif, Dhaulagiri, Machhapuchrre, Himchuli, Manaslu, and many more
  • Reach the Annapurna Base Camp passing across Machhapuchhre base camp
  • Many offers and discount during the off-season
  • Warm welcome and hospitality of the local people
  • Experience the unique culture of the locals

Outline Itinerary of Annapurna Base Camp Trek in February

Day 1: Arrival in Kathmandu

Day 2: Drive from Kathmandu to Pokhara (850 m) – 8 to 9 hours

3rd Day: Drive from Pokhara to Nayapul (1,070 m) – 2 hours then trek to Tikhedhunga (1,480 m) – 5 to 6 hours

Day 4: Trek from Tikhedhunga to Ghorepani (2,800 m) – 6 to 7 hours

Day 5: Trek from Ghorepani to Tadapani (2,610 m) – 7 to 8 hours

6th Day: Trek from Tadapani to Chhomrong ( 2,170 m) – 7 hours

Day 7: Trek from Chhomrong to Bamboo ( 2,400 m) – 6 to 7 hours

Day 8: Trek from Bamboo to Deurali ( 3,200 m) – 7 to 8 hours

9th Day: Trek from Deurali to Annapurna Base Camp via Machhapuchhre Base Camp (4,130 m) – 5 to 6 hours

Day 10: Trek from Annapurna Base Camp to Dovan ( 2,600 m) – 5 to 6 hours

Day 11: Trek from Dovan to Jhinu Hot Spring ( 1,800 m) – 7 to 8 hours

12 Day: Trek from Jhinu to Pothana ( 2,100 m) – 6 to 7 hours

Day 13: Drive from Pothana to Pokhara ( 850 m) – 6 to 7 hours

14th Day: Drive back to Kathmandu ( 1,400 m) – 8 to 9 hours

Day 15: Departure

Route of Annapurna Base Camp Trek

Arriving at Kathmandu airport, the representatives will pick you up and drop you off at your hotel. Helping you check- in they leave for the day. You can roam around or rest after the tiring journey.

You Annapurna Base Camp Trek in February begins on the second day of the trip. This day you head towards the beautiful city of lakes, Pokhara from Kathmandu. Heading out of the capital, you take the Prithvi Highway to reach your destination.

After a long day’s journey, you stay in one of the hotels for the night. Waking up early on the third day, you have your breakfast and drive towards Nayapul. From there, your trekking journey begins as you walk to Tikhedhunga.

Walking past small settlements, rivers, forests, and waterfalls you reach your destination. From there, you will be heading towards Ghorepani, a popular viewpoint of this trek.

The next day you wake up early and climb the hill to view the stunning sunrise. After that, you head towards Tadapani viewing scenarios of many marvelous peaks.

Then from there, you trek to Chhomrong, the gateway point to do Annapurna Base Camp Trek. The following day you walk till Bamboo passing trails of dense and dark forests.

You will be trekking to Deruali and stay the night there. Finally, the most awaited day is here, you will be heading to ABC via Machhapuchhre Base Camp. After many uphill and downhill walks you reach the base camp.

Staying the night there, you descend to Dovan the next day. From Dovan, you head to Jhinu danda and take a refreshing bath in the natural hot spring. After relaxing your muscle, you trek to Pothana from there.

You will be driving back to Pokhara from Pothana. And then drive back to Kathmandu retracing the roads. Your Annapurna Base Camp Trek in February comes to an end as you head to the Tribhuvan International airport.

Reason to Visit Annapurna Base Camp Trek in February

People usually wonder, is Annapurna Base Camp Trek in February worth it? Well, yes it has its own benefits and we have mentioned a few of them below:

Clear and unobstructed view

Even though it is winter, the skies are crystal clear. It is sunny and warm during the day giving the unobstructed view of peaks and landscapes. Along the way, you can see many marvelous peaks like Mount Annapurna, Manaslu, Himchuli, and many more.

You will be accompanied by the beautiful view of nature throughout the trek.

Privacy in Routes

As February is the off-season time of the year. The routes will be less crowded during this time. Moreover, you can roam around the trails without any disturbance from other trekkers.

You get to enjoy the peaceful environment and view the beautiful mountains without any hassle or noise. Besides, you will be getting all the privacy you want in February.

Empty Accommodation

As there are less no. of trekkers in these routes. You will find empty lodges and tea houses. You can choose and get any room you prefer. Likewise, you don’t have to worry about sharing your room or waiting in a queue outside the bathroom.

Also due to the low crowd, you get to enjoy their hospitality at its fullest. Your ordered food will be delivered faster than usual.

Bargain price

This season will be a paradise for budget travelers. As there is less crowd the price of many items drops significantly like flights, meals, accommodation, and many more. If you can bargain then it will come handy during this time.

Temperature of Annapurna Base Camp Trek in February

Each month has a different Temperature around the Annapurna region. Even though February is one of the winter months. The temperature can be different in every destination. It can be freezing cold in one and chilly in another.

The temperature drops with every climb in altitude. Lower regions are mostly chilly with warm daytime. While the temperature in the upper region can hit below zero.

Just like, the minimum temperature in Pokhara can range up to 7.6 degrees while the maximum can reach up to 19.4 degrees. Same way in Ghorepani, the minimum temperature can range up to -2 degrees and the maximum can range up to 8.2 degrees.

As you ascend in the trails and reach high elevation, the temperature can range in the negative. Like the temperature in Annapurna Base Camp can range from -2 to -14 degrees during February.

Weather Around Annapurna Region in February

Weather plays a vital role in deciding how challenging your trek around the Annapurna region will be. When trekking in February, people usually think that the weather will be very cold. But actually the weather begins to get warmer during late February.

As you have chosen the month of February for trekking you need to be well-prepared at all times. The winter season is short in Nepal, as by late February the weather condition improves.

During early February, the weather can be chilly and cold but by the end of February, it gets mild to warm. The lower regions become warmer during late February while the temperature slowly begins to drop in high altitudes as well.

Even though it’s winter, the skies are clear and give out the unobstructed view of peaks and landscapes. If you can handle cold then trekking during February will not disappoint you.

Annapurna Base Camp Trek in February Difficulties

The routes of Annapurna Base Camp is one of the most popular trekking destinations of Nepal. The beautiful trails are suitable for both solo and group trekkers.

This trek is a moderate level climb which is not much difficult with proper planning and preparation. However, the routes are adventurous and demanding which requires patience.

Even though the routes are not very harsh you will face various difficulties. So, we have mentioned a few of them below:

Altitude Sickness

Altitude sickness is one of the major and common problems you will be facing in this Trek. Annapurna Base Camp is the highest point of this trek situated at an altitude of 4,200 m.

This problem occurs when traveling above 3,500 m altitude. But not every trekker suffers from it so it is better to be precautious then scared. Altitude Sickness occurs due to thin air and low oxygen in higher places.

Some symptoms of this sickness are headache, breathing difficulty, sleepless nights, vomiting, nausea, and many more. As it worsens you might even find difficulty in walking.

If you notice any of the symptoms immediately inform your guide. They will give you further instructions on whether to stay or return back.

Distance

You will be walking a total of 115 km around the Annapurna Base Camp trek. Each day you will be covering about 11 to 15 km distance. Normally, the walking speed of a person is 5 km per hour so covering this distance is not much longer.

The trials are not much harsh but walking in rocky terrain can be a bit challenging and difficult compared to the hilly routes. The paths will be covered in snow during February which creates one of the difficulties.

Walking in snow-covered paths is very challenging so, be careful. It is recommended not to trek more than 600 m per day.

Duration

This trek is two weeks long, but if you prefer you can complete it within 7 to 9 days. The itinerary can be extended or reduced according to your choice. Each agency provides you with different and unique Annapurna Base camp trek packages.

However, it is advisable to choose an itinerary with longer days. As longer days have a short hour walk. Usually, you will be walking for about 5 to 7 hours each day. But if you choose a shorter itinerary your walk will be longer. You will be walking 8 to 9 hours per day.

Trekkers who have no experience in walking for long hours can easily get exhausted and tired. Due to which they will find the trails uncomfortable.

Lack of Training

The trails of Annapurna Base Camp are not very steep or difficult. But it can be challenging for newcomers. As you will be walking the path that leads you to the base of the world’s 10th highest peak.

It is best to be prepared beforehand if this is your first time trekking in the Himalayas. You will be making many uphill and downhill walks in these trails. Also, as you will be trekking in February the snowy paths will be a huge obstruction.

Walking twists and turns in the snowy trail will be very difficult even for experienced trekkers. If your body is not fit, you will get exhausted pretty quickly. And catching up with others can be a problem.

Not only that but the downhill walk will be easier compared to the uphill walk. As even a short period walk can be tiring when making ascend in high altitudes. You need to be mentally fit as well.

Budget Management

If you are a budget traveler then you might face problems in maintaining expenses. As the goods and services are expensive in higher altitudes. Managing the budget will not always go according to your plan.

The price increases as you climb higher in altitude. Because the people in the higher regions depend on porters and animals for transportation. There is still no road transportation available in many rural areas.

For eg, Lays chips can cost 40 rs in lower altitude but it can cost up to 80 rs in high places. There is a huge price difference in the lower and upper regions. So, it can be a disadvantage for budget travelers.

Type of trekkers

How difficult the trek will be can also depend on the type of trekker. This trek is suitable for both novice and experienced trekkers. But it is going to be harder for beginners compared to experienced trekkers.

Trekking experience in the mountains will be different for the first-timers. As they might find it much harder to cover the average distance than the experienced ones.

Walking in steep and rocky terrains will be a huge challenge for beginners. So, for your first time, it is better to hire a porter and walk comfortably. Enjoy the moment and don’t stress out.

Useful tips for Annapurna Base Camp Trek in February

Stay Hydrated

Staying hydrated is the first thing you should do when trekking at high altitude. You will be walking for hours so dehydration is common while trekking. So, always carry your personal water bottle and refill it before beginning your trek.

The price of mineral water can cost up to 1$ in high altitudes. So, that way you can save money as well. You can refill your bottle from the lodge you will be staying in. But they can charge you extra cash for that.

Pack Light

When going on treks it is known to always pack light. Don’t carry or bring along unnecessary stuff. That way it will only be eating up space in your bags or luggage.

Climbing in trails with heavy bags can be tiring, so you might slow down your team as well. Always make a list of things necessary for the trek and only pack them with you.

Physical Exercise

You can always hear from trekkers that being physically and mentally fit is very necessary before starting a trek. Trekkers will be requiring huge stamina to complete the Annapurna Base Camp trek in February.

So, you can increase your stamina by doing physical exercises on your own. Like running, swimming, long walks, short hikes, and many more. You can do these exercises on your own.

The Final Say

We hope after reading the article you gained some useful information related to Annapurna Base Camp Trek in February. Trekking on these routes is not impossible so don’t hesitate and miss this amazing opportunity. Overall, it is an adventurous journey in the Himalayas.

title: Is It Safe To Travel Nepal?
excerpt: Are you in doubt whether is it safe to travel Nepal? The short answer is ‘Yes.’ You may have heard countless stories of petty theft and travel scams from the most popular countries in South Asia for…
html:
Are you in doubt whether is it safe to travel Nepal? The short answer is ‘Yes.’

You may have heard countless stories of petty theft and travel scams from the most popular countries in South Asia for backpackers and travelers alike. The locals and ex-pats may have warned you about the incidents and tipped you on how to stay safe. So, let’s address it- is it safe to travel to Nepal? Here’s the deal-

If you don’t put yourself in a position where people can take advantage of you and keep your wits about you, you will have the experience of your life.

In this article, we have drafted the expert’s advice on how to be safe while traveling in Nepal. But before that, let’s get to know a little more about this beautiful nation.

Nepal has topped the list of best destinations to travel in the world by Forbes and Lonely Planet in 2017. According to the data published by the Nepal Government in 2018, Nepalese tourism saw one million-plus visitors — that’s 134.5% more than there were 10 years ago!

The tourism industry has been working hard to stand tall after the violent earthquake that rattled the nation in 2015. Thanks to the combination of efforts of the government, local businesses, and natives. They are successful to manage to be back and back with a bang with the record number of tourists in recent years.

Nepal, apart from being gifted in terms of cultural and natural heritage, is also cheap and easy to navigate. And as long as you follow your instincts and the guidelines, you will be totally fine and safe to travel to Nepal.

To help you stay safe, here are a few tips you’ll want to keep in mind in no particular order:

1. Make Sure Someone Knows Your Itinerary

It’s always a good idea to leave your travel itinerary with someone you trust. Let someone know where you’re meant to be at the exact date and time. Emails and phone calls are the best ways to communicate your travel plans, including the hotel booking details, flight numbers, and the ETA and other necessary outlines of your trips. There are many remote locations in Nepal where the phone network or wifi may not be available. Include notations in the details when you expect to be in or out of range as well.

In the event that things go south, you’ll have someone who can act immediately to aid and assist, which may be vital for your survival, especially against natural causes.

2. A Lot of Research

Although it’s self-explanatory, we still want to focus on a few extras while traveling in Nepal. Avid research will provide you with a better understanding of the situation and will prepare you for any circumstances.

One of the best ways to do research is to use our best friend on the internet- Google. Go for phrases like- “Is it safe to travel to Nepal?” Or “Any new changes in policy for tourists in Nepal?”. Getting to know travel restrictions, bans, immigration laws, and safety tips will always be helpful.

In cases of natural disasters, civil unrest, or other emergencies, your embassy will be able to assist you. So check your government website for more information, and know-how to reach them. And note the important phone numbers in case of emergencies.

Note: Dial 100 for Emergencies- That’s 911 for Nepal!

3. Don’t Trek Alone

With the exception of a few popular trekking routes in Nepal, you’re strictly advised to hit the road in a group. If you’re a backpacker traveling alone, you would want to hire porters and travel guides. There are many restricted areas in Nepal where the law forbids you from trekking alone. This applies to all travelers. Trekking in groups is advised especially to those who have moderate to low experiences in high altitude treks.

Traveling in a group gives you a lot of advantages over solo tours. The guides would be helpful in arranging accommodation, itinerary, weather information, and the extras along with accurate information on the particular location you’re interested in.

They are helpful mainly during mishaps, unforeseen situations, and medical emergencies.

4. Packing List

Layering is the key to conquer your ultimate adventure in Nepal. Being a geographically diverse nation, Nepal boasts a hot and humid climate in the south, warm and temperate on the hills and freezing cold in the north where mountains lie. So you need to pack based on location, the weather, season, and most importantly, altitude.

The rule of thumb- the higher the altitude, the more the layering. Bring thermal shorts or trousers, a fleece jacket, and a light down jacket with a hood or down vest. The temperatures in the mountains will reach below the freezing point every night. The accommodation facilities will not have a heating system. So your clothes are the only life support at those temperatures.

If you’re traveling below or around 3,500 m, pack clothes that are light, with fast-drying fabric and good breathability.

Your backpack can make or break your dream of completing the trek. Pack too few items, and you would miss out on the essentials. Pack too much and you would have a difficult time carrying them around (unless you’re hiring a porter). So, pack smart!

5. Carry Cash

Many places – including other major cities beyond Kathmandu – either don’t accept credit cards or have a minimum transaction amount. For this reason, it’s a good idea to stock up on enough cash to get you by.

Although ATMs are available all over the country, many of them are routinely out of order. Therefore the best way to cash out would be to visit one of the exchange agencies located in Kathmandu. Also, note that not all international debit cards are supported by the ATMs in Nepal. The amount would be given out in Rupees and they come in 100, 500, and 1000 Rupee notes.

Your trekking route may not have any ATMs along the way and even if they do, they are usually out of stock. So it’s always recommended to carry enough cash when traveling.

Note- Traveller’s check is rarely accepted in Nepal.

6. Learn Common Courtesy

Even just a few Nepalese phrases can help you make some new friends, build trust, and get help if needs be. ‘Namaste’ with a smile and joined hands like those on Buddhist prayers will get you immediate attention, followed by ‘Sanchai Hunu Huncha?’ which roughly translates to ‘How are you?’. It’s always a good idea to download Nepali on Google Translator so you have it offline as well, just in case.

Similarly, being a spiritual epicenter of Hinduism and Buddhism, there are some cultural norms you’re supposed to follow. Touching someone’s head is considered very rude. Also, you don’t want to rush in a river or lakes in your bikini in trekking trails. Kissing or PDA is generally considered not appropriate and is frowned upon in Nepal.

Oh, and about tipping in Nepal!

There is no minimum suggested tip at restaurants, cafés, or pubs. While it isn’t mandatory or a part of everyday routine for locals, it’s certainly respected and appreciated.

That brings us to some idiosyncrasies in Nepali people. Using chin to point at an angle to show direction, moving their heads to imply ‘Yes’ and ‘No’, referring to the word timepass and chill as an expression for anything that is frivolous, vaguely silly, killing time, and a guilty pleasure are some of the most common ones. Don’t be surprised if they call you Dai/Bhai (brother) or uncle, those are the terms generally used for non-relations. The locals find it more endearing than calling you, Mr. Bob.

7. Staying Healthy in Nepal

Standing at 4,600 feet above sea level, the capital city is the gateway to the high altitude trekking routes. The popular destinations reach as high as 18,380 feet and the average height looms around 13,000 feet in major trekking routes.

At such dizzying heights, the temperature frequently drops below zero and the wind chills are unimaginable. That coupled with less amount of oxygen in the air, AMS (Acute Mountain Sickness) is a common health issue. If you are a beginner or have limited experience, you should take the time to acclimatize to the conditions.

Make sure to pack some Diamox (Acetazolamide) before your trip and start the medications as per the instructions from guides. Give yourself plenty of time to rest and acclimatize before you start exploring the higher altitudes. Also, carry all the extra necessary medication you’re on from your country. Bring medical or vaccination certificates if needs be to ensure you’re safe to enter and travel to Nepal.

The tap water may not be safe to drink in many places. We suggest you use cleaning agents which are described in FAQs below.

8. Buy travel insurance

It’s always better to be safe than sorry. And this makes more sense here while trekking in remote locations in Nepal than anywhere else. In case something goes south, you want to be sure someone has your back and you’re covered. Travel insurance helps you fund your medical treatments, take care of your belongings, and rescue operations chiefly during mountaineering and high altitude climbing operations.

It’s smart to get insurance coverage before setting off for the airport in your country. But if you haven’t done it already, worry no more. Kathmandu offers you with the varieties of packages you can choose from according to your needs.

9. Drug Possession Laws in Kathmandu

Once known as a paradise for hippies for being the last destination on the Glorious Hippy Trail, Nepal has changed a lot.

The possession and consumption of grass are illegal and is forbidden by the new constitution of Nepal. You may not get shot by the police for possession, but it is a serious crime to be in possession of even very small quantities of them. Prison terms for drug offenses can be up to many years and it can take up to a year to even appear before a Judge for sentencing, although it’s not so common.

Additionally, if you involve with these drugs here, it increases your chances of getting into trouble. Possessing drugs here is illegal, and you don’t want to end up in a Nepali prison. Also, getting in prison will take away that privilege to travel to Nepal the next time.

10. Book Flights Ahead

Being a country full of mountains and highlands, along with unpredictable weather, the cancellation of flights is very common. During winter seasons in high altitudes, the fog covers up the whole area leaving very less visibility for the planes to the land.  It is the main reason for flights being canceled. This will be a huge issue if you’re traveling on a tight schedule. So, we advise you to spare a couple of days between the completion of the trip and tickets back home.

Conclusion:

So long as you are extra cautious, try not to do anything illegal, and stick to the guidelines, we assure you will have a safe and enjoyable time in Nepal. You should not ever put yourself in a position where people can take advantage of you. That pretty much guarantees the safety of any visitors and ranks Nepal among the safest countries to travel.

You may also like:

  • Manang Trek
  • Annapurna v/s Everest Base Camp Trek
  • Mardi Himal Trek
  • Annapurna Panorama Trek

FAQs

1. So, is Nepal Safe for Solo Travelers?

Generally speaking, Nepal is a safe destination for solo travelers. However, if high altitude and restricted areas are your goals, then you’re better off with a partner or a group. The travel agencies will hook you up with a team of other travelers and you will not need to look for one yourself.

2. Is Nepal safe for Solo Female Travelers?

Statistically, Nepal is one of the safest countries in the world for female travelers. The sexual harassment cases are unheard of in years, there have been no registered cases on crime against female tourists and the number of solo female travelers is on the rise.

Dressing modestly, not wandering around the backstreets late at night and not being drunk or drugged, using your common sense, and being aware of local customs. And Voila! You’re all good and perfectly safe to travel to Nepal!

3. Is it Safe to Take a Taxi in Nepal?

Self-driving cars are almost non-existent and you would not want to jump on the limited ones available. Even for an experienced driver, the use of opposite lanes, ignorance of rules, poor driving skills of local drivers, and bad road conditions are going to be a hassle. That leaves you with two choices- public bus, or taxis. Public buses are cheaper, but usually, pack and it would be hard to communicate about your destination as the buses are rarely marked with numbers.

Taxi is the way to go! And taxis are safe in Nepal. The rides around the evening and night time are quite expensive compared to those during the day. However, they are, in general, moderately priced and very safe.

4. Can You Drink Tap Water Nepal?

No. Water supply system in Nepal is not well organized and is often contaminated from the very source. This is the reason you should not drink tap water in Nepal. Apart from major cities, many remote parts of Nepal are yet to connect to the supply system and depend upon local water bodies for drinking water. Although Nepalese do not have a choice there, you do.

Always carry purification tablets when you’re going on a trek. Bottled water is available in almost every teahouse, and you can opt for boiling if you rent an apartment in the cities.

Before we wrap up the article, here are some ‘honorable mentions’ for your safety!

  1. Nepalese have a thing called ‘Nepali Time’ that things happen in. So don’t stress yourself over delayed flights, late pickups, and getting behind schedule.
  2. Carry hand sanitizers and toilet papers, they come in handy, big time.
  3. Haggling is very common and expected. So counter offer the sellers after they quote you.
  4. People will expect you to take your shoes off before entering temples and monasteries. Failure to do so might make others feel disrespected.
  5. There are no red right areas in Nepal, and anything that has to do with sex tourism is considered illegal. For any other scenario, remember the slogan, ‘No glove no love.’

Nepal performs strongly in the Personal Freedom and Safety & Security index. This ranks Nepal as one of the safest destinations to travel for all types of visitors from all around the globe. Also, with the lowest crime rate in history, political stability, and a high number of tourists every year, Nepal also boasts as one of the most traveled destinations for westerns. So, feel free to pack your bags, get a ticket and fly to this wonderland without having to fear about safety to travel to Nepal, a few precautions and basic instinct is all it takes to finally tick your dream vacation off from your bucket list.

Happy Travelling!

title: Annapurna Circuit Trek Cost
excerpt: Annapurna circuit is one of the most beautiful natural treks in the world. The breathtaking views of snow-capped Annapurna mountains are a highlight of this trek. The trek passes through stunning…
html:
Annapurna circuit is one of the most beautiful natural treks in the world. The breathtaking views of snow-capped Annapurna mountains are a highlight of this trek. The trek passes through stunning foothills of the Himalayas, serene rivers, glaciers, and other natural landscapes.

Annapurna circuit trek cost estimate is an important part of the trekking journey and depends upon itinerary and quality of services. Transportation, food and drinks, accommodation, guides and porters, visa and permit, are some of the factors related to cost.

The cost also depends upon trek route and side trips. If you decide to include Tilicho lake trekking in your itinerary, it will cost you extra in the overall Annapurna Trek cost. Similarly, a solo Annapurna circuit trek cost is comparatively lesser than a trek with a professional guide.

Read on to know more about cost and other related information in detail. You will also learn about various cost factors and individual estimates, and tips about the Annapurna circuit tour.

Factors Affecting Trekking Cost

Transportation costs

The transportation cost is one of the most important factors that you must consider before starting on the trek. You can either take a local bus or private car as routes have well-paved roads.

Kathmandu to Besisahar drive on a local bus will cost you around USD 10 per person. However, if you take a private cab it will cost you around USD 110 for the ride to Besisahar from Kathmandu.

You can also start your trek in an anti-clockwise direction. However, it is not recommended as it has high chances of trekkers getting altitude sickness. Flight from Kathmandu to Pokhara will cost you around USD 200 but depends upon the season of travel.

Accommodation costs

The Accommodation cost is another factor to consider for trek. The accommodation costs in high altitude regions is significantly greater when compared to lower altitude regions. Kathmandu and Pokhara have various accommodation facilities that range from basic hostels to five-star hotels.

You will get a basic hotel facility as per the package and you can change the accommodation as per your requirement. You will stay in teahouses and lodges along route. Luxurious facilities like Wifi, hot water, and electronic charging in your accommodation are available at an added cost.

The cost of hotels in Kathmandu costs around $110-250 for 2 days if you choose to stay in five star hotels. In higher altitudes, the lodges and tea houses provide clean rooms with twin beds, a mattress, a pillow, and a warm blanket. These accommodation facilities will cost around $3-5 per day and prices move higher up in high altitudes.

Permit costs

Annapurna Circuit Trek cost also includes various permits and entry cards for the trek. If you hire a trekking company, they will arrange all the trekking permits and the cost included in their package.

ACAP entry fee for foreigners is US $30 and ACAP entry fee for SAARC nationals is US $10. TIMS permit for foreign nationals is US $10 for group travelers and US $20 for individual travelers. The Cost of the TIMS permit for SAARC nationals is US $3 for group travelers and US $6 for individual travelers.

Guide and porter cost

Your trip gets more comfortable and safer with a guide and porter. You can also trek without a guide or a porter. If you are an expert professional trekker and have proper knowledge of the region, you can trek solo as well.

But if you are a beginner, it is better to hire a guide and be safe. A guide will take you through easy, comfortable, and safe routes while enjoying the majestic views of snow-capped mountains. A professional guide costs you around USD 30- 35 per day in the Annapurna region. Furthermore, the guides can get hired through your trekking company.

Similarly, trekking with luggage is quite challenging. So you can hire a porter as they can carry around 20 kgs of luggage. They cost you around USD 18-20 per day and are also hired by your trekking company. If you feel confident and physically competent to trek while carrying a 15 kilograms luggage, you can also trek alone.

  • Manang Trek

  • Mardi Himal Trek
  • Annapurna Panorama Trek

Food and drinks cost

The food and drinks facilities are of wide variety in Kathmandu and Pokhara. You can get a basic meal from $3 to $30. The restaurants and cafes in cities have intercontinental cuisine.

However, you will be dining in tea houses during your trek. The teahouses serve traditional Nepalese meals of “Dal Bhat”. You can find modern menus like pizzas, pastas, burgers, noodles, and others along trails. The food gets expensive as you move up in the higher altitudes. In brief, the food costs range from USD 5-10.

However, drinks like bottled water cost around USD 1 to 5, Masala teas cost from USD 0.5 to 2 and Hot water per cup costs from USD 0.5 to 2. Besides that, you can also get mint tea, rhododendron tea, garlic tea, and others along with teahouses in a variety of prices.

Cost of Gear

The Annapurna Circuit trek cost must include trekking equipment. A moderate to difficult level trek requires quality trekking equipment for a safe and comfortable trekking journey.

The cost of the trekking equipment depends on an individual and varies from person to person. If you are a professional trekker, you can easily manage the trek. But if you are a beginner, you will need quality trekking gear.

Most trekking companies provide trekking equipment at rent so that you can return them after the trek is over. However, you can also invest in your trekking equipment according to your preferences and requirements if you are an avid trekker.

Some of the major trekking equipment are:

  • Duffel bag and a day pack
  • Warm sleeping bag
  • Trekking trousers and pants
  • Warm and waterproof jacket
  • High-quality trekking boots
  • Trekking shirts with a second layer fleece
  • Headlight
  • Hiking boots
  • Warm gloves and socks
  • Regular shoes or sandals
  • Thermals
  • Inner and outerwear
  • Trekking Gears
  • Toiletries
  • Other accessories
  • First aid
  • Important documents

An estimated cost of Annapurna Circuit trekking equipment is around USD 500. You can also rent them at around USD 1-10 per day from Thamel.

Miscellaneous cost

Besides, the transportation, food, accommodation, and equipment costs, there are other costs for the Annapurna Circuit Trek as well. These additional trek costs are commonly known as miscellaneous costs.

Personal costs like electrical charging devices, hot showers, extra drinks, or the tips fall under these costs. These miscellaneous costs also include first aid kits, souvenirs, or other items. Moreover, the miscellaneous costs depend upon your desires and requirements. These costs can get reduced for a more budgeted travel package.

Visa costs

All non-Nepali citizens (except Indian nationals) require a visa for entering Nepal. You can get it before arriving or directly on arrival. Likewise, you can get a visa on arrival at the International Airport in Kathmandu.

You can apply for a visa online as well before arriving in Nepal. The cost of the Nepal government-issued visas for 15, 30, and 90 days is $30, $50, and $125 respectively. You can visit the Nepal Department of Immigration’s official website for more details.

Travel Insurance

The route is a highly challenging which requires physical strength and endurance. You will trek in steep terrains in high altitudes hence they are quite risky. Proper travel insurance is essential for trek.

The insurance must cover flight cancellation, baggage loss, and any injuries or medical costs. You should ensure that coverage includes altitude above 4,000 m A lot of travel insurance companies provide insurance at a reasonable price. Hence, travel insurance is an important part of the Annapurna circuit trek cost.

How Much Does it Cost while Trekking Solo?

Solo Annapurna Circuit Trek cost is comparatively cheaper than with hiring a guide. However, the trip is more comfortable with a guide and you don’t have to worry about finding a proper accommodation and safety.

At around $1000, you will get a proper guide that takes care of all your food and accommodation arrangements. The guide will assure you have a comfortable trip as all your itineraries get managed and handled by the guide.

Your trek itinerary gets lengthened without a guide which will further increase costs. Guides can also bargain and get you the best deals as they know people around the trail. Solo trek without the guide will cost you anywhere between $800 to $1150.

While solo Annapurna circuit trek is comparatively cheaper, it is more comfortable and safer to trek with a professional trek guide.

Route Itinerary – Outline

Day 1: Arrival at Kathmandu

Day 2: Drive to Syange/ Jagat for 5hrs

Day 3: Trek to Dharapani for 5hrs

Day 4: Trek to Chame for 5hrs

Day 5: Trek to Pisang for 4/5hrs.

Day 6: Trek to Manang for 5hrs.

Day 7: Acclimatization day at Manang village (you can trek to Tilicho)

Day 8: Trek to Yak Kharka for 4hrs

Day 9: Trek to Thorong Phedi for 4hrs

Day 10: Cross to Thorung la pass then trek down to Muktinath for 9hrs

Day 11: Trek from Muktinath to Jomsom for 5hrs

Day 12: Drive to Tatopani either by local bus or private jeep.

Day 13: Trek to Ghorepani for 9hrs

Day 14: Trek to Hille for 5hrs

Day 15: Trek to Nayapul and an hour drive to Pokhara.

Day 16: Fly/Drive back to Kathmandu.

Day 17: Final Departure from TIA

How to Minimize the Cost?

  • Try getting offseason deals as the prices of packages and flights are lesser in off-seasons.
  • Carry tea bags, coffee powder, and others so you can save some money on teas and coffees.
  • You can also rent the trekking equipment.
  • Carry water purifiers along trails to purify water for drinking.
  • Tipping the staff and guides and porters depends upon your desire
  • Bargain well to get best deals
  • You can tip around 10 percent of the total cost as a general rule.

The Final Verdict

Solo trekking Annapurna circuit cuts down the guide and porter’s prices, but it significantly increases the risk of accidents and injuries while traveling. Hence, the guidance of an experienced tour guide will help you immensely during the trek.

Allocating the budget is an important part of any trekking adventure. The budget naturally rises if you choose to have a comfortable and luxurious trek. However, the Annapurna circuit can also get completed on a tight budget. We hope you learned about Annapurna circuit trek cost through this article.

The overall total estimate of the cost (excluding international flight costs) is around US$ 2,000 for Budget Travel, US$ 3,000 for Average Travel, and US$ 5,000 or more for Luxury Travel. Cost for Indian and the cost for Nepali is similar with absence of visa costs. Contact us for more details regarding this spectacular trip!

title: Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek – Itinerary, Best Time, Difficulty
excerpt: When the least traveled trek is no more disregarded, you just visit it. And this goes the same for Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek, which was once brushed aside. Fortunately, the trek has been acknowledged…
html:
When the least traveled trek is no more disregarded, you just visit it. And this goes the same for Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek, which was once brushed aside. Fortunately, the trek has been acknowledged now than ever before for its sweeping views, scenic landscapes, and gorges.

It too has got luscious forests atop the villages and hillsides that look so fantastic. And so are the traditional villages along the route where locals are always affectionate and welcoming to guests. Outsiders are made to feel home with a hospitable environment and warm services.

Sadly, this can’t be said the same for trails of Kanchenjunga Circuit, which is somewhat more challenging than other hikes. The trek is one of the toughest with unpaved paths that continuously run hills and valleys.

Filled with a large chunk of rocks and boulders makes the trek not just hard but also lethargic. On top of that, hikers may have to get over the altitude sickness that occurs after gaining elevation adding to Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek difficulty.

Shortness of breath and severe headache compels so many trekkers to drop the idea of continuing the trek further. Harsh weather and unpredictable climatic conditions too bring off the hike. In doing so, it contributes to the never-ending Kanchenjunga Circuit trek difficulty.

The Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek route starts from Kathmandu with a long drive to Birtamod, coming after Suketar. It runs across several villages including Kesuwa, Tserma, Ramche, and Pang Pema to reach the circuit.

Best Time for Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek

Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek is willing to host the trekkers all year round. But its remoteness and unforeseeable weather doesn’t allow hikers to travel the spot any time of year. Some seasons involve high risks, whereas the rest of the others are relatively fine to make a trip.

Generally, Autumn and Spring are the best time for Kanchenjunga Circuit trek. Specially mid months of these season.

In that matter, Autumn is perhaps the most incredible time to mount Kanchenjunga Circuit. It exudes lovely weather starting from September to till winter knocks the door again. The average temperature in autumn is 15 Degree Celsius, causing the day to be warm and pleasant.

But as soon the sun goes down, the temperature falls by half and the nights get chilly cold. Expect the weather to be more crisp and cold after Tseram whatever the season is. Autumn usually brings nostalgic memories with intense fall colors booming throughout the forest and valley below.

The cold wind blowing from the mountain in the evening with vivid foliage, clear sky of the morning, and bright days makes the season lovely. The king of all seasons, Spring too, has favorable weather for trekking Kanchenjunga Circuit.

After the foggy winter, March brings a beacon of light to lift the soul of hikers. Sharing a crisp winter and scorching summer, Spring offers a perfect atmosphere for travelers.

As compared to the higher region, the temperature during spring in Kanchenjunga Circuit below the valley is 25 Degree Celsius. Spring rewards its long waiting visitors with green foliage, popping flower buds, and dazzling rhododendrons.

Considered as Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek difficulty, winter and monsoon receive too few visitors. Its hash weather, heavy snowfall, and frequent rain doesn’t endorse trekkers. It instead suggests them not to climb the circuit in winter as the temperature ranges from -15 to -25 Degree Celsius.

Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek Itinerary

Day 01: Arrival at Kathmandu

The scheduled day marks your arrival at Nepal’s only International Airport. To receive you and also give a warm welcome, our officials will be waiting at the airport’s lobby. After a short and sweet encounter, they’ll drive you to your hotel where you can get some rest. For a change, you can also go on a walk in the busy street of Thamel and get some air. Head back to the hotel in time if you don’t want to have dinner outside.

Day 02: Explore Kathmandu City, Drive to Birtamod

Maximum Altitude: 300 m

Drive Distance: 439.7 km

Drive Duration: 10 hours

Before defying Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek difficulty, we’ll have some playtime at Kathmandu. As the city boasts so many amazing places to visit, we’ll explore a couple of them in and around. Most of these scenic sites are listed in UNESCO’s world heritage site, including Pashupatinath Temple, Swyambhunath Stupa, and Durbar Squares.

They will help us break into the primordial culture and history of Nepal through a series of temples, idols, and open courts. Royal palaces and the national museum has a collection of ancient statues, old portraits, and artifacts. Overnight, we’ll take a bus to Birtamod.

Day 03: Drive to Suketar

Maximum Altitude: 91 meters

Flight Distance: 7-8 hours

Flight Duration: 246.8 km

Early morning, we’ll have breakfast, then continue our journey to Suketar. The day is going to be pretty hectic and stressful following a long drive to the mountainous region. The drive will last roughly 10 hours, depending on how fast the shuttle is.

However, there’s nothing to be upset about as we have a splendid view to glance throughout the trip. Along the way, a scenic view of beautiful landmarks, luscious meadows, and a vibrant city will be right before our eyes.

The natural vista from the backseat looks astounding with an unspoiled countryside village, terrace farm, and busy streets. Driving as long as 153 miles through Mechi Highway, we’ll arrive at Suketar. At this point, we can say, the trip indeed adds to the Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek difficulty.

Day 04: Trek to Lali Kharka

Maximum Altitude: 2,265 m

Trek Duration: 5-6 hours

Trek to Lali Kharka may be long, but it’s tremendously easy with a straight flat route. The trek doesn’t last more than 5-6 hours and passes breathtaking scenery. The path running to Lali Kharka is a bit dusty but easy to helm. It winds through tropical forests, beautiful meadows, and small settlements to reach Lali Kharka. Inhabited by people of different cultures and ethnicity, the village is incredibly beautiful. For might, we put up in a guesthouse.

Day 05: Trek to Kesuwa

Maximum Altitude: 2,120 m

Trek Duration: 5-6 hours

Starting the day with a hearty meal, we continue our trek descending through rice fields and millet. After crossing the suspension bridge over Phawa Khola, our trail heads up to a small Gurung village popular as Bhanjyang.

For a while, we’ll stop here to catch a breath and have lunch that usually includes tea and snacks. The place is extraordinary of all we have traveled yet as it provides us a glimpse of Kanchenjunga and Kyabru for the first time.

Leaving behind the village, we’ll scramble up the trail and get through the pass before descending to Kesuwa. Finally, after traversing almost 7 hours on the trail, we’ll reach Kesuwa. Overnight in a teahouse.

Day 06: Trek to Mamankhe

Maximum Altitude: 1,270 m

Trek Duration: 5-6 hours

Easily one of the most beautiful spots on the way to Annapurna Circuit, Mamankhe is our next destination. So, without wasting much time, we’ll head towards the trail that walks through mixed forests.

The hike is a bit easy compared to the previous one with a flat walkway leading to Kabeli Khola. For most of today’s walking, the trail provides us a lovely view of small waterfalls that too in a string. Making headway to the north, we’ll walk uphill before stopping at a teahouse in Yangpang to fill the empty stomach.

After enjoying the magnificent Mt. Jannu and having a meal, we’ll return to the trail. Ascending uphill for about half an hour or more will take us to Mamankhe. Calling it a day, we’ll spend the night at a local teahouse. We’ll also use the free time to prepare for the next Kanchenjunga Circuit trek difficulty.

Day 07: Trek to Yamphudin

Maximum Altitude: 2,080 m

Trek Duration: 2-3 hours

Today’s trek is mostly upward on a smooth surface so we can have a slow start. After enjoying the morning meal, we’ll steadily climb the hill alongside Kabeli Khola. The cliff lying just beyond the stream en route offers a great view.

A little while later, our trail leads firmly straight up the valley and plunges down underneath the rock cliff on debris. Walking a few miles ahead, we’ll reach a small suspension bridge. On the other side of the cross over, we walk uphill and pass through a small hamlet to arrive at Yamphudin.

Upon reaching the village, you can relish a sublime view of forests and landscapes. Being exhausted with that long trip, we’ll rest in a teahouse at night.

Day 08: Trek to Tortong

Maximum Altitude: 2,995 m

Trek Duration: 7-8 hours

Trek to Tortong will take us somewhere from 7 to 8 hours. So, without further ado, we’ll set off on the trek. From Amje Khola, we’ll ascend a sharp hill through a well-marked route up to Chitre. There’s a pretty good chance that we may see Himalayan yaks grazing on lush-green pastures along the way.

After coming out of the visually appealing scenery, we’ll make our way through subtropical evergreen forests. It’s filled with bushy Spanish mosses as well as Rhododendron and spruce.

Moving forward from the teahouse, our trail rises upwards through an indigenous woodland. From here, we’ll enter an opening and come across a suspension bridge before slowly heading uphill to Tortong. We’ll stay the night in a teahouse at Tortong.

Day 09: Trek to Tseram

Maximum Altitude: 3,870 m

Trek Duration: 6-7 hours

Leaving Tortong, our trail is upward sloping off the hillside on the right bank of Simbuwa Khola. The trek should take us somewhere between 6-7 hours traversing above the stunning Lalung Valley. For the better part of the excursion, we have a lovely Tuplung Peak joining us.

With an eye-pleasing view through dense rhododendron forest and marvelous Yalung Glacier, we’ll eventually reach Tseram. The sight from the village is some of the best you have ever seen. Accommodation is arranged in a lodge where you can have dinner and get a sound sleep.

Day 10: Trek to Ramche

Maximum Altitude: 4,580 m

Trek Duration: 5 hours

Embracing the bright morning of Ramche with a warm breakfast, we’ll carry on with our trek. The journey from Tseram to Ramche takes about 5 hours at a slow but steady pace. The trail sets forth with an uphill scramble until Yalung Glacier.

Walking through the valley, we’ll get a truly satisfying view of a mountain range and bright green forests to relish for. The sloppy trail then heads west of Ramchaur to Lapsang, followed by Ramche. Overnight in a teahouse.

Day 11: Rest day for a tour around Ramache and Kanchenjunga Base Camp

After the difficult walk of the last eight days, it’s time we take a day off from the trek and get full rest. But instead of sitting tedious and killing time, we’ll rather take a hike above the village and climb down before evening.

Although there are many beautiful spots to travel on, we’ll walk the valley around its vast curve. All of sudden, we are exposed to the southern wall of the mountain where the cliff forms a half-open steep-sided hollow.

Stretching 9 miles, the cirque provides a pristine view of Kanchenjunga massif and sweeping valleys. We too descend onto glaciers and below Talu while hiking towards Oktang. After exploring the magnificent Khumbakarna glacier from the east of Mt. Jannu, we return to the village. As usual, overnight in a teahouse.

Day 12: Trek to Mirgin La

Maximum Altitude: 4,480 m

Trek Duration: 7-8 hours

From Tseram, we descend to the valley, coming through many small settlements of Lapsang. Subsequently, we’ll reroute the trail towards Mirgin La pass and Ghunsa before sloping downhill to the northside of Kanchenjunga. Winding the way through Mirgin La, we’ll get the most scenic view of Mt. Jannu. To ease off and spend the night, we’ll set up a camp in the valley.

Day 13: Trek to Ghunsa

Maximum Altitude: 3,595 m

Trek Duration: 3-4 hours

It’s easily the shortest trek on Kanchenjunga Circuit, but the physical strength that takes to complete the Gunsa hike is intense. So, we start early trekking and descend the steep hill to Lamba Sumba Kharka. The place has got an even more awe-inspiring view to offer on the face of Jannu’s southwest.

From right here, the trek gets less difficult, with most of the trail inclining downhill up to Ghunsa. Perched at 3,475 m elevation, Ghunsa is a Tibetan village in Taplejung. Far from car horns and screams, we’ll be able to enjoy the mind-blowing view of waterfalls and creeks.

You may see the prayer flags fluttering in the wind and some tea houses run by locals. Lodges are famous for their local millet wine, but trekkers don’t drink it due to altitude sickness. We’ll set up a camp to spend the night.

Day 14: Trek to Khambachen

Maximum Altitude: 4,050 m

Trek Duration: 6-7 hours

Today we’ll set off on the trek early morning as it’s a long journey ahead. After having breakfast, we’ll immediately rush towards the trail coursing the bank of Nupchu Khola on the north. Walking past alpine forests and green pastures with scented wildflowers, we’ll turn up to Rampuk Kharka.

Using the suspension bridge, we’ll get to the other side of the village where there’s a pouring waterfall. From here, our trail roves around a mudslide area, so we have to be extra careful. The dazzling Mt. Jannu once again crops up, but this time with a zoom.

The trail in front is incredibly tricky, preceding through rocks and mountains up to Kambachen. We’ll be spending the night in a teahouse.

Day 15: Trek to Lhonak

Maximum Altitude: 4,780 m

Trek Duration: 6-7 hours

With a total elevation gain of 730 m, expect another long and exhausting trip to Lhonak. The trek kicks off via Ramtang village, passing some of the most remote sides. The settings are, of course, terrific with shimmering snow peaks and vibrant valleys.

Scrambling uphill for a long time, we’ll stop by Ramtang to grab lunch. From here on, we’ll take a rugged trail on the hillock filled with large boulders. Without leaving the riverbank once, we’ll get to the waterfall, which is fabulous to watch.

Soaking up the incredible views of enticing mountains and gushing river below the suspension bridge to Ramtang Monastery, we’ll take the journey to Lhonak. With that, we’ll discontinue the trip and spend the night in a teahouse.

Day 16: Trek to Pang Pema

Maximum Altitude: 5,140 m

Trek Duration: 4-5 hours

You’ll start noticing the lack of oxygen from Pang Pema. Hence, keeping that in mind we’ll have a slow start while walking to Kanchenjunga Base Camp. It’s the highlight of the trek and also the toughest section of Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek difficulty.

Minor headache and nausea is common while trekking Kanchenjunga Glacier so it may be hard to keep the momentum going. The trek of 3 hours alongside hills and forests will lead us all the way to Pang Pema. Overnight in a teahouse.

Day 17: Acclimatization and exploration around Pang Pema

As the trek quickly gains elevation from Pang Pema, there’s a great chance of us enduring altitude sickness. Hence, to prevent the sickness, we’ll take a time off from the trip and allow the body to adapt with the changing temperature.

There are tons of places to hike here whether going to the lower slopes of Drohmo or ascending terrains. Either way, you’ll get a stunning view of glaciers and shimmering Mt. Kanchenjunga. It’ll also help you combat with the Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek difficulty to come ahead on the trek. Overnight in a teahouse.

Day 18: Retreat trek to Khambachen

At the crack of dawn, we ascend the ridge from northside of Pang Pema to catch an unspoiled view of snow peaks. After sneaking a look at the staggering view, we descend to Kambachen with no Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek difficulty. The trek is mostly downward so it’ll be quicker and less difficult to walk. At Khambachen, we’ll stay in a teahouse.

Day 19: Trek to Ghunsa

Maximum Altitude: 3,595 m

Trek Duration: 5-6 hours

Getting refreshed with a tasty breakfast in Ghunsa, we’ll restart our trek climbing upward to Gyabla. Scrambling the way out and up from Pangpema, we’ll trek to the south of Kanchenjunga towards Ghunsa. The trek rises sharply up the hill, offering a sublime view of mountains as well as canyons and rivers till arriving at Ghunsa. After watching the grand view for some time, we’ll get back to the teahouse for a restful night.

Day 20: Trek to Kyapra

Maximum Altitude: 2,730 m

Trek Duration: 6 hours

The day starts with an ascend to a steep trail following Tamur and Ghunsa Khola. The route walks through a teeming forest of conifer, rhododendron, birch, and oak. Walking the edge of a steep hill provides a great view with a rolling river down into the valley. Passing through the last of Tibetan village Kyapru, we trek a few miles farther for about 1 hour to reach Tang. Overnight in a teahouse.

Day 21: Trek to Sakathum

Maximum Altitude: 1,580 m

Trek Duration: 6-7 hours

The entire walk to Sakathum from Kyapru takes around 7 hours meandering on a wobbly trail. It’s pretty hard to keep up the pace for the first few hours while rambling to Amjilasa. But after then the trek gets less challenging with a steep descent. As the atmosphere changes promptly from here, the Ghunsa Khola Valley can be seen at a distance. Not too far off is a small village in Taplejung where we’ll wrap up our expedition.

Day 22: Trek to Chirwa

Maximum Altitude: 1,180 m

Trek Duration: 5-6 hours

Shoving off from Sakathum, we head on our way to Chirwa on a rather easy trail. After walking a few miles, we’ll meet the junction of two rivers, Ghunsa and Simbuwa Khola. Together the river joins Tamur Kosi, which we’ll chase until switching the trail.

On the way, we can see plenty of side streams and creeks, putting up an overwhelming view. After hiking continually for almost 7 hours, we’ll finally end up at the beautiful village of Chirwa. Overnight in a teahouse.

Day 23: Trek to Phurumbu

Maximum Altitude: 1,542 m

Trek Duration: 6 hours

After a nice breakfast to celebrate the lovely morning of Phurumbu, we’ll get all our stuff packed and crawl towards the trail. As we walk ahead, the rural village gets wider, making the way down to rich vegetation. Running across several villages, we’ll reach Sinwa from where the trail walks downhill and on a bridge over Sisne Khola.

The trail from Sinwa to Phurumbu still has a village to pass and a suspension bridge over Yaphre Khola. After trekking for around 6 hours, we’ll be now gawking at the amazing Phurumbu village. The trip includes stops at a local teahouse with neat rooms for a comfortable night’s sleep. Also, it’ll help us get over the Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek difficulty.

Day 24: Trek to Suketar

Maximum Altitude: 2,420 m

Trek Duration: 4-5 hours

It’s the last time for us on the trail of Kanchenjunga Circuit as we’ll get back to the city tomorrow. From the ground level of the valley, we scale up along the cliff for around 3 hours to Taplejung village. The locals are so kind and easygoing to strangers that you can make a conversation with them despite the linguistic barrier. After crumbling up two-hour foothills, we’ll access Suketar. As always, we’ll stay the night in a family-own teahouse.

Day 25: Drive to Birtamod

Maximum Altitude: 300 m

Drive Distance: 242.9 km

Drive Duration: 7 hours

Since it’s going to be a frantic day today following a 7-hours long drive, we’ll rise up early in the morning. With the trekking part so done, we’ll shortly dash towards the driveway after breakfast. Next to the verdant hillsides and typical Nepali villages, we’ll enjoy the spectacular scenery till reaching Birtamod. On reaching the town, we’ll straight drive to the hotel so that you can ease off.

Day 26: Drive to Kathmandu

Maximum Altitude: 1,350 m

Drive Distance: 442.3 km

Drive Duration: 10 hours

It was a tiring day yesterday and today is no different with nearly a 10 hour drive to Kathmandu. To cope with the strain, you need a power booster that is provided by a complete breakfast meal. From there on, we’ll drive to Kathmandu via B.P. highway.

The trip is quite fun with phenomenal scenery of high cliffs, pine forests, and mountains. Once we enter the valley, we’ll drive you to your hotel where the farewell bash is already arranged. You may enjoy the delicious treat before going to bed.

Day 27: Transfer to airport for final departure

Early in the morning, our representative will arrive at the hotel to drop you at the International Airport. They’ll also watch you back in case you need any other service until you don’t board the flight.

Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek Distance

Kanchenjunga Circuit roosts in eastern Nepal straddling between Nepal and Sikkim. Three out of four trek routes to the circuit alone lie in Nepal. But don’t mistake for the trek route to get easy as it’s challenging from all sides, be it northeast, west or southwest.

The total Kanchenjunga Circuit trek distance from Suketar is 200 km. It means the trekkers on the way to the circuit have to walk between 9 km to 11 km per day in order to reach the destination on time.

Given the long route, the hike takes at least 27 days to accomplish starting from Kathmandu. However, the itinerary may differ depending on how long you plan to stay in the region. During the expedition, you’ll pass over many villages, lush green forests, and landscapes to reach the circuit.

The verdant valleys, cascading waterfall, and moving glaciers put up a grand show which no trekkers can afford missing. Amidst the natural grandeur, don’t forget about the Kanchenjunga Circuit trek difficulty that arises from bad weather and high altitude.

title: 5 Days Everest Base Camp Trek
excerpt: 5 Day Everest Base Camp Trek: Do you want to visit Everest Base Camp, but don’t have enough time? Then our 5 days Everest Base Camp Trek is suitable for people with limited time on their hands…
html:
5 Day Everest Base Camp Trek: Do you want to visit Everest Base Camp, but don’t have enough time? Then our 5 days Everest Base Camp Trek is suitable for people with limited time on their hands.

Usually, the classic route takes about 10 to 14 days off your schedule. But our package lets you visit and return in 5 days. Don’t worry; you won’t miss out on any of the adventures.

Similarly, you will get to experience both trekking and helicopter ride on this journey. Moreover, you will be trekking for the first three days and do the helicopter ride for the next two days.

Your trekking journey begins as you fly out to Lukla from Kathmandu. After your arrival, you trek to Phakding and stay the night. The next day you head to Namche and from there hike to Syangboche the following day.

You catch your helicopter ride from Syangboche and head towards Everest Base Camp. Spending some time there, you fly back to Lukla and then to Kathmandu the next day.

On this trek, you will be viewing various magnificent peaks of the Khumbu region. Such as Everest, Nuptse, Lhotse, Ama Dablam, and many more. You will also enter the Sagarmatha National Park, where many endangered plants and animals live.

Another attraction would be learning more about the lifestyle and culture of the Himalayan people. Many ethnic groups reside in this region like Sherpa, Bhotia, Rai, Thakali, and Magar. Among them, the majority of the people here belong to the Sherpa community.

This 5 days Everest Base Camp Trek package is full of an exciting and adventurous journey. You will be exploring the beautiful Khumbu region on this trek. The beauty of this region will blow your mind away.

Highlights of 5 days Everest Base Camp Trek

  • Visit Everest Base Camp
  • Helicopter ride to the base camp
  • Visit Namche Bazaar, the largest Sherpa village
  • Stunning view of various snowy peaks
  • Walk-through Sagarmatha National Park

5 Days Everest Base Camp Trek Itinerary

As you may know, our 5 days Everest Base Camp Trek is a short version of the original trek. We have made this package suitable for travelers with limited time. It is a perfect opportunity to reach the base of Mount Everest and explore the region in a short time.

To know more about the 5 days Everest Base Camp Trek Itinerary, you can read further below:

Day 1: Fly To Lukla from Kathmandu then Trek to Phakding

Flight Duration: 35 to 40 minutes

Flight Distance: 138 km

Maximum Altitude: 2,843 m above sea level

Trek Duration: 3 to 4 hours

Trek Distance: 7.5 km

Maximum Altitude: 2,660 m above sea level

Today your 5 days Everest Base Camp Trek journey begins in the high Himalayas. Waking up early, you get ready, eat breakfast, and wait for your guide to pick you up from the Hotel.

Meeting up with your guide, you guys head towards the airport and board your flight to Lukla from there. The airtime of the trip is quite short, so enjoy your time in the clouds. Soaring into the sky, you get the spectacular view of the monuments, mountains, and valleys.

Viewing these mesmerizing scenarios, you arrive at Lukla. This place is well-known for having a narrow airstrip. This flight is one hell of an adventure for thrill lovers.

After your arrival, you meet up with the porters and other remaining staff. From here onwards, your trekking journey begins as you move toward Phakding. Heading out of the town, you descend in the trails and head towards Monzo.

As you walk a bit further, you reach on trails that follow through the side of Dudh Koshi River. You will follow the trails to Phakding. This day’s routes are not very harsh and challenging.

Phakding is a popular stop or rest point for trekkers. This village consists of several guesthouses where you stay for the night.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Day 2: Phakding to Namche Bazaar

Trek Duration: 5 to 6 hours

Trek Distance: 7.4 km

Maximum Altitude: 3,440 m above sea level

Today you head towards Namche Bazaar from Phakding. After having your breakfast, you pack your bags, head out of the city, and set off towards the north. You begin the trek by walking along the sides of the Dudh Koshi River.

After walking for several hours, you do an uphill climb in the trail. And pass through several small villages like Zamphuti and Benkar. On your way, you will see many shops and guesthouses situated here.

You will have crossed two suspension bridges over the Dudh Koshi River before reaching Monzo. This is a small village located in the valley of Dudh Koshi River. Now, you head in the south direction towards Jorsale.

Walking in these trails, you see the beautiful vista of mountain peaks and landscapes. Viewing them, you ascend in the trails entering the colorful forest of rhododendron.

As you walk a bit further, you arrive at the entrance of Sagarmatha National park. This park is one of the UNESCO Heritage Sites of Nepal. You need to provide permits in the checkpoint to enter the park.

After that, you move ahead in the trails and reach Jorasele, where you have your lunch. The trail begins to get harsh and challenging from here onwards. The routes are rugged and steep till the Khumbu river.

Crossing the river with the help of a suspension bridge, you get the glance of Tabuchi. Then making an uphill climb on the routes, you get your first glance of Mount Everest.

A bit further from there, and you arrive at Namche Bazaar, the largest Sherpa settlement of this region. This town is the center for trading in the Khumbu region.

You get to see many lodges, shops, restaurants with wifi here. It is also well known for cheese made of Yak milk. You can roam and explore the valley.

Stay here tonight.

Day 3: Namche Bazaar to Syangboche

Trek Duration: 2 to 3 hours

Trek Distance: 4.5 km

Maximum Altitude: 3,790 m above sea level

Waking up early this morning, you have your breakfast and head towards Syangboche. Heading out of town, you ascend in the trails following the narrow path. Walking in the tracks, you get to see the magnificent Mount Everest.

This day’s journey will be a tiring one as you have to make many ascend and descend in the trails. Along the way, you will pass through many prayer wheels, mani walls, and monasteries.

This day you will get to see the spectacular peaks of Mount Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse, and many more. Also, the beautiful view of landscapes is quite eye-catching.

This trek lets you experience the lifestyle and culture of the locals, monks, and nuns closely. After walking for a few hours, you arrive at Syangboche. This place has varieties of accommodation you can choose from.

Among all, Everest View Hotel is quite famous among the travelers for holding a Guinness world record. This hotel holds a record as “hotel at the highest altitude in the world.”

Day 4: Flight to Everest Base Camp via Helicopter then Fly Back to Lukla

Flight Duration: 15 to 20 minutes

Maximum Altitude: 5,364 m above sea level

Today is an exciting day in your 5 days Everest Base Camp Trek journey. This day is the most awaited day of your trip when you reach Everest Base Camp. You will be visiting your destination via helicopter ride.

After a delightful breakfast, you board the helicopter and begin your trip towards the base camp. Flying into the sky, you can witness the beautiful Khumbu valley below.

Also, the snowy peaks look stunningly breathtaking from above. After a few minute’s ride, you reach your destination. You will be staying here for about 10 to 15 minutes due to altitude problems.

You get to witness the beautiful Mount Everest and various other peaks from here. Reaching the base of Mount Everest gives an overwhelming feeling to the travelers.

You can also add the option to visit Kala Patthar, the viewpoint. This place gives an up-close view of Mount Everest along with the panoramic view of other peaks. It is the highest point of the Everest Base Camp Trek.

After spending some time exploring the area, you return to Lukla for the night. You can roam around this town and visit restaurants or cafes. Today is the last day in this region, so live this moment.

Day 5: Flight Back to Kathmandu from Lukla

Today is the final day of your trip, as you will be returning to Kathmandu. Waking up early, you have your breakfast and head out to the airport. You catch an early flight back.

Viewing the mesmerizing scenarios of peaks and valleys, you arrive at Kathmandu. The remaining day is unplanned and free. So, you can rest or visit places during this time.

Best time for 5 days Everest Base Camp Trek

Everest Base Camp Trek is Possible at any time of the year. However, you will be trekking as well as flying on this trip. So, your experience differs according to the season you choose for travel.

Many travelers prefer Spring and Autumn, the best time to visit the Everest Base Camp. These are seasons when the beauty of nature is at its peak. Also, the climatic conditions are suitable for both flight and trekking.

To know more about the best time for 5 days Everest Base Camp Trek read further below:

Spring

Spring is the beginning season of the year. This season brings new chapters and the lost greenery of the hills along with it. As winter has just finished, the forest’s paths have buds of flowers ready to bloom.

March to May is the month for spring. The weather and temperature are quite favorable during these months. The skies are clear and bright, giving out the best view of the peaks and landscapes.

Also, it is sunny during the day, so don’t forget to bring your caps and scarfs. As for the night, it can be a bit cold in high elevation. This season is perfect for Nature lovers.

Autumn

Autumn is the peak season of the year. The season when the beauty of nature is at its best. The forest paths are covered with colorful flowers and vegetation during this time.

September to November is the month for Autumn Season. These are the months when even the climatic conditions are in its peak time. The weather is mild during autumn, making treks quite comfortable.

The skies are clear, and there are no signs of rainfall and snowfall during these months. It is warm and sunny during the day, while it can be chilly during the night.

Winter

Winter is the off-season for Everest Base Camp Trek. This season is the coldest time of the year when there is an occurrence of heavy snowfall in this region. The routes and peaks are covered in white, making the views look fantastic.

December to February is the month for the Winter season. The weather is warm and windy during the day time, but it can be freezing during the night. Also, the flights are usually delayed depending upon the climatic condition.

The routes can be challenging due to paths covered in snow. But the skies are crystal clear, giving you the fantastic view of the snowy peaks. However, the trek is possible during early December and late February.

Monsoon

Monsoon is the least preferred season of the year. This season is the time for continuous rain showers in the lower region. However, there are fewer chances of rainfall in high altitudes.

June to August is the month for Monsoon Season. Trekking in lower regions during these months can be challenging and thrilling. Also, most of the flights are canceled and delayed during these months.

The routes are slippery and muddy due to rain showers. Also, the views get hidden behind the dark rain clouds making the trek dull. However, due to heavy rainfall, the paths are full of new species of plants and flowers.

5 Days Everest Base Camp Trek Difficulties

Trekking in high altitudes is never an easy task. You will face various difficulties along the way. So, we have mentioned a few possible challenges you can meet in this trek below:

Route Difficulty

Even though you will be trekking for only three days, the routes will be exhausting for beginners. During your journey, you will be walking in steep hills and rugged paths.

The routes are full of challenges and thrilling adventures. You will be walking for about 5 to 6 hours per day, which can be harsh for people that are not familiar with walking long-distance.

Weather Condition

Weather always plays a vital role in the treks. Your adventure and excitement depending on the weather condition. You will be trekking and flying on this trip so that is why clear weather is quite necessary.

If the weather condition is excellent, you get to enjoy your journey viewing various magnificent peaks. Also, your flights won’t be canceled or delayed. But if the weather condition is unfavorable, you might even get stuck here.

So, always check for weather forecasts during your trip to Everest Base Camp.

Physical fitness

5Day Everest Base Camp Trek is a moderate level trek that is suitable for both beginners and experienced. However, you need to be physically and mentally fit to finish this trek.

You won’t be needing any technical training, but physical exercise is a must. These physical exercises can be done in your home or on your own. You don’t need to hire a trainer or visit the gym.

Physical exercises require running, swimming, hiking, long walks, meditation, and many more.

Altitude Sickness

Altitude Sickness is always a significant problem when trekking in high elevation. On this trek, there is no acclimatization. So, suffering from Acute Mountain Sickness is quite common for trekkers.

Some of the symptoms are dizziness, vomiting, nausea, headache, breathing difficulty, and many more. If you find any of the symptoms, then immediately inform your guide. They will give you further instructions on what to do.

While walking in high altitudes, always drink plenty of water and take rest in stops.
