title: 7 day Everest Base Camp Trek
excerpt: Of so many wonderful hikes in the world, Everest Base Camp is the most surreal walk. It’s jam-packed with natural grandeur and otherworldly scenic views that blows up a traveler’s mind. The trek…
html:
Of so many wonderful hikes in the world, Everest Base Camp is the most surreal walk. It’s jam-packed with natural grandeur and otherworldly scenic views that blows up a traveler’s mind. The trek offers a spectacular sight of Mount Everest and the overwhelmingly impressive landscapes that’s nowhere to be seen.

Walking the steep hills is stressful but worthwhile as it delivers a great view down the valley. The swishing sound in the trees on a breezy morning and soaring ridge are phenomenally amazing. The walk alongside Dudh Koshi River also gives trekkers immense satisfaction of getting in through nature.

On foot, travelers will explore so many unique landscapes, encounter new people with different cultures, and take a glimpse of wildlife. The old trail running towards Everest Base Camp provides a spectacular view of primordial monasteries, old Chortens, and meadows.

With just a week left in hand to accomplish 7 day Everest Base Camp Trek, we’ll rush to Tribhuvan airport on the first day of the expedition. After landing at Lukla airstrip, we’ll climb 3.8 miles on a well-marked trail up to Phakding.

The route above is irregular and steeper, so we’ll have to take gentle steps and complete a destination at a time. Ascending 7.4 km for nearly 6 hours on day 02 of 7 day Everest Base Camp Trek, we’ll arrive at Namche. Mostly inhabited by Sherpa people, the town is used for acclimatization by too many hikers.

Next, we’ll head towards Tengboche which is popular for its ancient Tibetan monastery. Trekkers usually stop at the village to rest and offer their prayers to the deity after finishing the trek for the day. From there, we’ll climb steep hills and follow a zig-zagged trail alongside fabulous Ama Dablam and Pheriche Village.

After hiking for around 5 hours, we’ll get to Lobuche which is small in size and has a few villages. Most trekkers here prefer to book a room in a lodge instead, placing a tent. Finally, after Lobuche, we’ll climb uphill to Gorak Shep before setting the foot on Everest Base Camp.

Highlights of 7 day Everest Base Camp Trek

  • Dreamy flight to Lukla with a marvelous snow peak view and visionary landscapes
  • Warm hospitality and fine etiquette from locals en route
  • Culturally rich villages, ancient monasteries, and stunning mani walls to spot
  • Luscious hemlock forest with pine, juniper, birch, and scrub
  • Possibilities to come across wild animals inhabiting Sagarmatha National Park
  • Exquisite view of Ama Dablam alongside Cho Oyu and Nuptse

Best time for 7 days Everest Base Camp Trek

Everest Base Camp never minds hosting the visitor all year-round. It’s pleased to embrace more and more trekkers and give them the taste of each season. However, not all trekkers are delighted to travel the base camp at any time.

Most of them only plan the trip during autumn and spring as the season tends to have moderate weather. The views are pure magical with exploding fall colors and full blossom rhododendron all through the forest.

In autumn, the temperature doesn’t exceed 24 Degree Celsus and neither drops below 5 Degree Celsius, giving off lovely weather. Meanwhile, the temperature during spring ranges from 12-20 Degree celsius making days quite warm and night super chilly.

When the winter starts to roll in, the climate at base camp gets frigid with the temperature dropping below -11 Degree Celsius in late autumn. Simultaneously, on the other side of winter, spring has more cold start with the temperature falling up to -2.6 Degree Celsius.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Difficulties of 7 day Everest Base Camp Trek

It may be nothing compared to what trek difficulties, Mount Everest, possesses but Everest Base Camp is not easy either. The long jagged trail, continual rising steep trail, and cliffs make the trek incredibly challenging and tedious.

With the elevation gain after each climb, trekkers have to deal with acute mountain sickness. Most people start showing symptoms of altitude sickness right from Namche that get worse with each scale above.

Therefore, the ailment has to be treated on time so that it doesn’t turn into High altitude Pulmonary edema. For that, trekkers must drink a liter of water every 2 hours and avoid climbing more than 500 m a day.

Trekkers on the Everest Base Camp trail must be fit enough to travel at least 6 hours a day for one week. While it doesn’t have any technical climb, the hiker should still pull off an intense workout regimen and follow a strict diet.

Food and Accommodation at 7 day Everest Base Camp Trek

The food at 7 Day Everest Base Trek is simply appetizing although not as varied as that in Kathmandu City. Most of the time, it’s basic with a local Nepali dish, boiled rice, fried vegetables, pulses, and pickles. Some lodge and guest houses also serve Tibetan noodle soup, spaghetti, and cheese omelet but they cost high due to inaccessibility.

The quality of accommodation on Everest Base Camp Trek depends on the cost and location. Hotels and lodges at lower hills like Lukla are standard with a well-facilitated room, lovely interior design, and high-quality services.

The quality of amenities declines as you scale up towards base camp. It limits within tea houses and local homestays, providing minimal facilities. They’re comfortable but basic with a single or double bed, woolen blanket, and a pillow. Hot showers and chargers are available for an extra buck.

Accommodation is of a high standard at Kathmandu varying from 5-star hotels to pricey lodges and guest houses. You can also find cheaper dwellings that cost anywhere between US$3 and US$5. Hotels that come cheaper are gross and usually of a poor standard so it’s better to spend a few extra dollars rather than have such dwelling.

Essentials for 7 day Everest Base Camp Trek

Even though it’s moderate trekking, Everest Base Camp also demands the right gear from hikers. The weather in the Himalayas is unpredictable so the equipment that you’ll need depends on the season. To determine what to bring on the trek, first, you need to understand the climate in the base camp lying at an altitude of 5,364 m

Clothing

  • Lightweight fleece shirt and jacket to prevent cold at campsite
  • A set of windproof clothes if the place endures a strong wind
  • Lightweight moisture-wicking t-shirt
  • Quick-drying pants
  • Rainwear jacket in case it rains

Footwear

  • Quality mountaineering boots to walk the rugged trail
  • 2 pair of synthetic socks
  • Climbing shoes suited to all kind of terrain
  • Casual slippers

Other Miscellaneous

  • Trekking poles to walk steep hills and stairs
  • Water Bottles to drink water and prevent altitude sickness
  • Personal first aid kit including prescribed medications
  • Spare camera battery and charger
  • Portable power bank and binoculars

Itinerary

Day 01: Flight to Lukla, trek to Phakding

Maximum Altitude: 2,860 m

Flight distance: 138 km

Trek Distance: 9 km

Flight Duration: 40 minutes

Trek Duration: 3-4 hrs

Our 7 day Everest Base Camp Trek kicks off with a short flight to Lukla airstrip from Kathmandu. Thus, after picking you up from the hotel, we’ll drive to the city’s only international airport and board the flight.

Next, 40 minutes, we’ll be occupied sighting the dynamic landscapes, rising hills, and rushing waterfalls. After landing at Lukla airport, we’ll take a quick tea break to have our brunch.

Though small in area, Lukla is a ginormous town in itself with varieties of shops and guest houses. Hikers can walk along the street and even do the last-minute shopping here before climbing steppe trails to Phakding.

After you’re done with picking the items, we’ll ascend the trail on the left bank of Dudh Koshi River and walk ups-and-downs toward Phakding. After almost 3-4 hours of a hike on an even trail, we’ll make it to the village which is where we’ve our lodging.

Day 02: Trek to Namche Bazar

Maximum Altitude: 3,440 m

Trek Distance: 7.4 km

Trek Duration: 6-7 hrs

Rising to the warm sunshine and breathtaking view of Phakding, we’ll have the delicious meal provided by the lodge. Sometime later, we’ll carry on with the trek by trekking alongside Dudh Koshi river valley.

The trail above and around offers an astonishing view of the Rhododendron forest. As we scramble further, there are few villages like Monjo for trekkers to stop and have lunch and drinks. Leaving the villages behind we’ll delve into Sagarmatha National Park, just after getting the permit.

We’ll cross the suspension bridge several times while on a way to Namche. At the other end of Dudh Koshi River in the west, there’s an imposing Jorsale village. We’ll stop here for a few minutes so you can stock the food and water as there are no shops ahead.

Trek above Jorsale is difficult with a steep climb that takes 2 hours or more depending on the pace of walking. The trail alone drains a lot of energy so we’ll have to be physically fit at least to pass this section. Finally, after trekking for about 6 hours, we’ll arrive at Namche Bazaar, the Sherpa town. Overnight stay at a lodge in the village.

Day 03: Trek to Tengboche

Maximum Altitude: 3,860 m

Trek Distance: 9.2 km

Trek Duration: 4-5 hrs

Amid the lofty hills and glorious mountain surrounded by, we’ll wake to the beautiful morning of Namche. The trek isn’t long today so you’ll get to enjoy the vista for a little more time with tasty breakfast before fleeing the trail.

This will also provide us a direly needed acclimation to prevent sickness at high altitude. The trek doesn’t start easy with a steep climb for several hours. From a far distance on the route, we’ll be able to hear a yak bell sound and sight magnificent Tengboche monastery.

After coming above the ground level, we’ll have a little easy hiking until the old wooden bridge. From there, the trail picks up an altitude that only pro hikers can traverse at a reasonable speed.

Hence, we’ll take a slow and steady walk uphill alongside a lush-green forest towards Tengboche village. It’s a lovely village in Khumbu with glorious history and rich Tibetan culture. It has the oldest monastery in the Khumbu region carrying the heritage of several years. Tonight we’ll rest at a teahouse in the village.

Day 04: Trek to Dingboche

Maximum Altitude: 4,400 m

Trek Distance: 12 km

Trek Duration: 5 hrs

Our next destination on the 7 day Everest Base Camp Trek is Dingboche which climbs more than 500 m altitude from the village. So, after having breakfast, we’ll gently climb downhill on the trail and cross the screeching river from where the trail ascends uphill.

For better or worse, time runs by rambling along the river valley on a dusty trail today. The trek above is exhausting with a sharp incline for the most part. However, the views are absolutely incredible from the top with differing landscapes and glistening snow peaks.

At this point, the climb becomes tough with the lack of oxygen in the air. Mild symptoms like headaches and nausea are common on the trail. After climbing towards the mani stupa, we’ll have a slightly moderate trek all the way to Dingboche.

There’s no way we can make the hike any farther especially after that long travel. So, we’ll call it for a day there and spend the night at a local teahouse.

Day 05: Trek to Lobuche

Maximum Altitude: 4,910 m

Trek Distance: 5 km

Trek Duration: 5-6 hrs

The 7 day Everest Base Camp Trek has another long and tiring day awaiting hikers at Dingboche. The trail starts with a steep climb up the rim of the hill beside a wonderful view of the valley down.

For most of the day, we’ll walk a high flat ground and pass a village called Pheriche. After crossing an old wooden bridge over the river flown from Khumbu glacier, we’ll arrive at Dugla where there are small shops for drinks and food.

We’ll stop here for about an hour to have lunch and continue the upward trek along the way to Lobuche. The village is relatively exposed like that to Tengboche with few accommodation and houses. At an altitude of 4,910 m, it receives a strong wind so often, therefore most trekkers choose to stay inside rather than camping at the uneven ground.

Day 06: Trek to Gorakshep, Hike to Everest Base Camp

Maximum Altitude: 5,364 m

Trek Distance: 4.5 km

Trek Duration: 2-3 hrs

The walk today is only 3 miles but it can still take us more than 5 hours given the higher elevation and jagged trail. Walking over loose rocks and moraine is strenuous due to low oxygen towards Gorak Shep.

Thus, we’ll gently ramble the jagged trail with dust and pass the rocky moraine dune to reach Gorak Shep. Within a 2 to 3 hours trek, our trail unfolds a spectacular view of Mount Everest, airy ridge, and glacier.

Gorak Shep is a remote settlement placed on the brink of a frozen lakebed at 5,164 m Travelers use the village as a camp before trekking ahead and even stop at a teahouse to fill the stomach with something delicious.

From here, we’ll ascend the rocky trail at the northeast towards the base camp. Upon the arrival at the campsite, we’ve got a spectacular view of Mt. Everest as well as its neighboring snow peaks including Nuptse and Cho Oyu to sight. After spending a few hours and exploring the awe-inspiring landscapes and Khumbu icefall, we’ll descend the trail.

Day 07: Trek to Kala Patthar, Flight to Kathmandu

Maximum Altitude: 5,643 m

Trek Distance: 1.2 km

Flight Distance: 138 km

Trek Duration: 1 hr 30 min

Flight Duration: 4-5 hrs

It’s the last day of our 7 days Everest Base Camp Trek and we have a big one in the store to celebrate it. After breakfast, we’ll climb the mucky trail leading to Kala Patthar. The walk to this black rock mountain is straight uphill and takes about one and a half hours to complete.

Kala Patthar not only has easy access but an amazing view of Mt. Everest and Pumori. Hikers also get to glance at the vivacious valley, gorgeous landforms, and ice sheets. After you’re done watching the vista, we’ll board the flight at Kala Patthar and return back.

On the way home, we’ll stop at Syangboche’s Everest View Hotel to have breakfast. Throughout the flight, we have a majestic view of diverse topography, high cliffs, and mountains to glance one last time. After taking down the airport, our officials will drop you at the hotel.

title: 12 Days Annapurna Circuit Trek
excerpt: Annapurna Circuit Trek is one of the most popular treks in Nepal. With the magnificent views of the Annapurna Range along with the culturally rich trekking routes, it is one of the best trekking…
html:
Annapurna Circuit Trek is one of the most popular treks in Nepal. With the magnificent views of the Annapurna Range along with the culturally rich trekking routes, it is one of the best trekking routes in Nepal. Walking through the remote off the beaten paths passing through beautiful villages is what makes this trek so magnificent.

Trekking to the highest altitude of 5,416 m, Annapurna Circuit trek allows you to explore the Annapurna Region thoroughly. Passing the highest pass named Thorong La Pass, the 12 days Annapurna Circuit trek is an adventurous journey you shouldn’t miss out on.

Our 12 days Annapurna Circuit Trek itinerary starts with a long drive from Kathmandu to Bulbule. Reaching Bulbule our trek starts. You will be trekking from Bulbule to Chyamje. On the way, you will find many waterfalls and beautiful rhododendron forests. The trek further continues till you reach Manang passing through small villages like Bagarchhap, Chame, and Pisang.

Reaching Manang, you will have your first acclimatization. At the altitude of 3,500 m, there are chances of altitude sickness so acclimatization is very important. After staying the day in Manang acclimatizing and exploring, we shall continue our trek. From Manang, now we will gain some altitude. We will now trek to Ledar and reach High Camp which is also known as Phedi.

Trekking from Pedi to Muktinath, we will cross the Thorong La Pass at the altitude of 5,416 m. This is the highest point of the trek. Passing our prayers and taking blessings, we shall now head to Tatopani via Jomsom. We shall finally end our 12 days trek by driving from Tatopani to Pokhara.

Highlights

  • Be part of an adventurous journey into the remote areas of the Annapurna Region
  • Reach an astonishing altitude of 5,416 m at Thorong La Pass
  • Enjoy the magnificent views of the Annapurna Range and the neighboring peaks
  • Get your blessings at the religious pilgrimage of Muktinath
  • Enjoy the natural hot springs at Tatopani

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Annapurna Circuit Trek Difficulties

Annapurna Circuit Trek is a moderate level trek which can be performed by beginners as well. You don’t need any prior training for this trek. However, you should be physically and mentally prepared to trek through the remote trails. There are some difficulties you may face during your 12 days Annapurna Circuit Trek.

Altitude Sickness

Trekking to the high altitudes at above 5,000 m, there are high chances of you getting altitude sickness. So it may prove to be one of the difficulties during your trek. Altitude sickness occurs when your body has trouble adapting to the changing high altitude. As the air pressure becomes thin, the lack of oxygen increases the chances of altitude sickness.

Weather changes

In the high altitudes, the weather cannot be as steady. There can be frequent and sudden weather changes. So you should always be prepared. Especially during the summer season, rainfall can occur anytime spoiling your plans for the day. So you should be careful and choose the best time referring to the weather forecasts.

Remote trekking trails

The trekking trails are remote. Despite having motor roads for half of the trek after a long developmental time. There are still remote trekking trails during the trek. You should be careful during your trek. The trek takes you through many ups and downs. Mainly while crossing the Thorong La Pass, the trail is considered difficult. You should cross before the winds get strong. Various factors contribute to making the trekking trails difficult.

  • Annapurna Panorama Trek
  • Annapurna Circuit Trek Map with Fully Guided Itinerary
  • Best Time For Annapurna Circuit Trek

12 days Annapurna Circuit Trek Itinerary

Day 01: Drive Kathmandu to Besisahar and trek to Bulbule (923 m).

Maximum Altitude: 1,400 m

Drive Duration: 6-7 hours

Our 12 days Annapurna Circuit Trek starts with a long drive from Kathmandu to Bulbule. The drive takes around 6-7 hours. You will have breaks along the way for lunch.

Leaving the busy city behind, the drive will take you to the more natural and remote parts of the country. You will see beautiful landscapes align the way. The green forest along with the views will leave you amazed.

The drive takes you to Besisahar after 7 hours and you will trek to Besisahar for a short while. The trek will be just as beautiful walking through the remote trails with beautiful views.

After a short hike, you will see the beautiful village of Bulbule. You can enjoy the magnificent views of the mountains like Manaslu and Himalchuli from the small village. Today, you will spend the night at a tea house or a lodge at Bulbule.

Day 02: Trek from Bulbule to Chyamje (1,400 m).

Maximum Altitude: 1,400 m

Trek Duration: 5-6 hours

Today, we shall start our day with some healthy breakfast at Chyamje. Soon, we will head towards Chyamje at the altitude of 1,400 m.

The trek from Bulbule to Chyamje is a short trek through the beautiful trekking trails. leaving Bulbule, we shall head towards Bahun Danda. This palace got its name from the settlement and its inhabitants. The brahmin settlement is a great experience of the culture and lifestyle. Leaving the beautiful settlement, we will cross the Marshyangdi river passing through many beautiful small waterfalls and head towards our destination.

Crossing a suspension bridge, we will finally reach Chyamje and spend the night at a tea house or a lodge in the beautiful settlement at Chyamje.

Day 03: Trek from Chyamje to Bagarchhap (2,160 m).

Maximum Altitude: 2,160 m

Trek Duration: 5-6 hours

After a good night’s sleep and enough rest, we shall now head to Bagarchhap. Bagarchhap is a beautiful settlement with Tibetan influenced culture and lifestyle. The community is mostly Buddhist so you can see Buddhist prayer flags align the way as well.

Leaving the Chyamje village, you will trek down the beautiful trekking trails to a small place called Tal. Crossing the suspension bridge enjoying the beautiful views of the surrounding area, you will head towards Dharapani. Entering the Manang district, you can see beautiful sceneries and soon come across long stone stairs.

From Dharapani to Bagarchhap, you will see many chortens and old stupas. Reaching Bagarchhap, you can see the Buddhist cultures and lifestyles of people as well. You will spend the night at a tea house here.

Day 04: Trek from Bagarchhap to Chame (2,630 m).

Maximum Altitude: 2,630 m

Trek Duration: 4-5 hours

Our next destination is Chame. Chame is also known as the headquarters of Manang. Today you will trek for 4-5 hours covering a distance of 13 kilometers.

The trekking trails from Bagarchhap to Chame are filled with uphills and downhills. You will be able to enjoy the beautiful views of the mountains like the Lamjung Himal along with the lush green forests. You can also find yourselves some great markets in the area to explore.

Crossing a river along the way, you will reach Kopar. From Kopar, a trekking trail leads you straight to Chame.

Day 05: Trek from Chame to Pisang (3,300 m).

Maximum Altitude: 3,300 m

Trek Duration: 5-6 hours

Leaving the beautiful village of Chame behind, we will head towards Pisang today. Heading towards Pisang, we shall cross the Marshyangdi River. Crossing the suspension bridge, we will head towards Bhartang. Enjoying the beautiful narrow trails surrounded by forests of pine and hemlock, we will head to the Marshyangdi River Valley.

Crossing the valley, we will reach the Dhukur Pokhari. Beautiful meadows will greet you as you leave the valley with clear views of the mountains in the distance.

Soon you will also witness the Paungda Danda Rock shaped like a bowl. Crossing the rock, you will reach Pisang in a matter of minutes. You will rest at a tea house in the beautiful settlement at Pisang.

Day 06: Trek from Pisang to Manang (3,500 m).

Maximum Altitude: 3,500 m

Trek Duration: 5-6 hours

After a long trek, we shall finally cross 3,500 m altitude today as we head towards Manang. The small village of Manang is a great destination for amazing views and cultural exploration.

The trekking trail from Pisang to Manang has a great view of the neighboring peaks like the Pisang Peak and the Annapurna Range. The exotic flora and fauna along the way is another great highlight of the trek. You will come across many stupas and chortens along the way. Also, there is a small lama school along the way.

Crossing the Lama school, you will soon reach Manang Village. Rest up and enjoy yourselves as you will be spending the night at a tea house in the village.

Day 07: Acclimatization day in Manang.

Maximum Altitude: 3,519 m

Now that we have reached an altitude of 3,500 m, we should take a short acclimatization break. Today, we shall take an acclimatization day in Manang. Acclimatization is very important during high altitude treks to keep your body safe from altitude sickness.

Acclimatization does not mean you have to stay still. You can enjoy the day as an exploration day in Manang Village. There are so many things to do in this small village. You can also try to go on a short hike to Khangsar Hill to enjoy the beautiful view of Tilicho Lake. there is a 900-year-old monastery for you to explore as well. Spending the day in Manang, you can enjoy yourself and rest up for the next day.

Day 08: Manang to Ledar (4,250 m) Trek.

Maximum Altitude: 4,250 m

Trek Duration: 4-5 hours

The next day begins with beautiful views of the Annapurna Range and a trek to Ledar. The trek from Manang to Ledar is an uphill climb. At an altitude of 4,250 m, Ledar is a small village with beautiful views of the landscape and unique flora and fauna.

Walking through the trekking trails leading to Thorong La Pass, you will head to Ledar. You will pass through many beautiful places on the way like the Marshyangdi River Valley and the Jarsang Khola. Finally reaching Ledar, you will find the vegetation getting more sparse. We will rest at a tea house for the day,

Day 09:Trek from Ledar to Pedi or High camp (4,600 m).

Maximum Altitude: 4,600 m

Trek Duration: 6-7 hours

From Ledar, we shall head to Pedi or High Camp at the altitude of 4600 meters. The trek is an uphill climb taking 6-7 hours.

On your way to High Camp, you will cross a river and head towards the settlement at Phedi. You can enjoy the mesmerizing views of the mountains and the landscapes from the trekking trails. You will finally reach High Camp and settle down for the day at a guest house.

Day 10: Trek from Phedi to MuktiNath (3,710 m).

Maximum Altitude: 5,416 m

Trek Duration: 7-8 hours

Leaving Phedi, we shall trek for a long time today. Today we will reach the highest point of our trek. On our way from Phedi to Muktinath, we will cross the Thorong La Pass at the altitude of 5,416 m

You should leave early morning to cross this pass as the afternoon winds are too strong. We shall cross the pass before noon while enjoying the picturesque views of the mountains.

Crossing the pass, we will make our descent back to the Muktinath Temple. The temple in the lower Mustang region is a popular pilgrimage site.

Day 11: Mukti Nath to Tatopani via Jomsom (2,750 m)

Maximum Altitude: 2,750 m

Trek Duration: 1-2 hours

Drive Duration: 4-5 hours

After a morning visit to the famous pilgrimage site in Muktinath, we shall take our blessings and head to Tatopani. There is no direct route to Tatopani so we will pass through Jomsom.

Trekking to Jomsom from Muktinath takes around an hour or two. From Jomsom, we will drive to Tatopani. You can relieve your stress and the tiredness from the trek bathing in the natural hot springs at Tatopani.

Day 12: Drive from Tatopani (1,190 m) to Pokhara.

Maximum Altitude: 1,190 m

Drive Duration: 7-8 hours

Today is the final day of our 12 days Annapurna Circuit Trek itinerary. Today we shall end our trek with a long drive from Tatopani to Pokhara. The drive will be a scenic and exciting one as you glance at the beautiful sceneries from your window. Reaching Pokhara we will part our ways and end our adventurous trip.

Best time for Annapurna Circuit Trek

Knowing what the Annapurna Circuit Trek has in store for you, you must be in a hurry to take this marvelous journey. Are you wondering what the best time for the trek is? Well, we have brought you all the information you need about the trek at all times of the year.

Autumn

Autumn is the most preferred and the best time of the year for you to take our 12 days Annapurna Circuit trek. Let us assure you that your 12 days of the trek will be filled with nothing but memories of the beautiful views and the adventures this autumn. Lasting through the months of September to November, you can enjoy the beautiful Autumn season in Annapurna Region. The favorable temperature and clear weather will give you the best trekking experience. With the skies being clear, you can also enjoy the best views of the mountain ranges.

Spring

Another great time for your 12 days Annapurna Circuit Trek is the spring season. Lasting through the months of March, April, and May, the spring season brings about a different side of the trekking trails. With beautiful flowers blooming and all the exotic flora and fauna out for you to witness. The months of March to May are great for your trekking experience. The moderate temperature and the beautiful views will leave you mesmerized and in love with the remote trekking trails of the Annapurna Circuit Trek.

Summer

Summer in Nepal is incorporated with the monsoon season. This means summer consists of heavy rains. The summer season lasts through the months of June, July, and August. There are some great views during the summer season like the waterfalls. You will get to see many waterfalls during your trek during the summer season. As long as you check the weather and travel during the end of the summer season, the rainfall will be much lighter. Be prepared if you are trying to trek during summer. The roads may be slippery during the rain and the rainfall can cancel your plans or the day so prepare yourselves for these situations.

Winter

As for the winter season, the winter around the Annapurna Region gets pretty cold. Lasting through the months of December, January, and February, winter can be pretty harsh. Attempting the Annapurna Circuit Trek during the winter is not recommended. However, if you are trying to trek in the winter, try to trek during the winter so the temperature is not overwhelmingly cold. Prepare yourself mentally and physically. Carry all the warm clothes and other warm essentials for the trip.

Tips for your 12 days Annapurna Circuit Trek

  • You should be physically and mentally prepared for your trek. It is best if you indulge in some cardio and physical exercises prior to your trek. This helps build some stamina.
  • Proper acclimatization is important to protect yourself from altitude sickness. Also, you should stay hydrated to avoid any altitude sickness.
  • You should carry a water bottle for yourself. Also, don’t forget to get some water purifier pills with you to avoid any infections from the water.
  • Thorong La Pass is a difficult part of the trek. You should cross this pass before noon so the winds don’t get too strong. However, as it is at a high altitude take your time.
  • You should try to carry your own medicines for yourself. It is safer to keep your own medicines.

title: Mardi Himal Trek in December
excerpt: Annapurna Region is quite a popular trekking destination among the tourists. This region offers many exotic treks that take you on an adventure in the Himalayas. Some popular trekking routes are…
html:
Annapurna Region is quite a popular trekking destination among the tourists. This region offers many exotic treks that take you on an adventure in the Himalayas. Some popular trekking routes are Annapurna Circuit Trek, Annapurna Base Camp trek, and many more.

This is an idle trekking destination for nature and adventure lovers. You can find both short and long day treks in this region. The difficulty of the trek depends on the type of routes you will be visiting.

Among various treks, Mardi Himal trek is one of the most visited routes over the years. This trek is quite popular among foreigners as well as locals of the country. It lasts about 5 to 7 days in the Annapurna region.

This is a short but spectacular trek that wins the heart of the trekker’s with its beauty. Are you wondering whether you can do Mardi Himal Trek in December? Well, the answer is Yes, you can do Mardi Himal Trek in December.

Any time of the year is suitable for Mardi Himal Trek but each month has its own benefits and disadvantages. If you are planning to visit Mardi Himal during December then it is possible.

Winter season is the off-season time of the year. Due to cold weather and snowfall trekking during this month is quite not popular. However, December is the beginning month of the Winter season. Thus, there are fewer chances of snowfall during early and mid-December.

Traveling during this month is a great choice for peace lovers. The trails are quiet and not much crowded giving you all the privacy you want. Also, the gorgeous view of various magnificent peaks will add color to your trip.

The weather is dry during early December but has snowfall in high altitude by the end. The trails and forests covered in white look mesmerizing to the eyes. There is also a low chance of trails being blocked due to snow in December.

If you are planning to trek to Mardi Himal in December then you need to make proper plans and preparations. Bringing along necessary clothing and equipment is a must.

Look out for weather reports before and during your trek. To know more about Mardi Himal Trek in December read further below.

About Mardi Himal Trek

Mardi Himal trek lies in the Annapurna region beneath the magnificent Machapuchare. This trek is the newly discovered trek of the Annapurna region. The routes of Mardi Himal were opened for trekking in the year 2012.

Though the routes of Mardi Himal are new to the trekking world. It has been rapidly gaining popularity among trekkers. This is one of the best short treks in Nepal. Walking in this trail is not as hard as other treks in this region.

The route Mardi Himal Trek is a moderate level trek. This trek is suitable for both novice and professionals. There is no need for technical equipment on this trek.

The highest point of this trek is Mardi Himal Base Camp. It is at an altitude of 4,500 m above sea level. At this height, altitude sickness is considered common amongst trekkers. The scenic vista of the magical landscapes and mountain peaks is amazing.

Some peaks seen on the routes of Mardi Himal trek are Annapurna, Machapuchhre, etc. You will also be passing through the enchanting forest of rhododendron, pines, oaks, etc.

Many ethnic communities are found in the villages of this region. They live together in harmony and peace. Some of these communities are Thakali, Magar, Limbu, Sherpa, etc.

But the majority of people found in these areas belong to the Gurung Community. This trek is a mixture of culture and biodiversity. Passing through the Gurung villages you get to learn about their lifestyle and behavior.

To trek in the routes of Mardi Himal, you will be needing some special permits. Without them, you cannot complete the trek.

Highlights of Mardi Himal Trek in December

  • Visiting cultural and traditional villages
  • Exploring the Annapurna region
  • The striking view of various mountain peaks
  • Clear skies and dry weather
  • Trails covered in snow

Outline Itinerary

Day 1: Arrival at Kathmandu

Day 2: Drive from Kathmandu to Pokhara (7/8 hrs, 827 m)

Day 3: Drive from Pokhara to Kande (1 hrs, 1,700 m) then trek to Deurali (2.5 to 3 hrs, 2,100 m)

Day 4: Trek from Deurali to Low Camp ( 8 hrs, 2,990 m)

Day 5: Trek from Low Camp to High Camp ( 4 to 5 hours, 3,580 m)

Day 6: High Camp to Mardi Himal Base (4,500 m) then back to high camp and trek to Siding (1,850 m)

Day 7: Drive back to Pokhara (3 to 4 hrs)

Day 8: Drive back to Kathmandu (1,400 m)

Day 9: Departure

Weather condition of Mardi Himal Trek in December

Winter season is not much preferred by trekkers due to the harsh weather conditions in the Himalayas. The months from December to February fall under this season. The season of winter is dry in the Mardi region.

December is the first month of the winter season. Thus the season is just beginning making Mardi Himal Trek in December possible. In the earlier week of December, it is not much cold but as the weeks pass by, cold gradually increases.

There are very few chances of snowfall occurring in December. So you don’t have to worry about road blockage being a problem. The chances of snowfall are less till mid-week of December.

Even though it is the season of cold the skies are clear and walks during days are warm. Walking under the sun viewing the beautiful scenarios under the clear blue sky is a dream come true.

However, the nights are cold and as you climb high in elevation it gets colder. So, carrying warm clothes is highly recommended during these months.

The temperature of Mardi Himal Trek in December

In Nepal, there are three regions: Terai, Himalayas, and the hills. Each region has a different climatic condition and poses a different temperature. During Summer, the temperature in Terai exceeds above 40 degrees. While in the Himalayas it ranges up to 20 degrees max.

Likewise, the temperature during winter is higher in the Himalaya region in comparison to other regions. As winter is starting from the month of December. The temperature ranges from 9 to 12 degrees during the daytime.

As the night falls the temperature can drop up to -5 degrees. It is cold during the evenings and early mornings. With every 1,000 m climb the temperature drops by 5 degrees.

Climbing in the Himalayas during December is quite harsh and challenging due to the drop in temperature. But no matter how cold the weather is the sun will keep you warm during the day.

Mardi Himal Trek In December- Difficulties

Even though this trek is not situated at a higher altitude compared to other treks of this region. You still might face various difficulties that can make your journey harsh and thrilling.

Written below are a few of the Mardi Himal Trek Difficulties in December:

Route Difficulty

The route of Mardi Himal is a moderate level trek that requires a lot of stamina from the trekkers. The routes might not be much harsh for walking. But still, there are many up and downhill walks you have to do for this trek.

The uneven and exotic routes make the walk more thrilling and challenging. Also carrying a backpack and making the uphill climb might drag you down. So you need to have huge stamina to complete this trek.

Altitude Sickness

Altitude Sickness is common when trekking in elevation above 4,000 m altitude. Suffering from Acute mountain sickness is unavoidable in the high Himalayas. Each body gives a different reaction to altitude sickness. It might be hard to cope for some people while some can adjust without much hassle.

In this trek, you will be reaching an altitude of 4,500 m above sea level. Thus suffering from altitude sickness is common in Mardi Himal Trek. You should not panic but inform your guide immediately if you see any symptoms of this sickness.

Some of the common symptoms of Altitude sickness are:

  • Headache
  • Loss of appetite
  • Trouble in falling asleep
  • Vomiting
  • Nausea
  • Dizziness
  • Short of breath and many more

Do not hide if you have doubts about suffering from this inform someone directly. If not treated in proper time it can be risky for your life. Thus, walk slowly, take rest, and drink plenty of water.

Duration

This is a few days trek that begins from the city of Pokhara. You will be staying in this region for about 6 to 7 days. In these few days, you will be walking for about 6 to 7 hours a day.

If this is your first trek then walking up and downhill for 7 hours can be tiring and challenging. Thus it is better to not rush the trek and take it smoothly. As for experienced trekkers, these routes can be quite easy to walk.

To complete this trek, you need to be physically and mentally fit. It requires a lot of energy so physical training is a must on this trek.

Reasons to do Mardi Himal Trek in December

Visiting Mardi Himal to watch the beauty of nature is not the only reason. There are other reasons as well to do this trek in December. Some are written below:

Privacy

As December is the off-season month of the year. The routes are less crowded with trekkers during this time. You can get all the privacy you want without much trouble.

If you love walking in silence while viewing the beauty of nature. Then trekking in December is a great choice. The coldest months are yet to begin so the weather will be tolerable.

Also, you won’t be disturbed by passing people. So it gives you plenty of time to enjoy the beauty of nature.

Proper Accommodation

As only a few people visit this region during December. You get to enjoy the warm welcome and proper hospitality. While visiting in peak seasons you usually don’t get the room of your choice.

But in December it’s quite opposite, as most of the room is vacant you have plenty of choices. You also don’t have to wait in long queues to use the bathroom.

If you got bargaining skills it might come handy during this month. As you might even get heavy discounts with the right words.

Tips for Trekking to Mardi Himal in December

Here are a few tips you can follow when trekking to Mardi Himal:

Pack Proper Clothes

Packing proper clothing is quite necessary while traveling to the Himalayas. As you are traveling during December it is necessary to pack warm clothes for this trek. As you climb high in elevation it tends to get colder. So gloves, socks, jackets, trek pants, and bodywarmer are essential.

As the temperature drops during the night time. You need to carry sleeping bags to keep you warm. As the blankets in the hotel might not keep you warm.

Carry light Backpacks

The main priority is to carry as light as possible. You should only carry things that are necessary for the trek. Carrying extra can be a burden when traveling up and downhills.

The load can slow down your pace and make you tire down quickly. You should make a list of things that you will bring along in this trek. Thus, it makes packing easier.

Carry Water Bottle and water purification tablets

Carrying your own water bottle is very necessary when trekking in the high mountains. As there might not be shops in some parts of the routes. Also, mineral water bottles are expensive in higher regions.

If you bring your own bottle then you can refill it from the hotel or water station along the way. This is when water purification tablets come in handy. You might be unknown about the source of water. So you can use the tablet to kill harmful bacterias.

Drinking plenty of water is compulsory in this trek. As you will be sweating a lot so keeping your body hydrated is quite necessary. Don’t forget to refill your bottle before beginning the trek.

Proper Training

To finish the trek you need to be physically and mentally fit. You should have strong stamina to make the up and downhill walk each day. You can increase your stamina by doing various physical exercises.

Such as running, swimming, short hikes, walking about 3 to 4 hours a day, and many more. These exercises can be done on your own. You don’t need to visit the gym or hire a trainer.

  • Best Time For Annapurna Circuit Trek

Final Say

Mardi Himal Trek is an exciting trek in the beautiful Annapurna region. This trek can be done by both novice and experienced trekkers. You can make this your first trek. As the routes of this trek are quite easy compared to other treks.

Mardi Himal trek in December is quite an adventure you don not want to miss out on. So, if you are trekking during December visiting by early or mid-December would be a good choice.

Have a great time and make great memories.

title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek In January
excerpt: Trekking through the small snow-covered trekking trails enjoying the beautiful view of the snow called mountains. As you walk on the trails, your body warms up and the cold breeze of wind keeps you…
html:
Trekking through the small snow-covered trekking trails enjoying the beautiful view of the snow called mountains. As you walk on the trails, your body warms up and the cold breeze of wind keeps you cool. This is what trekking in Annapurna Base Camp in January feels like.

Annapurna Base Camp Trekking has become a very popular trekking destination in Nepal. It is mostly because of the magnificent views of the mountains along the routes and the destination. Every company and sources say that these treks are best done in the Spring and Autumn. But how is the Annapurna Base Camp trek in January really like?

Annapurna Base Camp trek in January may sound skeptical but it is a great time for seeing the best sides of the routes. If you are going to see the mountains, isn’t winter the best time? The mountain ranges in the Annapurna Region are all blindingly glowing with the thick snow on them. Isn’t that what you expect to see on your Annapurna Base Camp trek?

Our 13 days Annapurna Base Camp Trek starts from your arrival at the airport in Kathmandu. Picking you up and transferring you to the hotel in Kathmandu for your rest so you are prepared for your trek is our first priority. The next day is the beginning of our journey together. We shall drive to Pokhara comfortably on a tourist bus for the next 7-8 hours. Reaching there, we will rest for the day at Pokhara where you can explore the beautiful nightlife of the city.

The next day begins with another drive to Nayapul. Reaching Nayapul, our trek finally starts from Nayapul to Ulleri. The trek continues from Ulleri to Ghorepani. We will rest there and start the new day with the highlight of the trip. We will enjoy the sunrise view from Poon Hill Viewpoint early morning.

Leaving Poonhill, we will head towards Tadapani. From Tadapani, we will head straight to Annapurna Base Camp. on the way, we will stop at Chorong and the Himalaya. We shall explore the Annapurna Base Camp and then head down to Bamboo and spend the night there. A short trek from Bamboo is the Jhinu natural hot springs. You can replenish your energy there. Our trek will soon come to an end as we head back to Kathmandu with a long drive from Nayapul to Pokhara and Pokhara to Kathmandu.

Yes, the temperature and the weather are cold, but you can fight that obstacle with proper preparation. So let us enjoy the true beauty of the Annapurna Base Camp Trek in January.

Highlights of Annapurna Base Camp in January

  • You get to experience snowfall at the Annapurna region surrounded by mountains
  • The hills are still green with beautiful vegetation and views
  • You can see the glorious snow-capped peaked glowing with the thick snow
  • Experience the local Gurung culture and lifestyle
  • Magnificent views of the mountains over the clouds
  • Less crowded routes and pretty clear weather
  • Night skies are very beautiful with a starry night view

Weather and temperature in January

January is the middle of winter in Nepal. In the Annapurna region, the weather will be daily clear during this time. The peaks will face a lot of snowfall all through December and some in January as well. However, there is only a slight chance of snowfall in the lower regions of the trekking routes. Rainfall is not a problem during January. You won’t have to worry about rainfall during your Annapurna Base Camp Trek in January.

As for the temperature in January, it is pretty cold in January. However, there is a bright sun during the day. You won’t be cold as you will be trekking so it will end up being the perfect temperature for trekking. The mornings and nights are kind of cold but as you start trekking, you will feel the heat and cold making the perfect time for trekking.

The temperature in the day ranges from around 5 degrees to 10 degrees celsius. This is not very cold and as the sun is up, the temperature is pretty warm during the day. However, the nights can be pretty cold as the temperature drops rapidly. The night temperature in the Annapurna region drops below 0 degrees celsius to up to -10 degrees celsius.

So be prepared for the cold nights with some high-quality warm clothes and sleeping bags. The nights may be cold but the night skies are beautiful during January. You can see the starry night sky from the routes in the month of January. However, be sure to keep yourself warm during your trek in January.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Annapurna base camp trek Itinerary

Day 1: Arrive at Kathmandu airport and transfer to the hotel.

Day 2: Drive 6-7 hours to Pokhara (820 m) by tourist bus.

Day 3: Drive 4-5 hours to Nayapul (1,010 m) and trek to Ulleri (1,920 m).

Day 4: Trek 4-5 hours to Ghorepani (2,860 m).

Day 5: Early morning hike to Poon Hill (3,210 m) and then 6-7 hours trek to Tadapani (2,610 m).

Day 6: Trek 5-6 hours to Chorong (2,170 m).

Day 7: Trek 6-7 hours to Himalaya (2,920 m).

Day 8: Trek 6-7 hours to Annapurna Base Camp (4,130 m).

Day 9: Trek back 6-7 hours to Bamboo (2,345 m).

Day 10: Trek 5-6 hours to Jhinu hot spring (1,780 m).

Day 11: Trek 5-6 hours to Nayapul (1,010 m) and drive to Pokhara.

Day 12: 7-8 hours Drive back to Kathmandu (1,345 m) by tourist bus.

Day 13: Transfer to International Airport for your onward destination.

Food and accommodation in January

Annapurna Base Camp Trek in January is great for the views and favorable for trekking. But what about the food and accommodation during the trek in January? January is considered an offseason for trekking in the area so yes, you will be getting some cheap prices. However, the food and accommodation in the month of January may be either too beneficial for you or disadvantageous.

Accommodation in January is the same as any other time of the year. You will be spending your nights at a tea house in the location. The rooms will be twin sharing bedrooms with an attached bathroom. You will be provided with warm bed sheets. However, it is always better for you to bring your sleeping bags in case the temperature drops too low at night. The rooms are not air-conditioned.

You will find tea houses every 2-hour walk distance from the first one. Being an off-season there are chances of fewer tea houses being open. They may charge you less during the winter season. The less crowded routes will benefit you definitely as you will have enough rooms throughout your trek. The only downside is that most tea houses may not open because of the winter.

As for the food, the tea houses will serve you a balanced diet. But since it is the winter season, you will mostly have pickled vegetables, and the variety of food decreases. Despite the lack of varieties, the tea houses will provide you a balanced diet for your trek. For the drinks, you will get coffee and tea easily. But it’s better to carry some tea bags on your own.

  • Best Time to Trek Annapurna Base Camp
  • Annapurna Base Camp Trek Difficulty – Base Camp Adventure
  • Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return

Annapurna Base Camp Trek Difficulties in January

Trekking in the winter season is a fun activity as the temperature does not make you burn up on the trek. However, Annapurna Base Camp Trek in January has some difficulties you will have to overcome. The major difficulties you will be facing during your Annapurna Base Camp Trek in January are listed below:

Weather difficulties

Yes, the weather in January is mostly clear. The days are sunny making the temperature just right for trekking. However, as you head up on a higher altitude during your trek, the weather may not be as stable. Higher altitudes tend to have sudden weather changes. In the winter, there may be snowfall and some chances of rainfall from the rainclouds traveling from the higher regions. So be careful and always be prepared for some sudden weather changes on your trek.

Temperature

Another difficulty you are sure to come across trekking in the winter season is the temperature. The days are fine for trekking but the night is extremely cold in the winter season. Especially in the Annapurna region as the wind travels from the mountains, the nights are windy and cold. The temperature may drop down to below -10 degrees as the altitude increases. So be prepared and carry lightweight sleeping bags that can handle these low temperatures.

Altitude sickness

Annapurna Base Camp trek takes you to the maximum altitude of 4,130 m. Although it is not that high, there are chances of you getting altitude sickness during your trek. This is one of the difficulties you may face during your trek in January as the cold contributes to the symptoms. However, you can easily tackle this difficulty by taking proper precautions like acclimatization, staying hydrated. If worse comes to worst, you can always take medication for altitude sickness.

Remote area and trekking routes

With the popularity of the Annapurna Base Camp trek, the routes have been improved a lot from the past. Half of the trekking routes have been motorized. However, there are still a lot of remote trekking trails for Annapurna Base Camp trekking. So it is still a remote and off the road trekking in most areas. Therefore, you will have some difficulties during your trek due to the rough trekking routes and the climbs and descents. Be sure to be physically prepared for this journey.

Essentials for Annapurna Base Camp Trek in January

Since January is in the middle of the winter season, the temperature can drop quite low at night. So it is better to be fully prepared to tackle the cold winter nights. Unlike the summer and autumn seasons, the winter seasons can get pretty cold at night and also in the morning. So if you are packing you should always prepare layers as the temperature rises during the day.

Here are the basic essentials you will need for the Annapurna Base Camp Trek in January:

● Clothing

For your Annapurna Base Camp Trek in January, it is best to wear layers. So, make sure to pack your warm clothes in layers. The nights are extremely cold, but the trekking hours will be hot. So if you are wearing layers, you can dress appropriately for the cold mornings and the trekking hours during the day. However, make sure to carry some warm clothes as mentioned below:

  • Lightweight quick-drying shirts
  • Lightweight warm fur jackets
  • Warm inner clothes
  • 2-3 sets of underwear
  • Set of windproof clothes
  • Waterproof clothes in case of snowfall
  • Gloves and mittens for the cold

● Footwear

Ad for the footwear, you will need some warm footwear as well. However, as the trek consists of walking for about 5-6 hours a day, make sure to wear comfortable shoes for the trek. Some basic requirements during the trek for footwear are :

  • Hiking boots
  • Trekking boots
  • Warm socks (extra pairs)
  • Sandals

● Backpack

The cold weather in the month of January may require you to carry some extra stuff during your trek. But this is all for your own safety and preparedness for any situation. Here are some important things to carry in your backpack:

  • Annapurna Base Camp Trek Map
  • A headlamp or a flashlight
  • Backup chargers for your phone and camera
  • Energy Bars
  • Some hot packets
  • Lightweight but warm sleeping bag
  • Toiletries
  • Whistle in case of any emergencies

● Medical necessities

During your Annapurna Base Camp Trek in January, your guide and the crew will carry most of the essential medical supplies. So you can rest easy. But if you can you should carry some of your own medical supplies. You will know your body better than others. So carry the basic medical supplies that you know works for you.

  • Pain medication
  • Altitude sickness medicines
  • Cold medicines

Some tips for Annapurna base camp trek in January

Here are some tips for you to have the best time on your Annapurna Base Camp Trek in January while fighting through any difficulties.

  • Since it’s cold at night during January, make sure to bring sleeping bags that can easily withstand -10 degrees celsius.
  • Most of the tea houses on the trekking routes may not be open all the time. So it is always a good idea to carry your own water bottles. Also, carry some water purifier tablets while you’re at it.
  • Since the tea houses are far from each other and it is cold you can also carry some tea bags and a thermos for instant tea and coffee.
  • Make sure to bring layered clothing. It works best for winter. As the morning is cold and the day slowly gets warmer, layers will provide you with comfort for each time of the day.
  • The cold sometimes acts as a catalyst for altitude sickness. So keep yourself warm. In addition to that, stay hydrated and take proper acclimatization throughout your trek to not get any altitude sickness.
  • Don’t forget to bring your warm jackets and clothes. It’s always better to carry some warm innerwear for the night as well.
  • Do not forget to bring your own medicines. You know your body the best so bring some meds that work for you.

FAQs

1. What is the highest point of the Annapurna Base Camp Trek?

The highest point of the Annapurna Base Camp Trek is the Annapurna Base Camp at the altitude of 4,130 m

2. What is the alternative route for Annapurna Base Camp Trek?

You can also choose the alternative route for Annapurna Base Camp trek which is a short trek of 7 days. The trek takes you to the Annapurna Base Camp passing through the Machhapuchhre Base Camp.

3. Is Annapurna Base Camp Trek in January difficult?

Annapurna Base Camp Trek in January is a moderate level trek. If you are physically and mentally prepared, you can easily complete this trek. There are not many difficult routes or trekking trails. The weather and temperature may cause some difficulties but with proper preparations, you can easily complete this trek.

4. How much does Annapurna Base Camp Trek cost?

The standard 13 days Annapurna Base Camp Trek costs around USD 825 per person. This includes transportation during the trek, the guides, and porters along with the food and accommodations.

5. Is Annapurna Base Camp Trek without a guide possible?

If you are confident about the trekking routes, yes. You can complete the Annapurna Base Camp Trek without a guide. As long as you can easily understand the map and find your way, your trek without a guide is possible. But in the winter season, it is recommended to have a guide with you during your treks due to the weather changes.

title: Annapurna Circuit Trek in December
excerpt: Annapurna Circuit Trek is one of the incredible adventures in the world. The pristine landscapes of the Annapurna region is ideal for trekking in the Autumn and Spring. However, trekking the…
html:
Annapurna Circuit Trek is one of the incredible adventures in the world. The pristine landscapes of the Annapurna region is ideal for trekking in the Autumn and Spring. However, trekking the Annapurna Circuit in December is also possible. Trekkers will find a unique perspective of the region in December.

You will pass through the scenic landscapes of the Annapurna Conservation Area (ACA), home to abundant flora and fauna of the region. The Poon Hill viewpoint provides incredible views of the sunrise overlooking the snow-capped mountains including Annapurna I-IV, Manaslu, Mt. Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, and others.

Moreover, this trek also lets you explore the cultural settlements of Gurung, Tamang, and Magar communities. You will stay at cozy tea houses and lodges along the trail. The trails also pass through green hills, serene rivers, pristine waterfalls, vast valleys and other beautiful landscapes. If you love trekking along the quiet and peaceful trails, this trek is ideal for you.

Furthermore, trekking in the month of December is a challenge for adventure seekers. Crossing the majestic “Thorong La Pass (5,416 m)” will test you to the core. Trekking in late December comes with a high risk of accidents and injuries. Hence, if you are planning to trek, you should always choose early December as it is a favorable time for trekking.

Read further to know more about the Annapurna Circuit Trek in December and other relevant information.

Significant Highlights of the Trip

  • Awe-inspiring views of Mt. Annapurna, Mt. Dhaulagiri, Mt. Manaslu, and others snow-capped mountains
  • Gorgeous sunrise from Poon Hill viewpoint
  • Crossing the adventurous Thorong La Pass (5,416 m), which is the highest point of the trek
  • Passing by the natural landscapes of the Annapurna Conservation Area
  • Exploring the incredible flora and fauna of the Annapurna region
  • Visiting the famous pilgrimage site of Muktinath Temple
  • An opportunity to explore the culture, heritage, and lifestyle of the region
  • Exploring the Kali Gandaki Gorge, the deepest gorge in the world
  • Incredible hospitality of the local people
  • Relaxing hot water bath at Tatopani
  • Tasting the delicious cuisine

Outline Itinerary – Annapurna Circuit Trek

Day 01: Kathmandu to Bulbule

Day 02: Bulbule to Chamje

Day 03: Chyamje to Bagarchhap

Day 04: Bagarchhap to Chame

Day 05: Chame to Pisang

Day 06: Pisang to Manang

Day 07: Acclimatization day in Manang.

Day 08: Manang to Ledar

Day 09: Ledar to Pedi or High camp

Day 10: Phedi to Mukti Nath

Day 11: Mukti Nath to Jomsom Via Kagbeni.

Day 12: Drive from Jomsom to Tatopani Natural hot spring.

Day 13: Trek down to Ghorepani

Day 14: Trek to Poon Hill – trek down to Ghorepani and Nayapul – back to Pokhara.

Day 15: Back to Kathmandu.

How Difficult is Trekking the Annapurna Circuit in December?

Annapurna Circuit Trek is moderately challenging. The trek can be quite challenging for beginners who have not trekked the higher altitude before. Trekking the Annapurna Circuit in December is difficult but not impossible.

However, you should avoid trekking the Annapurna Circuit in late December as it comes with a lot of risks. Hence, with proper packing and preparation, you can trek in early December. Some of the major difficulties along the trail are as follows:

Altitude sickness

The Annapurna Circuit Trek in December is a high altitude trek hence the risk of altitude sickness is quite high along the trail. Minimal oxygen and air pressure causes Acute mountain sickness (AMS) in the high altitude region. Headache, nausea, dizziness, vomiting, tiredness, loss of appetite, and shortness of breath are some of the symptoms of altitude sickness.

Moreover, if not treated properly the altitude sickness can lead to severe forms of High-altitude Pulmonary Edema (HAPE), and High-altitude Cerebral Edema (HACE). You can descend to the lower altitudes until the symptoms of altitude sickness subsides.

Furthermore, you should get medical help if you show the symptoms of altitude sickness along the trail. Altitude sickness is prevalent in the higher altitude region as the amount of oxygen in the air gets thinner in the higher altitude.

Heavy snowfall

The weather remains perfect in the lower altitudes along the trail in December. But, the higher altitude regions can experience some occasional snowfall which makes the trails slippery and hence challenging. But, some trekkers might find it adventurous and fun too.

Furthermore, the icy paths and trails during December makes the trek slippery. Most of the trails in the higher altitude get blocked because of snow. The Thorung La Pass (5,416 m), which is the highest point of the trek, is quite tough for trekkers to cross. There are thick layers of snow along the trail to the majestic Thorung La Pass.

Rugged trails

The Annapurna Circuit Trek in December passes through the rugged terrains of the Annapurna region. Hence, the trek is quite challenging for first-time trekkers. Trekkers should take part in strength, stamina, and endurance training. You should indulge in hiking, cycling, swimming, jogging, paddling, and other cardiovascular exercises before the start of the trek.

Annapurna Circuit Weather in December

Annapurna region weather in December varies according to the altitude of the place. The weather remains warmer below the altitude of 4,000 m; the higher regions are comparatively chilly. Annapurna Circuit Trek in December has a temperature of around 5-10 degrees which gradually decreases as you go up the higher altitude.

Moreover, the temperatures in the night can drop around 0 to -5 degrees. You will get moderate weather at the beginning of December in the Annapurna region. There are ideal weather conditions in the lower elevations. You will get clear skies all along the trail and you can observe the snow-capped mountains in all its glory. With proper packing and preparation, you can trek the Annapurna Circuit Trek in December with ease.

Furthermore, you should not forget to pack warm clothes, thermals, crampons, and a trekking pole for the trek in December. Overall, the weather in the early part of December is ideal for the trek in the Annapurna region.

Food and Accommodations During the Trek

There will be several tea houses available along the Annapurna Circuit in December. You will stay in the local tea houses along the trail. You will find many other options in the lower areas including standard hotels. However, you will not have many options in the higher areas other than the basic and limited teahouses.

Food

You will get the basic Nepalese dish along the Annapurna Circuit Trek in December. Dal Bhat which consists of rice, dal (pulses), spinach, lentils, vegetables, pickles, gundruk, and meat is quite common in the tea houses. You will also get served noodles, pasta, burger, porridge, bread, sandwich, egg, and others.

Besides that, potato, cauliflower, broccoli, spinach, beans, etc are some of the most common vegetables found in the teahouses. You will also get served hot beverages including tea, coffee, garlic soup, Rhododendron tea, lemon tea, and others. You will also find various alcoholic beverages such as beer, rum, wine, etc but you should avoid them while trekking.

Accommodation

The Annapurna Circuit Trek in December is a teahouses trek and you will stay in most tea houses with basic facilities. December is an off-season in the region and hence you will find teahouses with ease as they remain mostly empty.

Therefore, you will get the best accommodation and all the facilities available. The room has twin beds, a mattress, blanket, pillow, and a cupboard. You can find an attached bathroom in some of the teahouses.

Moreover, you should bring your toiletries during your Annapurna Circuit Trek because you won’t find them in the teahouses. As December is an off-season trek, you will also find the best accommodations at a bargain price.

Pros and Cons of Trekking the Annapurna Circuit in December

December is the first month of winter in Nepal. You will not find any extreme harsh conditions in the Annapurna Circuit Trek in early December. Therefore, you will get to experience the winter wonderland along the trail. December also means empty trails, which makes for a quiet and peaceful adventure in the Himalayas.

Moreover, you can observe the beautiful snowy mountains and landscapes. There are snowy glaciers, icefalls in the region which makes the trek more adventurous. The breathtaking views of the snow-capped mountains and stable weather conditions is the highlight of the trek.

However, trekking the Annapurna Circuit in late December is quite challenging as the conditions worsens and the temperatures drop significantly. You might have to face heavy snowfall. This increases the risk of slippery trails, avalanches, and snow covered trails. Hence, it is generally recommended to trek the Annapurna Circuit only in the early parts of December.

Do You Need a Guide for Annapurna Circuit Trek in December?

Annapurna Circuit Trek is a challenging trek even during the peak seasons. Thus, trekking in December is even more difficult. Annapurna Circuit is more comfortable with the help of a guide in December. Hiring a guide will make the journey easier and more comfortable. A guide will help you along the Annapurna Circuit by providing the best and easiest route to reach your destination.

Guides assures your safety and security and also motivates you when you feel low during your trek. During the trek, you can take the help of the local people for interacting with the local people as they act as a translator. Hiring a guide will help you throughout the journey. The uncertain weather and temperature during December can cause emergencies. Hence, hiring a guide is essential for trekking in December.

Moreover, you can also hire a porter for the Annapurna Circuit trek in December. Porters can carry up to 10 kgs of your heavy load. They will cost you around 15-20 dollars per day and a guide will charge you around 20-25 dollars per day. You can also bargain and add tips based on their service.

Things to Consider For the Annapurna Circuit Trek in December

Some of the things you should consider for the trek in December are as follows:

Acclimatization

Altitude sickness is a major problem in the high altitude Annapurna Circuit Trek in December. Proper acclimatization and hydration is essential even for experienced trekkers. Trekkers should also walk at a slow but steady pace to tackle the risk of altitude sickness.

Some of altitude sickness include nausea, headache, vomiting, loss of appetite, shortness of breath, and others. If not treated properly and in time, it can turn fatal. Hence, trekkers should take necessary precautions by descending to lower altitudes and evacuating even if necessary.

Trekking gears

Annapurna Circuit Trek in December requires proper packing and preparation with the right gear and equipment. The correct trekking gear will provide a safe and comfortable trekking experience. Trekking pants, windcheaters, trekking jackets, waterproof trekking shirts, full sleeve shirts, down jackets, thermals, trekking boots, are some of the essential trekking gear.

Hydration

Staying hydrated is essential for the high altitude Annapurna Circuit Trek in December. Trekkers will not get enough oxygen levels for the trek which can cause altitude sickness. Getting hydrated will help to provide oxygen in your body.

Moreover, you can carry water in a hot water thermos along the trek so that you can drink water whenever necessary. However, the tap water is not suitable for drinking on the trail. Hence, you can use water purification tablets or boil the water during the trek.

Fitness levels

A basic level of fitness is essential along the trek. Trekkers should trek around 4-7 hours every day covering around 160km to 230km. You need to cross the majestic Thorong La pass (5,416 m) on a snow-covered trail. The rigorous climb through Thorong Phedi will test you to the core.

Thus, trekkers should train with the aim of trekking 7 hours a day. You can take part in various fitness training exercises before the trek. Trekkers should also take proper acclimatization measures and hydrate regularly to avoid altitude sickness during the trek.

Travel Insurance

You should get proper travel insurance for the Annapurna Circuit Trek in December. The rugged and remote landscapes of the region have the risk of many injuries and emergencies. Trekkers should get Travel insurance that covers flight delays, injuries, accidents, theft, loss of luggage, and evacuations.

Training Routine for Trekking Annapurna Circuit in December

A basic training routine two to three months before the trek is essential. The training regime should focus on strength, endurance, stamina, and mental fitness.

Physical training

Physical training is essential to gain strength, endurance, and stamina. It also increases your fitness levels. You should train with the aim of trekking 5-6 hours in the rugged terrains of the Annapurna region.

Moreover, these training regimes will help trekkers gain muscles in the arm, shoulder, and back. Besides that, trekkers should also eat a carbohydrate and protein-rich diet. Overall, physical training is essential for all trekkers trekking the Annapurna Circuit Trek in December.

Cardiovascular exercises

Cardiovascular or aerobic exercises will help to increase oxygen levels in your body. Cycling, jogging, running, hiking, and other exercises will help you immensely along the trail. You will also get help in reducing the risk of tackling altitude sickness. Moreover, these exercises will help you reduce muscle strain, injuries and gain flexibility.

Mental preparation

Mental preparation will help you in staying motivated and having an overall positive attitude during the trek. You can take practice hikes in a hilly landscape. You can also get the overall idea of the trek by talking to veteran trekkers and conducting some research on the internet. Hence, mental preparation is essential for all trekkers.

Permits for the Trek

You will need Annapurna Conservation Area Project Permit (ACAP) and Trekker Information Management System Card (TIMS) for this trek. These permits are available in the Nepal Tourism Board’s office in Kathmandu and Pokhara.

The cost of the Annapurna Conservation Area Project Permit (ACAP) permit is NRS 3,000 for foreigners. Trekker Information Management System Card (TIMS) is essential for the safety of trekkers in the region. These identification cards will help to locate if anyone goes missing along the trail.

Moreover, the TIMS Card fee is Rs 300 per pax For SAARC nationals trekking in a group. Similarly, The TIMS Card fee is NRS 600 if you are a Free Individual Trekker. The TIMS card fees are NRS 1000 per pax For foreign trekkers trekking in a group. Similarly, the TIMS Card fee is Rs 2000 per pax if you are a Free Individual Trekker.

Essential Tips for the Trek

  • Always travel with a guide in December as heavy snowfalls make it challenging for trekkers in the region.
  • Carry Diamox tablets to tackle altitude sickness along the trail.
  • Acclimatization and regular hydration is essential along the trek.
  • Pre-book all the accommodation facilities along the trail.
  • Always check the weather forecast before the start of the trek.
  • Alcohol consumption is not recommended as it can cause dehydration and altitude sickness.
  • Walk gradually with regular breaks and rest in the middle.

Packing List for the Annapurna Circuit Trek in December

Clothing

  • Trekking boots
  • Thermal Underwear
  • Woolen gloves
  • Waterproof trekking pants
  • Pair of Sandals
  • Full Sleeve shirts
  • Down jacket
  • Warm hat
  • Socks
  • Windcheaters
  • Umbrella/ Raincoat

Toiletries

  • Soap
  • Shampoo
  • Sanitary pads/ Tampons
  • Toilet Paper
  • Toothpaste
  • Toothbrush
  • Lip Balm
  • Face towel
  • Moisturizer

First Aid

  • Diamox tablets
  • Anti-nauseant
  • Water purification tablets
  • Paracetamol
  • Imodium
  • Antibacterial sanitizer
  • Mosquito repellent

Accessories

  • Sunglasses
  • Power banks
  • Extra batteries
  • Solar chargers
  • Sleeping Bag
  • Playing Cards
  • Annapurna circuit Map
  • Notebook
  • Books or Kindle

Important documents

  • Passport
  • Travel permits
  • Travel insurance

The Final Say

The Annapurna Circuit Trek in December is an incredible experience. Trekkers will trek in the pristine landscapes of the Annapurna region. The trek takes you to the foothills of the Himalayas and serene villages of the Annapurna region. The trek will reward you with some of the amazing Himalayan mountain vista.

Moreover, trekking the Annapurna Circuit in late December is quite challenging as the “Thorong la Pass” gets covered in thick snow. Therefore, it is highly risky to trek in late December. Besides that, there are many chances of injuries, accidents, and delays in the latter parts of December. Hence, you should only trek the Annapurna Circuit in early December.
