title: Mardi Himal Trek 6 Days
excerpt: There are some places in the world that remain under the shadow of popular ones but once they get light they steal it all. Mardi Himal Trek is one such trek that has opened recently and gained large…
html:
There are some places in the world that remain under the shadow of popular ones but once they get light they steal it all. Mardi Himal Trek is one such trek that has opened recently and gained large visitors. There is one picturesque peak known as Mardi Peak( 5,587 m) beneath the Mt Machapuchare(Fishtail) in the Annapurna region. And this trek which is stretched until Mardi Base Camp is popular as the Mardi Himal Trek.

Opened in 2012 A.D, Mardi Himal Trek takes 6 to 8 days to complete depending upon the itinerary. Due to its short itinerary, it has gained a good rise in the trekking world. The flow of trekkers to this particular trek is increasing every year. People come to explore and trek on the less-battered trails of Mardi Himal Trek. This trek is mainly known for its iconic mountain views, picturesque villages, and ever-green hiking trails.

As a region of the Annapurna region, there is no doubt about the lack of mountain views. Mardi Himal Trek allows you to enjoy the wide panorama of Annapurna Massifs, Mt Machhapuchhre, Mt Manaslu, Mt Hiunchuli, Mt Dhaulagiri and Mardi Himal itself.

Mardi Himal Trek 6 Days is the shortest version of the short and sweet standard Mardi Himal trek. Inside six days, you will be able to enjoy all of the things of much-hyped Mardi Himal Trek. You will start by escaping the tourist hub of Nepal; Pokhara to enter the village’s scattered trails.

Along the trails, you will walk through many traditional settlements, densely forested trails towards the mountains in the North. Your one-week-time at the surrounding of Mardi Himal will be a blessing for you. You’ll be overwhelmed by the view and trekking experience of this trek.

There is more to know about Mardi Himal Trek 6 days like its itinerary, best time, food & accommodation, and difficulties. Read the below-written things to get more info on this trek before actually thinking of doing it.

Highlights of Mardi Himal Trek 6 Days

  • Experience the much-liked short trek of Nepal
  • The shortest way to encapture the beauties of Annapurna region; only 6 days
  • Amazing walkthrough diverse and green floras and vegetation
  • Trek and enter into various iconic Gurung and Tamang’s settlements
  • Vigilant watch of popular and iconic mountains of Nepal like Annapurna and its Massifs, Mt Machhapuchhre, Hiunchuli, Dhaulagiri and some more
  • Breathtaking dusk and dawn views throughout all of the days of the trek
  • Dramatic trek from Mera Low Camp To Mera Base Camp

Best time for Mardi Himal Trek

Mardi Himal Trek 6 days is one of the shortest treks in Nepal. On short trips like this, you can enjoy the benefit of planning such trips any time of a year. The shorter is the trip, lower is the weather fear, and vice versa. But still, this trek has to be scheduled at the right time of year to experience the best. The two best times or seasons for Mardi Himal Trek are Autumn and Spring which are also known as the peak trekking periods.

Autumn recedes from Mid-September to December and Spring from February to April in Nepal. You can plan anywhere between these months to have an amazing and memorable trekking experience. During these peak times, the skies tend to stay clear and so the mountains, the weather is rain & snow-fall free, temperatures are also quite warm to trek. On account of these perks, most of the adventurers like to trek Mardi Himal Trek or any other during Autumn and Spring.

On the contrary, Winter, and Summer, the two so-called off-seasons for trekking, have some good days for this trek. December to January is taken as the Winter season but the actual cold conditions start to appear only after Mid-December. So, you can plan Mardi Himal Trek 6 days before the Mid of December. From late-December, the weather turns harsher with cold temperatures and even heavy snowfall.

And Summer or Monsoon is a highly not-recommended season for trekking in Nepal. Summer is the hottest and wettest season of all with regular and longer rainfalls. June, July, and August are the three months of this season, and trails are mostly wet, muddy, and slippery. However, the Late-August or Early-June’s day does not get much rain and you can plan this trek at these times.

See, there are plenty of times in a year to plan and do Mardi Himal Trek. But, we highly suggest you pick the Autumn and Spring months, they are the unbeatables. And, if you are a peace lover you can opt for the other times of Summer and Monsoon season. On the whole, whenever you feel like it is time for the Mardi Himal, you just let us know, Base Camp Adventure, we will turn your trek one of the best trips of yours.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

How Difficult are the Mardi Himal Trek’s 6 days

To be very straight, Mardi Himal Trek is one of the easiest treks that you can do in Nepal. This is the trek that is most suitable for the beginners as the earlier starters have rated it slightly difficult. The difficulty level of this trek also corresponds to its duration; the lower the trekking days, higher will be the trekking hours. If you are a beginner who has not trekked in the Himalayas before, choose the Mardi Himal Trek 9 Days. On this trek, you will have three extra days where you can trek all relaxed.

If still, you want the shorter version of Mardi Himal Trek, you got to be mentally prepared for the longer trekking days. On the standard Mardi Trek of 9 days, you have to trek for 4 to 7 hours daily. Now, you can imagine how much you will be trekking on the 6 days Mardi trek. Walking most of the hours of a day is not an easy thing for beginners, you have to build sound health and fitness. Mardi Himal Trek 6 day’s trekking durations are not problems for the experienced trekkers.

Another difficulty for Mardi Himal Trekkers can be altitude sickness. When you are trekking anywhere in the Himalayas at an altitude of above 3,500 m, you will get one sure fear factor i.e Altitude sickness. And, Mardi Himal Trek takes you to the base camp of Mardi Himal which sits at an elevation of 4,200 m It is obvious to feel some minor difficulties in the air if you are in the high areas and not used to high altitudes. These minor problems can turn severe if no precautions are taken. Stay hydrated, take and trek it easily to avoid this mountain sickness.

There are no other real difficulties in the Mardi Himal Trek. If you are good with the duration of this trek and altitude sickness then no one can stop from completing it. Your Mardi Himal trek will pass quite easily with lots of good memories and experience to hold on.

Similar articles you may like:

  • Base Camp Adventure Mardi Himal Trek Cost
  • Mardi Himal Trek Map
  • Mardi Himal Trek Without Guide

Food and Accommodations during Mardi Himal Trek

You can get food and accommodation facilities quite easily on the Mardi Himal Trek. The trekking trails of this trek are scattered with enough lodges and treehouses for its trekkers. But remember you have to be smart during the peak season like Autumn and Spring when the lodges can get quickly filled. In such times, you have to pre-book to avoid possible problems. If you are with us on this trek, we can manage all of the things, you don’t need to worry a bit also.

The food items provided by the teahouses of this trek are varied from Local menu to Continental. From any cost between 3$ to 9$, you can have Porridge, Fried Rice, Pasta, Spaghetti, Cornbread, Dal-Bhat, and some more. Dal Bhat is the most popular of them which is also called the trekking food of Nepal. Moreover, you can get tea, coffee, energy drinks, etc in all of the lodges that you entered. Water is also good to drink but you can add purification tablets to remain on the safe side.

Accommodation facilities on the Mardi Himal Trek are very basic ones with comfortable two-person-sharing rooms with or without attached bathrooms. These rooms can cost anywhere from 3$ to 5$ per night. Room charge increases with the quality of the room and services that you are getting. There are facilities for mobile charging, hot water but you have to pay an extra charge for that.

Detailed Itinerary of Mardi Himal Trek 6 Days

Day 01: Drive from Pokhara to Kande and trek to Pothana/Deurali

Altitude Gain: 2,125 m

Drive Time: 1 hour

Trek Hours: 3 to 4 hours

You will hop in for the 1 hour drive to Kande after breakfast. That one hour to reach Kande will be a scenic ride where you can enjoy the distant green hills and white mountains. After reaching Kande, the walk of Mardi Himal Trek 6 days starts for the very first time. Trail to Deurali( Pothana) is an easy route through forested and terrains. Your lunch will be at the famous Australian Camp’s lodge(2,000 m) before you finally reach Pothana. Upon arrival at Pothana, you will check into the hotel for the overnight stay.

Day 02: Trek from Pothana to Low Camp

Altitude Gain: 3,150 m

Trek Hours: 3 to 4 hours

On the second day, you will start the trek with an aim to reach Low Camp before dusk. Today’s trekking trail will meet up with the main trekking trail of Annapurna Base Camp Trek at Forest Camp(2,500 m). From Forest Camp after lunch, you will make a gentle ascent amid the beautiful Rhododendron forest to reach the top of the ridge. Climbing that ridge, you reach your overnight destination, Low Camp(3,150 m). From the top of Low Camp, you will take enough mountain views of Mt Fishtail( Machhapuchhre), Mardi Himal and several others. You will check-in one of the three teahouses of Low camp.

Day 03: Trek from Low Camp to High Camp

Altitude Gain: 3,700 m

Trek Hours: 5 to 6 hours

You will start today’s trek a bit earlier than the prior days of Mardi Himal Trek. That is you have to cover a good distance today to reach High camp. Your six hour long trek will begin by racing towards Badal Danda(3,200 m). Most of today’s trek will make you enjoy the dense and green Alpine zone of Annapurna region. This part of forest is widely dotted with catchy Rhododendron forest. You may encounter several faunas like Danphe Pheasant also.

Then you will pass the ridge of Mardi Himal to reach High Camp. Mardi High Camp is a small pasture which is either filled with grass or else snow. The number of peaks observable from the High Camp makes a long list. Enjoy the timeless overnight at the High Camp after gazing at the awestrucking evening view of Annapurna Massifs and Mardi Himal.

Day 04: Trek to Mardi Base Camp and return to High Camp

Altitude Gain: 4,500 m

Trek Hours: 5 to 6 hours

The most important and demanding day of Mardi Himal Trek will start with an ascend towards Mardi High Camp. You will make continuous uphill climbs through rugged and uneven trails until the Mardi High Camp. Pushing yourself for several difficult but scenic hours ,you will reach the highest point of Mardi Himal Trek. The trekking will offer you nice views of landscapes and mountains. But, the views that are sightable from the High Camp are something else. You can enjoy the visions of Mt Annapurna, Mt Machhapuchhre, Mt Gangapurna and some other peaks in one single turn.

After satisfying your eyes and soul with the iconic mountain and landscape views, you will start to head back towards High Camp. There are no teahouses facilities on the Mardi Base Camp. The descent from base camp is quick and easy drop but you need to be careful with the rugged and slippery trails. Another overnight at the same teahouse of High Camp.

Day 05: Trek from High Camp to Siding

Altitude Gain:1,700 m

Trek Hours:4 to 5 hours

After breakfast at High Camp, you will make descent towards Siding(1,700 m). It will be a 4 to 5 hours long down-hill trek towards the overnight village. The trail is down-sloped with rugged and rough trails, you may find it difficult to walk over it thus do it slowly. Upon your arrival at the Siding village, you will get to see many traditional houses. This village hosts the second-last day of every Mardi Himal Trek, no matter whether it is a 6 days or 9 days trek.

Day 06: Trek to Lumre before the drive to Pokhara

Altitude Gain:1,400 m

Drive Time: 2 hours

Trek Hours:4 to 5 hours

Here comes the last day of Mardi Himal Trek. You will enjoy the organic breakfast at Sidding before heading out for Lumre. On the trail to Lumre, you will cross several traditional settlements of Brahmin peoples. Your lunch will be organized at Lumre before joining the jeep ride to Pokhara. It takes only 2 scenic hours to reach Pokhara. And after reaching Pokhara, your wonderful 6 days of Mardi Himal Trek finishes.

title: Annapurna Circuit Trek Weather And Temperature
excerpt: Annapurna region is a naturally flocked area of Nepal where one can find awestruck mountains, amazing landscapes, and abundant vegetation. People celebrate the diversity of the Annapurna region via…
html:
Annapurna region is a naturally flocked area of Nepal where one can find awestruck mountains, amazing landscapes, and abundant vegetation. People celebrate the diversity of the Annapurna region via several treks and expeditions. Among all, the Annapurna Circuit Trek is the most-liked trek of not only the Annapurna region of Nepal but also the entire world.

There are no words that can explain “How exactly the Annapurna Circuit Trek is?” But if still, there has to be an explanation, it will be like this; Annapurna Circuit Trek is the finest trekking trail that Nepal has to offer to its adventurers. Annapurna region is popular for its iconic and staggering mountains, varied landscapes, and rich floras and faunas. And don’t miss the traditional peoples living in this region and their historic settlements. Annapurna Circuit Trek is the only trek of the Annapurna region that covers most of its parts. You get to enjoy all of the things that the Annapurna Circuit Trek is known for.

But before any trek, you need to be sure of various things like cost, detailed itinerary, best time, etc. Amid others, a must known fact is; The best time for Annapurna Circuit Trek. Is there only one best time for this adventure or several more, how can you know that?. Well, you need to go through our blog about “Annapurna Circuit Trek weather and temperature” for that. And, you don’t have to go anywhere, the below-written piece is all about the Annapurna region’s weather and temperature in various seasons.

Annapurna Circuit Trek Weather and Temperature in different seasons

A year in Nepal is classified in four seasons; Autumn, Spring, Summer, and Winter. Each of four seasons acts differently on the basis of light, weather patterns, and temperature. Thus, Annapurna Circuit Trek in Autumn is a different experience than the other seasons. And, you have to get insights into how each of the seasons host the Annapurna Circuit Trek. Let’s find out through the weather and the temperature of all seasons.

Annapurna Circuit Trek Weather and Temperature in Autumn

September

September is called the beginning of Autumn in Nepal but it’s Mid-September when it actually arrives. The first few weeks of this month still remain under the rain clouds of the Monsoon season. And that is why September is not completely considered as the arrival of Autumn in Nepal. September is a transitional month of where Monsoon turns into Autumn.

From Mid-September, the temperature and weather feel like Autumn. The day starts to turn brighter with clear skies and bright sun. The Lower Annapurna region which is below 2,500 m stays quite warm during this month with 18°C to 22°C. Higher areas are somewhat colder than the lower areas with the temperature around 8°C to 12°C.

Thorong La Pass(5,416 m), the highest reach of Annapurna Circuit Trek, and some other areas around it are the coldest. The temperature in such good height touches -4°C in the day time and even low in the night hours.

Once the half of September ends, the weather starts to get clear and clearer with days. After all, this month welcomes the peak season of trekking in Nepal; August. Until the end of this month, the environment will have already enrolled with Autumn completely.

October

October is the second but the real month to taste the perks of Autumn. The last month(i.e. September) shows some conditions of Monsoon and some of Autumn. Hence, that month can be a little tricky to come out in the Annapurna region. October is the best of the best month to enjoy the natural beauty of Nepal. Autumn is all known for its stable weather and warm temperature. And, you can experience that from the very first days of October.

The temperature of the lower areas of the Annapurna circuit seems very warm with an average of 15°C. But once night hours come, the temperature falls down to 7 to 8°C. On the contrary, the higher parts are colder as always. Thorong La Pass is the highest part of the Annapurna Circuit and is the coldest one below the freezing level.

The temperature drops even further when the night gets full grip over the day. Daytime temperature is easily bearable with warm clothes. So, don’t forget to pack some down jackets.

Being the midpoint of the Autumn season, the trekkers from all around the world are scattered all over Nepal’s treks. Annapurna Circuit Trek sees the highest numbers of flocks over others. The days are clear with no rain clouds and you can get lost with clear mountain views.

November

November is a special month as it gives farewell to everyone’s favorite Autumn. The temperature and conditions of November are more or less identical to October. However, it is slightly colder than the last month as the environment gets ready for the soon-to-arrive Winter season. Except for that, all of the circumstances are very-friendly to the trekkers.

The average day temperature across November is around 13°C, just like October.

Night and Morning temperatures are also the same with 7°C to 8°C. Parts that are above 4,500 m of altitude make you go nuts by the cold. Standing in the area near to or at Thorong La Pass(5,415 m) is the coldest. These areas remain below the freezing level most of the time during November. By the way, there is another level of excitement while standing around the frozen areas.

The last month of Autumn has so many perks for serving you. Weather is completely stable with very few chances of rainfall. One can enjoy the Annapurna Massifs and other mountains of the Annapurna region without any obstructions. Because of these facts, November hosts a huge number of trekkers from everywhere in the world.

Annapurna Circuit Trek Weather and Temperature in Winter

December

When November ends it opens the way for the coldest season of all, the Winter season. With Winter’s arrival, the temperature starts to drop causing snowfall. The ever-white mountains get more bright with the added snow. Winter is not only the coldest but also the driest which means no chances of rainfall.

The first few weeks of December is a changing period where Autumn is still available waiting for the Winter to come. So, you can expect warmer days until half of December. The days start to get really cold from Mid-December with the daytime temperature reaching 10°C to 5°C. And nights get even harsher where temperature can hit -5°C. The higher parts of Annapurna Circuit Trek are the most affected by the Winter. Thorong La Pass may receive heavy snowfall at the end of December.

Winter turns most of the mountain and higher parts of Nepal into whitish stones. Most of the Annapurna Circuit trails get flooded by the snowfall. As a result, the high areas like Thorong La Pass are strictly restricted to make an entry. The restriction is only after the heavy snowfall in the higher parts.

January

January is the central month of Winter and being the midpoint it is also the coldest month of all. With increasing temperature, there is regular snowfall in the higher and some lower parts also. Days become shorter and shorter than usual. Daylight also lowers during the winter.

Days start to get colder day by day with a normal daytime temperature of 1°C to -10°C in the higher areas. Whereas, the lower areas are kind of warmer than the high altitudes as their day temperature gets around 7°C to 12°C. Due to the harsh cold temperatures, the higher regions are not allowed to enter by the local government. And, there is no point of trekking during this month as most of the teahouses get shut down. The trails also become too difficult to walk on because of heavy snowfall.

January and as a whole Winter season is the off-time for trekking in Nepal. But remember, mountains during Winter become over-beautiful by the white-toned snow.

The views after a snowfall are worth bearing and daring the cold adventures. But, it is outrageously difficult to complete the whole circuit trek of Annapurna. Because of that, people like to do city tours rather than trekking in higher areas.

February

February is another transitional month that sees nature turning towards Spring from Winter. The transition takes place only after the midway making this month a combo of two seasons. Early weeks are completely shades of the Winter season with some heavy snowfall and cold temperatures. Chances of overcast days are equally possible during the first half of February. As a result, the massifs may get behind the clouds all day.

The areas of Annapurna Circuit Trek will still remain under the freezing level until Mid-February. The first half of February will see some cold temperatures from -1°C to -14°C in the higher areas of the Annapurna region. Lower areas will also receive cold temperatures but comparatively less than the higher areas like Thorung La Pass.

But, after the midpoint, the colors of Spring start to appear in the surrounding. Flowers start to bloom and temperature also turns warmer around the end of February. The late-February is the perfect time to observe the arrival of Spring in Nepal.

Annapurna Circuit Trek Weather and Temperature in Spring

March

March is the beginning of another peak trekking season in Nepal, Spring season. Spring is also taken as the most favorable time for the Annapurna treks. With Rhododendron flowers blooming all over the forests, you get to enjoy the reddish flowers over the green forest. The weather is stable throughout the March and temperature also becomes warm to trek.

Annapurna’s lower region’s daytime temperature during March is around 10°C. The night and morning hours are colder than the daytime. March is the coldest month of the Spring seasons due to the reminiscent of gone Winter season. But with warm clothes, anyone can outplay the cold to enjoy the serenity of the Annapurna region.

Places like Thorung La Pass and Thorung La Phedi remain inside the freezing temperature even in March. But, as the days move further, the temperature starts to turn warmer and warmer. Until the end of March, the Lower regions get much more friendly with the daytime temperatures around 18°C to 22°C. Trekkers from various regions of the world start to appear on the trails of Annapurna Circuit Trek.

April

Up to the start of April, the Spring season will have braced the entire Annapurna region. April is the best month of Spring to trek in the conditions of peak season.

The weather is completely stable now with clear skies and undisturbed mountain views all day long. You can enjoy the beauty of the Annapurna region on a bright and warm day.

Higher parts of the Annapurna region’s daytime temperature is about 8°C to -4°C. The night hours are cold as expected where temperature can go below the freezing level. Whereas, the mean daytime temperature is around 20°C when the sun is at its high in the lower Annapurna region. Nightfalls are a little chilly as always in the hilly regions.

By April, you will see hundreds of nature lovers with their trekking bags and poles on the track of Annapurna Circuit. In the month of April, the already bloomed flowers now dance with the air. The view from the Thorung La Pass is breathtaking with various peaks in front of your eyes. Hence, April is certainly the best time to do Annapurna Treks if you have time this Spring.

May

May is the last month of everyone’s favorite Spring season. The Spring is in the brink for its departure before the Monsoon arrives. The weather conditions are similar to April; warm temperature, stable rain-free weather. Skies are quite open with bright sun all around the day. This month is equally suitable for a trek as the other months of Spring.

Higher areas of the Annapurna region are the colder ones with temperatures around 0°C to 14°C. Whereas, it is about 18°C to 20°C of temperature around the lower parts of the Annapurna Circuit. This is the hottest month of the entire year in the Hilly area. Nights are also warmer than the other months with an average temp of 5°C.

Spring is your month if you don’t like the cold temperature at all. During this month, you get to trek in light and thin clothes.

There will be some rain falls during the last days of May which will indicate the incoming of the Monsoon season. Such conditions can make the trail all muddy and slippery. Place your trip before the midpoint of May month. The starting two weeks provide clear visibility of the Annapurna region mountains.

Annapurna Circuit Trek Weather and Temperature in Monsoon

June

June is the start of the Monsoon or Summer season in Nepal. It is also sometimes termed as the Rainy season; the season of rainfall. The rainclouds will be around the skies most of the time during June. Days in the lower region are quite warm and sometimes humid with temperatures around 16°C to 30°C. On the contrary, the higher parts are cooler than the lower with the daytime temperature around -4°C.

During June the rain can occur anytime as the clouds are always around. Rainfall makes the trekking trail muddy and slippery and increases the difficulty level of Annapurna Circuit Trek. However, there are some parts of this trek which lies inside the rainshadow area. Places like Mustang, Manang, Muktinath hardly get poured by the rainfall. But Annapurna Circuit Trek is a long-distance trek and its areas are very prone to rains. To be genuine, June or any other month of Monsoon is not liked by most adventurers. The rain clouds can hinder mountain views all day and without mountains, there is no pleasure of trekking.

July

July is a peak month for rainfall as this month receives the highest amount of rain. Rain clouds are flown to Nepal’s skies by the Bay of Bengal’s blow. Throughout the days of July, there are high chances of heavy rainfall. The temperature after rainfall is a bit cool otherwise the lower regions concede humidity. The average temperature of Annapurna’s lower region(below 3,500 m) is around 18°C to 6°C.

July’s temperature is good to go for trekking but the rain clouds and rainfalls create problems. Most of the trails are muddy and risky to trek on, plus trails can be eroded with landslides. Cons of Monsoon trekking easily outplays the pros of it. The mountain views aftermath of rainfall are worth watching but trails are too risky. The trails are populated with mosquitos, leeches during July. Because rain caused problems, people do not see Monsoon as a good trekking time.

August

August bids goodbye to the Monsoon or Summer season by thanking for all of the rains. The rainy season is about to end which is good news for the Annapurna Circuit Trekkers. But before that, there are 30 more days of Monsoon season. August also receives a comparable amount of showers but not as July. Dark rain clouds will not leave this quick, they make you wait for one more month.

The average daytime temperature of the lower Annapurna region during August is about 19°C to 23°C. With Monsoon about to leave, the Annapurna region is ready for the Autumn season. By the end of August, the temperature will head back to normal temperature. The skies will finally get freedom from the rainclouds and they will add brightness to the ever-white mountains. This is the case of very late-August, the three weeks of August will be full of rain attributes.

What to expect in the best season for Annapurna Circuit Trek?

Clear Skies

Clear skies are an inevitable part of the best excursion of Annapurna Circuit Trek. With clear skies, there is no fear of getting your mountain and landscape views obstructed. Clear skies mean no hindrance between your eyes and mountain views.

Therefore, you have to expect clear skies throughout the picking season.

Stable Weather

Trekking is a difficult thing if your picked season has unstable weather. Stable weather means no rainfall or snowfall, just an ideal climate to trek on. Hence, your desired season should have stable and constant going weather.

Warm temperature

Every popular trek of Nepal lies in the ever-cold Himalayas and higher regions. Higher parts are the coldest part of the world where temperature can turn quickly. Trekking in such areas in cold temperatures can cause you serious problems like altitude sickness. Therefore, you need to pick a season that has a warm temperature in its features.

Conclusion

Annapurna Circuit Trek is doable in every four seasons, as you know that “Nothing is Impossible”. The only thing is that this trek gets easier and harder as per your time of the expedition. If you choose Autumn to do this trek, the trip will go well. And if you pick the Winter months to complete this adventure then it is sure you will have added difficulties.

To pick the perfect time for Annapurna Circuit Trek, you need to go for the stable weather, warm temperature, and clear skies. Doing this way, you will face no problems rather you will have a lot of good experiences and memories.

title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek In December
excerpt: No matter how many times you walk Annapurna Base Camp, no traverse is as joyous as doing it in December. With a series of quiet rocky trails, chilly wind, and blue frost meadows, trekking in December…
html:
No matter how many times you walk Annapurna Base Camp, no traverse is as joyous as doing it in December. With a series of quiet rocky trails, chilly wind, and blue frost meadows, trekking in December is unlike anything.

Annapurna Base Camp Trek in December brings joy to people who like traveling alone. The month senses an utter silence in the air, making it a perfect time to sail out on the trail. Trekkers can feel the icy winter from far-off following the cold breeze and snowfall.

Routes that were once covered with fall leaves are long gone by the end of the month. Surely, the views are still breathtaking but it’s the weather in December that has everyone’s eyeball. As a pre-winter, the month experiences mild weather with just the right amount of heat and cold.

Morning and night can be slightly cold after mid-December but the days will still remain as placid as ever. Hikers won’t be shocked to see the rugged route stacked with snow after reaching a height.

With the winter looming on the sky of Annapurna, there is a gradual drop in the temperature every other day. On the bright side, trekkers can still catch the scenic mountain view of Annapurna and diverse landscapes.

Unlike in autumn, people won’t have to struggle a lot in finding proper accommodation. There’s a level of comfort on the trail with few or no hikers to walk around and cause a disturbance.

Check our Annapurna Base Camp Trek Itinerary

Highlights of Annapurna Base Camp Trek in December

  • A pristine view of astounding mountains including Annapurna massif and Dhaulagiri
  • Time-travel in pre-medieval monasteries
  • Stopover at local villages and fete with their warm hospitality
  • Exposed to diverse culture and religion within the Himalayas
  • Wonder in the luscious forest with a wide species of wildlife
  • Mix old and new suspension bridge over sweeping rivers
  • Natural spring bath in the stunning Jhinu Danda

The weather of Annapurna Base Camp Trek in December

Natural grandeur has so dominated Annapurna Base Camp that it makes no difference when you travel it. Still, to find yourself with the nicest weather and sublime view, walk the pathways in December.

This might resist the whole idea of winter but December has quite wonderful weather. Of course, there are no warm mornings like autumn and the nights are freezing cold. But this is promptly settled up by the bright sunny day that offers a clear view.

As a new season and coming right after autumn, December has warm weather in the early days. But right as winter takes off the region, the nights and mornings start getting cold. Hence, December exudes a light-hearted charm with a mix of two seasons, autumn and winter.

Trails of Annapurna Base Camp cheers trekkers with fall colors in early December. Unfortunately, those who visit the base camp in late months are left with mere frozen leaves and fog. Still and all, the days remain warm and better with mild temperatures.

The cold breeze from mountains often strikes valleys, causing night to be icy-cold. Therefore, the trekkers hiking campsite in December must suit themself with warm clothes.

Temperature of Annapurna Base Camp Trek in December

No doubt, Autumn is an ideal time to visit Annapurna Base Camp but December is still better than January. It comes just after September so there are a nice subtlety and taste of fall which is comforting.

Not in a whole but the climate in the first two weeks of December is just like the former. Weather is mild and not too hot or cold with an average temperature ranging from 5 to 10 Degree Celsius.

Unfortunately, this doesn’t go around to be the same for a very long time. By mid-December, the villages at higher elevation begin to encounter chilly mornings and nights. From here, the temperature continuously falls reaching sub-zero and finally minus.

By the end of the pre-winter, the temperature of Annapurna Base Camp Trek reaches -5 Degree Celsius. This poorly affects the weather and trails that are covered with thick snow until winter goes away.

  • Manang Trek | Hidden Valley Tour in Nepal
  • Nepal Heritage Tour | Kathmandu | Lumbini | Chitwan | Pokhara
  • Mustang Trek | Cost | Itinerary | Route Map | Base Camp

Why have Annapurna Base Camp Trek in December?

1. Little or no Rainfall

December may vary in temperature but rainfall wise, it remains pretty the same throughout the month. Annapurna Base Camp rarely has a dark sky full of rain clouds in the month. So far, the rainfall recorded in the Annapurna region is no more than 25mm, causing the trail to be dry. Hence, trekkers won’t have to combat the wet routes to arrive at the base camp.

2. Clear view

Even though it’s chilly cold at Annapurna Base Camp trek in December, the views are still stunning. During warm-bright days, you can easily geek at the glistening mountains far from the trail. The unique landscapes and valleys to look astonishing in December.

3. Exploration on the uncrowded trails

As December marks the start of winter, fewer and fewer trekkers visit the base camp. The trail which was jam-packed with visitors until late-September is almost barren. The empty route comes as a relief for few trekkers who can have it all for themself. They can take their time and explore the secluded parts and historic monasteries without any interruption.

4. The favorable temperature in day

Trekkers may withstand frosty morning and night with the change in weather. But this hardly affects the climate in the day with the average temperature ranging from 5 to 10 Degree Celsius. This suitable temperature eventually makes the Annapurna Base Camp Trek in December a true pleasure to have.

Accommodation at Annapurna Base Camp Trek during December

Scrambling the sloppy hills of Annapurna Base Camp is never easy in December. There are so many things to take care of from icy-cold weather to rustic trails and gears. Topping the list though is accommodation.

On a more than week-long trip, you’re likely to spend nights in different places. As of Kathmandu, it comes with a variety of dwelling options from low standard to 5-star hotels and lodges.

For most parts, the lodge will cost trekkers from as little as US$2 to 3USD. But with the improved facilities, the price can see a sharp rise of up to $250 per night. Guesthouses and luxurious hotels in Pokhara too differ based on excellence and budget.

Resorts and guest houses that accommodate visitors with room service usually charge higher. Unfortunately, accommodations available on the trek aren’t sophisticated like the one in Kathmandu.

Tea houses happen to be the most convenient accommodation of all. They cost little compared to any other amenities and come with basic facilities. Expect nothing but a single wooden bed, clean bedsheet, and a pillow.

In some teahouses, they even provide guests with a nice warm blanket. Showers are mostly cold so if you want hot water, be ready to pay extra bucks.

Food at Annapurna Base Camp in December

Unlike high-end hotels, tea houses in Annapurna Base Camp don’t come with fanciest dishes. Still, the food offered is toothsome and nutritious enough to provide strength to hikers.

Most tea houses cling on local staple food and provide trekkers Dal, Bhat, and Tarkari. Delicious ingredients, especially veggies are freshly produced on the farm. They are prepared using bags of spices to rich flavor which kind of linger in the mouth.

Other dishes arranged for lunch include flatbread, curry chickpeas, and Thukpas. Some tea houses even fill the heart of their guests with delicious momos, stir-fried noodles, and pizzas. Most trekkers enjoy hot soup during Annapurna Base Camp Trek in December as the month endures cold weather.

For more variety in food, take a tour of the streets of Thamel during your stay in Kathmandu. There are cafes and restaurants in every nook serving cuisines from Thai to Indian and Indo-western. But remember that they are highly expensive and can cost you a lot of money. So we recommend that you carry eno

Difficulties during Annapurna Base Camp Trek in December

1. Altitude Sickness

Altitude Sickness becomes a prime concern for every trekker after reaching above 2,500 m. For those who’re already struggling with several health problems are stricken even faster.

Therefore, it’s important that you take note of your pre-medical health condition before scaling up. If you feel like vomiting or lose appetite, take medicines immediately. Stop climbing and head back to the nearest station in case the situation got worse.

Adapt to the changing climate and temperature through altitude acclimatization. Take a rest for at least a day or two before trekking high altitude. Also, make sure that you only ascend up to 500 m a day.

2. Extreme Weather

It doesn’t happen instantly but as days roll away, there’s a drastic change in weather. By late December, the weather of Annapurna Base Camp is already worsening. There is heavy snowfall at different places, causing the temperature to drop below zero degrees celsius.

As the temperature falls rapidly, trekkers will experience bitterly cold mornings and nights. The days are warm but not as much as it used to be during autumn or spring. In adverse weather conditions, you might even have to batter heavy snowfall.

So, to avoid a miserable situation, stay updated with the weather forecast. Pack plenty of warm clothes and climbing boots for Annapurna Base Camp Trek in December.

3. Insufficient Accommodations

December may not be the peak time for trekking but don’t let that fool you. Finding shelter will still be a challenge for many trekkers traveling the base camp in late December. After frequent snowstorms and strong wind, many lodges and guest houses remain closed.

The last-minute search can put you at risk of not having too many options for dwelling. Even the cheap accommodation can cost a hefty amount ensuing urgency. Therefore, to prevent oneself from a huge loss, book the rooms days in advance.

4. Slippery Trails

Unlike September, you’ll witness a different backdrop and trails at Annapurna Base Camp trek in December. There are layers of thick snow on the route which not just makes trekking difficult but impossible at times. They are greasy and tough to get a grip on without crampons and mountaineering boots.

Preparations and Essential Equipment for trekking Annapurna

Annapurna Base Camp Trek encompasses trails anywhere from moderate to difficult ascents. Even though it starts off easy, the trail walking uphills are fairly challenging with the weather causing major hindrance. Therefore, early preparation has to be done to avoid unfortunate circumstances. It’s an essential part of the hike and shouldn’t be overlooked whatsoever.

Physical Strength

Examine your fitness level before hitting off the routes to Annapurna Base Camp. Although the trek is labeled moderate, you never know what lies ahead. There are several things that can pop up right away and impede your journey.

Don’t forget that you also have a whole backpack on your shoulder. Besides that, there’s a rapid gain in altitude and a steep terrain to ascend which all rely on your physical strength.

So taking that into account, prepare your body for all possible challenges. To start, acquire physical training almost two months before the trek. Spent hours if not days taking short hikes on your own favorite destination as many times as you can.

Build the endurance power through strings of exercise including cardio, push-ups, and squats. Follow a routine workout or even yoga would work fine to increase flexibility.

Mental Strength

Over the course of time, trekkers seem to have totally forgotten about the mental strength above physical. Many of them do not realize what consequence mental distress can bring while on a trek like Annapurna Base Camp.

There’s absolutely no way you can make it to the summit until your mind is prepared. Therefore, make an advance preparation so that your mind can relax throughout the journey. Take candy bars and snacks with yourself on the trek so that you can comfort your body and mind.

Essential Equipment

Even though trekking is no sweet whensoever; the season drives it quite apart. It decides what items you’ll need on an excursion and what you should be shopping for. To know which equipment you must bring on the way, study the length of travel and climate. Don’t rely on basic equipment to combat severe weather at Annapurna Base Camp trek in December. Here are some of the list of gears that might help you plan the trip.

Clothing and Footwear

  • Fleece pants and trousers
  • Long sleeve shirts for icy morning and night
  • High-insulated jacket to withstand cold
  • Gaiters to protect feet from snow
  • Woolen or synthetic socks
  • Mountaineering boots with crampons

First Aid and Hygiene

  • First aid supplies including ibuprofen to prevent headaches
  • Bandaids and ankle wrap tape
  • Prescribed medication
  • Hand sanitizers and toilet paper

title: Upper Mustang Trek Cost
excerpt: Are you in search of a short trek in the remote and isolated regions of Nepal? Wanting to experience the unique culture and lifestyle of the people in the isolated regions of Nepal? Well, the 10 days…
html:
Are you in search of a short trek in the remote and isolated regions of Nepal? Wanting to experience the unique culture and lifestyle of the people in the isolated regions of Nepal? Well, the 10 days Upper Mustang Trek must be the one for you. Taking you to the isolated regions of Nepal with a unique culture and lifestyle, Upper Mustang Trek is a peculiar trekking destination.

How much does the Upper Mustang Trek cost, you wonder? Well, the cost of the Upper Mustang Trek varies based on your choice of Upper Mustang Trek Routes, Upper Mustang Trekking Itinerary, and the facilities you use during your trek.

The standard Upper Mustang trek itinerary takes you through the route that takes up around 10 days of your time. Based on the routes you take, the trek may even last up to more than 10 days.

The Upper Mustang Trek takes you to the isolated area of Nepal nearing the border to Tibet. This border proximity can clearly be experienced throughout our Upper Mustang Trek. You will realize that the Upper Mustang Region has been extremely influenced by the Tibetan culture and has become a tiny Tibet of Nepal.

Filled with unique landscapes, high altitude deserts, sandstone pillars and caves, the Upper Mustang Region is different from the normal trekking areas in the Mustang Region. The trails are more and more rural and not accessible as the other regions.

The Upper Mustang Trek is a great way of being close to nature away from technological advances. The lifestyle of the people there is mostly cut off from the people in the cities. With a dry summer, there is hardly any rainfall in this region. And the winter is a hibernation season for the entire Upper Mustang Region. These unique features make Upper Mustang a highly desirable destination for trekking.

Now that we have learned about the Upper Mustang Region a little better, we should be able to prepare for the trek a little better as well. Preparing financially for the trek is the key to the best trekking experience.

Upper Mustang Trek Highlights

  • Exploration of unique Tibetan influenced culture and lifestyle
  • Experience the isolated Himalayan settlements
  • Ancient Buddhist monasteries
  • Rainshadow region
  • Palace of King Lo
  • Kali Gandaki Gorge

Upper Mustang Trek Package Cost

If you are traveling with a trekking company, your worries are slim to none. All you have to worry about is finding a nice and reliable trekking company. As long as you are traveling with a well-reputed and reliable trekking company, they will take care of your trekking arrangements leaving you with no worries regarding the trek.

The standard 10 days Upper Mustang Trek cost starts at the range of USD 1700-1850 per person which includes all your transportation, food and accommodation, medical kit, staff, and permit costs. This makes your trek a lot more convenient and stress-free. The company will take care of your needs and make arrangements for your safe and comfortable trekking expedition as per the Upper Mustang Trek itinerary.

As for our company, Base Camp Adventure, we have the following Upper Mustang Trek 10 days itinerary. As per the itinerary, we will be preparing the permits required and the transportation, food, and accommodation arrangements so you can have a comfortable trek and enjoy the trekking experience to the best.

10 days Upper Mustang Trekking Itinerary outline

Day 1: Fly to Jomsom, Trek to Kagbeni

Day 2: Trek to Chele

Day 3: Trek to Geling

Day 4: Trek to Tsarang

Day 5: Trek to Lo-Manthang

Day 6: Exploration Day at Lo Manthang

Day 7: Trek Back to Ghami

Day 8: Trek to Chele

Day 9: Trek to Jomsom

Day 10: Fly to Pokhara

Cost Factors

If you are trekking on your own in a group or solo without a trekking company making all the arrangements for you, here are a few important cost factors for you. You should be well prepared for the trek and plan for the trek financially so you don’t face any shortcomings on your actual trek.

Transportation cost

Transportation mode is the main determinant of your cost and your total time of the trip. You can shorten your overall trip duration by taking flights and private means of transportation. This will increase your cost but it is very time effective.

Also, you can cut costs by taking local busses to your destination. They leave at a fixed time and get you to your destination fast. The main transportation routes to be considered during your Upper Mustang Trek are mentioned below with the mode of transportation options.

Kathmandu to Jomsom Flight

You can opt for a flight straight from Kathmandu to Jomsom which will land near Jomsom in Pokhara. The flight costs around USD 153 for a one-way trip. It takes around an hour and 45 minutes to reach Jomsom straight from Kathmandu. This is a scenic flight with great views of the mountains and the landscape.

Kathmandu to Pokhara bus ride

If you do not want to take a flight on your way to Jomsom, you can also take a bus ride from Kathmandu to Pokhara and then another bus to Jomsom. The local buses run from Kathmandu to Pokhara and get you to Pokhara in 8 hours or less.

The fare of the local bus to get from Kathmandu to Pokhara is around NRs 500 – 600 which is approximately USD 5-6. This is a lot cheaper and affordable means of transportation. If you have time to spare you can get to live this experience along with saving some money.

Kathmandu to Pokhara Flight

You can also take a flight to Pokhara from Kathmandu. The flight costs around USD 120 per person. It will get you to Pokhara in a matter of 40 minutes. Also, the cost differs as per the seasons.

Pokhara to Jomsom Flight

From Pokhara, the easiest and fastest route is to take a flight to Jomsom. The flight from Pokhara to Jomsom takes around USD 111 per person. You will get to Jomsom from Pokhara via a flight in 25 minutes or less.

The flight is very mesmerizing with great views. You can get to Jomsom from Pokhara in private jeeps as well. The roads, however, are very bumpy so fasten your seatbelts for a bumpy ride.

Food and accommodation costs

As for the food, if you are traveling with a trekking company, you will be provided with 3 square meals. However, if you are traveling alone, you will have to manage your food costs along with accommodation.

You will be able to find tea houses and guesthouses along the way during the trek. The meals will cost around USD 5 per meal. You can enjoy your three square meals a day within USD 20 every day. The most common food you will find will be Nepali Dal Bhat with pickled vegetables.

If you reach higher up in the Upper Mustang, you will get to taste mostly Tibetan influenced cuisines.

You will get bottled water and a somewhat variety of drinks in the Upper Mustang Region. The cost of the drinks in the Mustang Region are as follows:

  • Bottled water costs USD 0.5 to 4
  • A cup of tea costs USD 1.5 to 4
  • A cup of coffee costs USD 2 to 5
  • A bottle of soda costs USD 0.5 to 4
  • A bottle of beer costs USD 2 to 5

As for your accommodations, you will be spending the night and resting in a twin bed sharing room. The rooms will be clean and provided with an attached bathroom. You will be sharing the room with other trekkers. You can also get a separate room but it will be expensive and unavailable in peak season. The cost will be around USD 6-9 per room.

Permit costs

Another cost factor for your Upper Mustang Trek Cost is the permit cost. For every trek, you will have to get proper permits to explore the area. As for the Upper Mustang Trek, you will need 3 main trekking permits.

Mustang Restricted Permit

Mustang is a protected region for its borders with the Tibet nation along with the fact that it is a unique region. The number of tourists entering the region is limited by the government in order to preserve the region. So Mustang Restricted Permit is a must for you to trek in this region. The permit costs you USD 500 per person for all nationalities to enter the Mustang Region.

Trekking Information Management System Card (TIMS)

Another important permit required for trekking in the Upper Mustang Region is the TIMS card. This card costs you USD 10 per person for trekking the Upper Mustang Region with a guide. An additional charge of USD 10 will be charged for trekking without a guide.

Annapurna Conservation Area Permit cost

As we enter the Annapurna Region, we will have to pay for the Annapurna Conservation Area Permit to further advance in the Upper Mustang Trek. The cost of the Annapurna Conservation Area Permit is USD 27 which is NPR 3000.

This permit is very important and you can get escorted out of the conservation area and have to face punishment for not having this permit on you. The reason for the requirement of these permits is to protect and preserve the area so they can forever remain as beautiful and glorious as it is now.

Guide and porter costs

Another contribution to your Upper Mustang Trek Cost is the cost regarding the guide and porter. Having a guide to help you through your trek is important. With a guide, you not only get someone experienced to guide you through the new trails, but you also get someone to help you in need.

Trekking through the unknown roads alone may be overwhelming. But if you have someone who has walked these trails for a long time, you will be able to do so easily as well. With USD 25 to USD 30, you can have yourself a trusty and experienced guide who will let you in on the great views and keep you safe throughout the trek.

As for the porter, this is completely your choice. If you are someone who likes being independent and strong enough to carry all their luggage, you can deny yourself the porter luxury.

But if you are someone who likes to enjoy the trek instead of worrying about the weight on your shoulder, get yourself a porter. They only cost you USD 20-25 per day making you trek a lot more exciting and free of carrying heavy stuff on your shoulders tiring you.

Trekking equipment cost

Being an easy trek of only 10 days, you will not really need any expensive equipment for your trek. You can also skip the trekking equipment cost from your Upper Mustang Trek cost in total.

All you need for a successful and comfortable trek is a trekking pole and some quality trekking boots to keep you up and going. These will support you throughout the trek. You can find trekking shoes that come at various styles and prices, you can choose the one you like. As for the trekking poles, you can rent them from the company as well.

Miscellaneous cost

Apart from all the above-mentioned costs, there will be other miscellaneous costs to deal with during your trek. These miscellaneous should also be considered for the Upper Mustang Trek cost estimation. Some of the major ms\iscellaneous costs you should be prepared for during your Upper Mustang Trek are mentioned below.

Charging electronics

Unlike the hotels and accommodation in the cities, you won’t have sockets in your room. You will be charged extra for charging your electronic devices. For around USD 5, you can charge your devices in the tea house.

Souvenirs

What’s the point of trekking in the Upper Mustang Region and not getting some souvenirs to remember this memory by right? So have some cash to buy some souvenirs during your trek.

Tipping the staff

The tipping is not compulsory but the guide and the porter will expect a tip from you for their hard work. Tipping them around 10 % of their daily charge is enough.

Hot showers

If you are traveling in the colder times, you will have to pay extra for hot water for showering.

Tips for cost reduction

  • It is always wise to carry some tea bags with you to save some money on drinks
  • Being a rain shadow region, you can enjoy this trek almost all season. So find some deals on flights and enjoy the discounts
  • A water bottle with water purifier pills are a must for water on the go
  • Tipping is voluntary and only 10 percent of the charge is sufficient
  • Renting trekking equipment is another smart move

Best Time for Upper Mustang Trek

Being a rain shadow region, Upper Mustang trek can be enjoyed in almost all the seasons with all season having their own different perks.

The most popular season for Upper Mustang Treks seems to be the Spring season through the months of March to May. This is mainly because of the Tiji festival. It is one of the biggest festivals celebrated in Upper Mustang and trekkers come to enjoy this festival together with the locals.

Another popular and best season is Autumn lasting through the months of September to November. It is the peak season for all treks in Nepal. Providing you with the best temperature and weather conditions for trekking, Autumn is popular even in the Upper Mustang Trek.

Mustang region faces a dry summer being a rain shadow region. This means no worries of muddy and slippery trekking trails. The lower regions like the Karnali Gorge, Jomsom, and Kagbeni may face some rainfall during June and July .

Winter, however, is extremely cold in Upper Mustang. Most of the Upper Mustang Region goes into hibernation during winter. People move to the lower parts of the Mustang Region to protect themselves from the harsh winter it faces.

These seasons play an important role in increasing or decreasing the total Upper Mustang Trek cost. As the price for the flight drops for Kathmandu to Pokhara or Jomsom during the summer, you can enjoy this discount to trek the Upper Mustang Region as it is still great for trekking.

We hope you now have the required essential knowledge about the Upper Mustang Trek costs and how to minimize your costs.

title: Annapurna Circuit Trek 10 Days
excerpt: Annapurna Circuit Trek is the most popular trek adventure to do in Nepal. Thousands of nature admirers every year visit Nepal for doing this particular trek. It is one of the longest treks in Nepal…
html:
Annapurna Circuit Trek is the most popular trek adventure to do in Nepal. Thousands of nature admirers every year visit Nepal for doing this particular trek. It is one of the longest treks in Nepal that revolves around unique settlements, lush forests, high hills, and snow-capped mountains. The standard itinerary of Annapurna Circuit Trek is around 15 to 20 days. This long adventure is for those who have extra days on their holidays but it does not suit everyone. There is a deal for those who have only 10 to 12 days to complete Annapurna Circuit Trek; Annapurna Circuit Trek 10 Days.

10 Days Annapurna Circuit Trek is a shorter version of the longer Annapurna Circuit Trek. It does not mean that this trek will exclude major highlights of the Annapurna Circuit Trek. Rather it tries to cover all of the important sites in a short period. The experience that is in the 10 days Annapurna Circuit Trek is more or less similar.

Within ten days, you will experience the best parts of the Annapurna region. And by completing this trek, you can easily guess what it is like to do the longer Annapurna Circuit Trek.

Shorter Annapurna Circuit Trek of 10 days runs through the hills to provide the attractive views of mountain vistas. Most of the Annapurna region mountains are easily, clearly, and closely viewable on this trek. Peaks can be Mt Annapurna and its siblings, Dhaulagiri, Ganesh Himal, Macchapuchere, and several more. The landscape views are also equally eye-catching, you will find quick changes in the landscapes in no time. Thorung La Pass(5416m) is the highest reach and the ultimate highlight of this trek. And the journey to this pass is quite exciting and adventurous.

Moreover, the short Annapurna Circuit Trek gives you a taste of a unique lifestyle and culture of Tamangs and Gurungs. They are the major habitats of the Annapurna region, living in the iconic villages. The settlements are very much explorable with nicely built stone houses. Marpha, Manang, Jomsom, Pisang are the major stops of this trek.

You will get to see the monasteries, Temples, Mani Walls, Prayer Wheels, and Gompas homed by these villages. Muktinath Temple(3710m) is the most sacred temple for both Buddhist and Hindu pilgrimages. You will get to receive blessings from this sacred temple and to see locals doing so.

Annapurna Circuit Trek in 10 days is the best package to do with us if you don’t have much time for the longer one. We will make sure of your enjoyment and good trekking experience. Contact Us for booking the trip, Base Camp Adventure.

But before that, you have to learn more about the 10 Days Annapurna Circuit Trek. That is why we are here with the article about the itinerary, best-time, difficulty, and packing list of Annapurna Circuit Trek 10 Days. Read it out thoroughly to know everything about this trek.

Highlights of Annapurna Circuit Trek 10 Days

  • A quick way to explore the vast Annapurna region
  • Snow-covered views of Annapurna, Dhaulagiri, Machhapuchhre
  • To see the quick turn of the attractive landscapes
  • Enjoy the trek through green vegetation
  • Get wisdom from Tibetan influenced cultures and lifestyles
  • Ascend down the dramatic Thorung La Pass
  • Receive blessings from the most sacred Muktinath Temple
  • Walk by the most iconic villages of Nepal

Weather and Temperature during 10 days Annapurna Circuit Trek

During Autumn

It is Autumn in Nepal when September, October, and November are on the calendar. Autumn is one of the peak trekking seasons where you will see numbers of trekkers in Nepal. The weather during Autumn months is perfect as the trekkers want to, neither too cold nor too hot. And there are no or very few chances of rainfall during the trek if you are opting for any of the Autumn days. Skies are clear and you can just enjoy the mountain views on a clear sunny day.

The temperature of the Annapurna region throughout the Autumn ranges from 10 to 15-degree celsius in the lower region. However, the higher regions(above 4,000 m) are always cold and the temperature of those regions can change drastically. Thorung La Pass’s temperature falls to -4 degree celsius only in the day. The night and morning hours can see some freezing temperatures.

During Spring

Spring is the season of blossoming flowers and another peak trekking time in Nepal. March, April, and May are the months of Spring where you will see clear views of Nepal’s landscapes. The weather is more or less like the Autumn season, there is not so much difference between Autumn and Spring. Days are warm and pleasant to walk on the flower dotted trails of Annapurna Circuit Trek. The Annapurna region sits in the rain-shadowed region which means there are no real chances of rainfall.

Mountains are washed with snow during this season in Nepal and there is no such thing to obstruct the views. The average temperature of the lower region moves around 18 to 22 degrees. But, the higher areas are colder than the lower areas with negative degrees on the meter. Thorung La Pass is the coldest place to be in the Annapurna Circuit Trek. Days temperature is easily bearable but the night and morning time demands extra clothing to survive.

During Monsoon

June, July and August are the three rainy months in Nepal. Monsoon is considered the off-season for trekking in Nepal. This season can be perfect for peace and adventure lovers. The Nepali trails during Monsoon are almost empty thus the peace lover opts for this season. But, anyone traveling in the Monsoon months has to be ready for any kind of water caused problems.

July is the peak rainy month of all which means August and June does not see much rainfall. The temperature of the lower region is warm before the rainfall and a bit cold after the rainfall, around 15 to 25-degree celsius. Lower areas are the most rain-getting spots of Annapurna Circuit Trek. The higher areas like Jomsom, Marpha, Mustang are the rain-shadowed areas. So, the rain-occurrence in the higher regions is much less than the lower areas.

During Winter

Winter is the coldest time of year in Nepal. December, January, and February are the shades of Winter. The weather and temperature during Winter turn a bit harsher than the other times. The lower Annapurna region sees temperatures around 7 to 12 degrees during the normal day. On the other side, the higher regions are colder than ever as expected. With every increase in the altitude, you will feel the decrease in the temperature.

People take Wintertime as the off-season and challenging trekking time. The cold temperature can cause problems. But if you are good with the cold climate and can endure this time of year, Annapurna Circuit Trek in Winter is a possible trip for you. Make sure you are equipped with all of the winter gear as the Thorung La Pass receives some snow falls during winter. The early-December days are not too harsh to trek on and high areas are also not restricted. But as the winter wraps Nepal totally, the higher areas around Thorung La Pass are closed for trekking.

So, what is the best time for Annapurna Circuit Trek?

Without any doubt, the Autumn and Spring months are the best time for the Annapurna Circuit Trek. During those periods, you can enjoy nature at its best without any fear of snowfall, cold, or rainfall. The temperature is also ideal throughout these months. Therefore, if you are ready for Annapurna Circuit Trek, pick either Autumn or Spring months. You will enjoy the trip thoroughly.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Difficulty during 10 Days Annapurna Circuit Trek

Annapurna Circuit Trek is not an easy thing to do, it is one of the longest treks in Nepal. The shorter version of Annapurna Circuit Trek i.e. 10 days is a bit less difficult as it will cover less distance than the longer version. Distance is not the only difficulty you will experience this trek, there are a few more things.

Here are the major difficulties of Annapurna Circuit Trek:

Distance

The full Annapurna Circuit Trek is a long journey. Don’t get much relaxed if you are trying 10 Days Annapurna Circuit Trek. The shorter Annapurna Circuit Trek covers the total distance of anywhere between 160 to 230 KM. In the Itinerary of 10 days, you have to trek for 6 to 7 hours for covering a distance of 8 to 15 KM per day. And the trails are not over the regular land rather it’s over rough and steep trails. Hence, distance can be a problem for any non-experienced trekkers.

Altitude Sickness

Altitude Sickness is always there in the Himalayas and Annapurna Circuit Trek being one of the Himalayan treks, the fear is here also. Annapurna Circuit Trek’s Highest point is Thorung La Pass at an altitude of 5,416 m. If you don’t know, altitude sickness is possible in any of the regions above than 4,000 m. Therefore, getting caught by altitude sickness is the possible difficulty of Annapurna Circuit Trek.

This sickness can hit anyone who is not used to high altitudes trekking. But, this does not mean you cannot do the trek if you are from the lower sea-level areas.

With proper precautions and care, you can easily avoid altitude sickness. Walk slowly without rush but with breaks, drink water regularly, and place the bottle always near the hand, don’t consume any alcohol or tobacco. This way you can place yourself away from the sickness.

Low fitness level

If you have a low fitness and pain endurance level, then you can face difficulty while trekking. Annapurna Circuit Trek is a long trek that demands an average level of fitness. Low fitness level means the person cannot walk for too long on the steep trail, he/she might feel to give up. Therefore, try your best to maintain a good fitness level before the trek. There are things that you can do to improve fitness like cardio-training, cycling, running, hiking, etc. Doing these things on a regular basis certainly boosts fitness level.

Food and Accommodation

The food and accommodation is not a problem all the time but it is hard to get these services during peak season. Autumn and Spring are the two peak times when the lodges and tea houses are mostly occupied by already reached trekkers. Annapurna Circuit Trek trails are the busiest trails of Nepal. And, getting the accommodation of your choice is almost impossible without pre-bookings. So, it is always better to go with the trekking companies, they manage all the things of the treks. You don’t need to panic a bit also.

Annapurna Circuit Trek 10 Days Itinerary

Day 01: Drive from Kathmandu To Beshisahar

Altitude Gain: 760 m

Drive Duration: 6 to 7 hours

Drive Distance: 185 Km

Overnight at: Besisahar

10 Days Annapurna Circuit Trek commences with the bus drive escape from Kathmandu(1,400 m). The bus ride for Besisahar will start early in the morning after breakfast. Beshisahar is 185 km west from Kathmandu and the drive is scenic and exciting. After 6 to 7 hours of bus drive, you will finally reach Beshisahar. This place is also popular as the starting point of Annapurna Circuit Trek. Overnight at Besisahar.

Day 02: Drive from Besisahar to Chame

Altitude Gain: 2,710 m

Drive Duration: 4 to 5 hours

Drive Distance: 65 Km

Overnight at: Chame

The bus will hit the road again through beautiful Marsyangdi Valley where you can enjoy the mountain villages and amazing scenery. Today’s drive is over the unpaved and rough road so be prepared for the shakes and bumps. The 65 km long bumpy ride ends after reaching Chame village. This village offers relaxing views of Annapurna II, Lamjung Himal, Manaslu, etc. Overnight will be at the lodge.

Day 03: Trek from Chame to Pisang

Altitude Gain: 3,115 m

Trek Duration: 5 hours

Trek Distance: 13.2 Km

Overnight at: Pisang

Chame village brings an end to your bus ride and starts the trek of Annapurna Circuit. The trek will be through a steep and narrow trail of the valley. On the way, you will view Pinguda Danda Rock(1,500 m), a curve-shaped rock pointed in the river. Throughout the day, you will enjoy walking on the green trails with mountains in the distance. Pisang provides amazing displays of Annapurna range peaks.

Day 04: Trek from Pisang to Manang

Altitude Gain: 3,540 m

Trek Duration: 5 hours

Trek Distance: 17 Km

Overnight at: Manang

You will start to trek through Upper Pisang towards Manang. After reaching Geru, you can sight on the north face of Pisang Peak, Tilicho, Gangapurna, Annapurna II, etc. Then trail reaches in a Tibetan settlement where you will get to receive blessings from century-old Barge Monastery. This monastery is the largest monastery of the entire Manang region.

Day 05: Acclimatization day

It will be the acclimatization day at Manang dedicated to making you used to the higher altitudes. The high parts of the trek are on the way and you have to make yourself comfortable. As an acclimatization day, you will hike around higher Manang areas where you will touch the height of 4,500 m. The hike takes around 5 to 6 hours to complete the round trip. Also, you can explore Praken Gompa which sits north from Manang.

Day 06: Trek from Manang to Yak Kharka/Ledar

Altitude Gain: 4,200 m

Trek Duration: 3 to 4 hours

Trek Distance: 9.4 Km

Overnight at: Yak Kharka/Ledar

After an acclimatization day around Manang, it is time to move ahead towards Yak Kharka(Pasture). The landscape viewable today is more like a Tibetan Plateau; semi-deserted hills. Your trek starts through the older part of Manang before climbing the plain Gunsang. And finally comes the vast and serene Yak Kharka after 4 hours of peaceful trek. The mountain views will always be there if you want to look up.

Annapurna, Gangapurna, Tilicho Peak, etc are the peaks visible throughout the day.

Day 07: Trek from Yak Kharka to Thorong High Camp/ Thorung Phedi

Altitude Gain: 4,525 m

Trek Duration: 4 to 5 hours

Trek Distance: 9.6 Km

Overnight at: Thorong High Camp

It will be another short trekking day with only 4 to 5 hours of stretch. You will leave Ledar/ Yak Kharka by touching the river beds of Jorsang Khola. Then crossing the bridge, you will join a trek to Phedi(4,420 m). You will follow a narrow trail across the landslide area. Then one more steep uphill climb brings the Thorung Phedi in front of you. You will stay at Thorong High Camp(Thorung Phedi) to acclimatize yourself one last time before climbing the much-awaited Thorung La Pass.

Day 08: Trek from Thorung Phedi to Muktinath via Thorung La Pass(5,416 m) and Drive to Jomsom

Altitude Gain: 2,700 m

Trek Duration: 9 hours

Trek Distance: 16 Km

Overnight at: Jomsom

This is the most important day of Annapurna Circuit Trek where you will ascend down the Thorung La Pass. It will be a long and challenging trek, therefore, you have to start very early in the morning. The trail to Thorung La Pass is steep and rough shaped but the view from the above is worthy enough to forget the pain. Thorung La Pass(5,416 m) is one of the highest passes in the world which provides a broad panorama of ever-beautiful peaks.

After the view, it is time to trek down for 3 to 4 hours until Muktinath. The Muktinath area is famous for its most sacred Muktinath Temple(3,760 m). This temple is equally significant for both Hindu and Buddhist Pilgrimages. You will get peaceful surroundings at the end of the day at Muktinath. And, after the visit of Muktinath Temple and area, you will join the jeep ride for Jomsom(2,700 m). Jomsom is an iconic village of the Mustang region where houses are nicely built with stones and woods. The apple garden of Jomsom is world-famous and worth rambling around.

Day 09: Fly from Jomsom to Pokhara

Altitude Gain: 820 m

Flight Duration: 25 minutes

Overnight at: Pokhara

After spending an awesome night at Jomsom it is time to fly to Pokhara. Pokhara flights are available from the Jomsom Airport. It takes only 25 minutes to land at Pokhara after flying from Jomsom. The air-ride will provide a bird’s eye view of the entire Annapurna region. Every second of the flight time is quite scenic and enjoyable. Soon after reaching Pokhara, you will get a hotel transfer to one of the deluxe hotels in Pokhara.

Day 10: Drive from Pokhara to Kathmandu

Altitude Gain: 1,400 m

Drive Duration: 6 to 7 hours

Overnight at: Kathmandu

Your 10 days Annapurna Circuit Trek ends after the drive from Pokhara to Kathmandu. The bus will retrace the same highway of incoming to reach Kathmandu. After 6 to 7 hours of scenic bus drive, you will arrive in Kathmandu.

You will get a hotel transfer to your hotel to call it the end of the Annapurna Circuit Trek 10 Days.

Packing list for 10 Days Annapurna Circuit Trek

Here is the guide to what to pack for a shorter Annapurna Circuit Trek. The below-mentioned packing list is suitable for both Autumn and Spring seasons. But, if you are picking any other time, make sure you backpack all of the extra clothing and gear:

Clothing

  • Strong and comfortable trekking boots
  • Spare shoelaces
  • Trekking socks(pairs)
  • Half-sleeved hiking shirts/vests
  • Trekking pants
  • Thermals undergarments
  • Full-sleeved hiking shirts/vests
  • Insulating down jackets
  • Woolen cap
  • Trekking Gloves
  • Raincoats(For unexpected rainfall)

Mediocre

  • Diamox tablets
  • Feminine hygiene products
  • Anti-nausea tablets
  • Band-aids
  • Mosquito and insect repellents

Toiletries

  • Bathing Soap
  • Toilet Paper
  • Shampoo
  • Sunscreen
  • Moisturizer
  • Hand wash
  • Hand sanitizer

Accessories

  • Sunglasses UV protected
  • Sleeping bag(-10c)
  • Cameras
  • Batteries
  • Water Bottle
  • Solar Chargers
  • Hot water Thermos

Important Documents

  • Passport
  • Passport-sized photos
  • Passport Photocopies

Conclusion

Annapurna Circuit Trek 10 days is designed for less-travel-time trekkers. The long Annapurna Circuit Trek is certainly the best Annapurna adventure but not the only alternative. 10 days Annapurna Circuit Trek is equally exciting as the longer one.

You won’t feel bad about not doing the longer Annapurna Circuit Trek but completing the short Annapurna Circuit Trek. It is more like a win/win deal to do.
