title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek in October
excerpt: There’s nothing quite like the beauty and magnificence of Annapurna Base Camp Trek in October. But better it gets with all the classic trails, old-style remote villages, and splendid landscapes. One…
html:
There’s nothing quite like the beauty and magnificence of Annapurna Base Camp Trek in October. But better it gets with all the classic trails, old-style remote villages, and splendid landscapes.

One of the most popular hikes, Annapurna Base Camp Trek is a dream with striking beauty. It’s some of the few natural attractions in Nepal that look splendid throughout the year. In spite of that, October manages to get the most out of the camp trek with wonderful views.

The season makes everything look grand dropping majestic background scenes. October’s effect can be noticed from the cheerful valleys to restful trails and mountains. At an altitude of 4,130 m, Annapurna Base Camp offers fresh air with clear views.

October falls in-between September and November. Hence, it prevents both monsoon rain and the bitter cold of winter. Days in October are warm and pleasant with clear skies and clean air. In comparison, the nights are slightly cold with a chilly wind blowing from the campsite.

Trekkers visiting the base camp in October are provided with a majestic view of Annapurna and Machhapuchhre. The trails passing through the forest are covered with spectacular fall foliage. This ultimately makes the trek relaxing and comfortable to walk.

People can watch rare birds migrate to the region in October to enjoy autumn. October witnesses great weather throughout the month so people get an unobstructed view of snow peaks. For more, they can explore vibrant valleys and unique landscapes of different colors.

Highlights of Annapurna Base Camp Trek

  • Stunning view of snow capped peaks such as Machhapuchre and Dhaulagiri
  • Pleasant atmosphere all day around with clear skies
  • Crowded streets with explorers from far off and near
  • Cultural exposure and good fellowship with locals
  • Reenergizing hot spring bath in Jhinu Danda
  • Unreal setting of sunset and sunrise from Poon Hill
  • Holidays and festivities with social gathering

Weather of Annapurna Base Camp Trek in October

October officially stamps the autumn season in Nepal. It comes right after September so there’s not a single trace of monsoon rain. The skies are clear like never before in October putting an incredible display of nature.

No drastic change in the weather can be spotted in the middle of day and night. Unlike the former and latter, September witnesses mild weather all through the month. The scorching heat of high noon can be a little too much for hikers. So, to only prevent the heat, it’s best that they carry a light hat or a cap.

Seldom it rains in October so no murky trails to walk or odds of terminating the trek. Besides, there’s an entire month left for winter wherefore travelers won’t taste the snowfall until, reach the altitude.

Other than the weather, trekkers of Annapurna Base Camp have a hypnotic view to rejoice for. With the leaves turning into fall colors from golden to tinted red and hues, the forest looks dazzling. Deep in the woodland, travelers can hear bird humming and animals exploring their home.

Temperature during Annapurna Base Camp Trek in October

It’s a typical trekking season in Nepal. Therefore, October boasts maximum crowds flown from all over the world. Out of all twelve months, it has the most pleasant weather with reassuring temperature which comforts hikers.

That’s probably the reason why most hikers end up planning the trek in October. Reckoned as fall, it offers a temperate climate to accomplish Annapurna Base Camp Trek in October. Unlike night and morning, the average temperature in daytime soars up to 25 Degree Celsius in the month.

Surprisingly, the nights are still cold but bearable. Trekkers can experience a drop in the temperature by 10-15 Degree Celsius than the day hours. For that, you might want to carry a couple of warm clothes and quality trekking boots.

Accommodations during Annapurna Base Camp Trek in October

Annapurna Base Camp Trek comes with a wide range of packages from regular to plush. But even the reasonably priced package delivers standard service to trekkers. Their stay in Kathmandu can be more satisfying though with the accommodation service varying from the regular tourist quality to 5-star level.

That said, the amenity during the trek isn’t awful either. Instead, travelers will have countless options to go with depending on the budget. There’s accessibility to every lodge, guest houses and few lavish hotels.

Most common accommodation of the trek, tea house also puts self-satisfying service. Their facilities bring standard rooms with both single and twin beds. As a supplementary, trekkers get a clean bed sheet, a towel and a blanket.

Usage of hot showers and electricity to charge batteries cost high and isn’t inclusive in the package. Since October is a peak season, it may be impossible to find a single room at the last minute. Therefore most people book the room in advance.

Annapurna Base Camp Trek Meals in October

They may not be top quality restaurant standards but meals in Annapurna Base Camp Trek are delicious. From traditional Nepalese food to asian cuisine, there’s a variety of food on the table.

As a guest in Kathmandu, trekkers are served with scrumptious meals from typical Nepalese to delicate western courses. But after the start of the trek the choice will be much less and limited.

Switching the meal time and again won’t be an option as menus remain the same. Lunch and dinner often settles with a typical Nepali dish, rice, pulses and vegetables. But for a change, you can have flat bread and pizzas.

They offer as many items as chinese stir fried noodles, stuffed dumplings and muesli for breakfast. Seasoned meals of October including veggies are fresh produce from the farm. They are very healthy and full of nutrients, providing sufficient energy to hikers.

Why trek Annapurna Base Camp in October?

October is autumn here in Nepal. And the season appears to favor trekking the most by offering a great atmosphere. It brings all popping fall colors with vibrant valleys and fantastic landscapes.

Trails through forest are often covered with the autumnal leaves, making it look magical. October is a festive season and a big holiday time so the villages and streets are filled with people more than any other time.

1. Favorable Weather

Each and every day of October is like an autumn present for trekkers of Annapurna Base Camp. From the hypnotic color display of fall to the clear blue skies and joyous routes, everything looks fabulous in the month.

But if anything surpasses that all then it’s the beautiful weather of October. Believe it or not but the month has visionary weather to offer visitors with bright sunny days and chilly nights.

October is looked after by September and November so it has little or no rainfall and neither heavy snowfall. The days are warm whilst the nights at high altitude are cold but endurable.

The average temperature during the day ranges from 20-25 Degree Celsius causing it to be hot. Meanwhile, there’s a drop in temperature in nights and mornings from 10-15 Degree Celsius.

2. Exchange of Culture

Travelers from all across the world opt trekking Annapurna Base Camp in October. So more stories are witnessed being shared on the trails and dinner tables in lodges.

There’s goodness and positivity all around as people of different nationals, cultures, and races come together. More happiness spreads out when people exchange healthy conversation on the histories and culture of their native home.

Other than that, trekkers also make interactions with the locals where they stay. They come to share the unique experience and their take on Annapurna Base Camp trek in October. This is the best and easiest way to build a connection with the native.

There are so many historic and religious sites around the corner that seem to inspire travelers. They give more reasons for the trekker to come together and talk about the rich historical past.

3. Season of Festivals

October is a time of celebration in Nepal with all big festivals on the doorstep. It’s the moment when the entire country awaits impatiently for the arrival of Dashain and Tihar. So how could the villages lying in Annapurna Base Camp Trek escape it.

Trekkers going in all for the occasion would mean to capture the essence of culture and tradition. It allows them to get a sneak peek of people’s tradition, cultural identity and way of life. People of different ethnic groups are inhabited alone in the region. So hikers visiting the base camp in October can notice a mixture in the style of celebration.

4. Clear mountain view

October definitely has the finest view to offer with clear skies and great weather. Unlike monsoon and winter, it has no dark clouds or gloomy fog to obstruct scenic mountain vista. People will be able to glance at the dazzling Annapurna from distant trails and hillsides. Not just that, they even get the mesmeric view of the colorful landscapes and forest beamed with flowers and vivid leaves.

Preparations and Essential Requirements

Setting off on a trek isn’t as simple as it looks. It takes days and weeks of planning and preparations for one single hike. So much goes in the groundwork of a hike starting from physical training to picking right gears and even more.

Trekkers have to build their body to such an extent that it can beat the tiring routes and altitude. The workout routine must be designed to help increase physical stamina.

Physical Preparation

Hikers of Annapurna Base Camp Trek often rely on their body to rise above the challenging routes. Hence, their priority must be to keep the body fit and train accordingly. They must have high endurance power to walk all-day long on the rough trails of Annapurna Region.

Preparation of Annapurna Base Camp Trek starts with training exercise.Therefore, it must be done at least a month or weeks before the trek. Stability is most important in any trek so taking short hikes more frequently can be great help.

Exercise for the trek involves as light as jogging and gym classes to squats and high planks. Cycling and walking remote areas can be helpful during Annapurna Base Camp Trek in October.

Mental Strength

Since it’s categorized as moderate level trek, people don’t call for mental preparation ahead of Annapurna Base Camp Trek in October. However, it’s evenly important that a trekker is as good with mental strength as physical to put up with the hike.

Altitude sickness becomes a real problem after ascending above 2,500 m altitude. So prepare advance on how to adapt your body with changing temperature and climate. The choices for food are limited at the base camp which may not be enough to build energy.

Thereby to avoid such circumstances, carry snacks and energy bars full of protein and carbohydrate. Also, allow your body to have a proper rest and drink a minimum of 3-4 litres of water each day.

Trek Essentials

After physical and mental preparation, next comes the essentials. In absence of right gear, trekkers can never endure Annapurna Base Camp Trek even if it’s in October. So start packing early as you might not want to miss any gear that could ease the trek. Here’s the checklist of a few essentials that can help you succeed in the trek.

  • Fleece trouser to withstand the bitter cold of morning and night
  • Windproof jacket for breezy days
  • Lightweight shirt and a hat to prevent heat
  • Trekking poles to ease weight on the body during ascent to steep hills
  • Stiff hiking boots to walk comfortably on rugged trails and rocky terrains
  • Extra pairs of socks
  • Navigation device including map and compass to find way if lost
  • Headlamps, extra batteries and charger
  • First aid-kit with ibuprofen to cure altitude sickness

Difficulties of Annapurna Base Camp Trek in October

Altitude Sickness

It makes no difference on which month you travel, probabilities of altitude sickness always remain on high altitude treks. So to cope with the sickness, preparation must be done beforehand. Pre-arranged the first aid kit with needed medicines, blisters, and band aid in it.

Don’t overlook the minor symptoms of acute mountain sickness as it might turn bad. You might even have to deal with the medical emergencies. Acclimatization is the best way to impede altitude sickness so take time to adjust the atmosphere and climate.

Food and Accommodation

Since October is a prime season for trekking, people from all over the world travel to Annapurna Base Camp in October. This eventually results in trouble finding rooms at lodges and tea houses. People may have to line up and wait for hours to get their orders in hand. So not to let that happen, plan the food and accommodations a little sooner.

Rugged routes

The routes are relatively well-marked at the start of the trek. But as soon as you’ll take altitude, there are more rough terrains and steep hills to scramble. The trails heading to base camp are uneven and full of ups and downs, increasing the difficulty level.

But if you’re used to hiking then the Annapurna Base Camp Trek in October won’t be that challenging. Taking extra days to rest and a little training session can also help beat the rough terrains.

FAQs

1. How high is Annapurna Base Camp?

Annapurna Base Camp is almost half the height of Annapurna I. It mounts up to an elevation of 4,130 m which is 13,550 ft high.

2. How much does it cost for Annapurna Base Camp Trek in October?

The cost of Annapurna Base Camp Trek in October is wide, ranging from $1000 to $1200 or even more. Foreigners have to pay a permit fee to enter the conservation area which costs around $30. This is almost $20 high compared to what SAARC nationals have to pay to visit the area.

The trek cost for the base camp can also vary depending on the facilities and standard of service. Luxurious hotels and guest houses often charge high which might cause a hike in the travel package.

3. What are the effects of extreme altitude?

Climbing too high and too quickly often leads to altitude sickness. The low oxygen in the air at high altitude usually causes problems like shortness of breath, headache and dizziness. To avoid the severe effects, try climbing the steep hills slowly above 2,500 m. Taking a break from smoking and alcohol during trek is also helpful in preventing sickness.

4. Is solo trekking possible in October?

October is on season for trekking in Nepal so trails are often crowded with trekkers. Starting from the trek, there is always someone to accompany by. But even if you’re alone then there’s nothing to worry as locals are just around the corner to help you.

5. Is the trek appropriate for beginners?

Due to its moderate level, Annapurna Base Camp Trek in October can be achieved even by beginners. However, precautions must be taken since they are unaware of the routes. To forbid unfortunate incidents, take a pro guide with you.

title: Mardi Himal Trek without Guide
excerpt: Mardi Himal Trek is an incredible trek in the diverse Annapurna Region of Nepal. The trails of this fantastic trek pass through the Himalayan landscapes of high mountain passes, alpine forests, green…
html:
Mardi Himal Trek is an incredible trek in the diverse Annapurna Region of Nepal. The trails of this fantastic trek pass through the Himalayan landscapes of high mountain passes, alpine forests, green valleys and others. This spectacular trek has gained prominence over the years as a popular alternative for the famous Ghorepani-Poon Hill trek.

The breathtaking mountain vista of Annapurna I, II, III, IV, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre, Mt. Dhaulagiri, Brahashikhari, Nilgiri, Gurja Himal and others will spellbind you. You can also observe the gorgeous Himalayan sunrise overlooking the silver mountains along with the various points along the trek.

Moreover, the natural trails of the foothills of Mardi Himal will enchant any nature lover. The off the beaten trails allow you to travel in peace and tranquillity. You need proper preparation and training that includes both mental and physical training before the trek. Trekkers should also pack appropriately and take necessary precautions whether you trek with or without a guide.

However, there are many perks of hiring a professional guide for the trek. They will provide you in depth information about the trail and keep you safe and secure. Trekking solo without a guide comes with its set of challenges but with proper preparation it is still doable. Read further for the detailed description of the Mardi Himal trek without guide.

Significant Highlights of the Trip

  • Breathtaking views of the sunrise overlooking the snow-capped mountains
  • Awe-inspiring 360-degree views of the Annapurna range including Mt. Annapurna I, II, III, Machhapuchhre, Mardi Himal, Mt. Dhaulagiri, Lamjung Himal, Annapurna South, Himchuli, Nilgiri, and others
  • A cultural exploration of the Gurung, Magar, and Tamang community
  • Opportunity to stay in the local tea houses and homestays
  • Observing the vibrant culture, heritage, and lifestyle of the locals
  • Tasting the delicious local cuisine
  • Incredible hospitality of the Nepalese people

Is the Trek to Mardi Himal Possible Without a Guide?

Mardi Himal trek is a moderate trekking adventure in the western region of Nepal. There are well-marked trails along the trek. With proper packing and preparation, the Mardi Himal Trek without guide is possible.

The trek in the foothills of Mardi Himal takes you along the lush jungles of Rhododendrons and Oak trees. You will also observe the snow-covered mountains of the region, which is an enchanting experience. All trekkers must have all the travel and trekking permits before you trek solo. You must also book all the food and accommodation along the trail so that you won’t face any hassles along the path.

However, the Mardi Himal trek with a guide is always the better choice. The solo trekkers have to manage all the facilities by themselves. Hence, the trek can get quite taxing as you will have to handle everything on your own. Besides that, you will have to take care of your safety on your own. The exciting trek is also possible solo, but trekking with a guide provides you with a better experience overall.

The Route to Mardi Himal Trek without Guide

Mardi Himal Trek is a popular trek in the Annapurna region. The Annapurna region is a diverse landscape with many dense forests, high mountain passes, serene waterfalls, and others. This exciting trek starts with the scenic drive from Kathmandu to Pokhara and a short trek to Pothana.

We then walk through the stope steps climbing up towards the village settlements passing by the forested area of Rhododendron trees. It takes around 5-6 hours of trekking each day during this exciting trek. The trek can get physically demanding at times. Trekkers need to walk through the narrow and steep ridges at times. But the trek is simple and comfortable overall.

We then take the trail to the famous forest camp passing by the forested area of Oak, Hemlock, Maple, and Rhododendron trees. The trail then leads us to low camp from the forest camp before arriving at the High Camp. We will finally arrive at the Mardi Base Camp situated at an altitude of 4,500 m

Moreover, the trail then descends back to the Mardi High Camp and then towards the Siding Village. We then drive back to Pokhara and further back to Kathmandu. Overall, this trek is ideal for both beginner trekkers as well as the expert veterans.

When is the Best Time for the Mardi Himal Trek without a Guide?

The time of the trek plays an essential role in your trekking adventure. There are various weather conditions along the trek and primarily impacts making the trek more challenging and comfortable. The best time for the Mardi Himal Trek without guide is Autumn (September-November) and Spring (March-May) and others.

Moreover, there are stable weather conditions in these seasons that are ideal for a trekking adventure. Autumn is a post-monsoon period, and spring is the pre-monsoon period in Nepal. Hence, there is relatively less rainfall in the Annapurna region. However, you can experience some rain as the weather in the high altitude region is unpredictable.

Spring

Spring is an ideal time for nature lovers to trek the foothills of Mardi Himal without a guide. The beautiful, diverse landscapes of the Annapurna region will enchant you. The trek will pass through the forested lands of Rhododendron and Oak trees. An incredible aroma and fragrance of herbs will follow you around the trail. The day time temperatures in the Annapurna region ranges around 15-23 degrees Celsius in Spring.

Autumn

Autumn is the peak season for travelling and trekking in the Annapurna region. The daytime temperature ranges around 15-20 degree Celsius in the Autumn season, which is ideal for trekking. Autumn is also the best time to culturally explore around the area. It is a festive period in the Nepalese calendar with many festivals like Dashain, and Tihar.

However, the weather in the morning and the night time will remain chilly throughout as it is a high altitude region. The weather and temperature also become colder as you move from lower elevation to higher elevation along the trek. Overall, the months of Autumn and Spring provide stable weather conditions and is the ideal time for the trek.

Different Types of Guides and Porters

Licensed Guide

Licensed Guides are well trained and certified by the government and can give you a complete tour of the route. A licenced guide is the best option for a safer and comfortable journey. They can answer all your queries and help you along the trail.

Furthermore, they will get you the necessary permits and help you stay away from the restricted areas. You will get instant help if you show symptoms of altitude sickness. They will also help you to tackle altitude sickness and guide you through the evacuation process if necessary. A licensed professional guide costs you around 35 USD per day food, lodging and insurance expenses.

Porter

A porter is someone who helps you to carry the luggage. They can carry up to 25 kgs and also help you to communicate with the locals. They charge around 25-30 USD per day on average, which includes their accommodation, meal, and insurance expenses.

Porter-Guide

Porter-guide is an ideal option for those who want to trek on a budget. Porter-guides are those that work both as a porter and a guide. They carry a limited amount of your luggage and also guide you along the trails.

Besides that, they are also fluent in various languages, and they can also work as an interpreter with the locals. Porter-guides around 30-35 USD, which includes their accommodation, food, and insurance charges.

How Difficult is the Mardi Himal Trek Without Guide?

The various difficulties that trekkers might face in the Mardi Himal trek without guide are as follows:

Navigation along the trail

This outstanding trek is an off the beaten adventure in the remote trails of the Annapurna region, and therefore there are high chances of getting lost when you trek without a guide. Hence, an accurate Mardi Himal trek map is an essential item that all trekkers must carry during the trek.

A local professional guide will know in even the narrowest of paths and helps you get out of any difficult situations. However, trekking solo is dangerous in that aspect, and you will have to find the trekking routes on your own. There are trail marks and signposts along the trail but still trekking with a guide is much more comfortable.

Altitude sickness and acclimatization

The high altitude trek that takes you above the altitude of 4,000 m. Hence, altitude sickness is quite common among trekkers. If you trek solo, you will have to decide for the acclimatization point on your own. Since you are on your own, the risk of medical emergencies related to altitude sickness increases significantly.

Furthermore, a professional guide on the other hand provides you with the best acclimatization points. They also help you in case there are any emergencies along the trail. Hence, acclimatization is best done with a guide’s help and guidance.

Trekking with a Luggage

This trek in the Annapurna region is also difficult as you will need to carry your luggage on your own. Trekking with luggage in the rugged up and down the trail is quite tricky even for the most experienced of trekkers.

Furthermore, you should pack lightly with only those items that are absolutely necessary. On the other hand, if you hire a porter guide or a porter, you will get incredible help in carrying your luggage, and you can trek without any hassle.

Accommodation and Food

Finding the best food and accommodation facilities without a guide is a challenge. A guide has much better connections and can help you find the best accommodations and meal facilities along the trek. One thing you must consider is to pre-book all your accommodations in advance.

Emergency Situations

Injuries, bad weather, accidents, and other emergencies are quite common in the high altitude trek. If you take a guide along with you, you can always get help in any conditions. However, if you trek alone, you will need to carry enough first aid kits and communication devices to remain in touch with your closed ones in case of any emergency.

Communication and Language barrier

Language barriers are another aspect that you must consider before the trek. Communication along the trail is scarce as there are no proper mobile networks. A guide who is fluent in multiple local languages will help you establish a conversation with the locals and help you along the trail. If you trek solo, you will have to figure out all these factors on your own.

Therefore, the Mardi Himal trek without guide is quite challenging and has many difficulties. You should take care of all these factors if you choose to take the Mardi Himal Trek without a guide.

Trekking with a Guide and Without a Guide – Cost Comparison

This exciting trek is relatively cheaper without a guide. However, trekking with a guide comes with various perks and considerable advantages. The trek gets quite safe and comfortable with a guide. You will also get the best accommodation facilities with a guide. If you are a backpacker or solo traveller, you will save money on accommodations, food, insurance, and service and tip charges.

Moreover, trekkers can save around $500- $600 if you choose to take the Mardi Himal Trek without guide. Overall, the choice of trekking with or without a guide is yours. You will save some money if you trek without a guide but will miss out on excellent services provided by a guide.

Perks of Trekking with a Guide

The Mardi Himal trek without a guide is risky and challenging at the same time. On the other hand, there are many perks of trekking with a guide. Some of the advantages are as follows:

  • You will get safety and security in comparison to trek without a guide.
  • A guide will help you immensely in case of altitude sickness, accidents, injuries, and other emergencies.
  • You will get the best accommodation and meal facilities as the guide has various communication channels.
  • Navigation is an integral part of the trek. With a local guide by your side, you will not have any fear of getting lost. They can also schedule your acclimatization points for your ease.
  • Professional guides will take care of your health and check for altitude sickness at all times. You will get essential first aid and evacuation facilities if necessary.
  • You can explore the diverse culture and lifestyle of the region.
  • The guides are a great help in case of any adverse weather conditions as they help you get into temporary stay and also checks the weather forecast before the trek.
  • You don’t have to worry about the trekking permits as the guides help you get them with ease. You don’t have to stay for long queues in the process.
  • You can interact with the locals and learn the local nuances so that you won’t offend the locals.
  • The guides will also help you spot and learn about the rare flora and fauna of the region.

How fit should you be for the Mardi Himal Trek without Guide?

The moderately challenging trek requires around 4 to 5 hours a day with backpacks. The trails do not have any technical climbing sections. Therefore you do not require any climbing skills of extreme fitness levels. However, there are some rocky sections in the High Camp and the Mardi Himal Base Camp. Thus, a basic level of fitness is essential for the trek.

Mardi Himal Base Camp trek requires a good training routine a few weeks before the trek. The training regime will help you gain physical strength, stamina, and endurance. Trekkers also should consult their doctor for a regular checkup before the start of the trek. In case of any pre-existing medical conditions, you must get proper advice from the doctor.

If you have experience trekking in Nepal, this stunning trek becomes quite easier for you. However, past trekking experience is not mandatory, and you can trek without any previous trekking experience as well. This fantastic trek is suitable for trekkers of all skill levels. You should train well for the trek and pack appropriate trekking gear.

How to Prepare for the Mardi Himal Trek without Guide?

Physical Training

Physical training is one of the most important parts of preparation for the trek. The training regime will help you gain a basic level of fitness. Cardiovascular activities like cycling, hiking, jogging, swimming, and others will help you achieve the required physical fitness required for the trek.

Moreover, trekkers should start their training regime for two to three months or at least two weeks before the start of the trek. The training routine will increase your strength, stamina and endurance. You should train with weights during the trek.

Mental Preparation

Mental preparation is an essential part of the training regime. You should mentally prepare for trekking in the difficult, rugged terrains during the trek. The trails of this exciting trek have many Himalayan landscapes including up and down rocky paths.

Moreover, you will require mental stability and preparation during the trek. You need to remain prepared in advance to complete the trek with ease.

Trekking Gear

You should also pack well for the trip, including proper trekking gear and equipment. You will require gears and equipment that help you in trekking. Read below for the packing list for the Mardi Himal trek without guide in detail.

Food and Accommodations Along the Trail

The trek to Mardi Himal is an off the beaten adventure. Hence, you will find a limited number of tea houses along the trail. These teahouses are community-based and provide you with basic food and accommodation facilities. The teahouses provide the traditional Nepali meal of “Dal Bhat“ which is a carbohydrate and protein-rich diet that will give you enough energy for the trek.

You can also find a limited number of international and western cuisine, including pizza, sandwich, burger, noodles, bread, porridge, and others. Hot beverages are also quite popular in the high Himalayan region. Tea, coffee, rhododendron tea, mint tea, hot lemon, hot chocolates are quite popular in the area. Alcoholic beverages can cause dehydration and increase the risk of altitude sickness among trekkers.

Moreover, you will have the basic accommodation facilities in the tea houses. The rooms in the tea houses are on a twin sharing basis. You will have to share a room with fellow trekkers. There are beds, mattresses, pillows, and a warm blanket in these teahouses. The toilets are generally shared and outside the teahouses.

One thing you must not forget is to bring your toiletries during the trek. The cost of one night’s stay at the teahouses ranges from $3- $6 per night depending upon the facilities provided. Facilities like charging, hot showers, and wifi are also available at some tea houses at an added cost.

Packing List for the Mardi Himal Trek without Guide

Packing for the Mardi Himal trek without guide depends upon the season of the trek. It also depends upon the desire and requirements of the trekker. The essential items required for the trek are:

Clothing

  • Comfortable trekking shoes
  • Wool or fleece gloves
  • T-Shirts (Full sleeve and half sleeve)
  • Windcheaters
  • Lightweight thermals
  • Waterproof jackets
  • Waterproof trekking pants
  • Hiking Shorts
  • Woolen socks
  • Convertible Trekking Pants
  • Warm Hat

Toiletries

  • Soaps
  • Shampoos
  • Toothbrush
  • Toothpaste
  • Toilet Paper
  • Lightweight towel
  • Sanitizer
  • Sunscreen with high SPF
  • Moisturizer

First Aid

  • Band-aids
  • Anti-nausea pills
  • Anti-diarrheal antibiotics
  • Allergies medication
  • Cold and cough medicine
  • Water purification tablets

Accessories

  • Camera
  • Power bank
  • Solar chargers
  • Extra batteries
  • Headlamps
  • Sleeping bag
  • Comfortable backpack
  • Maps
  • Hot water thermos

Important Documents

  • Passports
  • Trekking permits

The Final Say

Mardi Himal Trek is an outstanding trek in the Annapurna Region. This relatively new trek is an ideal adventure for those trekkers who wish to trek in the quiet tranquillity of nature.

Furthermore, the views of the snow-capped Himalayan mountains is the highlight of the trek. Overall, this spectacular trek is possible either with a guide or without a guide, but trekking with a guide is always recommended for your safety.

If you have further queries or need any travel-related details, please feel free to contact us.

title: Annapurna Circuit Trek Map
excerpt: If you are planning on going on a long trekking vacation then Annapurna Circuit Trek is the perfect destination for you. It is one of the most popular and longest trekking routes of Nepal. While…
html:
If you are planning on going on a long trekking vacation then Annapurna Circuit Trek is the perfect destination for you. It is one of the most popular and longest trekking routes of Nepal.

While trekking in these routes Annapurna Circuit Trek Map will be a helpful companion guiding you throughout the way. Maps are an essential factor before going on a journey.

Every trekker carries a map along with them whether it be Handheld GPS or paper map. Thus, Base Camp Adventure presents you with an updated high-quality Annapurna Circuit Trek Map that gives you detailed information about the trails.

In this modern era, you can just download the map and follow it through the GPS from your gadgets. But gadgets can not be solely trusted as they can break or run out of battery. So you can be cautious by carrying maps and compass as backup.

Annapurna Circuit trek has many routes you can choose from but we have made it easier for you by providing you with an 18 days Annapurna Circuit Trek itinerary keeping your safety as best interest.

Overview of Annapurna Circuit Trek

Annapurna circuit trek takes you on a scenic and cultural journey through the Annapurna Region. This route was voted as one of the best long-distance treks in the world.

Annapurna is a huge massif located in the north-central part of Nepal. This mountain is considered the world’s tenth highest mountain with a height of 8,091 m above sea level.

This circuit trek encircles the Annapurna Massif exploring the local culture, tradition, and the breathtaking view of nature along the routes.

The Annapurna region is protected by the Annapurna Conservation Area which is one of the largest preserved areas of the Himalaya region.

It includes Annapurna Massif, Annapurna Sanctuary, and many famous trekking routes such as Annapurna Circuit Trek, etc.

Annapurna Circuit Trek is one of the classic and diverse treks in Nepal. It is 18 days long trip within the mountain ranges located in the central part of Nepal.

The trekking routes for the Annapurna circuit were opened for foreign trekkers only in the year 1977.

The paths lead you through villages influenced by the Tibetan culture and tradition. It is inhabited by diverse ethnic groups such as Gurung, Magar, Tamang, etc.

On this 18 days Annapurna Circuit Trek Itinerary you get to view many mesmerizing mountains such as Dhaulagiri, Machhapuchhre, Manaslu, Gangapurna, Annapurna Massif, Pisang Peak, and many more.

Also, you get to walk past many paddy fields, pasture lands and subtropical forests viewing various waterfalls, enormous cliffs, beautiful landscapes, and villages.

Annapurna Circuit Trek Route is a walk in the off beaten paths which is considered moderate level treks. This is an amazing trek you don’t want to miss out on.

So don’t think twice and get ready to embark yourself on this action pack trek.

Summary of Annapurna Circuit Trek Route

After your landing at Tribhuvan International airport at Kathmandu. Our representative will be waiting for you there prior to your arrival. They will then pick you up and drop you off at your hotel.

As the rest of the day is unplanned you can roam around the city. Or just stay in the hotel as you must be tired after the long flight.

After a peaceful night, your journey begins on the second day of this trek. This day you will be driving towards Bhulbhule via Besisahar where you will stay for the night.

The next day you start your trek by heading towards Chamje passing through many villages and forest areas. You stay in one of the tea houses for the night.

From Chamje, you will head towards Bagarchhap where you will call it off in one of the lodges. Then from Chamje, you make a 3 to 4 hours walk till Chame where you will be staying for that day.

After a soulful night, you head towards Pisang crossing bridges and forest trails. And stay there for the night. Following day you head towards Manang via Ngawal and stay in one of the guest houses for the night.

You acclimatize in Manang and head towards Ledar from there where you will be taking a rest for the day. And the next day walk through steep trails till High Camp via Thorung Phedi.

From High Camp, walk for about 7 to 8 hours this day, reach Muktinath and call it a night in one of the tea houses. Then you head towards Marpha the next day where you stay for the night.

After that, you again follow the trails till Kalopani stays there for a night and head towards Tatopani from there. From Tatopani, you trek to Ghorepani and head towards Pokhara to Nayapul from there.

Reaching Pokhara you stay in one of the hotels for the night and drive back to Kathmandu the next day.

Details of Annapurna Circuit Trek Map

Arrival at Kathmandu

Maximum Altitude: 1,400 m above sea level

On the first day of your Annapurna Circuit trek itinerary, you arrive at Tribhuvan Airport situated in Kathmandu. After your landing, our respective representative will pick you up and drop you off at your hotel.

And help you check-in to your rooms. Now you have the rest of the day for you as the day is unplanned. You roam around or visit local markets, or just stay in your room and rest.

You stay here for the night.

Kathmandu to Bhulbhule

Drive Duration: 8 to 9 hours

Drive Distance: 186.8 km

Maximum Altitude: 840 m above sea level

Today is the day your journey begins for the Annapurna Circuit Trek. This day you drive from Kathmandu to Bhulbhule passing through Besisahar.

As you leave the city behind you get to see valleys surrounded by lush green hills throughout the road. You will be traveling through Prithvi Highway viewing beautiful scenic views of mountains and landscapes.

Following the roads, it gets bumpy as you reach Besisahar situated at an altitude of 760 m above sea level. You drive along the sides of Marsyangdi river viewing picturesque villages and snowy peaks.

From here reaching Bhulbhule is about 1 to 2 hours drive. Bhulbhule is situated at an altitude of 840 m

Bhulbhule to Chamje

Trek Duration: 5 to 6 hours

Trek Distance: 22.2 km

Maximum Altitude: 1,430 m above sea level

After a night in Bhulbhule, you head towards Chamje this day. You begin the trek by making a steep climb till you reach a cliff above the riverbed.

From there you make a descent in the trails till you reach a beautiful village named Jagat where houses are built of stones. It is situated at an altitude of 1,000 m above sea level.

Then heading in the trails you enter the wonderful Marsayangdi valley from where you make a slight climb into the forest path filled with beautiful vegetation.

Walking out through the paths you reach Chamje situated at an altitude of 1,430 m. From here you get to see the mesmerizing peak of Lamjung Himal.

You stay in one of the lodges for the night.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Chamje to Bagarchhap

Trek Duration: 5 to 6 hours

Trek Distance: 15.1 km

Maximum Altitude: 2,160 m above sea level

This day you will be heading towards Bagarchhap from Chamje which is a few hours walk.

Leaving the beautiful village behind you begin this trek by making an ascend in the paths viewing and passing the stunning terraced field. Then from here climb up entering the amazing forest of Rhododendron.

Walking out the forests you cross a suspension bridge over the Marsyangdi River. And again make an uphill climb in the zigzag routes till you arrive at the convergence of Marsayangdi and Dudh Khola.

Today you will have crossed various small streams and bridges before reaching Bagarchhap. The mesmerizing view of Annapurna II and Lamjung Himal is unobstructed from here. It lies at an altitude of 2,160 m

You stay here for the night.

Similar articles you may like:

  • Annapurna Circuit Trek Difficulty
  • Manaslu Vs Annapurna Circuit and Annapurna Base Camp Trek
  • Best Time For Annapurna Circuit Trek

Bagarchhap to Chame

Trek Duration: 4 to 5 hours

Trek Distance: 13.5 km

Maximum Altitude: 2,630 m above sea level

This day you will be heading towards Chame from Bagarchhap which is about 5 hours walk.

As you continue to walk the upward trails through the dense forest of pines and oaks. You walk past Danakyu before arriving at a beautiful village filled with the Tamang community situated at the laps of Lamjung Himal.

From here the trek is quite easy as you will be walking in flat land along the sides of Marsyangdi River moving past the villages of Thanchowk and Koto.

A little ahead from these villages lies your today’s destination Chame at an altitude of 2,630 m. You stay in one of the tea houses for the night.

Chame to Pisang

Trek Duration: 5 to 6 hours

Trek Distance: 13.6 km

Maximum Altitude: 3,190 m above sea level

This day you will be heading towards Pisang from Chame which is about a 6 hours walk.

Firstly you start the trek by crossing a suspension bridge above the Marsyangdi river and entering a lush green pine forest. You continue to follow the trail until you arrive at Bhratang.

From this place you make an ascend in the paths till Dhikur Pokhari viewing the magnificent peaks of Annapurna massif and Pisang Peak on each side.

As you head in the paths you arrive at Pisang situated at an altitude of 3,190 m. You stay in one of the guest houses for the night.

Pisang to Manang

Trek Duration: 5 to 6 hours

Trek Distance: 17.2 km

Maximum Altitude: 3,540 m above sea level

Today you will be heading towards Manang from Pisang which is about 6 hours walk.

You will be leaving Pisang and heading towards another village named Braga which is famous for having a 900 years old monastery. You will visit the monastery and continue to walk in the paths.

Crossing a wooden bridge over the Marsyangdi river you make a slight ascent in the trails through the forest of pines till you reach Ghyaru.

Then you continue to make an ascend uphill to Ngawal and then head down to Mungji which leads to the lower routes. And head towards Manang where you stay the night.

Manang is a beautiful village situated at an altitude of 3,540 m. You will have your acclimatization here to prevent altitude sickness and help your body adjust to the climate in higher altitudes.

You can spend your day exploring the inner and outer parts of the town. This town has many ancient monasteries you can visit. Or you can hike till the astounding lake of Gangapurna that gives out the panoramic view of Marsyangdi valley, Gangapurna, and Tilicho peak.

Also, you can explore a very old village of Tengi and return back to Manang. Overnight in one of the tea houses.

Manang to Ledar

Trek Duration: 4 to 5 hours

Trek Distance: 9.1 km

Maximum Altitude: 4,250 m above sea level

Today you will be heading towards Ledar from Manang which is a few hours walk. You begin the trek by making an uphill climb from Manang viewing the Annapurna ranges and Gangapurna till you arrive at Ghunsang.

From here you continue to follow the paths to Yak Kharka which is pasture land for animal grazing. Passing this place you enter a lush green forest and climb in the trails until you reach Ledar.

You stay here for the night.

Ledar- Thorung Phedi- High Camp

Trek Duration: 6 to 7 hours

Trek Distance: 7.3 km

Maximum Altitude (Thorung Phedi): 4,450 m above sea level

Maximum Altitude(High Camp): 4,925 m above sea level

This day you will be heading towards High camp via Thorung Phedi which is about 7 hours walk from Ledar.

Ascending in the trails you will cross a small stream and again make a steep climb to a tea shop. Then from here taking a steep climb in the uneven paths, you reach Thorung Phedi. Situated at an altitude of 4,450 m.

From there you continue to take the uphill paths till you reach High Camp situated at an altitude of 4,925 m. You get to see the wide-angle view of Annapurna, Manaslu, Lamjung, and many more from here.

Viewing the mountain peaks you head back to Thorong Peak where you stay in one of the lodges for the night.

High Camp to Muktinath

Trek Duration: 7 to 8 hours

Trek Distance: 16.4 km

Maximum Altitude: 3,800 m above sea level

This day you head towards Muktinath from High camp which is about an 8 hours walk.

Today you will be waking up early and again ascend towards High Camp. Reaching High Camp you climb up to Thorung La Pass situated at an altitude of 5,416 m above sea level.

This is one of the highest Passes in Nepal that gives a great view of the Kali Gandaki Valley and many mountain peaks such as Dhaulagiri, Annapurna, etc.

After a wonderful view, you head down the steep paths until you arrive at Muktinath.

This is a holy place for both Hindu and Buddhist that lies on the foot of Thorong La Mountain Pass 5,416 m . It is one of the highest temples in Nepal that reside in an altitude above 3,000 m

You stay in one of the lodges for the night.

Muktinath to Marpha

Trek Duration: 6 to 7 hours

Maximum Altitude: 2,670 m above sea level

This day you will be heading towards Marpha from Muktinath which is about a 7 hours walk.

You wake up early this morning and visit the Muktinath temple. After offering your prayers to the god you head down in the paths to Jharkot. Then from there make a steep descent to Khingar.

Following the trials alongside Thorong Khola, you reach Kagbeni, a beautiful village situated at an altitude of 2,804 m above sea level. Continuing the downhill paths through river beds alongside Kali Gandaki river you reach Jomsom.

Jomsom is a windy and beautiful town situated at an altitude of 2,743 m above sea level. From here you make a steep descent till you reach Marpha the apple capital nation of Nepal.

This town is famous for hosting apple brandy and many apple gardens. The local people living in this place belong to the Thakali community.

You stay here for the night.

Marpha to Kalopani

Trek Duration: 5 to 6 hours

Maximum Altitude: 2,460 m above sea level

This day you head towards Kalopani from Marpha which is about 6 hours walk. You begin the trek by walking along the river beds of the Kali Gandaki river and passing the villages of Tukuce and Larjung.

Along the paths, you get to view the outstanding view of Dhaulagiri massif. Viewing these views you descend the paths and cross a suspension bridge. Entering the dense forests you walk ahead in the paths.

You will have crossed many suspension bridges before you arrive at Kalopani. You can visit the famous Cultural Thakali Museum and view the magnificent massifs of Annapurna and Dhaulagiri that surround the village.

You stay in one of the lodges for the night.

Kalopani to Tatopani

Trek Duration: 6 to 7 hours

Maximum Altitude: 1,190 m above sea level

This day you head towards Tatopani from Kalopani which is about 7 hours walk. You begin the trek by making a descent passing through mani walls till Ghasa. And from here you walk past a beautiful waterfall named Rupse Chhahara.

We stay in this waterfall for a bit then head down in the paths to Dana village that offers another wonderful waterfall. Walking for a bit you cross a suspension bridge over the Kali Gandaki river and reach Tatopani.

This day you will have crossed many suspension bridges. Tatopani is a natural hot spring water situated at an altitude of 1,190 m. The local people believe that the water has healing power so you can take a dip there and relax your body.

You stay in one of the lodges for the night.

Tatopani to Ghorepani

Trek Duration: 7 to 8 hours

Trek Distance: 13.1 km

Maximum Altitude: 2,870 m above sea level

This day you head towards Ghorepani from Tatopani which is about an 8 hours walk.

You begin by ascending in the trails to Shika village through Ghara village. Along the way, you get to view the mesmerizing mountain peaks such as Machhapuchhre and Annapurna south.

Viewing the mountain peaks you climb uphill taking steps made of stone through forests of Rhododendron enjoying the scenic views.

Reaching Ghorepani you stay there for the night.

Ghorepani to Nayapul to Pokhara

Total Duration: 7 to 8 hours

Total Distance: 35.1 km

Maximum Altitude: 820 m above sea level

This day you head towards Nayapul and drive back to Pokhara. The total duration is about 8 hours today.

You wake up early and hike up to Poon Hill to view the sunrise that looks outstanding from there. As the sun rises over the mountain ranges shining its rays towards the valley this is a remarkable experience.

Spending some time there you now descend to Ulleri passing through forests of oaks and rhododendron. Then using a stone step you descend down the path till you reach Hille. From there walk in the trail you reach Nayapul.

Reaching Nayapul you take the transportation back to Pokhara via the Baglung highway. Pokhara is a beautiful city of lakes situated at an altitude of 820 m

The rest of the day is unplanned so you can visit attractions sites or go cycling through the city. There are many activities to do in this place.

You stay in one of the hotels tonight.

Pokhara to Kathmandu

Drive Duration: 7 to 8 hours

Drive Distance: 204 km

Maximum Altitude: 1,400 m above sea level

This day you head back to Kathmandu from Pokhara taking good memories of the trip along with you. Along the way, you get to see many small settlements and drive alongside the Trishuli River.

Arriving at Kathmandu the member of Base Camp adventure bids you farewell hoping your Annapurna Circuit Trek was Great.

Final Say

Annapurna Circuit Trek is one of the most amazing treks of the Annapurna region. You get to explore the region as well as encircle the magnificent Annapurna Massif.

You begin your journey by driving out of Kathmandu to Bhulbhule from where you begin your trek and ending it in Pokhara drive back to the starting point.

Throughout the trek, you get to see many striking views of Mountain peaks and walk in paths filled with unique species of flora and fauna. Also, experience the hospitality provided by the locals.

This is an amazing trek that helps you make memories that last for a lifetime. This detailed article on Annapurna Circuit Trek Map will help you complete your trek with no trouble.

title: Annapurna Circuit Trek Packing List
excerpt: Annapurna Circuit trek is an exquisite trek in the foothills of the Himalayas. The trails of this majestic trek pass through the diverse landscapes of the Annapurna region. You will start from the…
html:
Annapurna Circuit trek is an exquisite trek in the foothills of the Himalayas. The trails of this majestic trek pass through the diverse landscapes of the Annapurna region. You will start from the lowlands of Besisahar to barren, arid landscapes of the Mustang region. This high altitude trek is quite challenging especially for first time trekkers.

Proper clothing, including footwear, headgear, and gloves are essential for the trek. A first aid box or a kit with all the necessary medications and preventive medical kits will help you immensely during the trek. Besides that, you will also need some accessories, toiletries, and important documents as well.

Moreover, the season of the trek also determines the packing list for the Annapurna Circuit trek. If you trek on the peak season of Autumn and Spring, you can pack lightly with appropriate clothing and trekking gear. However, the offseason treks require dense packing with warm clothes and raincovers.

Furthermore, you should only pack those items that are essential for the trek. If your baggage is too heavy for you to carry, then you can always hire a porter. But what to pack for the Annapurna Circuit trek? You might wonder. Don’t worry, as you have arrived at the right place. Read further to know more about the Annapurna Circuit trek packing list and other relevant information.

Annapurna Circuit Trek Packing List

Clothing

Annapurna Circuit Trek is a high altitude trek that requires you to dress in layers. Proper clothing and dressing in layers will keep you warm from throughout the trek. Wool, cotton and denim are the most used materials in these trekking clothes as they absorb moisture very well.

Moreover, you can add or remove layers of your clothing based on the weather conditions. The starting point of the trek Besisahar is at an altitude of 1,000 m and reaches the highest point of 5,416 m at Thorong La Pass. You should also dress according to the season of the trek.

Lower body layer

Trekkers need to carry quick-drying, waterproof, and convertible trousers for the trek. You can either wear short or full convertible hiking trousers during the trek. Wool or fleece are the two most ideal materials for the high altitude trek. These waterproof trousers are warm and comfortable.

Inner layer

Trekkers should include at least five pairs of quick-drying and breathable underwear in Annapurna Circuit Trek packing list. The thermal wear will keep you warm and comfortable during the trek. At least two pairs of thermal wear are essential.

Upper layer

For the Annapurna Circuit trek, you can carry light synthetic upper layer clothing. You can wash and dry them quickly. Long-sleeved shirts protect you from sunburn and harsh winds during the winter trek. Short-sleeved shirts are ideal for summertime trekking.

List of clothing:

  • Hiking shorts
  • Hiking trousers
  • Fleece Windstopper jacket
  • Light thermal tops
  • Non-cotton underwear briefs
  • Down vest
  • Waterproof breathable fabric shell jacket
  • Polypropylene shirts (1 half sleeve and two long sleeves)
  • Waterproof shell pants with breathable fabric
  • Waterproof Gore-Tex jacket
  • Lightweight thermal bottoms
  • Fleece or wool trousers

Footwear

Footwears are an essential part of the Annapurna Circuit Trek packing list. Trekking boots and comfortable trekking socks will help you immensely during the trek.

Hiking boots

The hiking boots help you pass through the rugged terrains of the region. The trails of this lovely trek pass through the dense forestlands, muddy ground, riverbanks, and even snow.

Hence, you need a reliable pair of hiking boots during the trek. A good grip along with a lightweight, durability will help you with the trek.

Pair of Sandals/Flip-Flops

A pair of sandals or flip-flops is necessary during your stay at the teahouses and lodges during the Annapurna Circuit trek. They are essential while taking a shower or bathroom breaks before and after the trek.

Trekking Thermal Socks

Thermal socks will help you keep your feet warm during the Annapurna Circuit Trek. You need light, breathable, and observant socks. These will prevent blisters among the trekkers. A lightweight sock will keep you fresh in the summers.

Gaiters

Gaiters are waterproof protective garments that cover you from the ankle to the calf. They will help you from the water, stones, mud, snow, and dust. Gaiters are comfortable to wear and light.

List of footwear:

  • Lightweight inner socks
  • Hiking boots with spare laces
  • Heavy poly or wool socks
  • Cotton socks Gaiters
  • Trainers or running shoes

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Gloves

Gloves are a great piece of clothing to keep your hands warm and comfortable during the trek. They save you from cold and frostbite. These gloves must have water and wind protection. Mittens, lightweight wool or fleece gloves, and lightweight poly-liner gloves are some of the popular gloves during the trek.

Headwear

Headwears are another important part of the trekking adventure. The headband, beanie, sunglasses are some of the necessary headwears during this trek. These items will help you get protected from rain, snow, and harsh sunlight.

Hat or fleece hat

A Hat or fleece helps you during the summer. They will protect your face and skin from sunburn. A fleece hat is ideal for keeping you safe from snow in winters and higher altitudes.

Sunglasses

Sunglasses protect the eyes from the harsh sun. The sun in the Himalayas is severe as it gets reflected from the snowy mountains at higher altitudes. You will also get protected from the massive gust of wind.

Bandana or scarf

Bandana/ Scarf is an optimal gear for the Annapurna Circuit. Bandana/ Scarf helps trekkers to cover your mouth and nose.

List of Head wears:

  • Sunglasses with UV protection
  • A warm hat (wool or synthetic)
  • Prescription sunglasses
  • Bandana or headscarf
  • Headlamp with extra batteries and bulbs

Sleeping Accessories

Sleeping bags are the best companion during your trek. Although you will get blankets in the teahouses, they are not enough in the cold conditions. Therefore, a suitable sleeping bag will keep you warm during cold nights.

Moreover, you can also get yourself a sleeping bag liner. Both these sleeping accessories will help you immensely during the trek.

Trekking gear and equipment

The Annapurna Circuit trek packing list must include a range of trekking gears. Some of the trekking gear and equipment needed for the trek are as follows:

Hiking Backpack or daypack

A Hiking Backpack or daypack is essential for the Annapurna Circuit trek. You can carry all your trekking gears and necessary clothing on the backpack. The waterproof hiking backpack will help you immensely during the trek.

A porter or a porter guide will help you to carry the backpack if your luggage is heavy. A daypack is ideal if you do not wish to hire a porter. You can also keep your documents, toiletries, and other items in the daypack.

Trekking Poles

A Trekking Pole is essential during the steep, harsh terrain of the Annapurna circuit. Trekking poles will help you a lot to increase stability and reduce knee pressures.

Headlamps

A headlamp is an optional gear for a trekking adventure. Few sections of the Annapurna circuit trek requires early morning treks before sunrise. Hence, a good headlamp will come in handy on those occasions. Headlamps are also helpful if you arrive at your destinations in the dark.

Raincoats

Raincoats are a necessity in the Summer – Monsoon treks. You can also get a good rain cover for your backpack.

First aid

The first aid items will help you in case of any medical emergencies during the trek. Altitude sickness is one of the major problems in these high altitude treks. The common cold is quite common among trekkers during this high altitude trek. Besides that, muscle sprains, injuries are common as well.

Diamox tablets help you to avoid altitude sickness or acute mountain sickness during the trek. Paracetamol helps you to tackle fever and diarrhoea. The risk of injuries and other medical emergencies is quite high during the trek. Medical facilities are not readily available during the trek. A small first aid kit is a great help during the trek.

Diamox Tablets

Diamox tablets help to prevent altitude sickness among trekkers and are quite popular among trekkers. The tablet also helps to reduce the symptoms of acute mountain sickness like dizziness, headache, and nausea.

Colds and Coughs medicines

Trekking in the high Himalayan conditions is challenging due to the weather conditions. Cough and cold are one of the significant challenges of the Annapurna Circuit Trek. These medicines will keep you safe during the trek.

Blister Plasters

Blister plasters are protective measures for the painful blisters and small wounds after the trek. Hence, you can carry blister plasters during the trek.

Similar articles you may like:

  • Annapurna Circuit Trek Difficulty
  • Best Time For Annapurna Circuit Trek
  • How to Trek Solo in Nepal

Anti-Diarrheal Tablets

The food facilities along the trail are not of high hygienic value. Hence, diarrhoea is quite common among trekkers during the trek. Unhygienic foods and water can cause some digestive problem as well. Therefore, anti-diarrheal pills are thus essential during the trek in the Annapurna region.

Painkillers or Pain Relieving Ointments

Painkillers or Pain Relieving Ointments is necessary as muscle strains, physical pain, and headaches are quite common during the trek. These medications and painkillers help you to reduce pain. Pain relieving ointments are ideal for muscle pain or strains.

Water Purification tablets

Water purification tablets help to purify the water resources along the trail. The water resources along the path include rivers, waterfalls, and others. Water from these resources and even the tap is not fit for drinking directly.

Moreover, you need to purify the water before drinking to protect yourself from water-borne diseases. The bottled mineral water is quite expensive and not readily available during the trek. Hence, water purification tablets and solutions like Piyush are quite effective and practical.

Regular Medicines

You should pack your medicines that you take on a regular basis. You can schedule your medication during the trip on the consultation of the doctor.

Antiseptic solution

An antiseptic solution like Dettol will help you to tackle small injuries or wounds. They will stop the infection from the wounds to spread further.

Other medicines include:

  • Diamox/ Altitude Sickness tablet
  • Paracetamol
  • Imodium
  • Insect Repellent
  • Chlorine Dioxide Tablets
  • Water Purification Tablets
  • Small Bandages and plasters
  • Antiseptic Wipes
  • Antiseptic Cream

Toiletries

Toiletries are the items for the day to day activities during your trek. Some of the important toiletries you need to pack are as follows:

  • Toothbrush
  • Toothpaste
  • Toilet paper
  • Medium-sized towel
  • Anti-bacterial handwash
  • Multi-purpose soap
  • Deodorants
  • Nail clippers
  • Wet wipes

Important Documents

Passport

You must carry your passport during the trek. You will need to show the passports at various checkpoints during the trek.

Travel Permits

There are several Travel and trekking permits required for the Annapurna Circuit Trek. You can get these permits with the help of your trekking agency before the start of the trek.

Travel Insurance

A travel insurance package is essential during the Annapurna Circuit Trek. You might require medical attention and even emergency evacuation during the trek. The best travel insurance package covers the altitude of 4,000 m and above.

Other Miscellaneous Items for the Annapurna Circuit Trek Packing List

  • Camera with extra Batteries
  • Headphone
  • Power Banks
  • Oximeters
  • Chargers
  • Maps
  • Adapter Plugs
  • Journal for Writing
  • Travel knife
  • Book / Kindle for reading
  • Smartphone
  • Snacks
  • Protein bars, Snickers, granola bars, dark chocolates
  • Lightweight pillowcase

Essential Tips for the Annapurna Circuit Trek Packing List

  • Get a good backpack for the trek
  • You should pack according to the time of the trek
  • Always pack enough hygiene products
  • You should pack quick-dry clothes and towels
  • Always pack clothes in layers
  • Pack only essential items
  • Avoid packing luxury items
  • You should pack your waste on a separate plastic bag
  • Always should break-in your shoes ahead of the trek
  • You should rent sleeping bags, a down jacket and other trekking gears

Things to Consider in the Annapurna Circuit Trek Packing List

Season of the trek

The packing list for the Annapurna Circuit trek also depends upon the season of the trek. The autumn season (September to November) and spring season (March to May) is ideal for trekking. The stable weather conditions and the fewer chances of rainfall is the highlight of the trek in these seasons. The warm and favourable temperatures make trekking a pleasant adventure. You can pack lightly with appropriate clothing and trekking gear.

However, if you trek in the Winter season (December to February), you need to pack heavy with warm clothes. The Summer season trek (June to August) is hot and humid with maximum rainfall. Hence, you will need proper raincoats and rain covers to trek in the region. With adequate preparation, trekking in the Annapurna region is a great experience.

Weight of the baggage

The weight limit of the luggage is 15 kg. Hence, you should only pack those items that are essential for the trek. If your baggage exceeds the weight of the limit, then you can hire a porter.

Diverse geographical landscapes

The climatic conditions and geographic landscapes of the Annapurna region are quite diverse. The trek route ranges from low altitude plains to alpine forests of the region. You can pack your stuff and clothes as per the climatic conditions.

Shopping trekking gear and equipment

You can get trekking gear and equipment from Kathmandu. The trekking gear is available at a reasonable price. The

price of the trekking gear ranges from $500 to $1000. You can also rent the trekking gear and equipment at $1 per day.

The Final Say

The Annapurna Circuit Trek is a lovely adventure in the pristine Annapurna region. The Annapurna Circuit Trek packing list is a crucial part to consider during the trek. The packing list mostly depends upon the season of the trek.

Moreover, it also depends upon the trekker’s desire and requirements. You can hire a porter if you can’t handle the weight of your luggage on your own. Overall, this complete packing list for the Annapurna Circuit trek will help you immensely during the journey.

title: Mardi Himal Trek 5 days
excerpt: Mardi Himal Trek 5 days is an easy and adventurous trekking journey that takes you into the mountains through dense forests. Mardi Himal (5,587 m) is a peak, located beneath the well-known…
html:
Mardi Himal Trek 5 days is an easy and adventurous trekking journey that takes you into the mountains through dense forests. Mardi Himal (5,587 m) is a peak, located beneath the well-known Machapuchare ( 6,993 m) within the Annapurna region.

This 5 Days Mardi Himal trek is ideal for both beginners and professional trekkers. You can trek to Mardi and return back in a short amount of time. It is doable at any time of the year and is ideal for those who have a limited budget, short schedule, but still want to enjoy the Himalayas from up-close.

Mardi Himal Trek takes you through the lush green vegetation of Rhododendron forests, terraced fields, marvelous landscapes up towards the Mardi Base Camp (4,500 m). High Camp, Low Camp, Forest Camp, and the Mardi Himal Base Camp are some of the amazing places to be at.

Mardi Himal Trek 5 days provides a mesmerizing view of the Annapurna Himalayan ranges and also some of the snow-covered peaks such as Annapurna South (7,219 m), Hiuchuli (6,441 m), Mt. Machapuchare (6,993 m) and Mardi Himal (5,587 m) itself.

Apart from the mountains and other natural beauty, the Gurung people dominate the area with their antique culture, tradition, and lifestyle. These people are friendly and try to provide you with genuine hospitality and make your journey memorable.

During the trek, you can also meet some ethnic groups of people and also explore the ancient monasteries and stupas.

Trip Highlights of Mardi Himal Trek 5 days

  • Explore the adventurous and thrilling trails of Mardi Himal Trek.
  • Explore the beautiful Pokhara valley.
  • Scenic views of snow-covered mountains such as Annapurna South (7,219 m), Hiuchuli (6,441 m), Mt. Machapuchare (6,993 m) and Mardi Himal (5,587 m) itself.
  • Visit the beautiful High Camp (3,700 m) and the highest point of the trek Mardi Base Camp (4,500 m).
  • Walkthrough rivers, dense forest, and lush green vegetation.
  • Explore the Gurung culture and traditions, and lifestyle of the locals and other ethnic groups of people.
  • Unspoiled tourist destination and adventurous trekking routes.

Best time for Mardi Himal Trek 5 days

As 5 Days Mardi Himal Trek is an average rated trek, it is doable at any time of the year. However, you’ll need proper trekking gear and equipment with proper planning for the trek.

The best time to do this trek starts in spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November) season. During this season, the weather and temperature are mild and stable. The rivers, waterfalls, landscapes, gorges, and streams are at its fullest.

The atmosphere is clean and green throughout spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November) season. You can see the beautiful snow-covered peaks and Himalayan ranges without any distractions of bad weather or clouds blocking your views.

  • Mardi Himal Trek Difficulty
