Weather and Temperature of Mardi Himal Trek

Mardi Himal Trek 5 days is a short and amazing trek in the Annapurna region. The weather and temperature differ according to the seasons.

Spring and Autumn seasons

Every season has its own glory and the spring (March to May) and Autumn (September to November) seasons are popular with travelers and trekkers in Nepal. During the spring and autumn seasons, the weather and temperature is mild and stable throughout the day. You can enjoy the clean and dry environment all over the valley.

However, the nights and early mornings are cold but bearable. At day time the temperature is around 20 degrees Celsius whereas, at night the temperature drops down to 5 degrees Celsius.

During spring and autumn seasons, the trail blooms with green vegetation of Rhododendrons and rare flora and fauna. The sky is clear which provides mesmerizing views of the Himalayan range. You might face slight rainfall in the evenings during autumn seasons but only in early September.

Summer (June to August) seasons

Trekking in the summer (June to August) seasons is different from trekking in other seasons. You’ll experience heavy rainfalls during the summer season, mostly in evenings and nights. But the rainfall is lighter when you reach higher altitudes.

Due to the heavy amount of rainfall, the visibility gets poor and increases the number of leech in the forest. While you’re trekking in the summer season, make sure you wear long trekking trousers and carry insect repellant or table salts with you.

In summer, the temperature ranges from 10 to 23 degree Celsius during day time whereas the temperature ranges from 5-10 degree Celsius in the night and early morning.

Winter (December to February) season

The winter (December to February) season is very cold in the Annapurna region. As you reach higher altitudes, there is more chance for snowfall and very cold nights.

It can be difficult to stand against the cold climate conditions but the trails become much more adventurous and memorable providing heavenly views of nature. The snow enhances the beauty of nature and many experienced trekkers love to trek during these seasons.

The skies and the Himalayan ranges are clear and beautiful. You can enjoy the peaceful trails without any disturbance of a large number of crowds.

In the winter season, the temperature ranges between 9 to 12 degree Celsius. And the temperature drops to around – 5 degrees Celsius in nights and mornings.

Difficulties of Mardi Himal Trek 5 days

5 Days Mardi Himal Trek is an easy rated trek in Nepal. However, there are some difficulties that you might face during the trek. You’ll complete the trek successfully if you equip yourself with proper trekking gear and equipment and follow the instruction of your guide.

Altitude

As you elevate from 1,400 m to 4,500 m, there is a higher chance of altitude sickness and any individual can get altitude sickness.

In order to prevent altitude sickness, you’ll be taking easy and gentle steps towards your destination with lots of short breaks during the trek. Staying hydrated is also important and helps you overcome altitude sickness.

As you elevate higher the weather and temperature also drop resulting in a cold and chill atmosphere. So, be sure to wear proper trekking gear to face any kind of climate conditions.

Remote trails

5 days Mardi Himal Trek continues and takes you through some of the most remote parts of Nepal. Even if the trails are remote and rugged, it becomes a much more adventurous and enjoyable journey.

The trails are slippery and wet due to heavy rainfall in the summer season and in the winter season, the snow covers the trails which makes it hard for trekking. And the straight long descent towards Siding can be difficult as well.

Useful gear and equipment

The climate conditions can differ from time to time. You’ll never know what kind of weather and temperature awaits while you’re trekking.

In off-seasons, the weather and temperature change a lot. So, you’ll need proper gear and equipment with less and useful packing because they play a big role in the success of the trek.

Tips for Mardi Himal Trek 5 Days

  • Starting early is the best thing you can do during the trek. It helps you to escape from the hassles such as rain, heat, lack of accommodation and you can enjoy nature and the trek in a beautiful way.
  • Your body thrives for energy as you walk 5-7 hours a day. So, you need to clean and healthy food packed with protein and energy.
  • Keeping your body hydrated is another best thing you can do to complete the trek with ease and success. Your body dehydrates fast and can cause altitude sickness, headache, dizziness and many more. So, take short breaks time and again and stay hydrated.
  • If you are not experienced and have a hard time walking then we suggest you do some light physical exercises 2-3 weeks ahead of the trek. It’ll help you a lot to increase your fitness and stamina.
  • Wear comfortable and good quality trekking gear. You should be ready to face all the challenges that the Mardi Himal Trek has to offer.

Food and Accommodation

There is a wide variety of food and accommodation facilities to choose from, especially in Pokhara. However, as you start the trek and ascend higher and higher towards the remote area of Nepal, the option for food and accommodation becomes typical and limited.

During your stay in Pokhara, we’ll provide you with standard rooms that are clean and comfortable. You can choose from both typical Nepalese cuisine and International cuisine.

In the Mardi region, the area is remote and the food and accommodation are basic and average. However, the guide will try to provide some of the best for you.

The accommodation facilities are basic with twin beds that are clean and comfortable. Most of the time you’ll spend the nights in a lodge or teahouse. But at Siding (1,800 m), you’ll be spending the night with the locals at their home by paying them or Homestay. They will also provide you delicious food with great hospitality and care.

As Nepal has a wide variety of food and drinks, food like Dal Bhat, Dhindo, local bread, Momo, Pancakes and many more are available almost all around Nepal. These foods are delicious and will help keep you energized throughout the trek.

Itinerary

Day 01: Drive to Kande (1,770 m) and trek to Pothana / Deurali (2,125 m)

Driving duration: 1 hour

Walking duration: 3-4 hours

Upon your arrival at Pokhara (1,400 m), you’ll be taking a short ride towards Kande. Located in the Kaski district of Nepal, Pokhara is a beautiful place with religious temples, stupas, lakes, landscapes, caves, and other natural beauties. Pokhara is very famous with travelers and a tourist destination in Nepal.

After an hour drive from Pokhara, you’ll reach the small and beautiful village of Kande ( 1,770 m). From Kande, you’ll officially start your trek to Pothana/ Deurali (2,125 m).

You’ll reach Australian Base Camp (1,890 m) after an hour of trekking from Kande. From, Australian Base Camp you can witness beautiful views of sunrise, green hills, and Annapurna Himalayan range. You’ll reach Pothan after a short walk from the Australian Base Camp. Overnight stay in a lodge at Pothana / Deurali.

Day 02: Trek to Low Camp (3,150 m) from Pothana / Deurali (2,125 m)

Walking duration: 5-6 hours

Today, on the second day of 5 days Mardi Himal Trek, you’ll be trekking from Pothana / Deurali to Low camp (3,150 m). Low Camp (3,150 m) is a beautiful place that provides picturesque views of Mt. Machhapuchhre (6,993 m).

You’ll gradually ascend uphill for a few hours while passing through the dense sub-tropical forest and you’ll reach towards the Forest camp (2,900 m).

After some rest and food at the Forest camp, you’ll continue the trek. As you walk through the dense Rhododendron forest, you’ll witness some beautiful flora and fauna and might get to see wildlife animals such as Himalayan Thar, Langur Monkeys, and Musk Deer.

After walking about 3-4 hours from Forest camp, you’ll finally reach Low Camp. Overnight stay in a lodge at Low Camp.

Day 03: Trek to High Camp (3,700 m) from Low Camp (3,150 m)

Walking duration: 3-4 hours

On this day of 5 days Mardi Himal Trek, you’ll be trekking from Low Camp to High Camp ( 3,700 m). High Camp is a small and beautiful area that provides a mesmerizing view of Hiuchuli (6,441 m), Annapurna south (7,219 m), and Mt. Machapuchare (6,993 m).

After your breakfast, you’ll continue the trek by gradually ascending towards Middle Camp. Upon reaching the Middle Camp, you’ll walk through the dense forest of Rhododendron and Oaks forest until you reach a place called Baadal Danda (Hill above the clouds).

You’ll continue the trek after some rest at Baadal Danda. You’ll walk for another 2 hours along with the Mardi Himalayan range until you reach High Camp. Overnight stay in a lodge at High Camp.

Day 04: Trek to Mardi Base Camp (4,500 m) from High Camp and trek down to Siding (1,800 m)

Walking duration: 8-9 hours

After a pleasant breakfast at the High Camp, you’ll trek towards the most anticipated destination of the trek Mardi Base Camp (4,500 m). Mardi Base Camp provides an amazing view of Mt. Mardi (5,587 m) itself and other beautiful snow-capped mountains.

It will be a long trek, so you’ll be starting early in the morning from High Camp as you slowly ascend through the rocky trails for about 5 hours until reaching the Mardi Base Camp.

The view from the Mardi Base Camp is heavenly as you gaze upon the beautiful Mardi Himalayan range including the beautiful snow-covered peaks such as Hiuchuli (6,441 m), Annapurna south (7,219 m), and Mt. Machapuchare (6,993 m).

After spending some time at the base camp, you’ll head back towards High Camp and then gradually descend downhill towards Low Camp following the same trail.

After you reach the Low Camp, you’ll be taking a different route to reach Siding (1,800 m). The trekking trails can get a little difficult because of the continuous downhill descent, however you’ll be taking lots of rest and walking gently.

After a long and tiring walk, you’ll finally reach Siding. Siding is a beautiful village that offers you a traditional Nepalese culture and the typical lifestyle of the people. Homestay at Siding for the night.

Day 05: Trek to Lumre from Sidding (1,800 m) and drive back to Pokhara (1,400 m) by jeep

Walking duration: 3 hours

Driving duration: 2 hour

Today will be the last day of 5 days Mardi Himal Trek. After your breakfast, you’ll trek towards a place called Lumre from Siding (1,800 m).

You’ll continue the trek as you pass through the Kalimati and Ghalel village and finally you’ll reach Lumre.

After some rest and food at Lumre, a private jeep will pick you up and you’ll head back towards the beautiful city of Pokhara and the trip will come to an end.

Packing list for Mardi Himal Trek 5 days

Mardi Himal Trek 5 days doesn’t require any bulky packing and heavy clothes. It also depends on the time of year that you have decided to go on the trek. In the list below, we have provided you with a general packing list for Mardi Himal Trek 5 days:

Mandatory Documents

  • Citizenship and passport copy.
  • Passport size photo (required for permits).
  • Copy of valid visa document.
  • Trekking permits.

Important items

  • A comfortable sleeping bag.
  • A good quality backpack.
  • Trekking poles.
  • Trekking map.
  • UV protection sunglasses.
  • Refillable water bottles including a purifier.
  • A power bank and a day pack because as you ascend higher, there are no proper electricity and Internet facilities.
  • Basic first aid kit including your personal medicines.

Clothing

  • Rainproof pants and jackets for early September.
  • Windproof pants and jackets.
  • Hiking shorts.
  • Sun protection hats to avoid sunburn.
  • Pair of good quality and comfortable hiking boots.
  • 2-3 pairs of warm socks and 2-3 pairs of normal socks.
  • Warm hand gloves.
  • T-shirts (full or half sleeves).
  • Down jackets.
  • Fleece jackets.

Toiletries

  • Sunscreen lotions and cream to avoid sunburn on your face and body.
  • Quick-dry medium size towel.
  • Toothbrush and paste.
  • Multi-purpose soap and anti-bacterial handwash.
  • Wet wipes and tissue.
  • Nail clippers.
  • Face and body moisturizer.

Conclusion

Mardi Himal Trek 5 days is a short and easy trek filled with mesmerizing adventures, sceneries, and the beautiful culture and tradition of the Gurung civilization.

Located at the lap of Mardi Himal, you’ll walk through the foothills of Annapurna peak to Mardi Base Camp (4,500 m). You’ll enjoy the trails filled with beautiful nature such as the lush green vegetation with beautiful flora and fauna, rivers, waterfalls, landscapes, and the incredible Himalayan range and snow-covered peaks.

The 5 days Mardi Himal Trek is also suitable for any individual. For further details feel free to contact us.

title: Everest Base Camp Permit Cost
excerpt: Everest Base Camp Trek is a high altitude trek in the highest mountain of the world. Everest Base Camp Trek is an adventurous journey with the best views of the mountains and valleys in the region…
html:
Everest Base Camp Trek is a high altitude trek in the highest mountain of the world. Everest Base Camp Trek is an adventurous journey with the best views of the mountains and valleys in the region along with glaciers and flora and fauna.

Wondering what permits are required for the infamous Everest Base Camp Trek and what it costs you? Everest Base Camp Permit Cost includes the cost of various permits required for the trek in the Everest Region.

Usually, your trekking company deals with the permits and other requirements of trekking in the Everest Region. So trekkers usually don’t have much knowledge of the Everest Base Camp Trek permit costs and where to get them. Worry not if you are planning to travel solo without a company or just hungry for some information on the trekking permits in the region, you have reached the right destination.

Everest region is one of the many treasures of Nepal. It has defined Nepal for ages on end. So it is safe to say it is the most treasured one of all. So to protect this treasured region, Nepal has put in place some rules and mandatory permits for anyone touring in the area.

Being one of the most popular attractions among tourists all over the world, Nepal had to put some protective measures at place for the protection of this area. Hence comes the required permits for the area.

The Everest base Camp Trek Permits are an important measure for the protection of the area along with an alternative to keeping records of the activities in the Region. Also the Everest Base Camp Trek Permit Costs vary from one individual to another based on their nationality. The permits are also important for the Everest Base Camp helicopter tour.

Types of Everest Base Camp Permits

Trekking in the Everest Region does not only require you to prepare yourself mentally and physically but also prepare your trekking permits. Everest Base Camp Permits includes mainly 2 permits. However, the permits required for your trek depends on the routes you are planning to take.

The Everest Base Camp Permits Costs are explained below:

Sagarmatha National Park Permit

The route for the Everest Base Camp Trek goes through the Sagarmatha National Park. As mentioned above, Everest Region is considered one of the major treasures of the country and is protected inside the National Park.

As you reach the entrance gate of the National Park, you will have to show them your Sagarmatha National Park Permit to enter the region and go further. In the national park, you get to see the protected floras and fauna along with the exotic and endangered biodiversity and mountains.

This Everest Base Camp Permit cost varies based on the nationality of the individual. The information on the Everest Base Camp Permit Cost for the Sagarmatha National Park Permit is shown in detail below:

Permit Cost for Nepali citizens- NRs 100 per person

Permit Cost for SAARC Nationals – NRs 1500 per person which is approximately USD 15

Permit Cost for Foreigners – NRs 3000 per person which is approximately USD 30.

The trek permit as this one is also prepared by your trekking company so you don’t really have to worry much about the process of the permit.

Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Entrance Permit

Another important Everest Base Camp Permit cost involves Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Entrance Permit. This is one of the first permits you will require before beginning your Everest Base Camp Trek. The entrance of the Khumbu region requires you to show proof that you are not a harmful being to the region and its people.

Khumbu Municipality entrance permit is required for you to enter the Khumbu Region. This Everest Base Camp Permit cost is the same for all individuals regardless of their nationality. Every foreigner needs to pay NRs 2000 per person to enter the Khumbu region. The Khumbu Rural Municipality costs approximately USD 20 per person.

Gaurishankar Conservation Area Permit

Apart from the above two permits, you may also require the Gaurishankar Conservation Area Permit based on your Everest Base Camp Trek itinerary.

If you are planning on taking the Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek route, you will need this additional permit. The permit for Gaurishankar Conservation Area will cost you NPR 3000 per person which is approximately USD 30 per person.

Required documents for Everest Base Camp Permits

The required Everest Base Camp Permits are extremely important for your trek in the Everest Region. Not just for trekking but also for tourists travelling in the area are required to have these permits at hand.

There are a few documents that are required on your part in order to get these permits granted to you. You cannot just go and ask for a permit and get it with no questions asked. There will be a procedure for getting the Everest Base Camp Permits.

The documents that are required from you for obtaining the Everest Base Camp Permits are listed below:

  • Passport original with six months validity
  • Two passport photos
  • Nepal entry Visa
  • Cash for permit fees
  • Travel insurance is highly recommended for rescue

You may also like:

  • Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return
  • Luxury Lodge Trek to Everest Base Camp
  • Everest View Trek | Short Everest View Trekking Route

How to get the Everest Base Camp Permits?

Okay, so by now, your most rising question must be : where and how do i get these permits? Well, for starters, if you have a package with a trekking company, they will be responsible for all your trek permits. They will get the documents from and you and most probably get the permits ready before your arrival . You will be all set for the trek with your permits for your trek if you are planning your trek with a trekking company.

However, if you are someone who is trekking solo or without a guide or a company, you can get these permits easily. You will have two options where you can either get these permits in Kathmandu before your trek or at the point of entry.

In Kathmandu, you can go to the Tourism board and get these trekking permits after submitting your required documents and filling a form.

But if you are not willing to make an extra detour, you can wait in line and get the permits at the spot where the permit is required. For example, you can submit your documents and get the Sagarmatha National Park Permit at the entry gate of Sagarmatha National Park. The Everest Base Camp Permit costs will not vary based on where you get your permits.

Why are permits required for the Everest Base Camp Trek?

Ever wondered why you need permits for simple trekkings ? Well at first, trekking permits were introduced to help control border issues. This means it was to monitor and control people who would try to use these routes to cross the borders. However, later in the days, these permits were put into practice and passed on as a means of protecting and preserving the resources of the region from being harmed.

The Everest region was put under the Sagarmatha National Park region to protect its vegetation and the flora and fauna from getting exploited by the trekkers or travellers. There are many endangered animals which could have been the result of the exploitation from the travellers. So this permit requirement was a brilliant way of protecting this area and its components.

Apart from the protection aspect, the once required TIMS permit was replaced with the Khumbu Municipality Permit in favor of the local people. This permit acts as a way of supporting the locals and their lifestyle. The proceeds from the Khumbu Rural Municipality Permit goes to the people of the municipality as they are the ones who take care of the region and this is a way of returning the favor to them .

FAQs

Are the permits required for children as well?

The permit requirements depend on the age of the children. Any child under the age of 10 does not need any permits for the trek. As long as the kid is physically and mentally able to handle the trek, s/he can enjoy the trek without worrying about any trekking permits. However, make sure s/he is always accompanied by a guardian. Everest Base Camp Trek with Kids is another memorable way to spend your quality time.

Do you need a TIMS card for Everest Base Camp trek ?

No, TIMS cards are no longer required for the Everest Base Camp Trek. The TIMS card has now been replaced by the Khumbu Rural Municipality Permit as per 2018. This decision was made in favor of the local people as they are the ones who are now benefiting from the Khumbu permit which helps improve their lifestyle.

What are the places to apply for the Everest Base Camp Permits?

You can apply for the Everest Base Camp permits in either Kathmandu or in Monjo. You can take a day before your trek and get all the permits ready beforehand in Kathmandu then head over to your trek, but if you are not upto the detour, you can start your trek and get the permits at Monjo or at the entrance. The place to get your permit depends on you entirely.

Do I need cash in Nepalese Currency ?

For paying the Everest Base Camp Permit Costs, it is best to carry around cash. Better yet carrying around Nepalese currency is the best as the cost in USD may not be exact to the Nepalese currency and there is a chance of you paying more. However, to avoid any of these confusions, it is better to let your trekking company handle the trekking permit costs.

Hope you now have a clear idea of the Trekking Permits required for the Everest Base Camp Trek. Also, you must have had a better understanding of the Everest Base Camp permit costs by now and how and why they are imposed. We, at Base Camp Adventure, sincerely hope that this information was useful to you and wish you a safe and memorable journey ahead of you.

title: Manaslu Trek in September, October, November
excerpt: Manaslu Circuit Trek is one of the most popular trekking routes of Nepal and it is relatively new. It is perfect throughout the year but Manaslu trek in September, October, November is most famous…
html:
Manaslu Circuit Trek is one of the most popular trekking routes of Nepal and it is relatively new. It is perfect throughout the year but Manaslu trek in September, October, November is most famous among them.

Manaslu trek offers you everything that a classic trek offers. It includes beautiful landscapes, ancient culture, and local people. In addition to this, you will view the 8 different peaks above 7,500 m with different flora and fauna all around the trekking routes. If you are lucky enough you will see wild animals like Snow Leopard, Blue Sheep, Himalayan Tahr.

Though the Manaslu Circuit trek is not as popular as Everest Base Camp trek and Annapurna Base Camp trek, it greets several hundreds of tourists every year. The remoteness and undisturbed natural beauty is both an advantage and disadvantage of this trek. It attracts some tourists whereas some tourists feel the risk to go over this region for the trek.

Trekking towards the Manaslu region gives you the lifetime experience through its beautiful landscape and majestic vistas of the great Himalayan range. Choosing the perfect destination is not enough, you should also select the comfortable weather.

Trekking season and weather also affect your journey. Each season comes with its own flavor and limitations. The Autumn season starts from September and ends in November. Manaslu Trek offers you the clear, bright skies with soothing temperature.

The Autumn season is the best season for trekking in any part of Nepal. With the perfect view of mountains and rivers, you will continue your trek through the Manaslu region. The trails may be full of crowds because it is the peak of tourist season.

This season has less or almost no chance of rainfall. Due to all of these benefits Manaslu trek in September, October, November is regarded as the best time to visit around this region.

Highlights of Manaslu Trek in September, October, and November

  • Walkthrough the undisturbed beauty of the Manaslu region.
  • There are fewer crowds as compared to other trekking circuits.
  • Exploration of lesser-known and hidden valleys of the Manaslu Circuit.
  • Manaslu Circuit Trek is one of the most adventurous trekking routes in Nepal.
  • You can reach up to the Tibetan border which is on the northern side of the Manaslu region.
  • During this trek, you will see the beautiful mountains like Mount Manaslu 8,163 m, Simrang, Hiunchuli, Ngadi, Ganesh Himal, and a few more.
  • It takes you to antique monasteries, chortens, and gompas of this region.
  • You will get inspiration from the tradition and lifestyle of Tibetan Buddhist culture.
  • Also, you can explore the Tsum valley.

Manaslu Trek in September

September is the start of the Autumn season in Nepal which is also a post-monsoon period. Within the month of September too, you will experience different weather and temperature. During the first week of September, you might experience some rainfall that disappears as September progresses.

Monsoon clouds become active usually in late afternoon or evening. As September reaches towards its mid-level, the rain stops and the temperature starts going down. It makes the weather more stable and dry. The skies are clear and provide the picture-perfect view of snow-capped mountains. As you ascend higher, the temperature goes on decreasing.

Manaslu trek in September attracts tourists more than in any other month. The days are warmer but nights are quite cold. It is normal if the temperature goes below the freezing point. Manaslu trek in Autumn takes you to a height of 700 m to 5,160 m

The average temperature on the higher altitude is 7°C at the altitude of 3,860 m that goes up to 21°C at the lower Manaslu region like Bagat 1,290 m

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Manaslu Trek in October

October is the most pleasant time to visit the Manaslu Circuit Trek. This is the perfect month within the Autumn season. The weather is pleasant and stable which provides a clear sky. It is neither too hot nor too cold for trekking around the Manaslu region.

October is one of the busiest months of this season and a perfect month to explore the rare and undisturbed beauty of the Manaslu area. This region will be full of trekkers and adventure travelers. It would be better if you pre-book your transportation, food, and accommodations.

This month also hosts the two prominent Hindu festivals of Nepal and they are Dashain and Tihar. Manaslu in Autumn, especially in October offers you the best weather. Average temperature lies between 13-25°C in Manaslu during the month of October.

The average temperature of the day time fluctuates between 15 to 16°C. As altitude increases, the temperature continues to decrease and at night the temperature can go below -1°C. The temperature around the places above 4,000 m falls below -2°C.

Manaslu Trek in November

The end of the Autumn season starts with November. It is the perfect month to travel around Manaslu area because after this, it starts getting more cold and dry. November is one of the driest months of the Autumn season.

As you get to the higher altitude, the temperature goes down and it may fall below the freezing points. There is also an annual Manaslu Trail Race/Marathon in the Autumn season. If you are interested, you can join this marathon or even avoid it.

The temperature remains around 12°C at Arughat 3,087 m, which is also the starting point of your Manaslu trek. The minimum temperature can go up to -3°C at places like Samagaon and Samdo 3,690 m

The weather of Manaslu Trek in September, October, November

Manaslu trek in September, October, November is arguably the best season to travel around this region. This is the Autumn season (September-November) which is neither too cold nor too hot. You may see the most perfect view of Sky and mountains only in this season.

The environment feels stable and peaceful which is the perfect time to climb Larke Peak. Being one of the busiest seasons of the year, the prices for various legal permits also goes up. The Autumn season comes with its own flavor and uniqueness. Each month of this season provides you different colors and texture to your Manaslu trek journey.

Some essential tips for the Manaslu trek

  • It is always best to travel in the Autumn season because you have to face fewer difficulties as compared to other seasons.
  • Carrying crampons can be beneficial for you in these conditions.
  • Bring your tent, sleeping bags, and a few other equipments, if you are planning to travel in the Winter season.
  • Training and a few cardio exercises always benefit you while traveling through these trekking trails.
  • It is always better not to drink or smoke because it only worsens the conditions.
  • Drink plenty of water, eat energy bars and keep going through the trails with proper rest from time to time.
  • Altitude sickness is always a major challenge in high-altitude treks like Manaslu so prepare yourself for these conditions.

Pros and Cons of Manaslu trek in Autumn

Every season has its own pros and cons. While trekking through the Manaslu Circuit in Autumn season you need to understand that it has some limitations too. Some of the limitations are as below:

Pros

  • There are fewer crowds.
  • It has an ideal temperature for trekking.
  • The sky is clear and the days are bright and sunny.
  • As November starts, the temperature slows down.
  • Experience both the Monsoon and Autumn season within the month of September.

Cons

  • The initial week of September offers you rain and slippery trails.
  • The environment is quite humid as Monsoon is about to leave.
  • Earlier booking of food and accommodation is necessary.
  • Trails are also full of crowds.
  • As the season comes to an end the temperature starts to drop.

Essential gear and equipment for Manaslu trek

Yes, it is the perfect season for trekking in the Manaslu region of Nepal. However, you need to carry some basic gear and equipment to complete this Manaslu trek without any hassle. Autumn is dry and mild weather which provides a tremendous temperature, perfect for trekking.

The temperature still varies as you move towards the higher altitudes. Even though it is the Autumn season still you might experience rain in early September. Some of the essential gear and equipment for Manaslu trek in September, October, November are as below:

Footwears

  • Trekking boots
  • Waterproof socks
  • Woolen socks
  • Gaiters
  • Hiking Sandals

Clothing

  • Trekking shirts
  • Insulated Jackets
  • Thermals
  • Waterproof jacket
  • Windproof jacket
  • Trekking shorts, pants, and trousers
  • Rain Gear

Head and Hand gears

  • Sun Hat
  • UV protection sunglasses
  • Head Scarf
  • Lightweight gloves (windproof and waterproof)

Toiletries and Personal hygiene

  • Toothpaste/Toothbrush
  • Quick-drying towel
  • Small mirror
  • Multipurpose soap
  • Deodorants
  • Body and face moisturizer
  • Nail clippers
  • Wet wipes
  • Toilet roll

Important items

  • Sleeping bag
  • Trekking poles
  • First-aid kit
  • Water Bottles
  • Backpack
  • Water purification tablet or liquid

Luxuries/Extras

  • Trail Map/Guide
  • Binoculars
  • Novels
  • Small notebooks and pencils

Permits for the Manaslu trek in Autumn

Manaslu region is not widely opened as other trekking trails in Nepal. It is done in order to protect the ethnic culture, tradition, and lifestyle of people around Manaslu region. Tsum Valley is another great option to travel around which is new, as it was only open to travelers from 2008.

Some of the permits that you may require to enter the restricted and normal trekking routes are as below:

  • Annapurna Conservation Area Project permit (ACAP)
  • Trekkers Information Management System (TIMS)
  • Special Restricted Area Permit for Manaslu (Manaslu RAP)
  • Manaslu Conservation Area Project Permit (MCAP)
  • TSUM Valley Restricted Area Permit (If you choose to visit Tsum Valley too)

Advantages of Manaslu trek in September, October, November

Autumn is the best season to travel due to several valid reasons. Due to the following factors, you can easily understand why Manaslu trek in Autumn is the best time to travel around this part of the country.

Mild Temperature

Autumn (September-November) brings the best atmosphere to hike around the Manaslu region. It also brings perfect temperature which allows you to trek easily and comfortably. Monsoon is on its way to leave, so temperature automatically balances itself.

There is less humidity in the air so the environment becomes drier. The temperature also starts decreasing as you move towards the higher altitudes. Early September can bring you rain but it disappears as September moves forward. October is the best month among all three in this Autumn season. You will get a slight hint of Winter as November starts.

Beautiful scenery

You will start to feel the beauty of Autumn only from Mid-September. The ending of Monsoon fades away the clouds and brings you the clear sky. It will give you the opportunity to view the majestic views of the great Himalayan range.

You will see the seasonal fruits and vegetables walking through the trekking trails. The paddies in the fields turn into golden and hills are covered with Orange trees. The late-November brings the season of harvesting crops.

Safer

The Autumn season around the Manaslu region is much safer than any other season. This trek is also ideal for beginners as the trails are easy and the season is perfect. The danger of landslides or avalanches is not frequent in Manaslu Circuit which makes it safer than other trekking routes.

There is little or no chance of rainfall so the routes are in proper conditions without being slippery. No rain means fewer leeches, mosquitoes, bugs, etc. in the trails.

Festive season

The Autumn season is also a festive season in Nepal. It brings several festivals in Nepal like Dashain and Tihar. These two festivals are major festivals of Nepal especially, the Hindu people. You will be a part of the tradition, culture, and beliefs of Hindu people.

Proper accommodations

This is the best season for trekking in Nepal, the business and gathering of tourists in the teahouse increases. Manaslu Trek is also a teahouse trek in Nepal so there are various tea houses throughout the trekking routes.

Pre-booking of the teahouses may be necessary because it is the peak of tourist season. You may not find the proper rooms and services according to your choice. But, in the Winter season, the tea houses go out of service due to extreme cold, you need to be extra careful if you are planning to travel in the Winter season.

Limitations of Manaslu trek in September, October, November

Crowd season

September, October, and November fall under the Autumn season and Autumn is one of the most popular trekking seasons in Nepal. Manaslu is no exception in this regard, there are heavy crowds throughout the trails and even in teahouses.

There is nothing like privacy because you see tourists everywhere in the trekking trails. You will feel rush in the environment and you may miss some beauty and tradition of the Manaslu Circuit.

Higher price

As demand for food and accommodation increases due to peak season, the owner of tea houses increases the price of everything. If it was off-season or regular season, you might get the same room and food at a much lower price. The price of tickets, gears, food, and accommodation, etc. goes up.

Accommodations

There are plenty of tea houses throughout the path of Manaslu Circuit Trek. Saying that you cannot ignore the fact that this is a peak of tourist season. Nepal is the perfect destination for every adventure lover throughout the world. Most of the tea houses are full so it would be hard to find the rooms of your choice. It is best if you pre-book the accommodation so there is no second thought in your mind.

title: Mardi Himal Trek Map
excerpt: Mardi Himal Trek has been recently famous among trekkers, which is a hidden gem of the Annapurna region. While trekking these routes carrying the Mardi Himal Trek Map will be quite helpful. Before…
html:
Mardi Himal Trek has been recently famous among trekkers, which is a hidden gem of the Annapurna region. While trekking these routes carrying the Mardi Himal Trek Map will be quite helpful.

Before starting your trek, you should always make a list of things that can help make your trip easier. Some of them are Compass, Maps, flashlight, Whistle, etc.

Mardi Himal Trek Map can help you decide the easiest and shortest way to finish this trek without missing anything. Due to modern technologies, you can download and carry maps on your devices. It makes navigating the routes simple.

But you can’t solely depend on gadgets as they can break down or run out of battery. So you can print out the Mardi Himal Trek Map and carry it along for the backup purposes.

Overview Of Mardi Himal Trek

Mardi Himal Trek is a new trekking route in the Annapurna region. It is situated on the east side of Annapurna Base Camp Trek. It lies in the Gandaki Zone near to the city of Pokhara.

These trails were opened for trekkers in 2012. It is a short trek that reaches the base of Mardi Himal.

As you walk these routes, you walk past many villages built with stones. And forests filled with colorful rhododendron, pine trees, birch, etc.

Along the way, you get to see many mountain peaks such as Machhapuchre, Annapurna, Hiunchuli, etc.

You will be walking through dense forests till the elevation of 3,300 m. Then after that, you walk through rugged trails in the mountains from where the view of the snowy peaks looks mesmerizing.

In a short time, these trekking routes have been able to make its name. But still, it is not as crowded as other treks of this region. It is a quiet walk enjoying the beauty of mother nature.

Trek Route Summary

Mardi Himal Trek is a 9 days package that takes you through exciting adventures in a short time period.

As you arrive at the International airport in Kathmandu, the respective person will pick you up from there. And drop you off at your hotel and help you check-in.

The rest of the day is free as no plans have been made for this day. You can roam the local markets or stay in your room.

The next day you drive from Kathmandu to Pokhara on a tourist bus. In this drive, you get to view small settlements, large open fields, etc along the way.

You might reach Pokhara early so you can visit Phewa lakes or other attractions sites for the rest of the day.

On your third day, the trekking journey begins towards Mardi Base Camp. You wake up early and take an hour’s drive to Kande. From there you trek towards Deurali passing the Australian Base Camp. You stay the night in Deurali.

You make an ascend in the trails towards forest camp and walk through dense forests filled with various species of flora and fauna. Walking the paths you reach Low camp and stay there for tonight.

Walking through the lush green forests you head towards High camp for this day. Along the way, you will see the mesmerizing view of beautiful mountain peaks. Watching the beautiful views you reach your today’s destination and rest for the night.

The sixth day is the important day of your trek as you will head towards the highlight of this trip i.e. Mardi Himal Base Camp. You will walk through rough trails to reach here.

After reaching Base Camp you stay there for some time and trek down towards Sidhing. This day you will have walked a lot so you will spend the night in one of the tea houses in Sidhing.

You will have a delicious breakfast here and drive towards Pokhara. After reaching today’s destination you will stay here for the night.

On your eighth day, you head back to Kathmandu. This is your final day in Nepal so you can roam the local markets and buy souvenirs for your family. You will stay the night in one of the hotels.

Today you will return back to your home country with beautiful memories of Nepal.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Highlights of Mardi Himal Trek

  • Trek in off beaten paths
  • The spectacular sight of Mountains
  • Walk dense forest trails
  • Budget-friendly Trek
  • Traditional villages
  • Close view of Annapurna Massif
  • Reach base camp of Mardi Himal

Mardi Himal Trek Map Details

Given below is the detailed information about duration, altitude, etc you will be covering in a day. Mardi Himal Trek Map provides you with information that is helpful while planning this trip.

You will be following these routes to reach Mardi Himal Base Camp:

Kathmandu – Pokhara

Drive Distance: 200 km

Drive Duration: 6 to 7 hours

Maximum Altitude: 827 m

After arriving at the Tribhuwan International airport our representative will pick you up and drop you off at your respective hotel. You have the rest of the day for you so you can visit nearby markets.

It would be better to rest your body as you have to wake up early the next day. You stay the night in Kathmandu.

On your second day, you head towards Pokhara viewing the beautiful scenic landscapes and hills. Throughout the way, you will be accompanied by small towns, mountain peaks, large fields, etc.

Pokhara is a beautiful city that attracts many tourists as this is the starting point for numerous famous treks. You can visit Phewa Tal and ride a boat or just walk along the lakeside enjoying the lively environment.

You will spend the night in one of the hotels.

Pokhara – Kande (drive)

Kande – Deurali (trek)

Drive Distance: 26.8 km

Trek Distance:

Drive Duration: one and a half hour

Trek Duration: 3 to 4 hours

Max Altitude (Kande): 1,770 m

Max Altitude (Deurali): 3,200 m

Today after having your breakfast, you will head towards Kande using transportation. On your way, you will pass small villages such as Hyanja, Phedi, etc.

You travel via the Baglung Highway and reach Kande. From there, you trek towards Deurali.

You will make an uphill climb until you reach the Australian Base Camp. It is situated at an altitude of 2,165 m. The view of Mount Machhapuchhre is awesome from here.

Then you head forward in the trails and reach Deurali. You get the wide-angle view of Annapurna Massif and Pokhara valley along these routes. There are a limited number of hotels here.

You will stay in one of the tea houses for the night.

Deurali – Low Camp

Trek Distance: 8.5 km

Trek Duration: 7 to 8 hours

Maximum Altitude: 3,150 m

This day you will walk from Deurali to Low Camp. These routes don’t offer many human settlements, so you should carry enough water for today.

You will start by ascending through forests filled with pine trees and colorful rhododendron until you reach Forest Camp. It is situated at an altitude of 2,550 m.

Reaching the camp you make a steep ascent and again enter a beautiful forest. If you are lucky you might even sight some wild animals such as Snow leopard, Himalayan Tahr, etc.

Walking through the lush green forest you arrive at Low Camp. The view of Mardi Himal and Machhapuchhre is quite striking from up here.

You will spend the night in one of the tea houses.

Low Camp – High Camp

Trek Distance: 5.5 km

Trek Duration: 4 to 5 hours

Max Altitude: 3,600 m

This day you will walk from Low Camp to High Camp. You begin the trek through forests filled with colorful rhododendrons till you reach Badal Danda.

You will be walking past Badal Danda, a scenic viewpoint above the clouds. From here, you can see a wide 360 degree view of the valleys down below and mesmerizing mountains to your North. There are a couple of hotels available here.

Leaving the Badal Danda behind you walk ahead in the trail and after some time reach the middle camp. From here you ascend the paths, you can notice the tree lines getting lighter.

You reach your destination after walking for some time. There are high chances of viewing Danphe (national bird of Nepal) while traveling to High Camp.

Along these trails, you get to view many majestic mountains. The sunset view from this place will be a memorable one.

You will stay the night here in one of the tea houses.

High Camp – Mardi Base Camp

Trek Distance: 6.5 km

Trek Duration: 4 to 5 hours

Max Altitude: 4,500 m

Today you will hike towards Mardi Base Camp the highlight of this trek. Having your breakfast you will take an uphill climb in the trails and reach Upper View Point. It is situated at an altitude of 4,200 m.

From here following the trails you reach Mardi Base Camp. You will be impressed by the striking view of Mardi Himal and the unique landscape below.

You also get to see various other peaks such as Annapurna I, Machhapuchhre, Dhaulagiri, Ganesh Himal, etc.

High Camp – Sidhing

Trek Distance:

Trek Duration: 3 to 4 hours

Max Altitude: 1,850 m

After enjoying the scenic views you get from the Mardi Base Camp. You now return back to High Camp retracing your footsteps.

Reaching High Camp you have your lunch and head towards Sidhing. You will descend through the trails crossing lush green forests along the way.

Sidhing is a beautiful village where you will be staying for the night.

Sidhing – Pokhara

Drive Distance: 40 km

Drive Duration: 3 to 4 hours

Max Altitude: 827 m

Today you will head back to Pokhara via private jeep. Along the ride, you will see waterfalls, mountain peaks, villages, etc.

Arriving Pokhara you are free to do anything. You can visit attraction sites such as David’s Fall, Bat Cave, Phewa Lake, etc. If you like cycling then it is also available there.

Back to Kathmandu

Drive Duration: 6 to 7 hours

Drive Distance: 201 km

Max Altitude: 1,400 m

Today you drive back to Kathmandu via tourist bus. You will travel viewing the green hills and villages throughout the highway.

This is the last of your trek so you can visit local markets near you. You should visit Thamel as it is famous for its nightlife. The area is filled with tourists visiting pubs, clubs, restaurants, etc.

You will leave for your country the next day with beautiful memories of this trek.

Base camp Adventure Hopes the Mardi Himal Trek Map will be helpful for you to plan your trek. We have jotted down the routes that are easy for trekking and can be done in a short time period. Please feel free to contact us if you seek more travel-related information.

Best time to Visit Mardi Himal

The weather in these trekking routes changes according to the season you would like to visit in. There are four seasons to choose from Spring, Autumn, Winter, and Monsoon.

Spring Season

This is the season that brings new beginning along with it. The months of March, April, and May come during this season. These months are the crowded time of the year.

During this season, the hills get its lost greenery back and the paths are filled with blooming flowers. The skies are clear giving unobstructed views of the mountain ranges.

The temperature ranges from 17 to 20 degrees Celcius on average. It is warm and sunny during the day but can get chilly during the night, but it is not freezing.

Autumn Season

This is the season when the beauty of mother nature is at its peak. The months of September, October, and November come during this season. These months are peak season for trekking.

During this season, flowers will have already bloomed making the forests colorful all around. Also, clear blue skies that give the striking view of lush green hills and mountain peaks

The temperature ranges from 5 to 15 degrees. The weather is just perfect for trekking during the day, but it can be cold during the night.

Monsoon Season

In countries like Nepal, the summer and monsoon season are combined so the first few weeks are hot and later you face heavy downpours. The months of June, July, and August come during this season.

These months are the least preferred time for trekking. During this season, the routes are slippery, muddy and filled with insects such as leeches, mosquitos, etc.

The skies are covered with dark rain clouds hiding the view of mountain peaks. The temperature ranges from 5 to 10 degrees. It is quite challenging to walk during heavy rainfalls. You should carry raincoats along with you.

Winter Season

This is the season when the whole valley is covered in blankets of snow. The months of December, January, and February come during this season. These months are the offseason for trekking.

During this season the skies are clear giving the most beautiful view of snow peak mountains. However, the cold weather will be a huge obstacle for you.

The temperature ranges from 9 to -5 degrees. It is warm during the day and very cold during the night and early mornings. It gets below freezing point in high elevation.

  • Mardi Himal Trek Difficulty
  • Annapurna Base Camp Trek Distance
  • Mardi Himal Trek Cost

Difficulties Faced in Mardi Himal Trek

This trek is graded as a moderate level climb. You won’t be needing any technical equipment such as ropes, ice picks, etc for this trek. If you have experience in trekking, then it will be easy for you.

But for inexperienced trekkers, it can be difficult walking up and down the steep hills for about 6 to 7 hours a day. You can overcome this obstacle by training your body and increasing your stamina.

Another problem can be altitude Sickness as you will be traveling, above 4,000 m in this trek. Usually, trekkers suffer altitude sickness above 3,000 m, so drink plenty of water and stroll.

If you see any symptoms of headache, nausea, dizziness, etc you should inform your guide. They will give instructions on what should be done. Read more about Mardi Himal Trek Difficulty.

Permit required for Mardi Himal Trek

While going on a trek in the routes of Mardi Himal you need two permits. The ACAP (Annapurna Conservation Area Project permit) and TIMS (Tourism Information Management System).

You need to carry the permit along with you in this entire trek. It should be shown in checkpoints that are placed along the trails. This permit is non-transferable and can only be used once.

title: Langtang valley trek 11 days
excerpt: I bet you have heard people say they have seen heaven on earth. Would you also like to experience such pleasure? Then you would be interested in our Langtang Valley trek 11 days package. The trek to…
html:
I bet you have heard people say they have seen heaven on earth. Would you also like to experience such pleasure? Then you would be interested in our Langtang Valley trek 11 days package. The trek to Langtang valley will have you feeling as if you are in some mystical place.

Before explaining more about this trek we would like you to have some insight about the valley.

Lantang is a region in the Bagmati province, situated in the north-central part of the Himalayas. It is located around 51 km far on the north side of Kathmandu valley.

The region is famous for its Langtang National park, the park composes as the border with Tibet. The National park was established in 1976 which was the first Himalayan National park in Nepal.

This national park contains lake Gosaikunda which is sacred for the Hindu religion. Another religious spot would be the Monastery of Kyanjin Gompa.

Langtang valley is a part of National park, the park was created to conserve the whole Langtang area. It is considered one of the ravishing valleys in Nepal being a beloved to the trekkers for its remarkable beauty.

This valley trek is quite popular among trekkers for being a short trek into the Langtang region. It is an easy and fun trek that walks you through the glorious view of Langtang’s peak.

The valley has different types of climatic zone from alpine to semitropical. It also has a unique establishment of flora and fauna. It is surrounded by high mountains and landscapes that won’t fail to mesmerize you.

Langtang valley trek 11 days will also take you through the rich traditional and cultural ride of people living in that region. The community mostly found living in this region is Tamang.

Tamang Heritage Trek is a package offered by Base Camp Adventure that allows you to soak your soul deep in Tamang culture, traditions and way of living.

Langtang valley offers trails filled with forests of pine and rhododendron, ancient Gombas and unique culture of the Himalayan people.

The Base Camp Adventure has brought you 11 days Langtang Valley Trek, which is a complete package. It is packed with stunning landscapes, warm hospitality, and breathtaking scenarios.

Highlights of this Trek

  • Sight mountains above the height of 7,000 m
  • Unique species of flora and fauna
  • Lush forests filled with various trees, colorful flowers, etc
  • Langtang glaciers
  • Know the lifestyle of Himalayan people
  • Get the cultural experience offered by different communities

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Best time to trek in the Langtang valley

You have four seasons to decide from – Spring, Autumn, Summer, and Winter to make your trip. The climatic condition changes according to these seasons.

Each season has its own benefits and disadvantages. Usually, trekkers consider Spring and Autumn season the best time to trek in the Langtang valley. But that does not mean other seasons can’t be considered for trekking.

The months from September to mid-December fall under the Autumn season. Trekkers considered this season perfect for trekking in the Langtang valley. The climatic condition is quite stable.

It is warm during the day time and gives you the pleasure of walking beneath the blue sky.

However, during the morning and night time, the weather might be a little bit cold. But there are slight chances of fog covering the beauty of the mountains.

The autumn season is the peak season making the routes very crowded. Walking these trails you will find yourself a trekking companion heading towards the same destination.

Spring is considered the next best season after Autumn. The month of March to May falls under this season.

The days are long and warm making these routes quite easy for the trek. During day time the temperatures rise from 10 degrees to 20 degrees.

It is a new beginning not only for the year but also for you. As you can venture through the trails filled with wildflowers, unique vegetation, lush forests, etc.

June, July, and August fall under the Monsoon season. The trials are slippery and filled with bugs, leeches, and earthworms so you have to be careful on these paths.

On the brighter side, the routes are less crowded making the explore quite remarkable. Also, the rainwashed surrounding gives you a sensation of enjoyment.

However, the weather is hot in the lower region but it starts to drop as you make your climb in higher elevation. There are also high chances of fog blinding the visions of the mountain range.

During the winter season, the trails can be seen covered with snow. This season starts from the month of December and lasts till February.

Compared to day time, night times are much colder. It tends to drop below to minus degree in the night.

The valley is covered with blankets of snow. The weather conditions might be hectic due to snowfalls and cold winds.

Related articles you may like:

  • 8 Days Treks in Nepal
  • 5 Days Treks in Nepal

Difficulties faced in Langtang Valley Trek

This is a moderate trek making it neither too easy nor too hard. You will be walking for many days resting in tea houses and climbing into higher altitudes. However, some difficulties faced in Langtang valley trek are altitude sickness, routes difficulties, etc.

Route difficulty

Langtang valley trek 11 days is a short trek that can be finished in 10 to 11 days. Even beginners can finish this trek with ease. However, some parts of this trek can be challenging for you. It is a steep up and downhill climb. You will also be walking through narrow paths and ridges. You will be walking about 6-7 hours covering 15-16 km in a day.

For a noob trekker, this walking distance can be a lot. So you should prepare your body in advance by going on short walks and exercises.

Weather

The weather has always been a vital part of the trek. You can’t be sure as it keeps changing unexpectedly. Weather determines how memorable your trek will be.

One of the reasons why people prefer autumn and spring is due to the favorable weather and clear skies. The mountains are clearly visible during those times.

You can trek during winter and monsoon season too but the heavy rain and snow are unpredictable. You should read the weather forecast beforehand.

Altitude Sickness

Altitude sickness has always been a major problem for trekkers. While climbing higher altitudes the oxygen decreases causing Altitude sickness. When the oxygen is low you are short in-breath resulting symptoms such as vomiting, nausea, headache, fever, etc.

To reduce this problem acclimatization day is held where you rest in one of the stops. You let your body adapt so that it doesn’t cause problems for you while traveling higher in the elevation.

Physical Fitness

The trek might be moderate but you need to train your body before going on treks. Training doesn’t require anything technical. You should be both Physically and Mentally fit.

If you are Physically fit you get to enjoy and experience it better.

Langtang Valley Trek 11 Days Detail Itinerary


Below is the detailed itinerary of the 11 days Langtang valley trek.

Day 1: Arrival to Kathmandu

When you arrive at the international airport our representative will be there to pick you up. After the warm greeting, you will be dropped off at your hotel. Your flight must have been quite exhausting so you will rest for the day.

Day 2: Sightseeing around Kathmandu Valley

You will wake up early and get ready to explore the capital city today. Kathmandu is known as the city of temples.

You will visit some famous sites presented in the city i.e. Pashupatinath, Boudha Stupa, Swayambhu, etc. Some of them are UNESCO World Heritage Sites as well.

The Newari community will amaze you with their culture and heritage. You will also visit the Patan and Basantapur Durbar Squares which is mostly home for Newari people.

After an incredible tour, you will return to your hotel. You should rest for the day but if you don’t feel dull then you can roam around your hotel area.

Day 3: Kathmandu to SyabruBesi

Today you will start your journey towards the Langtang Valley. You will leave early this morning as it is a 7 – 8 hours drive from Kathmandu to SyabruBesi.

The distance between Kathmandu and Syabru Besi is about 80 km. Along the way, you will drive through the banks of the Trishuli river. The Scenic view of hills, mountains, rivers, etc will keep you busy throughout the way.

Some snow-capped mountains seen on these routes are Ganesh Himal, Mt. Annapurna II, etc.

Then we pass through many settlements that can be viewed on the way i.e. Trishuli Bazar, Betrawati, and Dunche. The roads are quite rough making the paths exciting.

From Dunche as you drive down the paths you reach Syabru Besi. Syabru Besi is a beautiful town at an altitude of 1,450 m

Tonight you will stay here.

Day 4: SyabruBesi to Lama Hotel

Today you will take a walk from SyabruBesi to Lama Hotel which takes about 5 – 6 hours. The distance between Syabru Besi and Lama Hotel is 11.3 km.

After your night there, you will begin your trek by crossing over the Bhote Koshi River through a suspension bridge. As you walk a bit further you will visit the Guru Rinpoche Gomba.

From the Gomba you will walk a stone-paved path and again cross a suspension bridge and climb up to trails that go through the lush green forest filled with colorful rhododendron and trees of oak, pines, maple, etc.

You can also view different animals inside the forests such as Wild boars, Red pandas, Langur monkeys, etc. Mostly the habitation of Langur monkeys is spread throughout these trails.

Then as you ascend furthermore from there you reach Lama Hotel. This Hotel is situated at an altitude of 2,470 m.

From the hotel, you get to view the snowy peaks of the mountains such as Naya Kang and Langtang II.

You will stay the night here.

Day 5: Lama Hotel to Langtang village

On your fifth day, you will head towards the Langtang village which is about 4-5 hours walk. The distance between the Lama Hotel and Langtang village is 14.8 km.

First, you will start by making a gentle climb than the climb starts to become steep as you walk the paths in the forest filled with oaks, maple, rhododendron, etc. In between the woods, you get a short glimpse of Mt. Langtang Lirung.

You then walk through many bridges made of logs before you arrive at Ghora Tabela. Ghora Tabela is a lush meadow situated at an altitude of 2,992 m.

This day you walk through many barren lands, helipads, lush green forests. You will then cross many streams, water mills, prayer mills, etc before you arrive at the beautiful Langtang valley.

Langtang valley is situated at an altitude of 3,430 m which is a large settlement. The people mostly living there are Tamang. The village is surrounded by walls of stones to protect their crops from the harsh wind.

You explore the village as you will be staying the night here.

Day 6: Trek from Langtang village to Kyanjin Gompa

On your sixth day, you will hike till Kyanjin Gompa which is about a 2 – 3 hours walk. You will be covering a distance of 6.8 km from Langtang village to Kyanjin Gompa.

The trails ascend leading towards a huge stupa from here you walk past Mani walls to reach mundu. Mundu is situated at an altitude of 3,543 m.

You will then walk through a narrow path above the Langtang River. As you cross small streams along the way you reach Kyanjin Gompa.

Kyanjin Gompa is situated at an altitude of 3,817 m. From here you get to view the mesmerizing mountains such as Mt. Ganchhenpo, Mt. Langtang Lirung, etc.

If you like cheese then you can visit the famous cheese factory or you can explore the lifestyle of people living there.

Day 7: Explore Kyanjin Gompa and a short hike up to Tsergo Ri

Today you will explore the valley and hike to the highest point of this trek Tsergo Ri.

The hike takes about 9-10 hours to go and come back from Kyajin Gompa. The distance between Kyanjin Gomba and Tsergo Ri is 17.7 km.

Tsergo Ri is at an elevation of 5,150 m. The stunning view of the Langtang valley and peaks of various mountains such as Langtang Lirung, etc is breathtaking from up there.

The striking views of the Langtang glaciers with unique glacial mass formation are also within walking distance from Kyanjin Gompa.

You can also walk up to Langshisha Kharka where yak pasture during the day time.

After a wonderful tour around the valley, you will return back to Kyanjin Gompa. The lively cultural display of the Tamang community will enchant you.

You will rest the night here.

Day 8: Trek Back to Lama Hotel

After a memorable day in Kyanjin Gompa now you will retrace your steps back to Lama Hotel. The distance between Kyanjin Gompa to Lama Hotel is about 21.6 km.

The walk is about 6-7 hours from Kyanjin Gompa. You will descend observing the snowy peaks and walking through lush forests alongside Langtang River.

Walking past Langtang village and Ghoda Tabela you arrive at Lama Hotel. You will have descended more than 1,430 m this day. Obviously, the climb down will be much faster than ascending.

You will be staying your night in the Hotel.

Day 9: Lama Hotel to Syabru Besi

Today is your last day in the Langtang region. You will be walking for about 4-5 hours covering the distance of 11.3 km.

You will take the same routes back going through forests of rhododendron, oaks, pines, etc. The stunning view of the Mountains, landscape, villages will seem more attractive as it will be your last night here.

You will climb downhill crossing suspension bridges and reach Syabru Besi.

After a few hours’ walks, you will rest here for the night.

Day 10: Back to Kathmandu

From Syabru Besi you will head back to Kathmandu. Passing through small villages, viewing the mountains for the last time before you reach the capital.

After you have arrived in Kathmandu you will be dropped off at your hotel. You can freshen up and roam the streets of Thamel. Nightlife in these streets is not to be missed.

You will spend your last night on this trip here.

Day 11: Drop off at the Airport

After having your breakfast, you will be dropped off at the International airport. Please check to see if you have forgotten any of your belongings. You will leave taking beautiful memories of this trek.
