title: Everest Base Camp Trek Map
excerpt: Everest Base Camp Trek is one of the major attractions of Nepal. Visiting the highest peak of the world at an altitude of 8848 meters so up close is on everyone’s bucket list. But only a few…
html:
Everest Base Camp Trek is one of the major attractions of Nepal. Visiting the highest peak of the world at an altitude of 8,848 m so up close is on everyone’s bucket list. But only a few adventurous brave people can commit to embark on the adventure.

Embarking on any journey requires detailed information about the place. For any journey, the main requirement is always a map. Getting lost in a strange place is a nightmare. To avoid such a nightmare from becoming reality, you should always carry a map with you.

With the Everest Base Camp Trek map, the chances of you getting lost are reduced. The age of technology does make it seem like maps are pretty useless. But with the trekking being in a remote area, a physical Everest Base Camp Trek map would seem like the most useful and important item.

With a challenging adventure as the Everest Base Camp Trek, you can never be too careful. You will always need an Everest Base Camp Trek map with you in case of any uncertainties. Also, wherever you go, it’s a smart move to do a little research about where you will be reaching or what you will be doing there.

With the map of Everest Base Camp Trek, you will not only be able to find the routes easily, but you will also know where you are at the moment and what the main attraction of the place is. For example, with a map, you will know that a certain monastery or religious landmark is nearing and prepare yourself accordingly.

Trek Route Summary

Standard Everest Base Camp Route

The 15 days Everest Base Camp Trek is the most popular route taken by trekkers. The trek starts with a flight from Kathmandu to Lukla. From Lukla, you will trek most of the day with around 5-6 hours of trekking every day. Passing through Namche bazaar on Day 4th for acclimatization, you will travel through religious monuments like Tengboche. Another acclimatization point at Dingboche is used during the trip.

You will reach the base camp on the ninth day of the trek. Taking the same way back, retracing your steps, you will return to Kathmandu on a flight from Lukla. This will mark the end of your Everest Base camp trek. This route is marked In blue in the map provided above.

Helicopter return (optional)

Another route for Everest Base Camp Trek is returning by helicopter. This allows you to have a clear view of the mountains from a higher altitude. The Everest Base Camp Trek with helicopter return includes all the same routes and stops as the base camp trek of 15 days. You will catch a flight from Kathmandu to Lukla and travel through Namche bazaar to the Everest Base Camp. The only difference is that you will be returning from Kala Patthar to Kathmandu by helicopter. Here you will enjoy the superb view of the mountains, the valleys, and the trails.

Three pass trek (optional)

The path in grey in the Everest Base Camp Trek map is the one that takes us through the three passes to reach our final destination i.e, the Everest Base Camp. This route takes us for a challenging adventure through the Valley of death. The three pass route takes us to the Gokyo village and Gokyo Ri to witness the glorious mountains standing tall in their full beauty.

This route takes you to a mystical journey through the three passes: Kongma-la Pass, Cho La Pass, and Renjo La Pass. This place provides the best view of the Everest Base Camp. The three pass trek provides the trekkers with a solidarity trek on the way back. This trek route takes a total of 18 days, unlike the classical trekking route.

Related Articles

  • 15 Days Everest Base Camp Trek
  • Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return
  • Everest Three Pass Trek

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Details as per the Everest Base Camp Trek Map

As per the Everest Base Camp Trek Map, the route for the classic Everest Base Camp trek follows the following routes making the stops below:

Kathmandu to Phakding

Lukla – Phakding Distance: 6.2 km | Max altitude: 2,610 m | Estimated Trek hours: 4 – 5 hrs

The main route shown as per the Everest Base Camp Trek Map is the classical Everest Base Camp Trek route. The trek starts from a flight from Kathmandu to Lukla and ends the day at Phakding.

Phakding to Namche: Rest one day for acclimatizing

Distance: 7.4 km | Max altitude: 3,440 m | Estimated Trek hours: 6-7 hours

From Phakding, this route leads us to Namche Bazaar through Manjoo. This stop is an acclimatization point where you will rest for the day to help better adapt to the altitude.

Namche to Tengboche

Distance: 5.9 km | Max altitude: 3,867 m | Estimated Trek hours: 5-6 hours

The next stop on this route is Tengboche. This is a Buddhist monastery worshipped by the sherpas. The map clearly shows how to reach the monastery from Namche Bazaar.

Tengboche to Dingboche – rest one day for acclimatizing

Distance: 9.1 km| Max altitude: 4,260 m | Estimated Trek hours: 5-6 hours

From the monastery in Tengboche, the route leads you to Dingboche. This is a small village on the way. You will rest at this spot for the day acclimatizing and head to the next stop the next day.

Dingboche to Lobuche

Distance: 6.6 km | Max altitude: 4,930 m | Estimated Trek hours: 5-6 hours

Lobuche is the next stop from Dingboche. There are two routes to reaching Lobuche. On the map, we can clearly see the routes we can take.

Lobuche to Everest Base Camp – Gorakshep

Distance: 12.1 km to Everest Base camp 1.7 km to Gorakshep:| Max altitude: 5,364 m| Estimated Trek hours:3-4 hours

From Lobuche, we can reach Everest Base Camp. At an altitude of 5,364 m, we will reach Everest Base Camp and enjoy the view of the breathtaking mountains. After the achievement of a lifetime, you will descend to Gorakshep.

Gorak Shep to Kala Patthar to Periche

Distance: 1.2 km to Kalapatthar 10 km to Pheriche | Max altitude: 5,545 m | Estimated Trek hours: 6-7 hours

The way back is now all descents. Only today, you will hike up to Kalapatthar in the morning. The view of the mountains in the early sunrise is to die for. This is one of the main attractions of the entire trek. Then you can descend to Pheriche.

Pheriche to Namche Bazaar

Distance: 14.2 km| Max altitude: 4,243 m | Estimated Trek hours: 7-8 hours

The return route is the same as the one you took to get up to the base camp. You will follow the same route you took from Pheriche to Namche Bazaar.

Namche Bazaar to Lukla

Distance: 13.5 km | Max altitude: 3,440 m | Estimated Trek hours:6-8 hours

From Namche, you will return to Lukla through Manjoo and Phakding through the same trails as before. The only difference is that the way will no long be uphill.

Flight from Lukla to Kathmandu

Distance: 138 km | Max altitude: 2,886 m| Estimated hours: 40 minutes

Your journey finally ends with the almost-cinematic view of the mountains and the valley. All this from your comfortable flight from Lukla to Kathmandu.

This trek takes only 15 days to take the daring journey and come back.

Alternative Route Map from Base Camp

Everest Three Pass Trek

You can also take an alternative route for the Everest Base Camp Trek looking at the map. Everest Three Pass Trek is a spunky trek that takes you through a remote trek trip through three great passes of the Everest Base Camp with the prodigious view of the mountains.

This route is similar to the classic Everest Base Camp Trek. The way up is the same. However, the way back has a lot in store for you. After reaching Diboche from Namche Bazaar, you will reach the first pass of the three- Kongma-la pass. This provides spectacular views of the Khumbu glaciers.

You will reach Everest Base Camp from the pass soon. On the way back you will trek to Gokyo lakes via Cho La Pass. Here, you will see awestruck views of the religious Dudh Koshi river and the valleys around it. the pass lets you see the majestic view of the highest peaks like Cho-Oyu, Chola, Lhotse, etc.

Unlike the classic Everest Base Camp Trek route, this route is remote and of a higher difficulty level so be careful on the descent. On the way back from Gokyo to Namche, you will pass through the last pass i.e, Renjo La Pass at an altitude of 5,360 m

The rest of the trek is the same as before. You will follow the trail back from Namche to Lukla and fly to Kathmandu. This trek takes you 18 days to reach the base camp and return back to your flight.

Return by Helicopter

Apart from the strenuous treks to and back from the base camp, there is an alternative route for your convenience. If you aren’t really good with descents or don’t want to walk back the same route, the same way you came up, you can always opt to choose the return by helicopter choice. There are many reasons to choose Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour.

This route takes you through the classic Everest Base Camp trek route letting you experience all the trekking adventure while giving you the opportunity to end the trek with a unique Helicopter return to Kathmandu. This reduces your travel time and provides you a great opportunity to enjoy the view of the mountains from a helicopter without straining yourself more.

This route allows you to reach the base camp and enjoy the majestic view from Kalapattar. The helicopter return route picks you up from Kalapatthar and takes you to Kathmandu straight through the mind blowing view of the mountains, valleys, and the glaciers and rivers.

The difficulty of the routes

15 days classic Everest Base Camp Trek

The venturesome trek to the Everest Base Camp is one of the most popular and daring treks in Nepal. The trekkers do face some difficulties to overcome this daring journey.

The uncertainty of the Lukla flight is one of the major difficulties faced by trekkers here. The Lukla flight is one of the main attractions of the flight with the tempting view of the valley and the mountains. But his flight is heavily affected by the weather. Unexpected changes in weather have known to cause many cancellations so make sure to check the weather carefully.

Being at an altitude of 5,364 m, you will have to hike up a lot. Altitude sickness is probable in the high mountains. So take your time to acclimatize in the stops as per the maps guidance and enjoy the trek without any problems.

Three Pass Trek Difficulty

Among the three routes mentioned above and shown in the map, the Three Passes Trek Route is the most challenging one. There are many things to consider before embarking on this journey. This route is often chosen by people to avoid human traffic on the way. The difficulty of this trek is higher than the classic route due to the sudden uphill on the way to EBC.

You can take this route to go to the base camp which will help you in reaching the base camp fast instead of taking this route on the way back. The alternative route is filled with glorious views but the trail is kind of steep and the altitude suddenly increases.

The difficulty almost everyone faces in this route to go to Everest Base Camp is the difficulty to acclimatize in the Gokyo valley. The route seems to take only a few hours of walking so the trekkers usually rush in without proper acclimatization leading to altitude sickness.

Als, you should be careful to choose the best season to travel through this road.

Seasons are important for both ascending and descending the route. If you travel during the rainy season, there are many chances of landslides or you sliding down the slippery roads. So keep in mind to check the season and the climate before booking your trip.

Helicopter Return

The trek to Everest Base camp with helicopter return is a deal stealer as the package provides you with so many different routes and a spectacular view of the mountains and the valleys. The only difficulty that can arise on this magnificent trip is the unpredictable weather changes.

Helicopter rides are fun and exquisite, especially in the mountain range. But they aren’t advisable in bad weather conditions. The safety is in question in bad weather. So before you decide to plan a helicopter ride home from Everest Base Camp, please keep in mind that weather affects your ride a lot.

Best Time to go to Everest Base Camp Trek

Everest Base Camp Trek is a challenging trek that takes you through uphills and rocky roads. The best time to go to Everest Base Camp in the spring season during the months of February to May. The routes to reach the base camp are dry during these months.

The winter season through December to February can also be a good time but the temperature is obviously low.

The rainy season, however, is not a good time. You should avoid embarking on the Everest Base Camp Trek during the rainy season. Especially during the Gokyo route, the roads are very steep and unsafe in the rainy seasons. So best keep yourself out of the route during the rainy season to avoid any mishaps.

Before setting on an adventurous trek to Everest Base Camp, you should research the best time to go trekking to get the most out of your journey.

Why Do You Need Everest Base Camp Trek Map?

Stay on track

Traveling through the steep snowy roads of Everest Base Camp trek, it’s easy to lose your way. Awestruck with the beauty of the place, you can get distracted from the route sometimes. These are the time maps come in handy. In the remote villages, charging your phones may be difficult. Also, wifi at such an altitude is rare. At such a time, carrying a map will be very handy.

Discover New Routes

With the Everest Base Camp Trek map, you can find out new routes to reach your destination. Discussing with your guide or your group, you can decide to take new routes to your destination. The map contains all the possible routes you can take to reach your destination and different attractions and stops on that particular stop. With the map, your Everest Base Camp Trek can be a surprising adventure with different attractions with you in control.

A Basic Necessity For A Solo Trek

Many adventurous trekkers embark on a solo trek for Everest Base Camp Trek. These trekkers are passionate about reaching the destination with their own efforts. If you are one of these passionate adventurous daredevils, you should get yourself an Everest Base Camp Trek map and initiate the adventure.

Other essentials for the Trek

Apart from the map of the Everest Base Camp Trek to guide you through the different routes of the Trek, there are other essentials for the trek like:

  • Trekking boots and hiking poles
  • Warm clothes like down jacket and fleece trousers
  • Personal medical kit
  • Portable chargers
  • Toiletries and water bottles

title: Everest Gokyo Trek Map
excerpt: Nepal is a prime destination for every trekker who awaits to go too far for adventure. It has the world’s most revered trekking regions that are simply breathtaking but comes with an extremity. One…
html:
Nepal is a prime destination for every trekker who awaits to go too far for adventure. It has the world’s most revered trekking regions that are simply breathtaking but comes with an extremity.

One of them being Everest Gokyo Trek, a sequestered and least-traveled region in Himalaya. Given the extremity of the route, tourists abstain from visiting the lake despite its majestic beauty.

Throughout the year, the route to Everest Gokyo dismays to witness the hoard. The major reason for Gokyo’s least to fame is it’s unexplored routes and weather conditions.

It is, therefore, most trekkers opt for a private flight to Gokyo via helicopter. A regular flight from Kathmandu to Lukla through Heli is how most people begin their excursion to Gokyo Lake. The journey, of course, will offer you a lot besides the unique highlands and peaks.

But for those who covet to explore Gokyo getting yourself a map is the second-best option. The map simply plays a decisive role from here. A well-marked route with the geographical location and landforms of the region helps you withstand the pitfall alone.

The way to Gokyo Lake boasts endless rocky trails, fastening old villages in Himalaya. A map in hand will thus help you overreach these routes and make sure that you don’t miss the track.

Everest Gokyo Trek Map:

The map to Everest Gokyo Trek outlines the topography of the region. This includes the study of the land surface, terrains and even the prehistory and culture of the region.

You can also expect to know the uniqueness of Gokyo in general at the presence of a map. Through the Everest Gokyo Trek Map, you can foretell the number of days to be spent in the trek.

You’ll thus be able to plan the rest of your schedules and travel itinerary in accordance. By assessing the distance clinched through the map, you’ll have a less stressful experience.

The route to Everest Gokyo Trek will take you to a 13-day trial walk from Lukla including your arrival. In about two weeks of trekking, you’re expected to discover the Himalayan landforms and their lifestyle.

The culture, of course, will see a major influence of the Sherpa clan. Old monasteries and gompas are evident with monks performing the everyday rituals.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Where is Everest Gokyo located in Nepal?

Everest Gokyo is Nepal’s best viewed and least explored regions so far. The lake lies at an elevation of 4,750 m with the mesmeric EBC just being 550 m afar.

Meanwhile, Gokyo Ri is located on the west side of the Ngozumpa Glacier, lying beneath is the mesmerizing Gokyo lake. This tremendously monstrous peak is regarded as the highest one in the Khumbu region of the Himalayas.

Typical stone houses built with mud and clay are the accentuate of this region. Other wonders including Mt.Everest, Makalu, and Cho Oyu are what to be seen from the foot of the peak.

What is the best time for Everest Gokyo trek?

The trails of Everest Gokyo is a multi-day trekking route that takes around two weeks to complete. The extremity of the trails, of course, being the hindrance might cost you even more.

Still, hiking here can be done anywhere around the year given its altitude of 5,357 m. However, if you yearn to get the most out of the trip, it’s best you trek the region in the spring.

Spring season is considered the best time of the year for trekking because of its eccentric scenic view. The sky is clear at this time around and gives you a closer and unclogged view of mountains.

Autumn is another relevant time around when Gokyo Ri draws trekkers in like never before. First-timers would surely find the place freakishly mesmeric with unreal views of Mountains and landscapes.

Weather is marvelous at this season as the end of monsoon gives you a clear picture of the valley. It even has to offer you a mesmeric view of natural wilderness with lush green forests.

Similar articles you may like:

  • Gokyo Valley Trek
  • Everest Three Pass Trek Difficulty
  • Everest Base Camp Trek Distance

Route on Everest Gokyo Trekking Map

Walking the unexposed and unheard routes of Everest Gokyo Trek can be an appalling experience. The journey becomes even unendurable in the absence of a crowd to convoy with.

It is when the Everest Gokyo Trek Map comes as a great help and rescue you from a ruffle experience. The Map indeed has an ample of well-recognized trekking routes all starting from Lukla.

The trailheads obviously split as soon as the route follows a different path instead of a single one. Needless to be fret of as the series of different routes still ends at the enticing Gokyo Ri.

The most popular trekking route followed by the trekkers at the Everest Gokyo Trek Map is stated below.

Kathmandu-Lukla-Phakding-Manjoo-Namche Bazar-Khumjung Village-Dhole-Machhermo-Gokyo Lake- Gokyo Ri

The route on the Everest Gokyo Trek Map is the shortest and quickest way to reach Gokyo Ri. The other three routes to Gokyo incorporate long trails with challenges that will extend your days in the region.

Flight from Kathmandu to Lukla

Flight Duration: 40 minutes

Flight Distance: 138 km

Maximum Altitude: 2,886 m

On your arrival at Kathmandu, the respective official will see you at the Tribhuvan International Airport. From there, you’ll be driven towards your hotel so that you get some rest.

After slowing up from the exhausting flight, you can go sight-seeing in the valley. Rambling around the city washed with gleaming lights and people gets you to ease.

To help get forthcoming, you can find a restaurant near and around and have local food. Meantime, you can even commune with your guide as well as fellow hikers to travel with.

For a night, you go back to your hotel, get a nap and prepare for the trip the next day. On the first day of the trip, You’ll take a flight to Lukla Airport which will take almost 35 mins.

Lukla to Phakding

Trek Duration: 4 hours

Trek Distance: 9 km

Maximum Altitude: 2610 meter

After an exhilarating flight with scenic views drifted throughout, you’ll be arriving at Lukla Airport. From there, you’ll get a head start to your trek by walking towards Phakding Village.

Reaching the village will evince you to the Sherpa community and their way of living. The day will see you crossing the suspended deck above the Dudh Koshi River.

While following the trails, you’ll behold the natural wilderness and landscape of Himalayas. Even the enrapturing Rhododendron forest is visible on your way to Phakding Village. Your trek for the day ends at Phakding where you’ll stay at one of the local hostelries.

Phakding – Namche Bazar

Trek Duration: 6 hours

Trek Distance: 12 km

Maximum Altitude: 3,440 m

You’ll early morning at Phakding will kick start having breakfast at the guesthouse. You then start walking to Namche Bazaar, best regarded as Sherpa Capital in Khumbu Region.

The closer you walk to the town, the more you take a peek at Mt.Everest and many other peaks. As you ascend the Namche Bazaar, there’s a possibility of you having altitude sickness.

Therefore, it’s best you wander around the town and get used to the temperature and climate. To make the best of the day, you can go on a short hike to Khumjung and Khunde.

In case you get lost or lose the track, get the help of the Everest Gokyo Trek Map. For the night in Namche, you can find a lodge or tea house.

Namche Bazaar to Dhole

Trek Duration: 5 hours

Trek Distance: 6.9 km

Maximum Altitude: 4,040 m

The following day, you’ll start trekking from the early morning. Along the trails to Dhole, you get a glimpse of exotic landscapes, nearby mountains, and peaks.

The influence of Sherpa culture and their lifestyle is sure to be witnessed at the village of Dhole. After trekking for almost 5 hours, you’ll stop by at a guest house in Dhole and take a rest.

Dhole to Maccharmo

Trek Duration: 6 hours

Trek Distance: 4023 km

Maximum Altitude: 4,150 m

From Dhole, you’ll lead the way towards Maccharmo with the help of Everest Gokyo Trek Map. The trek has you walking uphill the terminal moraine of Ngozumpa glacier. Amongst the region, it is the longest glacier to have come to know so far.

The glistening Ngozumpa is also the main tourist attraction in this region and the surrounding. While walking to Maccharmo, you can heed the disparity in the landforms and vegetation from Dhole.

You can also take notice of a mind-blowing view of the valleys and the snowy peaks from Maccharmo. Another day from your trek to Gokyo ends at Maccharmo where you’ll spend the night at a tea house.

Maccharmo to Gokyo

Trek Duration: 4 hours

Trek Distance: 6.8 km

Maximum Altitude: 4,750 m

The wait is soon to over as you now would be trekking towards Gokyo Valley. Your day from Maccharmo begins by trekking through the Ngozumpa glacier over a twisted path.

Amidst the eye-catching landscapes, monasteries, and peaks like Cho Oyo, your journey becomes no less than a joy.

From here, you’ll also find yourself surrounded by mountains like Mt. Everest, Kongde, and Pumori. After almost four hours of walking on a tricky route, you’ll finally arrive at beautiful Gokyo Village.

The village itself is fascinating to watch for many trekkers as it lies on the shore of Dudh Pokhari. To comfort you, there are true works of art in the form of monasteries on the way to the lake.

Once you reach the first Gokyo lake, all your exhaustion and torment from days long trek will disappear at once. After such mighty treks, you better stay the night at a tea house in Gokyo.

The next early morning, you’ll hike to Gokyo Ri to shrink the chances of getting altitude sickness. After a challenging trek of 4 hours, you’ll reach Gokyo Ri and get the spectacular view of Gokyo Lakes.

To enjoy the scenic view, you can spend some time at Gokyo Ro before descending back to the village.

Trek back from Gokyo to Dhole

Trek Duration:6-7 hours

Trek Distance: 9 km

Maximum Altitude: 4,130 m

It’s time to bid farewell to the quaint valley of Gokyo and head back to Dhole. To the end of your Gokyo trek, you pass through all Gokyo Lakes and leave behind Maccharmo.

Trekking across the Ngozumpa glacier and to Dhole will take you about 6 to 7 hours. Feel the tranquility and enjoy the beauty of the Himalayas from here.

Dhole to Namche Bazaar

Trek Duration: 5 hours

Trek Distance: 6.9 km

Maximum Altitude: 3,440 m

From Dhole, you’ll be returning on your way to the prepossessing Namche Bazaar. The walk to the whacking trail to Namche will take you 5 hours.

For your much tedious walk of 5 hours, scenic views of mountains, people’s lifestyle come as a great relief. A sweet and delightful night at Namche brings another day to an end.

Namche Bazaar to Lukla

Trek Distance: 7-8 hours

Trek Duration: 15 km

Maximum Altitude: 2,886 m

This is formally the last day of your trek to Gokyo. Follow the Everest Gokyo trek map and you’ll arrive at your last stop to Lukla. It brings a mixed feeling to every trekker as there will be no more sightseeing of mountains and geographical diversity.

On the way, you’ll find yourself getting through the bewitching dense rhododendron forest. Then other remarks to be added to your trek being the Sherpa village. Here you can spot traditional monasteries and gompas, prayer wheels and Mani stone.

While in Lukla, you can view the surrounding mountains, rocky cliffs and visit local shops one last time.

Flight from Lukla to Kathmandu

Flight Distance: 40 mins

Flight Duration: 138 km

Maximum Altitude: 1,400 m

No more walking the long trails and gorges as the excursion becomes easy from here. From Lukla Airport, You’ll take a direct flight to Kathmandu in the early morning.

This will take you about 40 mins to reach the valley. Since you still have a whole day, sightseeing of local temples and durbar squares comes as a great alternative.

You can also escape the city hustle by visiting local food houses and eatery. Getting a memento from nearby shopping malls is another great way to spend a day.

Departure to Airport

Now, it’s time to say goodbye to Nepal and return home with amazing memories collected. You’ll be driven to the Tribhuvan International Airport three hours before the flight. Throughout the time, you’ll get a helping hand and assisted till aboard the flight.

title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek in November
excerpt: Long-distance trek trails often cause hassle and fright among travelers. Even the idea of trekking thousands of miles fears them, let alone the challenges be. But, contrary to all of it, Nepal’s…
html:
Long-distance trek trails often cause hassle and fright among travelers. Even the idea of trekking thousands of miles fears them, let alone the challenges be.

But, contrary to all of it, Nepal’s Annapurna Base Camp has commanded every trekker’s attention. Despite its elevation of 4,130 m, it has emerged as one of the favorite trekking spots in the region.

It’s perhaps the second most popular trekking region after Everest Base Camp Trek. Compared to other trekking regions, the base camp is by far the most explored and crowded. The historic routes of Annapurna base Camp have captured the eye of every hiker.

The well-marked route to Annapurna has trekkers hiking throughout the year. And it can even be taken on with a mere help of a trekking map.

The trails to Annapurna base camp walk through the dense forest covered with bushy rhododendron trees. High altitude mountains with mesmeric landscapes will escort you till reaching the circuit.

Other than the sublime beauty of mountains and scenery, there’s so much to discover in the region. The diversity in lifestyle and culture of people and even the rituals perform are what best about the place.

To stand out, it’s the nobility and hospitality of locals here that has trekkers feel homey. The area is abode to many small and high peaks and incredible gorges and passes.

The Annapurna Base Camp trek is typically a 13-day trek. But in case you opt for a flight, the trekking time might cut down. Even your itinerary and length of the trekking days can result in your schedule.

The travel season, of course, is another hindrance. They’re the ones that’ll determine the length of your stay in the region. Annapurna Base Camp trek in November is perhaps the time when you’ll complete the trekking as scheduled.

Since the routes of Annapurna Base Camp are more clear in November, the solo trek is possible. You’ll hardly struggle, finding the track to the base camp. But in any case, you lost your way, the trek map is there at your service.

Trekking the base camp is possible in all seasons and throughout the year. But most of you won’t desire to visit the region in the monsoon.

Where is Annapurna Base Camp located at?

Annapurna Base Camp is a glacial basin located 40km north of Pokhara in Central Nepal. It is enclosed by a series of high mountains, most of which are above 7,000 m altitude.

The route to the base camp that connects so many landscapes is in itself an incredible adventure. The unstoppable trails, scenic mountain view, and gorges make the land a classic beauty.

Step in the valley and you’ll find yourself surrounded by spectacular peaks disperse around. This being the majestic Machapuchre, Annapurna I and Annapurna South.

Annapurna Base camp boasts more than 2 routes, enabling the trekkers to choose their own. Still, every single path to ABC runs at Chomrong and goes along with it till reaching the base camp.

You can ascend to the base camp walking the route without any stop. But if not pushed for time, you can take a detour to Ghorepani Poon Hill and even beautiful Ghandruk Village.

It is a prime trekking route for hikers and access to the Annapurna range. Ghandruk offers an equally stunning view to the hikers who stop by the village.

The major impact of the Gurung community and their culture can be found throughout the region. Of course, it’ll cost you an additional 3 days at least if you do not follow the path.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Which is the best time of the year to visit Annapurna Base Camp?

Annapurna’s unrelenting beauty with a diverse topography is something onlookers can’t pass over. Despite the challenges and adversity, hikers never stop trekking on the route.

In fact, the trail to the base camp remains crowded throughout the year. The travelers from around the work keep pouring down to travel the region at any time of the year.

Still, it’s better if you know which time around is remarkably perfect to walk the base camp. Notwithstanding, try best to avoid the trip to Annapurna base camp during monsoon.

The rushing rainfall will adversely affect the visibility of the mountains. Slimy roads will cause an accident while lodges and guest houses remain jam-packed.

You may not have anything special to do at this time with the dark clouds looming over the sky. And in the company of mosquitoes and leeches, you’d find the journey a horrific one.

An intrepid biologist can still pack their bags as the animals are most visible in monsoon. For an avid trekker, Autumn is the prime time to visit the Annapurna range.

With a dry climate, the sky becomes more visible and clearer. You can trace the sublime beauty of the Himalayas, varying landscapes and wildlife like never before.

Then, of course, the vibrant art and rich culture of Sherpa people living in the region. It takes you insight into their way of living and traditions practice from primordial time.

For those, who dislike overcrowding, better be accommodated by your trek guide in December. Due to heavy snowfall, many trekkers pull out to walk the routes of the base camp. And this is why the place sees fewer crowds in winter.

Starting from January, the region is persistently under the threat of avalanches. Therefore, trekkers traveling from Deurali to Machhapuchhre Base Camp must stay cautious.

The other great time for Annapurna Base Camp trek is Spring when it’s blue in the sky. Trails remain covered with the flower petals blossomed all through the forest. The exchange of cultures and values sprouts vastly in the area.

Why is Annapurna Base Camp trek in November considered the best?

The Annapurna Base Camp trek sees thousands of tourists visiting the region each month. But the flock of people walking the Annapurna Base Camp trek in November is something unbelievable.

Most explored, Annapurna has the world’s best crowd in November. All of them are dying to experience the sublime beauty of the region, its geography, and art.

Annapurna Base Camp trek in November has always more to offer to its visitor than any other month. The pulsating scenery, majestic Annapurna I, and lush green pastures are only a few to highlight.

The magic happens in the subtropical dense forest when the wide species of flower blossoms. It is a sight to watch the dense rhododendron trees and the diversity in vegetation.

With the winter making its way to the region, the night of Annapurna in November is chilly. The climate gets unpredictable at times so you might be prepared for any circumstances.

Normally, the temperature remains -5 Degree Celsius in Annapurna Base Camp during November. Meanwhile, the lower region is still hot as compared to the highland.

Annapurna Base Camp in November has less humidity in November and remains dry. The morning and nights are still quite cold and breezy.

The highlight of Annapurna Base Camp Trek in November

  • Panoramic views of mountains disperse around the region including Machhapuchhre
  • Traditional villages with affable locals to accommodate
  • Relaxing trails covered with dense rhododendron forest and subtropical forest
  • Magnificent view of snow peaks and highland pastures along the way
  • Discerning the lifestyle, cultures, and values of people living in the Himalayas
  • Exploring the wild species and vegetation of the Annapurna region
  • Cultural exchange while passing villages like Ghorepani, Deurali and Ulleri

Difficulties during Annapurna Base Camp Trek in November

  • As the climate is more favorable at this time, the place remains crowded
  • Difficulty in finding lodges and tea house with no visitors
  • Experience cold weather by the end of the season
  • Trails get slippery with snow-covered as you walk above

Essentials required during Annapurna Base Camp Trek in November

Walking the Annapurna Base Camp trek in November is a dream come true of every hiker. The sheer beauty of the valley with remoteness along with a green meadow will leave you bedazzled.

By virtue of warm temperature, and tranquil atmosphere, the place becomes a delight to travel. Still, for a grueling trip like Annapurna Base Camp trek, you’ll always want to make sure that you’ve got the right essentials.

The well-marked trails, detailed trek map, and signpost are sure of great help. But it’s best for you to be well-prepared and possess the items required during the trek.

Although it’s better if you travel light, getting the stuff you might think is indispensable. Having gloves, a windcheater jacket, and thermals are better than any apparel.

As the weather in the Annapurna gets unpredictable, it’s better you carry a lightweight down jacket. Go with the sturdy walking boots and lightweight trekking shorts that are proven comfort.

Sunglasses, head torch, spare batteries, and wash kit in rucksacks is no loss. Other items you can’t say no to include lightweight rain gear and trekking pole to walk the trails.

List of items required during Annapurna Base Camp Trek in November

  • Base Layers (lightweight short sleeve and long sleeve)
  • Mid Layer (lightweight fleece sweater)
  • Synthetic hiking pants and shorts
  • Light-weight waterproof jacket and trousers
  • Light-weight gloves, wide-brimmed sun hats, and sunglasses
  • Wool-blend hiking shoes and trekking poles

Other essential items

  • Medical kit (Blister Plasters, lip slave, sunscreen, aspirin)
  • Personal Toiletries (Shampoo, toothbrush, toothpaste, hand sanitizer, deodorant)
  • Head torch and travel adapter
  • Travel towel and Sleeping sheet

Optional Items

  • Map of Annapurna Base Camp
  • Binoculars
  • Journals, pens, and a small notebook

Food and Accommodation

Annapurna Base Camp trek in November is a trekking wonderment. In the presence of a clear blue sky, you’re to witness the absolute beauty of the region. The snowy peaks of Himalayas and it’s striking terrains are what add the charm of Annapurna.

As much as it’s topography, the local culture and arts of Sherpa people have also tempted travelers. The Annapurna Base Camp Trek Accommodation is a key factor why the region is treasured so much of all.

From the morning dawn till dusk, you’ll never have difficulty finding a place to stay at. The hospitality of the locals in the region is best on its own kind.

You can expect a warm welcome with an open heart in the guest house and lodges. As with the accommodation, they’ll get you delicious food unlike anywhere in the world.

The food is definitely not of a typical restaurant quality but the taste won’t disappoint you. For the first-timer, the experience of having a traditional cuisine of Himalayas is surely exciting.

The menu can see variation from your local meal (rice with lentils) to Chinese stir-fried noodles. The other exception being Pizza which is quite appetizing. Hot showers will be at your service all day long.

Teahouse Accommodation has found growing popularity among tourists over the past few years. They are well-built and organized with all facilities available to serve trekkers.

The service in the teahouse includes a wooden bed alongside a pillow, a simple mattress, and a blanket. The keeper will also take care of your basic essentials.

The teahouse on the route to Annapurna Base Camp has an electric heater shower. This will no doubt, comfort every visitor staying here especially in winter. Henceforth, they prove to be the perfect place to reside and relax before continuing the journey.

A lot of trekkers exchange cultures on their visit to the base camp. Some of them even become a part of their festivals, folk dance, and rituals performed in the monastery.

Annapurna Base Camp Trek in November will also see you walking through the picturesque forest. Along the trails, you’ll endure a tranquilizing atmosphere, sighting the mountains.

title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek Map
excerpt: Annapurna base camp trek is one of the most recognized trekking destinations of Nepal. Every year many trekkers make the climb to this base camp. If you are thinking of making a climb in this region…
html:
Annapurna base camp trek is one of the most recognized trekking destinations of Nepal. Every year many trekkers make the climb to this base camp. If you are thinking of making a climb in this region then don’t forget to carry Annapurna Base Camp Trek Map.

In this modern era, people mostly rely on technological gadgets. Handheld GPS has been taking over the trekking market. Through these gadgets, you can download and plan the paths in advance to decide the quickest and easiest routes.

But even the electronic devices can fail sometimes as you may drop it or no satellites overhead, etc. So you are recommended to carry paper maps and compass as a backup.

Annapurna is the 10th highest mountain in the world situated in the Gandaki zone. Its base camp has been a famous trekking point for many trekkers.

The trek through Annapurna Base camp gives you an extraordinary view of high mountains, multiple landscapes, traditional villages, diversity of flora and fauna, etc. It is a walk to the Lap of Mount Annapurna.

Along the way, you will see many mountains such as Annapurna I, Annapurna II, Annapurna III, Annapurna IV, and Annapurna South, Dhaulagiri, Nilgiri, Lamjung Himal, etc.

This trek gives you an insight into the culture and lifestyle of the people living in the upper hills. You also get the chance to explore the magnificent nature.

The trails are not very difficult even noob trekkers can trek in this region. There are many trekking routes for you to decide so it can be confusing.

Thus Base camp adventure has made Annapurna Base camp Trek map to help you decide the less time-consuming routes without missing out any adventure.

With the help of this map, you can know about the distance, altitude, places, etc which is an important piece of information. Following this map, many people have finished their trek easily.

You can get the proper description of the Annapurna Base camp trek map which is given down below.

Summary

The first day goes by in a blink of an eye as you reach Kathmandu and head towards your hotel where you will spend the night and rest for the next day.

The second day of your journey begins as you leave the capital city. You will be traveling a 7 hours drive on the bus from Kathmandu to Pokhara. Pokhara is a beautiful city which is also the gateway for many trekking regions.

Upon reaching Pokhara you will stay the night there then start your drive to Nayapul next morning. From Nayapul, you will trek to Ulleri viewing and walking through rivers, villages, etc.

The next day you walk through a forest to reach a small settlement of Magar/Gurung. Then from here, you will climb staircases made of stones all the way to Ghorepani. Arriving you can view the beautiful scenes of various mountains.

You will wake up early today as you will be hiking to Poon hill also called Photographer’s paradise. The view of sunrise from the hill is marvelous along with the beautiful sight of Mt. Annapurna and Mt. Dhaulagiri.

After the scenic views, you ascend towards Tadapani which is your stop for the day. From there you head to Chhomrong crossing many bridges and resting for a while in Jhinu Danda before entering the village.

On your seventh day, you head to Himalaya walking through rhododendron forests, crossing Chhomrong Khola and traveling uphill and downhill till you reach there.

To reach Annapurna Base Camp you trek pass many traditional villages viewing their unique lifestyle. You also pass-through forests filled with different species of flora and fauna.

The walk to base camp offers many mesmerizing views of natural diversity, landscapes, mountains, etc. Many variations of birds, waterfalls, chattering of monkeys make your trek more interesting.

This day you trek down to Bamboo through Machhapuchhre base camp viewing the snowy peaks along the way. You then climb down past Deurali, Himalaya and reach Bamboo.

Today you walk up and down hills before you reach Jhinu Danda where you stay for the night. After your night there, you trek back to Nayapul and drive back to Pokhara.

Staying the night in Pokhara you drive back to Kathmandu and fly back to your countries the next day.

Keep your Annapurna Base Camp Trek Map somewhere handy so that you can have a less hassled trip!

Highlights of the Trek

  • Reach Annapurna Base camp
  • Visit Natural hot spring
  • View the sunrise
  • Exotic flora and fauna
  • Visit traditional villages located in the hills

  • Annapurna Base Camp Trek Distance
  • Annapurna Circuit Trek Difficulty

Annapurna Base Camp Trek details

Drive from Kathmandu – Pokhara (via tourist bus)

Drive duration: 6-7 hours

Distance: 201 km

Maximum altitude: 820 m

When you arrive at Kathmandu airport the respective representatives will be waiting for you at the exit point. From there, they will pick you up and drop you off at your hotel.

As the flight might be tiring you will rest for the day as you have to spend the

You leave for Pokhara after having your breakfast. You will be traveling on a tourist bus through Prithvi Highway. The drive takes you through the charming landscape alongside the Trishuli river viewing many villages and small towns.

After you reach Pokhara you can freshen up and walk out to spend the evening by the lakeside. You spend your night in Pokhara.

Drive to Nayapul and Trek to Ulleri

Drive duration (to Nayapul): 2 hours

Trek duration ( to Ulleri): 4-5 hours

Drive distance ( to Nayapul): 45 km

Trek distance ( to Ulleri): 9.65 km

Maximum altitude (Nayapul): 1,010 m

Maximum altitude (Ulleri): 1,920 m

Today is the beginning of your Journey to reach ABC. You drive to Nayapul from where your trek will start.

After reaching Nayapul you will begin your walk by crossing the suspension bridge over the Modi River. Crossing the bridge and walking further ahead you reach Birethanti.

From there you will be climbing stone steps as you pass many villages such as Mathathanti, Hille, Tikhedhunga, etc.

Reaching Ulleri you get to glance at the mountains Annapurna south and Himchuli. You will be staying overnight at one of the guesthouses.

Ulleri – Ghorepani

Trek Duration: 4 to 5 hours

Trek Distance: 29.7km

Maximum altitude: 2,860 m

Today the trails are easy as you walk through dense forests filled with rhododendron. Walking on these trails for some time you will cross the Banthanti and Nangethanti villages.

You then ascend uphill in stairs made of stones and reach Ghorepani. The panorama view of Mount Annapurna will amaze you as you enter the area.

You will stay there for the night.

Hike to Poon hill then to Tadapani

Trek duration (poon hill): 1 hour

Trek duration (Tadapani): 6-7 hour

Distance (poon hill): 1 km

Trek distance (Tadapani): 9.7 km

Maximum altitude (poon hill): 3,210 m

Maximum altitude (Tadapani) : 2,610 m

Today you will wake up early in the morning as you are going on a hike to Poon hill. You will climb up a steep hill through trials of snow until you reach the top.

The view of sunrise you get from up there is very mesmerizing, you also get to view many mountains such as Dhaulagiri, Tukuche, Nilgiri, Annapurna I, Himchuli, Annapurna South, Lamjung Himal, etc.

After the fascinating view, you head back to Ghorepani grabbing your things. You descend through dense forests viewing the unique flora and fauna. The trail’s difficulty is moderate so you can easily walk this path.

You reach Tadapdani and call it a night.

Trek to Chommrong

Trek duration: 5-6 hour

Distance: 9.8 km

Maximum altitude: 2,170 m

Today you start your journey by walking uphill then downhill through trails of dense forest. As you walk further you will cross a suspension bridge built above the Kimrong Khola.

Ahead from there, you reach Jhinu Danda which is one of the Natural hot springs of Nepal. You will take a rest for some time and again start your walk until you reach Chommrong.

Chommrong is a beautiful village as you enter it you get the astounding view of Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre. You will stay the night here.

Trek to Himalaya

Trek duration: 6-7 hour

Distance: 8 km

Maximum altitude: 2,170 m

Today the difficulty of the trails is easy as you will be walking through forests of rhododendron, orchid, and ferns. As you walk out of the forest you will walk down the stairs of stones and cross the Chhomrong Khola.

Crossing the Khola you ascend uphill reaching Sinuwa then again descend through stone staircases to reach Bamboo. This day you will be climbing up and down many stone staircases.

As you arrive Bamboo you will walk across the forest trail and reach Dobhan then from there head towards Himalaya situated underneath the Hiunchuli peak.

When you reach Himalaya you will stay for the night. The amazing view of rivers you see beneath is breathtaking.

Trek to Annapurna Base Camp

Trek duration: 6-7 hour

Distance: 8.5 km

Maximum altitude: 4,130 m

The most awaited day of your trek is here when you visit the highest point i.e. Annapurna Base Camp.

You wake up early this morning and ascend towards Deurali traveling through stone stairs. Along the paths, the alluring view of snow-capped mountains will accompany you till you reach Machhapuchhre Base Camp situated at an altitude of 3,700 m.

From there you follow the moraines of South Annapurna and reach the Annapurna South (7,219 m) base camp.

As you reach the Base Camp you get to see the panorama view of snow-capped mountains such as Patal Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre, Annapurna Massif, etc.

Today’s journey might be a bit more difficult than previous days as you are gonna settle in a higher altitude. You have reached the base camp of the world’s 10th highest mountain.

So you will settle in the base camp and give your body rest for the day.

Annapurna Base Camp – Bamboo

Trek duration: 6-7 hour

Distance: 12.7 km

Maximum altitude: 2,345 m

Today you will be descending down to a lower altitude. As you walk down the paths following the moraine routes you reach Machhapuchhre Base camp.

From there you travel sighting the snow-capped mountains and entering through forests of rhododendron by following the routes of Modi Khola. As you walk through the forest viewing different shades of nature you descend past Deurali and Himalaya.

After walking for a few hours you reach Bamboo and stay overnight in one of the guesthouses.

Bamboo – Jhinu

Trek duration: 5-6 hour

Distance: 11.7 km

Maximum altitude: 1,780 m

After a wonderful night in Bamboo, you again start your journey as you ascend through forests filled with colorful flora and fauna towards Sinuwa.

From Sinuwa you head below towards Chhomrong Khola and ascend to upper Chhomrong through stone staircases. You again descend from there through dense forest viewing the wonderful landscapes along the way and reach Jhinu Danda.

Jhinu Danda is a natural hot spring which is a famous spot for trekkers on these routes. The hot spring is about 30 m down from Jhinu Danda. You can take a dip and relax your muscles.

After the relaxing bath, you stay there and have a peaceful night.

Jhinu Danda – Nayapul then drive to Pokhara

Trek duration (Nayapul): 2- 3 hours

Drive duration (Pokhara): 2 hours

Trek distance (Nayapul): 4.3 km

Drive distance (Pokhara): 45 km

Maximum altitude ( Nayapul): 1,010 m

Maximum altitude ( Pokhara): 820 m

Your trek is now about to come to an end as you will be heading back to Pokhara today.

After a relaxing time in the hot spring, you wake up early today and get ready to walk the trails for the last time.

Following the trails across Modi Khola, you descend viewing the beautiful landscape and mountains.

As you reach Nayapul you catch the vehicle from there and drive back to Pokhara.

After a tiring day, you can either rest for the day or you can roam the city. There are various options to do such as visiting lakeside, clubbing, cycling, etc.

You can also have a peaceful dinner on the lakeside viewing the Phewa Lake.

You will spend your night here.

Pokhara – Kathmandu

Trek duration: 7-8 hour

Trek distance: 201 km

Maximum altitude: 1,345 m

You can now say your trek has come to an end as you will be heading back to Kathmandu today on a tourist bus.

You will wake up early in the morning and drive back viewing the hills, villages, fields, etc along the way.

As you arrive in Kathmandu you will be dropped back to your hotel. You can freshen up and visit local markets nearby.

You can also give your body rest from all the walking you have done for the past couple of days.

This is your last night in Nepal as tomorrow you will be dropped off at the airport. And you head back to your country taking the beautiful memories you made here.

Permits required for Annapurna Base Camp Trek

Annapurna Base Camp is a part of the Annapurna Conservation Area. Before going on a trek both solo trekkers and group trekkers have to acquire an individual ACAP entry permit. To apply for the permit you should provide two passport size photos to the representative.

For the entire trip, you have to carry the permit along and show it in check-posts per request. The permit can only be used once. It is neither refundable nor transferable.

With the permit, trekkers are allowed to enter only selective places within the conservation area.

You also need to acquire Trekker’s Information Management System card to trek until the base camp. It is compulsory for both Free Individual Trekkers and Government-authorized agencies.

You will be needing a copy of the passport and two passport-sized photos to register for the Trekker’s Information Management System. You can get this card from the offices of Nepal Tourism Board in Kathmandu and Pokhara and the Taan Secretariat in Maligaon and Pokhara.

The Final Say

Annapurna Base Camp is gaining more and more popularity each year. Many trekkers trek in these routes every year fulfilling a wish in their bucket list.

The trails are not very difficult which is also one of the reasons that attract trekkers. The paths enter through forests filled with rhododendron, unique Landscape, lush forests, extraordinary flora, and fauna, etc.

With the help of our Annapurna Base Camp Trek map, you can gain information that is reliable and necessary while choosing your routes. Many routes have been declared to make a climb till the base camp. With the map that Base Camp Adventure has made it will be faster and easier for you.

It is quite important that always carry Annapurna Base Camp Trek Map with you whether it be digital or traditional. So that if you get lost by any chance you can follow it to reach the destination.

title: Everest Base Camp Trek with Kids
excerpt: The spectacular Everest Base Camp trek is not just for adults. With proper preparation and determination, kids can take part in this exciting Everest region trek as well. Everest Base Camp trek with…
html:
The spectacular Everest Base Camp trek is not just for adults. With proper preparation and determination, kids can take part in this exciting Everest region trek as well. Everest Base Camp trek with kids is a great family adventure in the foothills of the majestic Himalayas.

Since you will be traveling with kids, you need to extra careful at all times. You should put the kids and their demands on your top most priority. The kids should also be able to describe their conditions accurately during the Everest Base Camp trek. This is essential as it helps you understand your kid’s ability and you can plan your trek accordingly.

The Everest Base Camp (EBC) trek is one of the most trekked routes in the world. You will get to experience the stunning sunrise from Kalapathar along with the snow-capped mountains. The trails of this spectacular trek also pass through the UNESCO listed natural World Heritage site of Sagarmatha National park. The National Park has an immense role in conserving the flora and fauna of the Everest region.

Furthermore, the 360-degree panoramic view of the Himalayan vista is the prime attraction of the trek. The breathtaking mountain views of Mt. Everest, Ama Dablam, Nuptse, Taboche, Lhotse, Pumori, Cholatse, and others are enchanting. The incredible hospitality of the local people will make you fall in love with the place.

We offer this Everest Base Camp trek with kids at a reasonable cost. Read further for more information about the trek with kids. Book your trip now for an incredible family adventure in the mountains!

Related Treks:

  • Trekking to Everest Base Camp from Jiri
  • EBC Trek with Island Peak Climb
  • Luxury Lodge Trek to Everest Base Camp

For any inquiries please contact us.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Significant Highlights of the Trek

  • Observing the vibrant atmosphere of Everest Base Camp
  • Spectacular sunrise from the viewpoint in Kala Patthar (5,555 m)
  • Panoramic Himalayan mountain views including Mt. Everest, Mt. Nuptse, Mt. Lhotse, Mt Ama Dablam, Taboche, Lhotse, Pumori, Cholatse, and others
  • Walking through Sagarmatha National Park which a UNESCO listed natural world heritage site
  • Spotting the rare wildlife along the trail including Himalayan Thar, Snow leopards, Danphe, etc
  • A cultural exploration of the traditional villages and lifestyle of the Sherpa community
  • Tasting the delicious local cuisine
  • Incredible hospitality of the local people

When is the Best Time for the Everest Base Camp Trek With Kids?

The ideal time for the Everest Base Camp trek with kids is the Autumn and Spring season. These seasons are popular because of the stable weather conditions and the pleasant temperatures that are perfect for trekking.

The autumn months of September, October, and November provide stable weather and incredible views of the mountains. This peak season also attracts hundreds of trekkers in the Everest region. Moreover, the autumn season comes after the monsoon season. Hence, you can get the beautiful, unobstructed views of the Himalayas.

The spring season from March to May is another popular time to trek in the Everest region. You will see many colorful tents of climbers during this Trek in the spring season. Wildflowers bloom all over the hills painting them red and pink and providing a scenic environment. The stable weather and moderate temperatures are ideal for a trekking adventure in the mountains.

The trek in offseason (monsoon and winter) are also possible. However, the monsoon treks come with the risks of avalanches and landslides in the region. The winter season treks are challenging because of the extreme cold conditions. With proper packing and preparation, the offseason treks are doable in the Everest region.

How Long is the Everest Base Camp Trek with Kids?

The incredible EBC trek has multiple itineraries. On average, the trek is around 11-13 days on a round trip. It takes about eight days to arrive at Everest Base Camp from Lukla. This includes two days of necessary acclimatization at Namche and Dingboche.

Acclimatization is essential as the risk of altitude sickness increases as you cross above the altitude of 2,700 m Also, we need to ensure that we don’t climb or ascent more than 600 m per day. This rule is for trekkers of all ages, and especially kids and children.

Generally, six days of trek and two days of acclimatization is ideal for the trek. If your kids cannot adapt to the conditions quickly, you can add an extra acclimatization day. Overall, the length of the trek must depend upon the ability of your kids to trek and adapt to high altitude conditions.

How Difficult is the Everest Base Camp Trek with Kids?

The EBC trek requires six to eight hours of walking every day in harsh terrains of the Everest region. This includes lunch breaks and rests in the middle. We don’t stay idle even on acclimatization days and hike regularly.

There are also steep climbs in the middle with lots of ups and downs. The two most challenging aspect of the trek is the altitude sickness and the hike to Kalapathar.

Altitude sickness

Altitude sickness is a threat to trekkers of all skill levels in the trek. Moreover, children are even more susceptible to altitude sickness than adults. At higher elevations, the oxygen levels decrease significantly, and the air begins to thin. Trekkers will thus have a hard time breathing.

The primary key to tackle the altitude sickness during the EBC trek is to walk gently with plenty of acclimatization. You need to be extra careful on your trek from Lukla to Everest Base Camp and should not rush to your destination as it would increase the risk of altitude sickness.

Another important thing is to hydrate regularly during the trek. Water intake at regular intervals increases the oxygen levels in your body and helps you breathe normally. Hence, these tips will help you and your kids immensely during the trek.

Hike to Kalapathar

The hike from Gorak Shep to Kala Patthar is the most challenging part of the trek. The early morning trek to Kala Patthar rewards you with the incredible sunrise views overlooking Mt. Everest and the entire Himalayan range. Most of the pictures you see of Mt. Everest are from the Kalapathar viewpoint.

The harsh terrains during the Kalapathar trek from Gorak shep act as a hurdle for most trekkers. Climbing Kala Patthar for kids under 12 is very difficult. So, you must ensure that your kids are willing to climb to Kalapathar and have some experience in climbing. Alternatively, you can also make your kids skip the trek to Kalapathar.

How are the Accommodation Facilities Along The Trek?

Tea houses are the most common accommodation facilities along the trail. A teahouse is a small lodge with basic facilities, including twin beds, a pillow, and a warm blanket. You can also use a sleeping bag if the blanket provided is not enough.

Some tea houses provide running water and attached bathrooms, but these facilities are scarce once you arrive at Tengboche. Alternatively, you can use wet wipes to clean yourself and your kids. Besides that, the toilet is generally outside of the teahouses, and you will have to carry your own toilet paper.

A common dining room is an area where you can socialize with fellow trekkers and get proper heating during the nighttime. You will need to pay extra for charging electrical devices and hot water. A bottle of water can cost anywhere between $1-$3. You need to manage your expectations and practice caution as the conditions are not always hygienic in the high altitude tea houses.

Food Along the Trial

The tea houses generally offer meals three times a day. The food costs in the Everest region are high as all the food ingredients need to get transported or carried by porters. The food is not refrigerated, and hence you should avoid meat above Namche.

The standard dish served along the trail is the “dal bhat” which consists of rice, dal (pulses), vegetables, lentils, meat, gundruk, and pickles. You can get a limited variety of western and Chinese cuisine, including momo, pizza, burger, Chowmein, noodles, and others.

Breakfast includes toasts, eggs, and porridges, along with tea and coffee. Various soups and hot beverages like tea, coffee, lemon tea, mint tea, rhododendron tea, and others are a specialty in the Everest region. You can also taste Fried rice, Noodle soups, and Thukpa along the trail.

What is the Minimum Age Requirement for the Everest Base Camp Trek with Kids?

Most travel companies maintain the minimum age of eight for the Everest Base Camp trek with kids. Kids above eight-years and with some hiking experience can trek the trails of the Everest Base Camp with ease.

However, your child must be able to express his or her feelings without any hesitation after each day’s trek. This step is crucial for the safety of your child. Besides hiking, the child has to adjust to the cold conditions in the tea houses as there is no heating facility.

Furthermore, the limited variety of foods and lack of proper bathroom facilities are also some of the factors that make the trek difficult for them. The playful atmosphere and positive encouragement will help the kids immensely during this trek.

Essential Tips For The Everest Base Camp Trek with Kids

  • Train yourself and your kids two-three months ahead or at least two weeks before the trek. The training should include cardiovascular activities like hiking, cycling, swimming, jogging, and others
  • Carry board games and a deck of cards to play with the kids as they might get bored during the free time
  • You and your kids should acclimatize and hydrate regularly to tackle altitude sickness
  • Carry snacks to munch on for the trek. It should include protein bars, granola bars, chocolate bars (for kids), and others
  • Start your trekking early
  • Carry anti-nausea tablets like Diamox for overcoming the symptoms of altitude sickness
  • Walk slowly with gentle steps and do not rush during the trek
  • Get an excellent travel insurance package for the whole family with a coverage of more than 4,000 m in elevation
  • Increase your and your kid’s diet intake including food containing high calorie and protein

You may also like to read:

  • What to Expect in Everest Base Camp (EBC) Trek?
  • How Difficult is Everest Base Camp Trekking
  • Everest Base Camp Trek FAQs

For any inquiries please contact us.

Everest Base Camp Trek with Kids – Packing List

Trekkers need to pack their stuff as per the time of the trek. You should always pack only the items that are absolutely necessary and not overpack. The packing list for the Everest Base Camp trek with kids are as follows:

Clothing

  • Trekking shirts
  • Waterproof trekking pants
  • Windproof/waterproof jacket
  • Thermal wears
  • Fleece jackets
  • Down jacket
  • Trekking boots
  • Woolen trekking socks
  • Woolen gloves
  • Warm woolen cap
  • Raincoat

First Aid

  • Water purifier (SteriPen or chlorine tablets)
  • Rehydration salts
  • Anti-nauseant medication
  • Mosquito and insect repellent

Toiletries

  • Toothbrush
  • Toothpaste
  • Soap
  • Toilet paper
  • Shampoo
  • Sunscreen
  • Quick-dry towel
  • Sanitizer

Important documents

  • Passport
  • Trekking Permits
  • Travel insurance

Others

  • Reusable water bottles
  • Local SIM card
  • Snacks
  • Deck of cards
  • Phone
  • Camera
  • Solar chargers
  • Headlamp

Things to Consider For the Everest Base Camp with Kids

There are many factors to consider for the Everest Base Camp with Kids. Some of them are as follows:

Guide and porter

The trek is quite popular; hence the trails are well marked. Hiring a guide and a porter depends entirely upon your requirements. A guide can be a great companion and help you navigate the trail. They also provide incredible insights along the trek, and you and your kids can experience the beautiful local culture.

A porter will help you with your and your child’s luggage. Porter’s cost depends upon the weight of your luggage. Some guides work as porters, as well. However, they only carry the weight of a specific limit.

Fitness and Stamina

The Everest Base Camp trek with kids requires a basic level of fitness. Thus, you and your kids should undergo a training program that includes various cardiovascular activities, including cycling, jogging, swimming, hiking, and others.

These training activities should start three to four months ahead or at least two weeks prior to the trek. Generally, kids are very good at maintaining their stamina during the trek.

Acclimatization

Altitude sickness poses a potential threat for you and your child in the Everest Base Camp trek with kids. Acclimatization is essential for trekkers of all skill levels and age groups.

You can find health posts of the Himalayan Rescue Mission at Pheriche and Namche. They provide consultation and medical services to trekkers. Regular hydration along with acclimatization, is a must to tackle the problem of altitude sickness.

Trek Permits

The Everest Base Camp trek with kids requires travel permits, including the Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Permit and the Sagarmatha National Park Permit. The Sagarmatha National Park Permit is available in the Nepal Tourism Noard’s office in Kathmandu or Monjo, Chubu region. The local area permit or the Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Permit is available at Lukla or Monjo.

Travel insurance

Travel insurance is an essential part of any trekking journey. An excellent travel insurance package must cover various heading, including flight cancellation, medical emergency, theft, rescue and evacuation, and others.

Moreover, a helicopter evacuation might be necessary in case of a medical emergency, injuries, or altitude sickness. The cost of helicopter evacuation is anywhere between $5000 to $10000. Hence, an excellent travel insurance package is essential for the Everest Base Camp trek with kids.

The Final Say

The Everest Base Camp trek with kids is a great Himalayan adventure with your family. Your kids will love the pleasant trekking atmosphere and the beautiful sight of the snow-capped mountains.

This family adventure in the Himalayas is a once in a lifetime event. The Everest Base Camp Trek with kids provide an incredible trekking opportunity in the lap of mother nature. Contact us for more details regarding this exciting trek.

title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return
excerpt: Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter return package is for those who have less time. This is also for those who want to enjoy the luxury of helicopter return. The height of Annapurna is 8091m and…
html:
Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter return package is for those who have less time. This is also for those who want to enjoy the luxury of helicopter return. The height of Annapurna is 8,091 m and base camp is 4,130 m This is one of the most popular trekking routes all around the world. This region is popular for trekking, hiking, expedition, and climbing. This region has an amazing blend of natural and cultural aspects. This majestic landscape provides you a wide range of landscapes, flora, fauna, ethnic Gurung villages and culture. There are countless reasons to go for this amazing trek.

The trail passes through villages, steep hills, rivers, and sanctuary. From Annapurna Base Camp you can see magnificent Hiunchuli, Fishtail, Annapurna south and many more. You will also see a few high cascading waterfalls on the way. There is a natural hot spring near Jhinu Danda, you can clean yourself there and be pure. About 55000 people trek here every year. No doubt, the Annapurna region offers you much more than scenic beauty.

Like any other Annapurna treks, you will start this trek from Pokhara too. Pokhara is the tourist capital of Nepal. Pokhara is a beautiful city residing in the shadow of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail). This lake city offers you every adventure, thrill, and relaxation that you need when you are on holiday. You can start this journey alone. It is moderate in nature. You can do this trek in any season. Yet, in Monsoon and Winter, you should be extra careful.

Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return offers you the best deal on this tour. This tour encompasses beautiful places like Pokhara, Nayapul, Ghandruk, Chhomrong, Sinuwa, Deurali, Machhapuchhre Base Camp and Annapurna Base Camp.

Related Article:

  • Annapurna Base Camp Helicopter Tour with Landing

For any inquiries please contact us.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

When to visit Annapurna Base Camp?

Nepal is rich in geography and offers you a wide range of climatic conditions. The best time depends on you. What you expect to view and how you wish to trek, is the basic question you should ask yourself.

Autumn (September-November)

This season is often regarded as the best for Annapurna Base Camp Trek with helicopter return. The clear sky and view from the helicopter always appeal to the trekkers to choose this package. This is the peak season. The climatic condition is favorable for this trek. The weather is pleasant and comfortable. It is the perfect season to view all the mountains seen from this journey. Everything is clear this season. Majestic view of Annapurna I, II, III, IV, and Dhaulagiri will attract you.

Winter (December-February)

As Annapurna Base Camp rises to 4,130 m and it is near to Tibetan Plateau, winter here is freezing cold. Heavy snowfall occurs at the peak of the Winter season. This season is not favorable for Annapurna Base Camp Trek with helicopter return. There is snow everywhere. The helicopter may not land or take off. The tea houses and lodges are also closed during this season. The mountains are full of snow. It is beautiful scenery. People living in high altitude migrates towards the lower altitude.

Spring (March-May)

This is the most delightful season for Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter return. This season has warmer and longer days. Rhododendron covers the forest area and hill area of this circuit. The panoramic view from Annapurna Sanctuary makes you feel nostalgic. Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges are closets from this region.

Summer/Monsoon (June-August)

We call it Monsoon here. The chances of rainfall are also low in the upper range. The lower range of Annapurna Base Camp is hot and sizzling. There is greenery everywhere. As you go up temperature decreases. Mudslides and leeches make your trek difficult in this season. This trail is less crowded in this season which may be the perfect season for some of you. The sun is bright but it may be difficult for photography. Bring sunglasses.

Permits and Regulation for this Trek.

You need two permits for this trek. First is the Annapurna Conservation Area Project. The second one is the Trekkers’ Information Management System. The cost for the Annapurna Conservation Area Project is as below.

For SAARC nationals, the cost is 1000 per person and for other nationals, the cost is 3000 per person.

The same goes for Trekkers’ Information Management System. For SAARC nationals, the cost is 1000 per person whereas the cost is 3000 per person for other nationals.

Food and accommodation.

Tea houses and lodges are available. This is the most popular trekking circuit so you don’t have to worry about food and accommodation. Lodges might cost you $2 to $3 per day.

There are fancy hotels too but that will increase your cost to this trek. They expect you to eat where you stay. The tea-houses offer you varieties in the food items. They offer you different varieties in the egg itself. You will find chapati, packet noodles, potatoes, momos, cereals, etc. on the menu. In addition to that, you will also get Pudding, Marconi, Dal Bhat Tarkari and many more.

Dal Bhat Tarkari is a most fulfilling and less expensive food item. You will have tea, coffee, and some hot drinks for drinks. They sell some alcohol as well.

Difficulties

  1. The thin oxygen level creates difficulty in breathing.
  2. Altitude sickness is not common but you should be careful.
  3. Lodging and fooding may not be as you expected.
  4. Be careful at steep trials.

Highlights

  1. The most popular trekking route in the world.
  2. You will visit the popular Gurung village that is Ghandruk and Chhomrong.
  3. Majestic view of Mount Annapurna I, II, III, IV, and south.
  4. Reaching the highest point of this trek is Annapurna Base Camp 4,130 m
  5. Bath at Jhinu, a natural hot spring.
  6. You can visit various temples and stupas during this trek.
  7. You will enjoy Annapurna Panoramic view from Annapurna Sanctuary.
  8. We will return from Annapurna Base Camp through Helicopter.

Itinerary

Day 01: Pokhara-Nayapul-Ghandruk.

Your journey of Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return will start here from Pokhara. Pokhara is the tourist center of Nepal. If you are in Kathmandu, you can take a bus or flight to Pokhara.

Lake city Pokhara is famous for various reasons. You can enjoy the view of Machhapuchhre known as Fishtail. The nightlife of Pokhara is enjoyable. It is the gateway to Annapurna Circuit. From Pokhara, you will drive to Khimche. After reaching Khimche, you will trek too beautiful village Ghandruk 2,020 m

Ghandruk is a small village in Kaski district. It is a Gurung Village. You can see Gurung culture and ethnicity here. They are generous people. You will only walk for 1 hour to reach Ghandruk from Khimche. This will be your first trek of this journey. You will stay here tonight. You will see beautiful Annapurna South, Fishtail and many more. There are good food and lodging facilities available here.

Day 02: Ghandruk-Chhomrong-Sinuwa.

After having your breakfast here, you will start your trek to Chhomrong. The trail from Ghandruk slowly goes up. You will reach Komrong Danda in a few hours. You will trek down from Komrong Danda to Komrong Khola.

During this trek, you will witness local culture and tradition. You will also see the panoramic view of different mountains. You will again trek up from Komrong Khola to Chhomrang. Chhomrang is another beautiful village of Gurung people. These people are loving and unforgettable. They will treat you like their own sons or daughters. Leaving this village behind, you will trek downwards to another river.

From this riverside, you will again climb to Sinuwa village 2,340 m This is a small village. It has a few tea shops and lodges. You will have your tea here. You will also have rest and dinner here. The view of mountain vista will amaze you.

Day 03: Sinuwa-Bamboo-Dovan-Himalayan-Deurali.

The journey starts again after having light breakfast in Sinuwa. If the weather is nice, you will have the best views on this journey. With this view in your eyes, you will move forward to Deurali.

Your last destination for today will be Deurali 3,200 m The journey from Sinuwa to Deurali encompasses various forests of Rhododendron. This will be an uphill journey. It takes you 6-7 hours. You will have a silent walk to the jungle, feeling your own heartbeat.

The landscape, cool breeze and scenery all around will attract you towards nature. Walking through this route you will realize the importance of struggle in life. The lifestyle of people living here will inspire you to improve your lifestyle.

Day 04: Deurali-MBC-Annapurna Base Camp.

Today is the day that you are waiting for this whole journey. You will be at Annapurna Base Camp 4,130 m

From Deurali, you will start today’s journey. It will take you a 5-6 hours walk. The trails continue to go up. As you come closer the trails become higher. There are signs saying, avalanche area. You will not stay here long because it is not safe. Danger can occur at any minute.

The mountains are clear and close. Before reaching Annapurna Base Camp, you will reach Machhapuchhre Base Camp(MBC). The view from there is unexplainable. Once you reach MBC, you will have a view of Ganga Purna, Glacier Dom, Himchuli, Gandharva Chuli, Annapurna South and many more.

You will continue from there. You will have a pleasant walk from MBC. The air becomes thinner and thinner. You may experience some altitude-related symptoms. From Annapurna Base Camp, you can see huge Annapurna I 8,091 m, Annapurna South 7,219 m, Machhapuchhre 6,997 m and many more.

Day 05: Annapurna Base Camp-Pokhara by Helicopter.

Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter return comes to an end. You will enjoy every bit and byte of Annapurna Base Camp, and it’s time to return to Pokhara.

This may be your first helicopter ride. If this is not your first helicopter then it may be your first ride from this altitude of 4,130 m The helicopter will land you in Pokhara. It will take you 20-25 minutes ride from Annapurna Base Camp to Pokhara. This may be in your books of adventure. Helicopter ride from the world’s tenth highest mountain.
