title: Trekking in Nepal in June
excerpt: Nepal is the most visited trekking destination in Asia. Trekking options are available all year through. From the dry months of April to the wet months of June, you will find many trekking options in…
html:
Nepal is the most visited trekking destination in Asia. Trekking options are available all year through. From the dry months of April to the wet months of June, you will find many trekking options in Nepal.

You may ask, “How is trekking in Nepal in June possible when it is raining?”

Well, with proper rain gears and appropriate preparation, you can opt for the treks in Nepal June.

There are many options for both short and long treks for June. The rain-shadow areas are some of the finest destinations you can trek to. You can also opt for near and short trekking destinations.

Trekking in June can be really refreshing, thanks to the greenery of Nepal. The petrichor on the lush hills will add calm and serenity in your mind, body and soul.

June brings an opportunity to experience rain-washed vegetations, colorful flowers, and less crowd. The reason is that the time of monsoon is a time of agricultural richness here.

Weather While Trekking in Nepal in June

It is monsoon as well as the summer season in June. So, the weather is hot and humid. The greatest temperature can be more than 30 degrees in the day and in the night it is around 18 degree.

In most parts, the average temperature can remain around, 24 degrees during the afternoon and at night it can get 19 degrees. This is the temperature of Kathmandu.

Whereas in Pokhara, the average temperature can be around 32 degrees and at night it can be around 21.7 degrees.

In the Annapurna Base Camp, the temperature can drop and might also reach to lower than 0 degree at night. So, it is better to dress in layers and also have a sleeping bag with liner.

As this is the time of monsoon in Nepal, rainfall is quite common. But it is most likely to rain during the afternoon or in the evenings. So, you can start the trek early in the morning and reach your final destination before it rains.

Pokhara receives about 400 mm of rainfall. The southern slopes in Eastern Nepal receive more than 200 mm of rainfall. The rain shadow area beyond the Himalayan ranges receives less than 50 mm of the rain.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Highlights

Every season has its own features and so does monsoon. Yes, it can be quite a blissful trekking experience June, the time of monsoon.

Exploring Geography

Just like any other seasons, June gives a great opportunity to explore the geography, climate, and cultural diversity too. But what is more popular is that it is also a better time to experience the agricultural activities. The local planting style will have you mesmerized which is mostly done in June.

Clear Views

After the evening rain, you will get crisp views in the morning. The sunrise is something that no one should miss. The golden rays touching the snow capped mountains is a must-watch view.

You also get the best views after the rain clears off. You will see the lush green hills. And the beautiful terrace farming with the local vegetations and the colorful flowers.

Less Crowd and Cheaper Deals

Since it is not the peak season, there is less crowd in the trekking trails. The trekking is more peaceful this way. Also, you will have more chances of beautiful photographs without the crowd.

Less crowd can also get you good deals on accommodations, flights and shopping for souvenirs. You can have the opportunity to choose some of the best tea houses in the best deal.

Essentials While Trekking in Nepal in June

Rain gears are a must while trekking in June. You need a good pair of water-proof trekking boots since the roads usually get muddy and slippery. You also need to invest in a good pair of rain-proof jackets and trousers.

Do not forget to pack a fleece jacket for the evenings. All the clothing gears should be breathable. Dressing lose can help during the day while sleeping bag with a liner can help in the evenings.

Permits are also a must-have during the trek. And, the permits vary depending on the region you are trekking to. You can easily get the necessary permits from Nepal Tourism Board throughout the year. And, June is no exception.

Along with clothing and permits, do not miss first aid kits and your personal toiletries. You also need a water bottle and water purification tablets along with it.

Whatever you pack, it is very important to protect your belongings from getting wet. So, a rain-proof cover for your backpack will help you.

Tips for Trekking in Nepal in June

  • The trails can get muddy, so a good pair of trekking shoes are your best friend.
  • Leeches, bugs, mosquitoes are common in this season, so carrying some table salt or insect repellent is helpful.
  • There is also a risk of landslides and floods so hiring an experienced guide will help you go from the best routes.
  • Start the trek in the morning because it usually rains in the afternoon.
  • Prepare for a few extra days because there are high chances of flights getting delayed.
  • Get travel insurance as they will recover in case of flight cancellation or other emergencies.
  • Carry a waterproof backpack for ease

Destinations for Trekking in Nepal in June

Annapurna Circuit Trek

Annapurna Circuit Trek is one of the most popular trekking destinations in Nepal. Most of the trails in Annapurna Circuit trail lies in the rain shadow area. So, trekking in the region in monsoon will be no difficulty in this region.

Annapurna Circuit Trek is popular as the term ‘Classic Himalayan Trek’. This glorious trek encircles the Annapurna region and you have a lot you can experience if you choose this trek.

While starting the journey from Besisahar, you are more likely to experience more rainfall.

Frequent thunderstorms in the lower elevations are common. But, as you go higher to the rainshadow area, you will have easy trekking in the dry surrounding.

In the north of the Himalayan range is the high and dry Tibetan Plateau. The highest point of this trek is the Thorong Pass which is on the elevation of 5,414 m You will also walk through the valley of Upper Manang.

This is not affected by rain while offering greater views.

There is a famous Hindu pilgrimage site Muktinath there. The world’s deepest river gorge of Kali Gandaki Valley is also another highlight of this trek.

Upper Mustang Trek

Upper Mustang, the forbidden kingdom is one of the top trekking destinations in Nepal. It is a rare privilege to enter the valley. It borders with Tibet and has Tibetan influence as well.

This is a rainshadow region which experiences least to no rainfall. So, trekking in Upper Mustang in June is less problematic due to rain or humidity.

On top of that, the people of the Buddhist villages there are always happy to see new guests coming in.

The beauty of the trek includes hidden Caves, Monasteries and the peaceful ambience of the Buddhist Community.

Upper Dolpo Trek

The Upper Dolpo Trek is the northern part of Dolpo. The Northern side of the Himalayan Region is good for trekking during the monsoon. So, this trek is a really good option to choose for trekking in June.

This adventurous trek offers you some of the most spectacular views of the Tibetan plateau and Dhaulagiri range. Trekking to this trans-Himalayan region in June is absolutely possible.

Gosaikunda Lake Trek

Gosaikunda Lake Trek is a short trek alternative you can do in the month of June. The alluring waterfalls, rivers and exotic landscapes are some of the best highlights.

Now you might be wondering if the water resources are overpowering in the monsoon but the altitude is not affected. June is one of the best times you can visit Gosaikunda. It is best if you visit in early June as the monsoon gets bigger in the later month.

The early June is still dry and this is a short trek. So it is perfect for the trekkers who have less time or want to start trekking in another destination.

This short trek is good if you do not like the crowd. Unlike other popular trekking destinations, Gosaikunda Lake Trek is much quieter and peaceful. A short trek like this is good during June because it takes about a week or so to complete, and you can get away from the rain.

This trek in the Langtang region is a moderate trek and is possible throughout the year. So, June is an option too. This is a close destination from Kathmandu to trek to.

Conclusion

Trekking in Nepal in June can be amazing and adventurous at the same time. The accommodations, permits and all the requirements are easily accessible and the deals can be really good too.

The Himalayan region in the northern – central part is favorable areas for trekking in June. And you also have a lot of options to choose to trek this month.

Fewer crowds give you benefits in the best deals and also the trails are quieter. So the month of June adds the best you want in your peaceful holiday. The experience is different than other season so this is another edition you can experience in your journey.

For more details, you can contact us.

title: Mardi Himal Trek Difficulty
excerpt: Mardi Himal Trek falls on the difficulty of moderate. This is a newer trek compared to the Everest Base Camp Trek but is absolutely stunning. It will surprise you with some of the best views you can…
html:
Mardi Himal Trek falls on the difficulty of moderate. This is a newer trek compared to the Everest Base Camp Trek but is absolutely stunning. It will surprise you with some of the best views you can have on any trek.

People from all age group can do this trek well.

Indeed, there are a lot of factors that contribute to making a trek easy or difficult. For starters, preplanning can get most of the job done.

Well, there are a lot of factors that contribute to Mardi Himal Trek Difficulty. The duration of the trek, your financial constraints, the route you choose and many more affect any trek.

The peak season is in the Autumn and Spring just like in the case of other treks. Mardi Himal Trek is quite affordable so increasing the number of days that you trek should make it less difficult.

Mardi Himal Trek is one of the best treks in the Annapurna Region. This trek gifts you a mesmerizing view of mountains like Annapurna, Machhapuchhre, Hiunchuli and more.

The highest elevation that you will climb is 4,500 m And the highest elevation that you will spend the night is 3,580 m

What Makes Mardi Himal Trek Difficult?

The trek gives you some of the best views is also one of the most amazing routes you can take with just a moderate difficulty level of the walk.

The routes are peaceful and quiet which adds its own charm in the trek. You can have a peaceful and smooth trek with your friends and team.

Not only this, but you can also have proper camping or tea house trek in Mardi Himal.

Another thing about the trek is that the route is minimal and is very enjoyable without much effort. You will have an amazing experience. You do not need expert trekking gears and only basic pieces of equipment are enough for the completion of this trek.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Mardi Himal Trek Difficulty

“The hidden treasure trek” of Mardi Himal is a must and almost everyone can do it. Beginner trekkers have rated the trek as moderate difficulty. Well, for most trekkers, it is an easy trek when compared to a lot of other treks.

There are many options in days you can choose from according to your difficulty tolerance.

Between 4 to 10 days, you can choose the trek duration as per your wish. The trek is customizable and suitable for people with no trekking experiences. The longer the trek, the easier it is for the trekker.

Mardi Himal Trek is a teahouse trek, which means that there are plenty of resting points on the way. The trek is also suitable for everyone because there are no vertical climbings. The route is quite easy and doesn’t involve difficult climbing or so.

You have to walk about 5 – 6 hours every day on this trek. Beginners also find the long uphill climbs a bit difficult. But resting points along the way makes the journey relaxing.

There are a lot of teahouses and other resting points available throughout the trail.

Because of the well-organized teahouses and resting points, there is no difficulty of altitude sickness. So the elevation of 4,500 m ascend will be easier than expected.

There is the Mardi Himal viewpoint in that elevation too.

You do not need high-end trekking gears like ropes and ice picks. There is no difficult vertical climbing. This is the reason everyone can do it.

Yet, the hardest part is reaching the Base Camp from the high camp. The paths are steep and rocky making this part of the journey a rough one. The trails along the route of this trek are not paved and are rocky.

It can get a bit difficult when it rains as the roads might get slippery. Also, the forests can get slippery in the rain too. But with adequate rest, and proper hydration will lead to a successful and memorable trek.

Duration of Mardi Himal Trek

The journey begins from Pokhara. You will drive to Phedi and start off the trek along with the greenery. Mardi Himal is about 8 days away from Pokhara and the itinerary you choose brings changes in your duration.

If you are a beginner, choosing more days can be efficient so that you do not have to rush during this trek. Enjoying the trek without difficulty in your health is important.

And if you have previous trekking experiences then you can choose less number of days to trek.

If you want to explore more and take your time to enjoy the moment a little more, then you can choose more days as well.

You will walk about more than 4 hours daily. You start off with a 4 – 5 hours walk to Phedi from Pokhara. You will walk 5 – 7 hours from Phedi to reach the forest camp. After this walk, you will feel like the uphill starts.

The uphills are the difficult part of the trek. Not only you have to climb up all the way but you also have your load of the backpack. The weight drags you down so make sure you rest once in a while as well.

This duration of the walk can be difficult for beginners. Before the trek proper exercise and training are necessary. A moderate trek like this also needs exercises prior to the actual trek.

You will walk about 4 hours or more on a daily basis until you reach the high camp at 3,700 m elevation. You will then trek to 4,500 m The high altitude may cause shortness of breath so hydration is important.

After a 6 – 7 hour trek you will reach Siding Village in the high camp. And the final 2 -3 hours trek to Lumre is your last trek. We will then take you back to Pokhara.

Altitude Sickness in Mardi Himal Trek

A common but unavoidable problem during the Mardi Himal trek is altitude sickness. Altitude sickness is common in the higher elevations and is a very crucial issue in the trek.

The different body reacts differently to altitude sickness. Some may find it very difficult whereas others can adjust well.

During the Mardi Himal trek, you will reach the maximum height at 4,500 m So, the risk of altitude sickness is quite common in the trek.

Some of the symptoms of altitude sickness are headaches, shortness in breathing, nausea, and diarrhea. You should not ignore any of the signs. Altitude sickness is very dangerous and might even cause death.

Drinking plenty of water and allowing your body to acclimatize are the ways to fight this issue. You should never drink alcohol during this trek as this causes dehydration. Carry a water bottle at all times and do not rush.

Accommodations on Mardi Himal Trek

The hotels and lodges are a bit pricey in Pokhara and Kathmandu but the teahouses are quite affordable during the treks. There is also no difficulty in getting all the accommodations but pre-booking can be really helpful in getting the best deals.

Restaurants and cafes are easily available from one stop to another with varieties of options in food. You do not have to worry about eating and sleep along the trail because the accessibility is pretty easy.

One thing that you have to manage for yourself is to bring a few snacks and food for the journey. Since the food is expensive as you go on higher elevations, it is better if you buy it in Kathmandu and Pokhara.

Bottled water can cost you a lot of money in the long run. Instead, you can use water purification tablets and get water refills at the tea houses for a cheaper price.

Essentials for Mardi Himal Trek

All the necessary items that you need in a trek depends on the route, season and difficulty level. Mardi Himal Trek is not so difficult, so only normal trekking gears will do the job pretty well.

You will definitely need the basic essentials and your personal requirements. Other than that, you need to invest in items like a strong trekking boot. This will be your best friend along the journey or you might even bring an extra pair of comfortable shoes.

A good pair of trekking trouser and jacket is a complete weather protection shield for you. This is perfect for layering during winter and also appropriate for summer. Flexible and comfortable clothing is another essential.

Carrying a water bottle and water purification tablets will change the entire game. This will also save up a few dollars.

Likewise, carrying sleeping bags and tents all depend on your choice of the trek. The amount of clothing depends on the season you choose for trekking.

Moreover, a trekking backpack holds all your necessities. While all the mentioned items are modifiable, there are other things you need to carry as well. They are:

  • Toiletries and personal hygiene
  • First aid kit
  • Extra cash
  • Cameras and other electronics
  • Chargers and other appliances

Few Tips and Details You Need to Know for The Trek

  • If you are looking for a short off-the-beaten-path then a package of 6 days is suitable for you. You can have plenty of time to enjoy the trek and the views. This package is short yet gives you enough time to enjoy the journey.
  • If you have difficulty and want no rush in your journey then feel free to choose between 7 to 10 days package. It will give you enough time to explore and trek with ease.
  • If you are a professional and want to do it fast then 4 or 5 days trek is perfect for you. Yes, it is possible and you can still have the chance to witness a spectacular view of mountain ranges from the viewpoint.
  • The highest point to spend the night is 3,580 m There will not be any problems of altitude because you won’t be spending so much time on the higher elevations.
  • Mardi Himal Trek can be pretty much done around the year but the best time is around spring and autumn season. If you want, you can do it whenever you want with all the necessary essentials.
  • It is better if you pre-book everything. It will save up your time and money. It also makes your accommodations available just in case the places get packed.
  • Buying mineral waters all the time can be expensive. So if you invest in a water bottle and purification tablets, it will be much more practical and efficient.
  • Renting is an alternative if you want to save up. Buying trekking gears will cost a lot of money. You can opt for renting items like trekking stick, tents, sleeping bags, etc.
  • There will also be expenses on other factors. They can be having access to the internet, hot showers and charging your electrical appliances. These will cost you money on an hourly basis.

Last Say,

Mardi Himal Trek Difficulty can be easily overcome with right preparations.

Make sure you spend the time to rest once in a while and avoid continuous trekking. It helps you overcome the feeling of fatigues. After all, you are there to enjoy the trip and get the best of it.

Allow us to guide you through the trek and make it a lot more exciting and memorable.

title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek Training
excerpt: Annapurna Base Camp Trek is one of the most loved treks by trekkers around the world. The Annapurna Base Camp trek takes you to the lap of Annapurna ranges. It gives you a beautiful view of the rich…
html:
Annapurna Base Camp Trek is one of the most loved treks by trekkers around the world. The Annapurna Base Camp trek takes you to the lap of Annapurna ranges. It gives you a beautiful view of the rich mountain ranges in Nepal.

In case of difficulty, it is a moderate trek and everyone can do it. But Annapurna Base Camp Trek Training is a bonus for the comfortable trek. There are a few things that you need to consider before the trek.

The highest elevation on this trek of Annapurna Base Camp is 4,190 m You will see mountains like Annapurna, Dhaulagiri, Hiunchuli, and Machhapuchhre. You will also enjoy the simplicity of the Gurung Community.

This journey along with the adventure brings many challenges. The higher elevations bring cases of altitude sickness and a lot of other health-related issues.

If you are a novice trekker, prior training is a must. That does not mean you need advanced mountaineering training. However, you need to have some basic physical training to complete this trek smoothly.

But, you do not need to be an athlete for it. There are some requirements such as building up your stamina. These allow you to enjoy your treks with comfort.

These are some of the things that you will learn during the Annapurna Base Camp Trek Training sessions. It is best to undergo such training.

What is Trekking to Annapurna Base Camp Like?

You need more than 10 days to complete Annapurna Base Camp Trek. You will hike most of the time. At times you will climb steep hills and rocky stairs.

You will walk for more than 4 hours on a daily basis with a backpack. You will be doing this for most days of your trek at the higher elevations of 2,000 m to 4,130 m Training is important if you want your muscles and body to be able to cover the distance in a completely new environment.

There is 20% – 30% less oxygen at higher altitudes and your muscles will get weaker faster.

You will walk about 6 km – 15 km distance per day.

Annapurna Base Camp is a beautiful place to trek to and the journey is absolutely memorable. With a little bit of preparation, you will be able it enjoy it and save it as one of the best experience ever.

You are in for amazing landscapes, forest, the local settlement, and the mountains.

However, the ABC trek doesn’t need any mountain climbing experience or prior trekking experience. But it definitely needs preparations and proper training for the trek.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Why Annapurna Base Camp Trek Training?

Before starting, you need to understand why you need to undergo training.

While trekking to higher altitudes, the amount of oxygen decreases. This, as a result, affects your body in several ways. Your body takes time to adjust to the changing altitude.

You have to walk 6 – 7 hours daily on an average on this trek. You also need to carry a heavy backpack throughout the trek. These are not things that you do on a daily basis, so sudden changes as such will take a toll on your body and health, if not prepared.

Trekking does take a lot of effort and can drain you. Training yourself before a trek will add to preparing your body so that it doesn’t feel the drastic change.

The training is only basic fitness activities, not heavy workouts. If you skip this, you might have to deal with the consequences later.

Training helps you increase your stamina. It also helps your body to get well adjusted to the changing environment and increased physical activity.

What Should Annapurna Base Camp Trek Training Include?

The kind of training completely depends on your where you live in and your surroundings. Short hikes are a way to start and choosing a hill area is the best. So look for the most suited area.

You do not need any heavy and muscular strength as a part of your training. But as a part of your training, you do need to prepare yourself to walk for about 5-7 hours on a daily basis with a backpack of a minimum of 5 kg.

We recommend you to train yourself for about 12 to 16 weeks prior to the trek. Some specific training that you can consider are

Aerobic Training or Cardiovascular

Aerobic gets your heart pumping and is perfect to adapt on the higher elevations where the air is thin. This kind of training includes exercises like cycling, swimming, running and more.

This also helps in balancing the oxygen volume that your body can use.

You can also include hill training and cardio as a part of your training. If you already workout at a gym, you can give an hour extra to include these exercises to increase strength.

Strength Training

Strength training specializes on the strength that you need in the trek with the weight you carry. This training includes exercising with free weights, bands, etc. Gym machines are also excellent for strength training.

This training will help build up power in both upper and lower part of your body. Exercising that involve calves, hamstrings, quads, and hips are also important. Strengthening your muscles like upper back and shoulders are a part of this training.

Altitude Training

Now the thing about altitude training is that you cannot train at the actual high altitudes as the Annapurna Base Camp. So, what you do is exercise as a mimic for altitude training.

You can take short treks to nearby hills and mountains in your home country and learning to adjust to the change in the environment. It also includes proper acclimatization time and proper rest.

Walking 3-5 hours per day with weight on your walk is a good way to start. The key is getting active and getting as much hill work in as possible.

Look for an appropriate area from where you live to start your training.

In some cases, extra days will also help your body to adapt to the environment during the trek. This will also help in recovery from altitude so that you can get proper rest and ready for the next day.

Tips Before Annapurna Base Camp Trek

  • You can choose the number of days you want to complete this trek. Choosing a package with more days will make the journey more relaxing and without any rush.
  • The main key is staying hydrated all the time. You can drink a lot of water and get a lot of rest. Rest recharges your body and water helps you to deal with the changing altitude.
  • An extra service you can have are trekking guides. You can do this trek pretty much with and without a guide but having a guide and a porter will make your trekking trips a lot more comfortable.
  • It is best to start early so that if you reach your destination early you will have enough time to enjoy the area as well as acclimatize properly.
  • Do not rush your body and keep your pace. Your body will adjust on its own with the change in altitude and you should give time for it.
  • Do not underestimate a high altitude trek like this one. Never ignore any sign of altitude sickness as this is a serious issue. Drink plenty of water and allow your body to acclimatize well.
  • Manage your time well. Training will help you with the timing as well. You do not want to be the one to slow down your trek.
  • Make sure the team you go with train properly as well. They should not come unprepared.
  • Starting off with easier treks will help in your training.
  • The best time is autumn and spring. The best time is September-October and April-May.
  • In the case of gears, a good hiking boot, an insulating jacket and sleeping bag with liner is a must for the trails and weather.
  • Take your favorite snacks with you to munch along the trek. It will make the journey less boring and refreshment once in a while are fun.
  • Mentally prepare yourself because this indeed is a long journey.

Conclusion

If you hurry to your destination, your body will not be able to handle the pressure. But completely losing a hold on yourself will affect your group and slow them down.

So to maintain the pace, you need to be fit physically as well as mentally and prepare for the trek.

Training is also important depending on the season you choose to trek and the package of days you choose.

Training for 4 – 6 hours daily can increase your efficiency and the journey will be easier. With proper exercises and gears, you will have a successful journey.

title: Mardi Himal Trek Cost
excerpt: Mardi Himal Trek is one of the most exciting treks you can have in the Annapurna region. This is a pretty moderate trek and is suitable for everyone. Also, it is quite a cost-effective trek. Well…
html:
Mardi Himal Trek is one of the most exciting treks you can have in the Annapurna region. This is a pretty moderate trek and is suitable for everyone. Also, it is quite a cost-effective trek.

Well, the total Mardi Himal trek cost depends majorly on the number of days you choose to spend trekking. This adds up the trek cost in the end.

Mardi Himal Trek is a less sought- after trekking in comparison to the iconic Everest Base Camp or the Annapurna Circuit Trek. This makes it less crowded, budget-friendly and unaffected by pseudo-culture.

The solitary trails can be a bonus since it gives you complete relaxation and an amazing experience. We can help you with the customized itinerary just to fit into your needs.

Allow us to supply you detailed information on the Mardi Himal Trek Cost.

Things that Affect Mardi Himal Trek Cost

There are many factors that influence the Mardi Himal Trek Cost.

  • Number of days you choose to trek ( this can be 10 days, 7 days, 6 days, 5 days)
  • The transportation cost
  • The routes you choose for the trek
  • Seasons and time of the year
  • Accommodations
  • Items packed
  • Trekking permits
  • Taxes and company service charge
  • Guides and porters (optional)

These are some of the unavoidable aspects to spend on. However, there are others as well that add to the cost like the amount you spend on buying bottled water or use rented gear and so on.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Mardi Himal Trek Cost and Trek Duration

The costs can vary as per the number of days you want to take the trek. The longest trek can be of 10 days. The overall cost for the package is about US$ 500 – US$ 700 (NRs. 56655 – NRs. 79317 approx.) per person.

As the number of days increases, you will be adding in the cost per day. This, in the end, increases your total cost.

E.g. For a 7-day itinerary, the costs can be around US$ 375 (NRs. 42491 approx.) per person.

Cost of Accommodation During Mardi Himal Trek

You will enjoy accommodations in the hotels and lodges as per availability. You will stay at hotels in Kathmandu and Pokhara that can be fancy and standard as per your choices. Whereas, during the trek, you will stay in tea houses since it is a tea house trek.

There are 3-star hotels in Kathmandu and Pokhara. But during the trek, you will be staying in tea houses are that are normal local houses that provide you with a room and basic services.

The accommodations are mostly twin-shared basis and you will spend about US$ 20 – US$ 30 (NRs. 2273 – NRs. 3409 approx.) per night. Single supplement is also available on request but will cost you few more amount.

The cost of accommodation differs as per the season you choose to trek. During the peak season of spring and autumn, the prices can go higher. But in other seasons, you can get cheaper deals with no crowds.

The cost of hotels and lodges also depend on the availability of the tea houses on the routes.

The availability of accommodation depends on the route you choose. Some highly trekked routes have better facilities and services and could cost a bit more than the paths less taken.

Also, the tea houses that you choose to stay offer food too and if you choose to stay in the house you eat food in, they are more affordable.

Cost of Food During Mardi Himal Trek

You will have authentic Nepali food for lunch and dinner. The meal is usually a set of a typical local dish, daal-bhat-tarkari to fill up your stomach to add up power for the trek.

For breakfast, you will have tea with some eggs, toast and seasonal grains that add protein to your diet. Mostly, breakfast and dinner are a part of the accommodation where you stay overnight.

There are also other choices of foods available on the trail these days. You can have your choices of meals that include cuisines from Nepal, India, and others.

The meals per day cost around $2-$6. You will have to pay extra if you choose to order something off the menu.

It’s better to carry snacks and energy bars and avoid buying them on the trail. These are a lot expensive here.

Soft drinks or flavored drinks are also available on the trail and can cost you about $3-$5. For water, it is better if you carry water bottles and water purifying tablets. Buying bottled water can cost you around $1 per bottle.

It is a lot more cost effective if you choose to refill your bottle at tea houses.

Cost of Transportations During Mardi Himal Trek

First, you need to reach Pokhara from Kathmandu. For this, you can either choose to fly to Pokhara or hit the road.

A flight from Pokhara to Kathmandu will cost you about US$ 120 per person. But a road trip will cost you about US$ 10 to US$ 30. The road trip cost depends on the type of vehicle you choose like a bus, jeep, private car, etc.

If you choose a simple bus ride, it will cost you cheaper- about US$ 10 or so. If you choose a jeep, it will cost you about US$ 20 to US$ 25 per person. But if you want something even more personal and relaxing then you can hire a private car and will cost you about US$ 30 or more.

After reaching to Pokhara, you will drive to Kande from where your Mardi Himal trek begins.

Cost of Guides/Porters During Mardi Himal Trek

Guides aren’t a mandatory part of this trek but since this is not a well-maintained trail like the popular ones, it is best to be accompanied by someone who is familiar with the route. Guides can be of great help when it comes to dealing with the locals too.

A licensed guide will charge you about US$ 20 – US$25 per day.

Porters help you with your load, you will feel a lot energized and lighter when someone else takes your load. They are generous and are some of the locals who are doing a seasonal job and are well aware of the routes too.

A porter will charge you about US$ 16 – US$ 20 per day. If you want a guide cum porter, he will charge you within US$ 18 – US$ 20 per day.

Cost of Permits During Mardi Himal Trek

Permits are easily available for this trek. You will need an Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP) and (Trekkers Information Management System) TIMS card for this trek.

The ACAP permit costs about US$ 20 approximately which is NRs. 2000. The same is for the SAARC nationals i.e. US$ 20 approx.

The TIMS card costs US$ 10 which is NRs.1000.

You can get all of these permits in Nepal Tourism Board office, Pradarshani Marg if you are in Kathmandu. If you are in Pokhara you can get the ACAP permit in the Nepal Tourism Board Service Center in Damside, or at ACAP entry permit counter in Besishahar, Lamjung.

You can get the TIMS card from TAAN lakeside office in Santi Patan, Pokhara.

Additional Cost During Mardi Himal Trek

Whenever you are trekking, you also spend on something that is not planned. For example, you might need a sleeping bag there so you rent it if you need it. Same with the extra tips you might give to the porters and guides.

Likewise, if you want, you can make donations to the local schools and other public places.

While trekking, you will be drinking a lot of water and as you climb up, you might end of buying a lot of bottled water than expected. And these add up to be expensive and unexpected.

Another expenses include wifi and charging your electric equipment. The tea houses that you stay or eat your meals in offer wifi services for a couple of dollars. They also offer charging ports for a small amount. The cost of wifi can be about US$ 0.5 – US$ 2 per hour.

Further, using a bucket of hot water for shower or asking for a flask of hot drinking water is applicable for small charges. You might be charged for about $1-$3 for a bucket of water.

If you do not prefer to buy all your trekking equipment, you can rent them from Kathmandu or Pokhara, you can rent them for about $1-$5 per day depending on the gear.

Also, souvenirs too add up to your cost. These are available anywhere and everywhere and you might be spending from $1 to $500 for souvenirs depending on what you buy.

Some Tips to Organize Your Mardi Himal Trek Cost

During this trek, it is best to prepare a budget and be more organized and practical. Here are some tips to manage your Mardi Himal trek cost:

  • To save up some cash, buy your favorite snacks from Kathmandu and Pokhara.
  • It’s better if you rent your gears than buy them if you are not a frequent trekker.
  • It is more practical to hire a local guide or porter.
  • Pre-booking makes the accommodation available and you can also get them cheaper.
  • Having travel insurance will help you in case of medications and last minute cancellation.

To Conclude

Mardi Himal Trek gives you one of the finest experience with the most mesmerizing view guaranteed. The best times are spring (March-May) and autumn (Mid September – November) but you can do the trek throughout the year.

Mardi Himal Treks is a customizable trek, so it is quite affordable than other popular trekking trails and is suitable for all age groups. Depending on the itinerary you plan, the Mardi Himal trek cost also varies.

Expenses should be well managed and it is better to know more before you spend it. There are multiple options you can choose from the packages available and decide which one suits best for you.

title: Trekking in Nepal in May
excerpt: May in Nepal is when summer starts to come. The warmer weather brings the beauty of the lush green forests with it. It is almost monsoon by the end of May in Nepal. Light drizzle is quite refreshing…
html:
May in Nepal is when summer starts to come. The warmer weather brings the beauty of the lush green forests with it.

It is almost monsoon by the end of May in Nepal. Light drizzle is quite refreshing but is not bothersome.

One of the best reasons for trekking to Nepal in May are the mountain expeditions held at the base camps. With that in a notice, you might get a chance to visit some of the popular climbers from all over the world.

May is one of the best seasons for mountain expedition and also for trekking. You can trek during this pre-monsoon month and have one of the best times here. The views are clearer at the higher elevations and the availability of accommodations are quite frequent.

The weather is humid even at the higher elevations so you can pretty much trek with only a T-shirt on. But it is best if you dress in layers. The mountain weather is quite unpredictable so you need to trek prepared with the layer of clothing with warm dresses as well.

Basic rain gear should keep you dry. Also, it is better if you start trekking earlier in the morning than in the latter half of the day.

Other than that, the atmosphere is vibrant and beautiful with blooming Rhododendrons. There are lots of different options to choose from where you want to trek to. All the accommodations will also be available for trekking in this month of May.

Highlights of Trekking in Nepal in May

  • Best time for mountain expeditions
  • Lesser crowds
  • Easy accommodations
  • A unique experience of trekking in monsoon
  • Warmer weather
  • Can trek with less packing because of summer
  • Wide options of trekking destinations
  • Easy access to trekking permits
  • Vibrant and beautiful atmosphere
  • Stunning view of newly blossoming flowers and greenery

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Weather while Trekking in Nepal in May

Nepal has a diverse topography so there are differences in weather according to the location. Since it is the end of spring and monsoon is just around the corner, the significant heat could bring rain.

As for the temperature, it is above 25 degrees in the day and around 8 degrees at night at the elevation of 2,500 m Also, the temperature differs and decreases as you ascend. The highest temperature is 30 degree and the lowest 0 degrees or less.

Also, because May is a shoulder month it has both the qualities of early summer and late spring. But, frequent hail showers, thunderstorms, and rain can also occur.

Nonetheless, you will have a memorable trekking experience.

Accommodations while Trekking in Nepal in May

The accommodations are easily available throughout the month. Also, the popular trekking trail gets less crowded.

You can also find restaurants and tea houses at their full service. There are also a variety of meals that you can choose from.

No food goes to waste or get stocked because it is still peak trekking season. So restaurant owners do bring in a variety of food choice.

However, pre-booking is still necessary. This saves you from a lot of hassles caused due to uncertainty.

Travel Essentials while Trekking in Nepal in May

The travel essentials consist of different things as compared to other regular trekkings. Of course, you will need all your regular trekking gears but the pre-monsoon calls in for a bit of preparation against the rain.

Nepal has three regions as mentioned, so layering is very important in clothing. You can take the clothes off when hot and put it back on when cold. Make sure you also invest in a pair of good trekking boots.

The weather is warmer and doesn’t require heavy packing. It will keep you on a safe side just in case any rain was to come.

The jackets you choose can be windproof and rainproof. You will also wear another layer of clothing, preferably fleece, for higher elevations.

The most basic and important essentials for trekking in May are as follows:

  • Trekking boots
  • Trekking trousers, jackets, etc.
  • A water bottle
  • A trekking pole
  • First aid kits
  • Personal hygiene items and toiletries
  • Rain jacket/coat
  • Rain cover for your backpack
  • Extra socks, inner wears, etc.
  • A light sleeping bag or a sleeping bag liner

Best Treks in Nepal in May

Given below are some of the best treks you can enjoy in Nepal during May.

Everest Base Camp Trek

Everest Base Camp Trek is a moderate trek. Mount Everest is definitely the main attraction of the EBC trek.

May is an excellent time for mountaineering expeditions. So a lot of Everest expedition teams assemble around the Everest Base Camp. If you are lucky you might get to interact with them and learn about their experiences.

The warmer temperature makes the trekking easy. The trails are clear with no snow hence the trekking is easy. Sagarmatha National Park and the enchanting Buddhist monasteries are other highlights.

Also, the world’s most beautiful mountain, Ama Dablam is also visible on the way.

Acclimatization at Namche Bazaar will make your trek a lot easier. The forests come alive and so does the rhododendron in the higher altitudes.

Making a way from Lukla to Namche Bazaar, you will see the vegetation and the local Sherpa community. Khumbu Glacier and Kala Patthar add a unique feature to the trek. The monasteries at Tengboche portrays the cultural aspect of the trek.

Annapurna Circuit Trek

Annapurna Circuit Trek is another trekking that anyone can enjoy at the most. The highlight of May is that it is a popular month of this trail for trekking.

About 20% of visitors visit Annapurna Circuit every year on the month of April to May.

The trek starts from Besisahar in Marshyangdi River and ends up in Kali Gandaki gorge. It is also the deepest gorge in the world.

Thorong La Pass is the highest and the most challenging point in the trek. But this point gives you the most majestic view.

You will see different mountain ranges of the Annapurna region from ABC. The majestic view of the Dhaulagiri, Manaslu, Nilgiri, Machhapuchhre, etc. is visible.

This trek is very ideal for May and starts from the lowland area of elevation 800 m Also, there won’t be any snow in Thorong La pass making the trek easier.

You can witness the wide species of birds and animals in the Annapurna Conservation Area. And the accommodations include delicious local food and apple pies. May also brings a lot of greenery and the valleys are clear with wonderful views.

Manaslu Circuit Trek

Manaslu Circuit Trek trek introduces you to the isolated Himalayan foothills on western Nepal. You will walk across the remote villages and patches of settlements to witness the world’s 8th highest mountain, Mt. Manaslu.

This trek is quite difficult and hence, demands fitness training and preparations.

In May, the highest temperature for Manaslu Circuit Trek can be 25 degrees and the lowest of 5 degrees. The trek starts from Arughat to Besi Sahar after passing over Larkya La Pass.

The tea houses at Dharamshala is another highlight. Gurung community will add to an adventurous and unforgettable trek. The temperature at day is 20 degree and the views are very clear.

If you want, you can also walk past Tsum Valley, the hidden valley of Buddhism. On the way back home, you will go through many waterfalls, rivers and lush forest that adds beauty in the trek.

Langtang Valley Trek

Langtang Valley Trek is one of the closest treks on the north of Kathmandu.

You will walk through Rhododendron, pine trees, and the bamboo forests. You will also pass through Langtang National Park which is one of the specialties of the trek. You can spot animals like red panda, langur, snow leopard, musk deer, bear, etc.

On exploring the Langtang Valley you will pass through the Yala Cheese Factory before you reach Kyangjin Gompa. From Kyangjin-Ri, you can see the view of Langtang and the other Himalayas.

The views include mountains from the Langtang Himalayan Ranges. You can see mountains like Langtang Lirung, Ganchhenpo, Dokpu, Naya Kangri, Yala peaks and more. You can also see Mt. Ganesh, Mt. Manaslu and Jugal Himal as well.

The trek is quite accessible and short which is suitable for family with children too.

The temperature will be warm and the trails are clear and open for this trek in May. The highest temperature can be around 25 – 30 degree and the lowest can be 0 degrees.

You will also see some of the finest Buddhist heritages including Kyanjin Gompa monastery (3,740 m). The Tibetan lifestyle influences the living style because the locals have more connection to Tibet.

Upper Mustang Trek

Upper Mustang or the forbidden kingdom is one of the top trekking destinations in Nepal. It is a rare privilege to enter the valley. The place borders with Tibet and has Tibetan influence as well.

Having the influence of Tibet from the north, the cultures are similar. Upper Mustang culture and local dialects resemble that of Tibet.

Upper Mustang is home to Lo-Manthang. Lo-Manthang is the capital of Mustang and the only walled city in Nepal. The locals are Loba people.

You need a special permit to trek to Upper Mustang because it is a restricted area in the Himalayas.

At the end of the valley, a 2000-year-old cave is absolutely mystical and magical. You will pass through the beautiful villages of Mustang. You can learn the mystical culture and ancient traditions too.

After a short flight to Jomsom from Pokhara, you will make your way to the Kagbeni Village. The culture, language and the natural diversity of the village will make you feel like you are somewhere different.

From Kagbeni, you will head towards Lo Manthang. Lo Manthang had a monarch until recent times. You can still witness the Lo Manthang palace.

You can walk through the trails of Mustang passing many Buddhist shrines and monasteries. And you will also pass Muktinath temple, Vishnu Temple, and Jwala Mai.

You can also camp beneath the stars for a better view of the sky at night.

Poon Hill Trek

Poon Hill is one of the shortest treks you can take for the most spectacular view of the mountains up close. This is one of the best options for short treks in Nepal and everyone can do it from kids to adult.

On the way, you will witness the local Magar community in the village of Ghandruk. You will also see and enjoy the simplicity of their lives and also Ghandruk museum.

The Poonhill trek includes the view of beautiful waterfalls, scenic beauty of the forest and the mountains all the time. This aspect adds a feeling of calm and serenity throughout the trek. You can have a relaxing journey for the entire trek.

It is best to hike in the mornings to catch the sunrise hitting the peak of the mountains. The main highlight of Poonhill is the magnificent views of the mountains in sunrise and sunset.

The golden peak of the mountains visible from Poon Hill is extraordinary. You can witness the mountains like Annapurna II, Annapurna South, Himchuli and Machhapuchhre.

The trip starts from Pokhara where the views are already visible. But the best part is you go closer to the peaks and experience the soft mountain air that soothes your soul.

It is a pretty short trek and requires no trekking experiences. It is also easy and pretty much possible all year through.

Conclusion

May is the season highly suitable for trekking and it will give you nothing but an experience to cherish for a lifetime. Mountaineers’ expedition to different trekking destinations, May has wide options to choose from.

The weather is warm, the air is refreshing and the feeling will be nothing but relaxing.

Also, without any busy trail and lots of accommodation choices, this is the season to spend your holidays in a very satisfying way.

title: Annapurna Base Camp in April
excerpt: April is one of the best seasons for the Annapurna Base Camp Trek. Depending on your preference and convenience, you can complete treks to Annapurna Base Camp in April in about 10 – 12 days. April is…
html:
April is one of the best seasons for the Annapurna Base Camp Trek. Depending on your preference and convenience, you can complete treks to Annapurna Base Camp in April in about 10 – 12 days.

April is spring in Nepal and the weather is perfect for trekking to Annapurna Base Camp. The views are crisp and clearly visible at this time and everyone loves spring. The environment is green and bright with blooming rhododendron. It is the best time of the year to spot species of birds and butterflies.

The route starts from Kathmandu to Pokhara through a 25-30 minutes flight. You can also choose a 7-hour bus ride if you want to enjoy the journey a little more. After Pokhara, you will head to Ghorepani followed by Chhomrong.

After Chhomrong, you will reach the Annapurna Base Camp. Annapurna Base Camp is about 40 km northeast of Nayapul.

Annapurna Base Camp in April is absolutely pleasant and affordable. And the friendly and welcoming people add to making your journey more interesting. The geographical, cultural and ethnic diversity, is quite unique.

Weather of Annapurna Base Camp in April

The weather is absolutely in your favor during the April trek to ABC. The heat of the sun is moderate and low wind makes it perfect for trekking. Also, the amount of rain and snow is negligible.

You will have the most picturesque view because the views are clearer and most visible.

It is quite cold at the higher altitudes and the weather of the mountains are a bit challenging at times.

The lowest temperature at Annapurna Base Camp in April is -9 degree. The temperature remains about 10 degree during the day and 0 degrees at night.

This is the weather when rhododendron blooms out to kiss the rays of sunshine. You will enjoy the beauty and view of nature.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Highlights of Annapurna Base Camp in April

Picturesque Views

Due to lesser clouds and a suitable spring climate, the views are clear. You could also catch a heavenly sunrise and sunset views from Poonhill.

Moreover, the climatic conditions are moderate and the precipitation is low. Due to this, you will have the scenic view of the mountains. The mountains include Dhaulagiri, Annapurna I, II, IV, Nilgiri, Gangapurna, Lamjung Himal, Manaslu, and others.

You will also pass through Machhapuchre Base Camp on the way to Annapurna Base Camp.

The Ethnic Community and Culture

Nepal is already famous for the varieties of festivals and celebrations. April is when there is Nepali New Year.

What better way to start a new year than at Annapurna Base Camp?

The festivities are an important way of learning about the rich Nepali culture. And the hospitality of the locals will make you feel special and welcomed.

Passing through the villages of Chhomrung, Sinuwa, Ghorepani, Tadapani, Ulleri etc will give you good memories. You will also see ethnic groups like Magar, Gurung, Ghale, and Tamang.

Exploring in the Wild

April also gives you the opportunity to explore the premises of Annapurna Conservation Area. You will be able to witness the biodiversity of the area.

The days are longer so you get more time to explore and wander during the day.

The highest elevation is 4,130 m Rhododendron can be easily found within 1,200 m – 3,600 m You will also witness beautiful cascading waterfalls and river like Modi Khola.

The trails are well managed. You will walk through stone stairs most of the time and the routes are easy to walk and you can enjoy the lush nature.

Travel Essentials for Annapurna Base Camp Trek in April

April is the best time of the year to trek in Nepal. It is neither hot nor cold so the best part of trekking during April is the items of clothing that you have to carry.

You do not need to carry a lot of warm clothes because the weather is already cool. Just a good insulating jacket will do.

Since monsoon is not close, you won’t have to prepare for it too, a simple rain jacket should get the job done. Light clothes are light on your back too.

Some travel essentials you should not miss out on for Annapurna Base Camp in April are:

  • Sturdy Trekking boots
  • Trekking trousers and jackets
  • Extra pair of comfortable sandals
  • Water bottle to minimize buying bottled water, just refill them for a cheaper price.
  • Water purifiers
  • Rain cover
  • Swimwear and sunscreen
  • Personal Hygiene items and sanitizers
  • First aid kit
  • Camera and gears
  • Electric appliances for charging

Best 5 Alternatives of Annapurna Base Camp in April

Annapurna Circuit Trek

Annapurna Circuit Trek is one of the top alternatives to ABC trek in April. This trek is a perfect combination of local culture, natural land, and the picturesque scenery. It is also one of the major routes in the Annapurna region.

Passing through the Marshyangdi River you will reach Manang. The beautiful Gurung community will treat you with all the love during your stay. Thorang-La Pass will lead you to Muktinath and then to Tatopani for the natural hot spring.

Poon hill is perfect for the most majestic view of Annapurna and Dhaulagiri range. You will pass through Ghorepani for this. The 18 days trek will give you the satisfaction of everything in one.

From Poon hill, you go to Nayapul and that is the end. The natural hot springs, the tea house, and the religious Muktinath temple are all in this trek.

Highlight

  • Chance to experience the local culture in Manang
  • Natural hot springs
  • Wide panorama of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges
  • Thorong-La Pass, the highest point of Annapurna Circuit Trek
  • Muktinath Temple

Annapurna Panorama Trek

The Annapurna Panorama Trek is of 10 days. This short trek is especially for the panorama of the beautiful mountain ranges. The snow-capped mountains will look gorgeous and the season is perfect to have a clear view.

The journey begins from Nayapul. You will trek through the beautiful Ghandruk village. The Gurung community are something that you will see widely in this trek.

Mountains like Annapurna I, Annapurna III, Annapurna IV, Dhaulagiri, and Machhapuchhre are visible. From Poon hill, you will see the entire panorama in front of your eyes.

Along the way, you will find the wonderful sight of rivers, hills, and villages. You can also spot rhododendrons in the forests.

Highlight

  • Short trek
  • Surrounding full of many rivers, hills, and greenery
  • Wondrous views of snow-capped mountains
  • Beautiful Gurung community

Tilicho Lake Trekking

On the height of 4,920 m, Tilicho Lake is the highest lake in the world. The route to Tilicho lake is filled with Buddhist Community which links with Annapurna Circuit.

Follow the trails of Marshyangdi River and pass through Dharapani, Manang, and Khangsar. With the adventurous trek through Khangsar, you will reach to Tilicho.

Tilicho Lake Trekking includes a frequent change in climate. And there is a risk of altitude sickness as well. Proper physical exercise is a must and proper hydration during the trek is important.

On this trek, you will cross through Thorung La Pass to reach Muktinath. You will enjoy the view of Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges along the way.

Relax in Pokhara at the end on this 17-day trek.

Highlight

  • Highest Lake in the world
  • Opportunity to experience the Buddhist community
  • Route links with Annapurna Circuit
  • View of Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain range
  • Visit Muktinath

Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek

Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek is a short and easy trek of 8 days. Despite the short trek, you will be able to see the Annapurna range very close.

The views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna I, Machhapuchhre, Nilgiri, Annapurna South, Annapurna II, Annapurna III, and Tukuche are spectacular.

Making your way through Modi Khola, you trek towards Birethati from Nayapul. You will make your way to Poon Hill through Ghorepani.

The golden light on the top of those snow-capped mountains is amazing when the sun rises and sets.

You will walk your way back to the beautiful Gurung village, Ghandruk. You can also see Mt. Annapurna and Mt, Machhapuchre clearly from here.

Highlights

  • Easy and short
  • Beautiful sunrise and sunset
  • Many beautiful rivers and villages on the way
  • Gurung community in Ghandruk

Ghalegaun Home Stay Trek

Ghalegaun Home Stay Trek is famous for the exploration of Gurung habitats. The journey will take you on a closer view of the Gurung community. Their way of celebrations and programs will make you feel like a family.

When it comes to Annapurna, the view is clear and crisp. April makes the time perfect to enjoy the scenic beauty and enjoy the Gurung culture. They will show their authenticity in traditional attire as well.

From Samba Chhyoling Gompa to Uttar Kanya Temple, you will find richness in culture in simple ways.

Highlights

  • View of Annapurna Massif
  • View of Annapurna range, Lamjung, Ganesh Himal and Manaslu
  • Closer look on Gurung community
  • Local cultural programs

Last Say

You can enjoy Annapurna Base Camp in April displaying clear views and warm weather.

The beautiful forests, plants, and animals add another zeal to the trip. The local people and their way of living present simplicity in the finest way possible.

You can also enjoy a lot of other alternatives than the Annapurna Base Camp trek. No matter which path it is, the journey is worthwhile.

title: Trekking in Nepal in April
excerpt: April is the second best season for trekking in Nepal. In Nepal, April is spring and the temperature is the most favorable for trekking. Due to this, Trekking in Nepal in April is quite popular and…
html:
April is the second best season for trekking in Nepal. In Nepal, April is spring and the temperature is the most favorable for trekking. Due to this, Trekking in Nepal in April is quite popular and it does attract a lot of trekkers from around the world.

With an end to winter, April brings a clear view of the mountains and the wilderness back to life.

April is the perfect time to travel to Nepal if you are a nature lover. The blooming flowers and the color add a welcoming vibe to the environment.

The color of Rhododendron contrasts best with the white of the snow-capped mountains. You might also spot a wide range of wild birds and rare animals too.

The season is highly popular for trekking, a huge crowd is obvious. Pre-book your treks if you are planning to trek in Nepal in April.

April also includes few of the Nepali festivals and celebrations.

Weather while Trekking in Nepal in April

The weather in April is perfect for trekking in Nepal. The climate is warm in the lower elevation and cold in the higher elevation but quite moderate.

The mornings and evenings of the higher altitude can be a bit colder. But the day is warm and pleasant. The days are longer and soothing for a relaxing trek.

Over 3,500 m, the temperature can get below freezing point at night. The temperature at 2,000 m is about 20+ degree during the day and about 7 degrees at night.

The high pass routes are snow free and the views are clearer. The warm sun leads to fewer clouds.

Even though the weather is favorable, occasional thunderstorms or rain can occur. The average amount of rain in April is 57mm. Make sure you carry a light rain jacket and rain cover.

In Annapurna and Everest region, rainfall is less than 25m and the trails are still good for trekking.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Highlights of Trekking in Nepal in April

Clear Views and Easy Trails

One of the main reason why April is famous in Nepal for trekking is the weather of the time. The views and the skies are very clear during this season. You will be able to see most of the mountain ranges of the Himalayas.

Mountains from Annapurna region, Everest region, Machhapuchhre region, etc. can be visible. No matter which trekking route you choose, the visibility is majestic.

The paths are best for trekking purpose. This season, the snow clears off and the walks will be easier.

Scenic Views with Natural Treasure

Whether it’s aerial sightseeing or trekking, the scenes will have you mesmerized. Himalayan ranges of the Annapurna region, Everest region, Manaslu region includes spectacular mountains. Some are Annapurna, Machhapuchhre, Everest, Nilgiri, Dhaulagiri, Makalu, and Ama Dablam.

The forests are more lush and green this season. This makes the vegetation of Nepal more vibrant and beautiful. Rivers,lakes, and waterfalls will refresh your mind and soul during the trek.

Festivals, Cultures, and People

Festivals like Buddha Jayanti is in April. Holi is also another festival that people celebrate. The color of joys and friendship will keep you tied to the bond for an entire lifetime. Not to forget, Nepali New Year is in April too.

Wide Options for Treks

April is a perfect season for trekking and visiting Nepal. All the aspects are in favor of trekking this season. But the best part is you have multiple options to choose your route of trekking.

The top trekking destinations are from Annapurna and Everest region. Shorter treks include Poon Hill trek, Mustang trek, and more.

Easy Availability of Permits

Unlike any other season, April invites people from around the world. Many trekkers choose the peak seasons so it becomes quite crowded which is why pre-booking is important. Despite the crowd, you will get the trekking permits easily.

You can easily have access to the permits in the entrance gates or in Nepal Tourism Board Office, or TAAN office.

Tips and Essentials for Trekking in Nepal in April

There are certain tips for a successful and enjoyable trekking experience.

  • It is beneficial if you involve in physical fitness before the trek to make the journey easier.
  • While trekking, it is very important to keep yourself hydrated to fight altitude sickness. Also, take frequent rests during the trek.
  • For clothing, it is important to dress in the layer. The lower elevation will be warmer whilst the higher elevation will be colder. The temperature also depends on the unreliable high weather.
  • It is always best to trek is with a professional guide and hire a potter, especially in the difficult treks.
  • April brings light rain so, bring a light rain jacket and backpack rain cover for extra protection.

Famous Trekking Destinations in April

Annapurna Base Camp Trek

Annapurna Base Camp trek is not only perfect in April but is also one of the easy trekking destinations. You will see different mountain ranges of the Annapurna region from ABC. The majestic view of the Dhaulagiri, Manaslu, Nilgiri, Machhapuchhre, etc. is visible.

You will also pass through the Machhapuchhre Base Camp on the way.

ABC is famous for its awesome teahouses. The trek is also famous for the natural hot springs at Jhinu Danda.

The higher altitude is where the Gurung and Magar settlement is at. The locals’ way of living and working will give you a different feel.

You can witness the wide species of birds and animals in the Annapurna Conservation Area.

Everest Base Camp Trek

With this moderate trek to the Everest Base Camp, you can make the best out of your time in April. The main purpose people visit EBC is because of the view of the highest mountain in the world, Mount Everest.

April is the perfect time for a splendid view of Mount Everest. But the world’s most beautiful mountain, Ama Dablam is also visible on the way. With acclimatization in Namche Bazaar, the trek will be easy.

Making a way from Lukla to Namche Bazaar, you will see the vegetation and the local Sherpa community. Khumbu Glacier and Kala Patthar add a unique feature to the trek.

April makes the view clearer and the weather warmer for this trek. The monasteries at Tengboche portrays the cultural aspect of the trek.

You will encounter protected plants and animals at Sagarmatha National Park. Since April is one of the best seasons, the permits are easily available.

You will also meet travelers from around the world to share experiences with.

Manaslu Circuit Trek

Manaslu Circuit Trek trek introduces you to the isolated Himalayan foothills, preserved areas, and the remote villages. This trek is difficult but with enough exercise anyone can do it.

You will witness the world’s highest mountain Mt. Manaslu. The tea houses at Dharmashala, Gurung community will add to an adventurous and unforgettable trek.

You will also walk past Tsum Valley, the hidden valley of Buddhism. The locals are friendly and treat you with love.

On the way back home, you will go through many waterfalls, rivers and lush forest that adds beauty in the trek of April.

Langtang Valley Trek

Langtang Valley Trek is one of the closest treks from Kathmandu. April makes the valley dry and the humidity is low so the season is perfect for trekking.

The temperature can be between 5 – 10 degree during the day and up to -2 during mornings and night at the Kyanjin Station.

Rhododendron, pine trees, and the bamboo forests will go with you on this delightful trek. You will also pass through Langtang National Park which is one of the specialties of the trek. You can spot animals like red panda, langur, snow leopard, musk deer, bear, etc.

The views include mountains from the Langtang Himalayan Ranges. You can see mountains like Langtang Lirung, Ganchhenpo, Dokpu, Naya Kangri, Yala peaks and more. You can also see Mt. Ganesh, Mt. Manaslu and Jugal Himal as well.

The vision is clearer with the perfect shade of the blue sky.

You will also see some of the finest Buddhist heritages including Kyanjin Gompa monastery (3,740 m). The Tibetan lifestyle influences the local living style because the valley used to be the trade route to Tibet a long time ago.

Makalu Base Camp Trek

The camping trek of Makalu Base Camp is in the eastern region of Nepal. It lies in the area of Makalu Barun National Park and Makalu Barun Conservation Area.

This is a challenging trek but with physical exercise, everyone can do it. April is one of the months which is very good for the Makalu Base Camp Trek. It has five major ecological zones so you will see wide species of rare flora and fauna.

One of the main treasure of this trek is the Makalu Barun National Park in Solukhumbu district. The trial of this trek will take you to the Arun River Valley here. You will reach the Base Camp through Shipton Pass.

You can see the south face of the world’s fifth highest mountain, Makalu. You can also see Mount Everest, Chamlang Himal, and Lhotse.

You will also walk past the Barun Glacier. The lower part of the Barun and Arun valley leads you to the communities of Rai, Sherpa, and Shingsawa farmers. The locals have a very simple lifestyle and are very friendly.

The journey takes you on some of the most remote areas of Nepal. Makalu Base Camp trek is not popular like the other treks because of the inaccessibility. The journey is adventurous and you will enjoy to the fullest nonetheless.

Upper Mustang

Upper Mustang, the forbidden kingdom is one of the top trekking destinations in Nepal. It is a rare privilege to enter the valley. It borders with Tibet and has Tibetan influence as well.

Having the influence of Tibet from the north, the cultures are similar. The people also speak the same language there. Upper Mustang resembles the culture of Tibet as well.

April is a dry season in Mustang so there won’t be the monsoon. In fact, it is best if you start your trek from Lower Mustang in this season. The temperature is warmer in the lower Mustang region.

This time is also perfect if you want to cross higher passes. Due to a warmer temperature, the river will melt in the lower region. The climate and the temperature make it a perfect time to trek to Upper Mustang.

At the end of the valley, a 2000-year-old cave is absolutely mystical and magical.

Moreover, you will pass through the beautiful villages of Mustang. After a flight to Jomsom from Pokhara, you will make your way to the Kagbeni Village. The culture, language and the natural diversity of the village will make you feel like you are somewhere different.

You can learn about their own world and share some story about yours.

From Kagbeni, you will head towards Lo Manthang. Lo Manthang used to have their own king before. But you can still witness the Lo Manthang palace.

To cross Kagbeni you will require a special permit. You can walk through the trails of Mustang with many Buddhist shrines and monasteries. And you will also pass Muktinath temple, Vishnu Temple, and Jwalamai.

Conclusion

The beginning of April brings a pleasant time and surrounding perfect for kindling trekking experiences. Regardless of which route you choose to explore, the journey will be worthwhile.

The trekking in Nepal in April has many offerings that will make the best out of your adventure holiday. The love and warmth of the locals to the cultural richness, there are a lot of aspects to take back home and spring is no doubt the best season.
