title: Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek Cost
excerpt: Ghorepani-Poonhill trek is one of the most renowned short treks in the Annapurna region of Nepal. This trek is perfect for people of all age groups and budget. The total cost of your Ghorepani Poon…
html:
Ghorepani-Poonhill trek is one of the most renowned short treks in the Annapurna region of Nepal. This trek is perfect for people of all age groups and budget.

The total cost of your Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek depends on your choices. It depends on how comfortable and relaxed you want to be during your trek.

You can adjust most of the factors that determine the Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek Cost. This way you can adjust to suit your needs and requirements.

Hence, the Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek Cost can vary depending on the chosen factors.

Cost of Permit for Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek

You need two different permits for Ghorepani-Poonhill trek.

TIMS (Trekkers Information Management System): USD 20 (NRs. 2000).

Every trekker wishing to trek in Nepal must have this permit.

ACAP (Annapurna Conservation Area Entry Permit): USD 28 (NRs. 3000).

In this trek, you will enter the Annapurna Conservation Area. Hence you will need to buy the entry permit to continue this trek. Some of the money from the entry permits go in the conservation of the area and surrounding forest.

Note: Anyone below the age of 10 is not liable to buy ACAP. The locals do not need these permits. Hence, you need not buy these permits for your local staff if you are trekking with any.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Mode of Transportation

Your journey to Nepal usually begins in Kathmandu. Kathmandu has the only international airport in Nepal.

For your Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek, you need to first travel to Pokhara and then to Nayapul where your actual trek begins.

The mode and an average cost of transportation to and from these places are as follows:

Kathmandu-Pokhara-Kathmandu

  • Domestic flights: USD 120 (NRs. 12000)
  • Deluxe bus: USD 7-8 (NRs. 700-800) per person for one way
  • Super Deluxe Bus (Tourist Buses): USD 15-22 (NRs.1500-2200) per person for one way
  • Local Buses: USD 3.5-5 (NRs. 350-500) per person for one way
  • Private Jeeps/Cars: USD 40-60 (NRs. 4000-6000).

Pokhara- Nayapul

  • Public Buses: USD 1-1.5 (NRs. 100-120)
  • Tourist Buses: USD 5 (NRs. 500)
  • Private Jeeps/Cars: USD 20 (NRs. 2000)

The local transportation is always cheaper. It is a unique adventure and experience in itself.

The range for deluxe bus and a super deluxe bus is due to different factors. These factors include the provision of A/C, Wifi, spacious seats, water, towel and so on.

You can rent the private jeeps and cars in different areas or your hotels. You can share the cost of the jeep or car with fellow trekkers/ travelers.

Cost of Accommodation

You will be spoilt for choices while in Kathmandu and Pokhara. You can find 5-star hotels to basic lodges in these places.

Cost for accommodation in Kathmandu and Pokhara: USD 5- 250. This range is due to the wide choices of hotels.

On the trails, you will have limited choices in accommodation. You can choose from the local lodges to the tea houses. Some places along the way also have home stays. The cost of accommodation on the trails does vary. This can be due to the season you choose to trek in and your bargaining skills.

Cost for accommodation on the Ghorepani-Poonhill Trek: USD 3- 5 (NRs. 300-500) per night. Almost all the tea houses offer clean sheets, mattress, pillow, and blanket. You can ask for extra blankets. Hot showers are only available in the more standard lodges.

Cost of Food and Drinks

You get a variety of choices in your meals during your Ghorepani-Poonhill trek. Most of the tea houses along this popular trekking trail offer a blend of traditional local, Asian and continental choices in meals.

The meals are all home-cooked, fresh, hygienic, tasty and healthy. The cost of the food during this trek is around USD 2- 5 depending on where and what you eat.

Staying hydrated throughout your trek is highly recommended. There is a wide range of choices in liquids like green tea, local tea, soft drinks, coffee, bottled water. The price of bottled water can range from USD 0.2- 1.

The price of meals and drinks are slightly more on the trails than in the city. This is due to the remoteness of the trails and the difficulty of transportation. The prices also vary between high and low trekking seasons.

Cost of Activities During your trek

Nepal is famous for many things besides trekking. Nepal is famous for sightseeing, adventure sports, national parks and so on. There are also a variety of things you may or may not want to do during your trek.

Once on the trails, there are many beautiful villages, cultural shows, museums. Or simply, relaxing in one of the villages or in the hot springs along the trails.

Hence, the choices you make on what activities to do or skip can determine your cost of Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek.

Gurung Museum: There is a beautiful museum run by the locals in Ghandruk. It is a traditional museum that presents the art, culture of the ethnic Gurung. Beautiful, traditional dresses, ornaments, household items, pictures are on the show.

You can also see the traditional dresses worn by the local Gurungs. The proud, Gurkhali weapons used by Gurkhas are also on display.

Traditional Costumes and Jewelry center

There is a Traditional Costume and Jewelry Center on your Ghorepani poon Hill Trek. The local Gurung costumes and pieces of jewelry worn are on display.

If you choose, you can also try on the local Gurung dress with the jewelry for pictures. These make great memorabilia to take home. This center is again run by the local.

Kathmandu Sightseeing: Kathmandu, the capital city in Nepal is the city of temples. It is full of beautiful ancient palaces, temples, and stupas. Hence, a sightseeing tour of Kathmandu is a must for any trekker or traveler visiting Nepal.

The average cost of Kathmandu Sightseeing tour is 100- 200. This range depends on places, mode of transport, meals, entry fees included in the tour.

Pokhara Sightseeing: A day of relaxation in the city of Lakes, Pokhara is time well spent. You can enjoy the day by relaxing near the lakes or visit the many popular spots in Pokhara.

Any of the extra activities you wish to get engaged in will add to the total cost of your trek.

Duration of the trek

The average duration of Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek is 8 to 10 days. You can add or reduce the number of days to suit your needs. Each day you spent trekking includes cost- Cost of accommodation, meals, drinks, guide and so on.

Cost of Guide and Porter

Ghorepani-Poon Hill trek is possible with or without a guide or/and porter. It is always safer and recommended to go with a guide and porter.

The Ghorepani Poon Hill trek follows one of the most popular trekking trails in Nepal. Yet, there are places where the trails can get confusing. There are also areas where the trails are not well-maintained. There are also diversions in places. So, it is good to trek with a guide or porter to not lose your way.

A porter can carry anywhere from 15-20 kg. This will help lighten your load. This way you can focus on the trails and enjoy the beautiful trails and landscape.

You can get information about the local flora, fauna, landmarks, peaks from your guide. A guide can also tell you the best tea houses to stay at, the best way to get there, places with the best food. A guide can also help you interact with the locals. A guide can usually speak most of the local languages of the area.

You can hire a professional and licensed Nepali guide with a cost of USD 30- 40 (NRs.3000-4000) per day. The cost of hiring a porter can range from USD 20-25 (NRs.2000-2500) per day.

You also have the option of hiring a porter-guide. A porter-guide does the work of both a guide and porter. A porter guide will carry less luggage. A porter guide is a person who is on the way to becoming a guide.

This will cost less than an actual guide. The cost of a porter-guide is around USD 25- 30 per day.

Average Total Cost

As mentioned above, the cost of Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek depends on your choices on many factors.

An average trek package of Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek costs around USD 450- USD 600.
Further, the season you travel in, the group size also affects the Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek Cost.

Miscellaneous Costs

Some other costs that you need to consider for your Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek are:

Travel insurance

Many of the reputable and good trek and tour companies do not accept trekkers without travel insurance. You need to get travel insurance from your home country. A good travel insurance needs to cover the following:

  • Emergency rescue and evacuation services
  • Treks to foreign countries including Nepal.
  • High altitude treks.

The Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek is an easy level trek. Yet, the risk of high altitude sickness, injuries, sprains, accidents is there. This trek requires walking on rough terrains for 4/6 hours on a daily basis. It is also a high altitude trek.

Having a travel insurance is a great safety precaution for unpredictable situations.

Tipping

Although tipping is not part of the Nepali culture, it is common in all areas related to tourism and hospitality.

Tips are also expected and appreciated for services provided. This includes your guide, porter, waiter, cook, tea house. It is not mandatory. So, you can tip according to the satisfaction you had from their services.

Wi-fi or internet connection

Most of the lodges, restaurants in the lower regions of the trek have free wifi. These are not reliable at all times.

Some places in Ulleri and Ghorepani charge you for using wifi. This can be around USD 1 for a day and so on.

Recharge

Once on the trails, you may have to pay for charging your electronic devices. The electronic devices can include your phone, camera, laptop.

For the cost of USD 1, you can charge your electronics for an hour or two. The cost may differ from place to place.

Souvenirs

Shopping for souvenirs can be an endless journey in Nepal. From handmade, local clothing to carved jewelry, Nepal has something for everyone.

Souvenirs can be a great memorabilia of your trip or something to take home to your friends and family. The cost of souvenirs can start from a few pennies and go a lot higher.

Additional Tips to manage the costs of Ghorepani Poon Hill

  • The costs during the best seasons to do this trek may be more than the non-peak seasons. This can be due to discounts on tour packages, flight tickets, the cost of tea houses, meals and so on.
  • Have enough small denominations of the local currency to last you for the duration of the trek. Cash is the way to go on the trails. ATM’s are few and far between on the trails. These are not reliable either.
  • Most of the tea houses, restaurants and cafes on the trails do not accept cards of any kind. Use your credit cards while in Pokhara or Kathmandu.
  • Bargaining for the cost of your rooms, souvenirs, guide, and porter is acceptable. Remember USD 1 is equivalent to NRs. 115.

Final Say,

The Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek cost depends on a number of factors. Hence, the total cost of your trek depends on your choices on these factors.

The Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek is budget friendly. You can adjust the cost to suit your needs and preference.

The Ghorepani-Poonhill trek is a short and memorable trek to the high altitudes of Nepal. It gives you a beautiful glimpse into the majestic natural beauty and rich culture of Nepal.

If you have any further queries or questions related to trek or tour in Nepal, feel free to contact us.

title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek Difficulty
excerpt: Meta Description: How difficult is the Annapurna Base Camp Trek? The difficulty level of Annapurna Base Camp trek depends on a number of factors. The Annapurna Base Camp trek is one of the most…
html:
Meta Description: How difficult is the Annapurna Base Camp Trek? The difficulty level of Annapurna Base Camp trek depends on a number of factors.

The Annapurna Base Camp trek is one of the most sought after trekking destinations in Nepal. Compared to other popular treks of the Everest and Annapurna region, Annapurna Base Camp Trek is not a difficult trek. It is possible for almost anyone to do this trek. It is accessible to groups of all ages.

Like all treks, the difficulty of Annapurna Base Camp differs from person to person. And, with proper preparation and determination, this can be an easy trek for anyone to do.

The many factors that determine the difficulty of the Annapurna Base Camp trek are as follows:

Duration of the Trek

The average duration of the Annapurna Base Camp is 11 days. You can adjust the number of days of the Annapurna Base Camp trek according to your choice. You are free to extend or reduce it.

This trek requires around 5/6 hours of walking per day for the duration of the trek. An experienced trekker can reach their destination sooner. An inexperienced or novice trekker may take longer.

For experienced trekker, you can reduce the duration of the trek to add to the challenge and thrill. Or you can stick to the average duration for a relaxed and chill experience.

For beginners, the 15-18 days Annapurna Base Camp trek can be ideal. These have good resting days. The duration length will be a great time for the body to adjust to the high altitudes. It reduces the chances of altitude sickness as well as over exhaustion on the trek. This duration allows you to trek more comfortably.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Distance

The Annapurna Base Camp Trek route covers around 115 km. The distance is a short one compared to other popular treks.

You can extend it to include the beautiful and quaint villages along the trails. You will be walking 10 to 20 km each day. This trail is a popular one and hence has signs at different intervals. It is usually packed with trekkers from all over the world. It’s busiest in autumn and spring season.

The trekking trails are well maintained on this trek. Yet, the terrains can be rocky in the mountains. It is more difficult than normal hilly trails. The moraine trails are rocky and have steep slopes at times.

Weather and Temperature

The weather conditions that you encounter during your Annapurna Base Camp trek also plays a vital role. The season you choose helps determine the difficulty level of your trek as well.

Nepal enjoys four distinct seasons. Depending on the seasons, your trekking experience and difficulty may differ.

Autumn Season: October and November

This is the best season to do Annapurna Base Camp trek. With moderate and stable weather conditions, this is a peak trekking season of Nepal. The average temperatures of 12-18 degrees Celsius make for warm and bright days.

The crystal clear skies with least chances of rain add to the comfort of the trekkers. The trails are at their best condition. After the monsoon, the dust will have settled as well.

Spring Season: February through April

For those who enjoy the blossoms of flowers and active wildlife, this season is the best. The flora and fauna in the Annapurna region are at their best in Spring. You can see colorful landscapes of blossoming local flowers and lush green forest.

The chance of rain and snow is also less. There are also fewer crowds than autumn. The temperatures are also a warm 18-22 degrees Celsius. It is a comfortable time of the year to trek ABC.

Monsoon: May through August

For novice trekkers, this season is a poor time to trek. It can be a great challenge for the experienced trekkers. With muddy and slippery trails, this season provides extra thrill and challenge. You will also encounter some pests problem like mosquitoes, leeches.

Winter: December and January

Winter is another challenging season for trekking in Nepal. For those who don’t mind snowfall and freezing cold weather, this season can be great. You can enjoy the majestic views of snowcapped mountains on the trek. Winters no doubt add to the Annapurna Base Camp trek Difficulty.

Annapurna Base Camp Trekking Grade

It is a moderate level trek on the difficulty scale. Everyone and anyone can enjoy this trek. The experience of a professional trekker and a novice trekker will be different. Professional or experienced trekkers might find this to be easy.

Yet for the novice trekker, this trek might be a challenge. With simple and basic fitness training, a novice trekker can change the level of difficulty of this trek.

Type of trekker

Depending on the type of trekker you are, you can adjust the preparation, duration to change the difficulty level. For experienced and professional trekkers, the Annapurna Base Camp trek can be a short and easy trek. A physically active person with no experience may find the Annapurna Base Camp strenuous.

Walking at high altitudes is more demanding than walks at low altitudes. Every human body reacts differently to the altitude. Depending on your body, you may need to adjust the duration of the trek. Do not choose a rapid trek if you don’t have any high altitude experience.

The experience of Annapurna Base Camp trek of a physically inactive person will be different from the above two. The difficulty level of this trek can seem extreme for such a person.

Such a person needs to have the right physical fitness training for a comfortable and safe Annapurna Base Camp Trek.

Choose a duration or itinerary that has enough rest days, acclimatization period.

Physical Fitness and Training

Annapurna Base Camp is one of the most reliable treks in Nepal. The trails are not so steep nor too difficult. Depending on the type of trekker you are, the physical training may differ. For a professional and seasonal trekker, this is an easy trek. As such, minimum training and physical preparation should suffice.

For a physically active person, a month or two of training and preparation is enough. Annapurna Base Camp trek is a high altitude trek. The altitude will affect everyone differently. You will need to train to improve your core muscles, flexibility, and endurance. This helps to reduce the effects of high altitude treks like these.

For a novice and physically inactive person, 3-4 months of prior training should be best. You need to be able to comfortably walk 5/6 hours a day on rough terrains. For this, you need to build your core muscles, leg muscles. You also need to do cardiovascular and strength training.

If possible, you should take actual hikes to nearby hills. This gives you actual training on walking on rough terrains for extended periods. Being physically prepared for your trek allows for a comfortable and safe trek. You can freely enjoy the experience instead of being sore and bitter the whole way.

Trail

The Annapurna Base Camp is one of the most popular treks of Nepal. It is a well-maintained trail. Yet, the trail is definitely not a straight nor a smooth one. The first few days involves a lot of uphill trekking. This can be challenging for some. The upward and downward slopes are the challenging parts of the trails.

You need to focus on the trails. The trek itself is not strenuous. Being physically fit and maintaining a healthy diet will help in reducing the Annapurna Base Camp trek difficulty.

This is an 11-24 day trek. You will need to walk 5/6 hours for most of these. This trek is more difficult than traveling on a smooth, low altitude trail. The trails along with the altitude of the trails will consume a lot of energy. Hence, you will need stamina and endurance to overcome the monotonous and steady up and down movement.

Altitude Sickness

You will be trekking to an altitude of 4,130 m on this trek. It is not as high as some of the other popular treks in Nepal. Yet, altitude sickness can and do occur on this trek as well. Being pre-informed about altitude sickness helps you to notice any symptoms. It also helps you take proper precautions.

Having enough rest days and keeping yourself hydrated throughout the trek helps reduce the risk of altitude sickness. Maintaining your own pace also helps. You should keep your health and safety as a priority on the trek.

Budget

Budget is another important factor that determines the difficulty of a trek. Longer packages cost more and shorter packages cost less. Yet, longer packages allow for great periods of relaxing, acclimatization and slow pacing. This allows for greater comfortability. It also reduces the chances of high altitude ailments making the trek less difficult.

Shorter packages are tightly scheduled. They are best left to the professionals and seasonal climber. These leave less room for rest and acclimatization days and proper pacing. The risks are slightly higher on shorter packages. If possible, do not compromise on the acclimatization days. This will increase the risk of high altitude ailments along with mental exhaustion.

For people who don’t care about the budget can skip the trek and opt for a helicopter tour. Or else choose the luxury Annapurna Base Camp package. You will have single rooms, duration, and itinerary of your choice, personal guides and so on.

Trekking Gears, Clothing and Supplies

Make sure you go through the packing list for Annapurna Base Camp Trek. Packing can be a challenge in itself. Not having the right equipment and supplies can be troublesome. You will not find everything you need for the trek on the trails. Hence, packing all the required gears and supplies is essential.

While packing, make sure to include both light, warm weather clothes and thick, woolen clothes. The unpredictable weather makes sure you require both types of clothing. Having the right clothing ensures a comfortable trek.

Having the right shoes is the key factor. A good pair of shoes can make or break your trek. Make sure you break into your shoes before your actual trek. A new or uncomfortable pair of shoes can lead to blisters, sense of discomfort, slips and injuries.

The right gear also helps to make the trek more comfortable and easy.

Equipment like trekking poles can also be great to reduce Annapurna Base Camp Trek difficulty. It provides the right support and necessary balance. It can be great for descents and the steep stairs. It helps reduce the stress on your knees. Hence, good preparation makes Annapurna Base Camp Trek a lot easier.

Conclusion

The Annapurna Base Camp trek is perfect for all types of trekkers. Anyone with the right mindset and a little bit of training can do this trek.

The Annapurna Base Camp trek is one of the most well-rounded treks. It gives you a glimpse into the rich diversity of culture, lifestyle of Nepal. Along with this, it offers majestic views of some of the highest mountains in the world.

Annapurna Base Camp trek also provides you the opportunity to choose the difficulty level. With your choice of the many factors, you can personally determine the difficulty level of your trek.

The Annapurna Base Camp trek provides a lifetime of memories. If you have any further queries, questions about this trek, feel free to contact us.

title: Everest Base Camp Training Plan
excerpt: Treks to high altitudes like the Everest Base Camp trek do require prior training. You will be trekking to altitudes of 5,364 meters during this trek. And the distance of 130 km. You must have…
html:
Treks to high altitudes like the Everest Base Camp trek do require prior training. You will be trekking to altitudes of 5,364 m during this trek. And the distance of 130 km. You must have physical training along with mental determination to complete this trek.

An Everest Base Camp trek is highly sought out for many reasons. You will be trekking to the base camp of the highest mountain in this world, Mt Everest.

Reaching the Everest Base Camp gives you a great sense of accomplishment. You will enjoy the majestic beauty of the region and get a close look at the rich culture of the nation, Nepal.

To get the most out of your adventure to the beautiful Everest region, you must have a plan. A schedule that will train your body to prepare for the trek. Our body needs to be in a state where it does not feel stressed or drained.

This is why an Everest Base Camp Training plan is a must.

This includes both physical and mental conditioning. Let us guide you through.

Physical Conditioning

There is no single physical exercise routine that works for all. You need to find one from the options that work for you.

For a successful trek, choose a training program that focuses on stamina, endurance, and flexibility training.

Some of the popular ways to become fit are as follows:

Cardiovascular Training

Physical fitness training with any type of cardiovascular conditioning is good for your body. Keep this in mind when planning for the Everest Base Camp trek. Cardiovascular training is also called aerobics training.

Cardiovascular training works on the ability of the heart and lungs to supply oxygen-rich blood. This is necessary for the muscles during a sustained physical activity. This ability is a great help for high altitude treks.

The aerobic training helps ensure you can trek for long periods of time.

The best and easiest ways to do this is by going on walks, runs, hikes and jogs with a backpack.

Make sure the weight you are carrying is like the one you intend to carry on your actual trek.

If these are not for you, you can walk inclines on your treadmills. After a few days, start doing these with a backpack.

Other great options for these exercises are rowing, swimming, cycling. These aerobic exercises help stimulate your heart and breathing rate.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Strength Endurance Training

Strength and Endurance training is also great for the Everest Base Camp Tour.

For a comfortable mountain trek, you need to focus on building strength on your legs, upper, and lower body. It not only makes your trek a comfortable and enjoyable one but will also reduce the risk of injury.

To strengthen your lower body, you can try doing lunges, squats, and step aerobics.

To strengthen your core muscles, you can do sit-ups, sings, shoulder press, back and shoulder flies.

This will help become stronger. You can then carry your backpack (comfortably) which may weigh up to 15 kg while trekking.

Trekking Conditioning for Everest Base Camp

While training for your Everest Base Camp trek, you need to try to replicate the situations of your actual trek.

Nothing does this better than going on actual treks. If possible, go for weekend treks to nearby hills.

Make sure you do these practice treks with boots, clothes, backpacks that you plan on wearing on your Everest Base Camp trek. This will also ensure all the equipment is well-broken in. You will also get comfortable using them on the actual trek.

This helps you to build endurance. These practice treks also help you to get used to walking for long periods of time.

If you cannot go on these treks regularly, mix these small treks with aerobic and strength conditioning training. This will help you prepare for the trek.

Altitude Training

There is no true way to train for altitudes. The only way you can do this is by going to high altitudes.

If that is not an option than the best thing for this is getting your body in top physical condition.

Maintaining your own walking pace is also key for this. Your body will adjust to the altitudes of the Everest Base Camp. This requires time. You cannot rush it.

Always stick to your own pace. Trek slow and steady.

If you feel unwell during the trek, notify your guides or trek doctor immediately. Monitor your symptoms carefully.

Altitude sickness is serious yet avoidable. It can affect people of all fitness level and ages.

Mental Conditioning

Mental toughness plays a huge role in the success and comfort of your trek.

Any treks like the Everest Base Camp trek requires you to concentrate on the trails. Your focus helps you avoid injuries.

You also may face different weather conditions. The weather in high altitudes could be challenging at times. You may face conditions of rain, snow, wind, dust and so on.

Along with this, you will be walking daily for 6/7 hours. This can take a mental toll on you. Hence, being mentally prepared for Everest Base Camp trek is vital to your comfort and success.

Things to consider before you start your Everest Base Camp Training Plan

Trails

Research about the trail you intend to take. There are many trails to Everest Base Camp. Some are more difficult than others. It will be easier to replicate the conditions of the trails and train accordingly.

Trekking boots

Use the boots you plan to use on the actual treks for your physical training activities. If you don’t have trekking boots, buy a pair. Break into them before your actual trek.

You don’t want to end up in blisters or sense of discomfort on your feet during the actual trek. A good pair of trekking shoes can make a huge difference on your Everest Base Camp trek.

Your Physical fitness level.

If you are not involved in any physical activity, then you can start a sensible training program for six to twelve months in advance.

If you are already involved in physical activities, then you can start training 1 or two months before your actual trek. The physical activities you do can be anything like running, swimming, cycling.

Determining how fit you are can help decide how early you should start getting trained for your Everest Base Camp trek.

Diet

You need a well-balanced diet to help maintain a good health. Don’t ignore your nutrition. When your physical fitness routine picks up and you train harder, your body places more strain on your carbohydrate stores.

Make sure you take your diet into consideration while training. Make sure to eat and drink well.

Season

Autumn (September-November) and Spring (February-April) are the best seasons for trekking in Nepal.

These seasons offer dry, clear weather along with moderate temperatures. They are perfect for treks.

Summer (June-August) and Winter (December-January) are challenging for treks. The trekking trails will be muddy and slippery during these seasons due to the rain and snow.

The temperatures can also be too hot or cold.

Reason for Everest Base Camp Training Program

  • Strengthens your heart, reducing the risk of heart attack and stroke
  • Improves breathing, circulation, and endocrine functions
  • Tones your muscles
  • Strengthens your bones and reduces the risk of osteoporosis
  • Helps you get in shape
  • Boosts mental performance and improves psychological well-being
  • Reduces anxiety
  • Complete enjoyment during your trek

Extra things to remember while training for your Everest Base Camp trek

  • The best way to get fit for your Everest Base Camp trek is to train hard and well
  • Do not rush. Always stick to and maintain your own pace
  • Always stretch before and after workouts for 5-10 minutes
  • Drink plenty of fluids. These can include 3-5 liters of water and juice depending on your body weight
  • Eat a well-balanced diet with lots of green vegetables and fruits
  • Reduce your training a week or two before your actual trek

Final Say

Everest Base Camp trek is possible for all. But an Everest Base Camp training Plan helps in making your treks are a lot easier. It allows your body to be flexible in order to face the actual situation.

This way, you can have a great time on your trek.

Everest Base Camp is an incredible trekking destination. Make sure you prepare well for a great and comfortable trekking experience.

For the best routes and seasons for the Everest Base Camp trek, feel free to contact us.

title: Everest Base Camp Weather in Autumn (September, October and November)
excerpt: The autumn season is among the best season to trek anywhere in Nepal, including treks to Everest Base Camp. After the hot and rainy summer, nature comes alive for the fall season. You can enjoy…
html:
The autumn season is among the best season to trek anywhere in Nepal, including treks to Everest Base Camp. After the hot and rainy summer, nature comes alive for the fall season. You can enjoy perfect and stable weather conditions. Trekkers can have a great and adventurous time on the trails.

A trek to the base camp of Mt. Everest, the tallest mountain the world is a destination not to be missed. The trek gives you the chance to explore the beautiful village life and culture of the world famous ‘Sherpa’ people. Plus, the closer views of the giant snow-covered peaks.

Trek to the EBC is possible throughout the year but it is best to organize your treks during the autumn months. It is that time of the year when the weather will be in your favor. This way you get to enjoy the trek and not worry about the weather-related issues like clothing, gear, and so on. It is always easier this way, isn’t it?

Well, the autumn season lasts for three months in Nepal. Each month have their own unique features. Allows us to guide you through the best these autumn months have to offer.

Autumn Season

Late September, October, and November are the autumn months in Nepal. These months see the most stable weather conditions in the high altitudes of Nepal. You can enjoy the crisp weather during these months.

The temperatures also range from a cool 6-22 degrees Celsius during this season.

The weather conditions of the trails are perfect. You can get a well-rounded trekking experience. And, during this time of the year, you can enjoy the beauty of the trek to its fullest.

Some of the best treks of Nepal is also possible and in high demand in autumn, including the Everest Base Camp trek.

Although the same season, the temperatures and weather conditions do differ slightly between the three months.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Everest Base Camp Trek Weather in September

September is the beginning of the autumn season. You can enjoy the last traces of monsoon in early September.

You may encounter some short bursts of rain during the first two weeks of September. The average number of cloudy days is 8-12 for September. Most of these occur during the first two weeks of the month.

The average temperatures during the first half of September range from 18 to 22 degrees Celsius.

By mid-September, autumn settles in. The average temperatures drop by 3-4 degrees Celsius. The nights are colder. The temperatures can drop to 4 degrees Celsius during the nights.

You can enjoy long, bright days during September. The average daylight hours are 8 during September. You can enjoy the beautiful sunsets from the comforts of the tea houses along the trails.

September is the beginning of the best season for the trek. The number of trekkers is not as high yet. You will get your choice of rooms and tea houses without booking.

You can also enjoy the calm and tranquillity of the trails at your own pace during September.

Highlights of the Everest Base Camp trek in September

  • Opportunity to witness two distinct seasons of Nepal
  • Hundreds of small streams and waterfalls along the way
  • Quieter and less crowded trails, tea houses

Everest Base Camp Weather in October

October marks the best time of the year for trekking in Nepal. It neither has the hang of monsoon not the hint of winter sweeping in. It is just perfect. The weather is neither too cold nor too hot.

It has all the favorable conditions for the best treks in Nepal. The days are warm and bright. October also offers the great visibility.

No wonder October is the busiest month to trek in Nepal. Thus, you may need to book everything in advance. This includes your flights, tea houses, rooms, guides.

With the least chances of clouds, you are almost guaranteed clear skies during October. This means you get great views of the mountain peaks and the landscapes very early on your treks. You can meet like-minded people on the trails.

During October, the average temperature is 12 degrees Celsius during the day. It can drop to -6 degrees Celsius during the night. The average sunshine hour is 6/7 hours per day.

You will be trekking in warm weather while enjoying the great, clear scenery around you. You can also enjoy fabulous sunrise and sunsets during October. No clouds will block your views.

Highlights of Everest Base Camp trek in October

  • Perfect and stable weather conditions
  • The cloudless sky in October gives you an exceptional view of the mighty mountains and surrounding landscape
  • Incredible sunrise and sunset views from the comforts of your tea house

Everest Base Camp Weather in November

November is the last month of the beautiful autumn season in Nepal. The perfect weather conditions of October continues to November as well.

During early November, you can enjoy warm temperature. And the temperature is around 12 degrees Celsius. The average temperature does decrease to 6 degrees Celsius by the end of November. The nights are colder with average temperatures of -12 degrees Celsius.

You can expect similar daylight hours of 6/7 hours per day. The days do get shorter by the end of November. This month is perfect for those who prefer cooler temperatures for treks. The temperatures are neither too warm or too cold.

If you are lucky, you may get to enjoy some light snowfall during the last week of November. Be sure to pack some well-insulated jacket and waterproof boots. This will come handy during your Everest Base Camp trek on the last week of November.

Highlights of Everest Base Camp trek in November

  • Cooler days for comfortable treks
  • Light snowfall during the end of November

Things to consider for Everest Base Camp trek during Autumn

Wind Speed

After you reach the higher altitudes, you must consider the wind chill factor. The average daily wind speed is around 8-11 km/hr (roughly 5-7 mph) in September. You must prepare for this.

Having a good quality windproof jacket, a buff is great. It protects you from getting cold. It is also great to prevent dry skin, throat ailments.

Alternative trails to Everest Base Camp Trek

These three months are the best months to do treks in Nepal. You will see a large number of trekkers, travelers, and climbers on the popular treks in the Everest region like the Everest Base Camp trek.

As Everest Base Camp is one of the best trekking destinations in Nepal, there are many routes to reach this destination. You can avoid the crowds and still reach Everest Base Camp during these months.

Some of the most popular ones are the direct routes to Everest Base Camp. To avoid the crowds try the Jiri-Everest Base Camp trek, Luxury lodge-Everest Base Camp trek.

These are longer and take you off-the-beaten-path. You get to experience the classic Himalayan trekking experience on these routes.

Festivals

Some of the biggest festivals in Nepal occur during the autumn season. The dates of the festivals do vary from year to year. Nepalese follows the Lunar calendar and celebrate different festivals like:

Dashain

This is the biggest festival of the Hindus. It is celebrated throughout the country. Nepalese from all over the world and country return home.

Family gatherings and parties take place. It is a festival that celebrates the victory of the good over evil. The festival spreads its charm for 15 days.

Tihar

The festival of lights, Tihar is a colorful festival. The shops and homes are decorated with colorful rangolis and ferry flights. It is a five-day festival, each day has a unique representation.

Mani Rimdu festival

This is the major festival celebrated by the Sherpa in the Everest region. It takes place in Tengboche Monastery, at 3,867 m The festival celebrates the victory of Buddhism over Bon religion.

You can see the locals of Khumbu region decked in their best enjoying the events of empowerment and religious functions. You can enjoy the masked dances and dramas enacted by the monks of the monastery.

Packing for Everest Base Camp Trek in Autumn

Make sure you do a checklist of your packing essentials for your Everest Base Camp trek in autumn. Do not forget to include suitable gear adjustable for all kinds of weather.

Though the weather is generally clear in autumn, it is always safe to walk prepared. The weather in the Himalayas could change anytime.

Final Say,

The weather and climate of the Everest Base Camp like any other mountain treks are uncertain. They change in every hour. This is a good thing, you will get to experience the varying environment. The only thing you need to consider is the gear that you choose.

Well, the weather during autumn tends to be the most well-behaved. It is quite calm this time of the year and the changes are very small. If you want to be on a safe side, opt for Everest Base Camp during autumn.

title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek Weather in Autumn
excerpt: Timing is everything when you have chosen to do treks in the Himalayas. Annapurna Base Camp Trek is a dream vacation for many trekkers around the world. The easier trails with the moderate climatic…
html:
Timing is everything when you have chosen to do treks in the Himalayas. Annapurna Base Camp Trek is a dream vacation for many trekkers around the world. The easier trails with the moderate climatic conditions make this trek popular among the travelers.

Annapurna Base Camp is doable throughout the year. Depending on the region and the season, weather, and temperature in Nepal vary. As you go higher, the weather changes. Yet, autumn is the perfect time to trek Annapurna Base Camp to feast on the magical sights. The autumn weather in the Himalaya is pleasantly warm, with crisp and clean air.

September, October, and November are the local autumn months in Nepal. These are the best months for Annapurna Base Camp trek.

From these three months, you can choose anyone. Each has a unique flavor and appeal.

Autumn in Nepal

Nepal has 6 seasons. Each last about two months. The six seasons are Spring, Summer, Monsoon (Rainy), Autumn, Pre-winter, and winter.

The 4 popular seasons worldwide are Spring, Summer (monsoon), Autumn (fall) and Winter. Rainy and pre-winter are usually considered as summer and winter respectively.

The autumn season of Nepal falls in the months of September, October, and November.

Moderate temperatures, mild wind, and low precipitation make Autumn a season of wonderful trekking conditions. The weather and temperature do vary between the months.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Annapurna Base Camp Trek Weather  in September

September marks the beginning of the autumn season in Nepal. You can feel the last traces of the monsoon in the early days of September. Occasional short storms and light rainfall can happen a few times during these part of September.

But, it is nothing like the torrential rainfall you may experience during summer (monsoon). Light snow also occurs at high altitudes.

Yet, by mid-September, autumn will make its presence felt.

The monsoon clouds exhaust themselves and dissipate by mid-September. You can enjoy clear skies, with a few, lingering harmless stray clouds. On an average September sees about 12 overcast days. These occur mostly in the early days of September.

By mid-September the weather turns dry and clear. The temperatures range from a warm 12-21 degrees Celsius. The trekking trails are also neither too wet nor too slippery.

You can enjoy long warm days and cool nights during this month. The weather is ideal. It is neither too hot nor too cold.

As September is the beginning of the peak season of Nepal, the number of trekkers is still quite less. You will have the trails to yourself. You can enjoy the magnificence of the landscapes, surrounding and scenery at your own pace. You will not have to rush for anything. You will get your choice of tea houses, rooms during September.

Festivals

Nepal celebrates a wide range of festivals. Every month you can enjoy a different festival. The festivals give you a glimpse of the local culture, tradition, and lifestyle.

Nepal celebrates Teej and Indra Jatra during September. As Nepal follows the lunar calendar, the dates of these festivals do change.

Teej is a beautiful and colorful festival. It is a festival mainly celebrated by the Hindu women of Nepal. You will see the women dressed in their finest on this day. You can see them dancing, singing, and merry-making throughout the day.

The women ask for blessings for a blissful and fulfilling marriage. The single women usually pray for a good and supportive life partner. The women visit the temples and in the queue dance, sing, joke, and mingle with the rest.

Indra Jatra is another great festival celebrated in the Kathmandu valley. During this festival, people worship Lord Indra, the king of the Gods. They thank him for the good monsoon and celebrate him. It is usually celebrated for a week.

Highlights of ABC (Annapurna Base Camp) Trek in September

  • See the nature and wildlife in its full glory. As the monsoon has just passed, the rivers, waterfalls, gorges, lakes are in their full glory. You can see many waterfalls and streams that dry up by October during this month.
  • Stunning views of lush green forests of rhododendron, pine, and bamboo in the lower regions of the trek.
  • Two seasons in one trek. You can experience the diversity of seasons of Nepal on this single trek.
  • Clear days make for amazing visibility. You can see the mountain and landscape scenery at their best in September.
  • Less crowded trails make for comfortable and relaxing pace. You will not have to rush to get the best rooms, a tea house in September.

Annapurna Base Camp Trek Weather in October

Within autumn, October is the best month to do trekking in Nepal. The days are bright and pleasant. The temperatures range between a cool 12-19 degrees Celsius.

On the higher elevations of 1000-3,500 m, the temperatures drop to 5 degrees Celsius at night. October experiences great and stable weather conditions. It also has amazing visibility.

You will get the best out of your trekking experiences this month. From perfect weather to great visibility, this month has all the best conditions for your trek.

As the autumn season settles in, you can enjoy the vibrant colors of gaiety throughout the trekking trails. You can enjoy the changing colors of the forests and flora of the region. The trees in the lower regions turn from their usual green to beautiful shades of yellow and orange. The leaves of the flora turn to different shades of ember, rust and amethyst.

The Annapurna Base Camp trails are dry, colorful and in their top shape during this month. It is also a great time to meet fellow travelers and trekkers. Many great friendships will blossom on these trails.

Festivals

Two of the biggest festivals of Nepal occurs during this month- Dashain and Tihar.

Dashain is the “festival of Victory”. It is a festival of family reunions. Nepalese from all over the world return home to celebrate this festival. It is a festival that brings families together and strengthens the family ties.

Tihar is the “the festival of Light”. You will see many shops, houses decorated and lighted. This is to welcome the Goddess of Wealth, Lakshmi.

Highlights of Annapurna Base Camp in October

  • You can experience the trekking trails in their ideal conditions.
  • Amazing visibility making for great views of the surrounding mountain peaks and landscape.
  • Opportunity to see the locals in their festive mood. An opportunity to take part in the local culture, tradition.
  • Dry and cool weather.

Annapurna Base Camp Trek Weather in November

The great weather conditions of October continues in November. Trekking to Annapurna Base Camp in November is close to perfect for trekkers.

The clean fresh air and mild temperatures of 7-18 degrees Celsius make it a great time to do trekking in Nepal. You will get unobstructed views of the mountain peaks and the surrounding landscapes.

The chance of clouded skies is almost nil in November.

Both the sunrise and sunset views are beautiful with clear skies and the magnificent view of Himalayan ranges. The last few days of November has a few cold days and nights as winter will be arriving soon.

So, you need to prepare accordingly.

Festivals

This is the month of the second biggest festival Tihar and Chhath in Nepal. You get to see the houses of local Tamangs, Brahmins, Chhetris, and other ethnic groups decorated in dazzling lights and colorful garlands.

Highlights of Annapurna Base Camp trek in November

  • Ideal trekking conditions
  • Amazing views of sunrise and sunsets in the mountains.
  • Great, unobstructed views of the surrounding mountain peaks, landscapes, villages.
  • May get to enjoy light snowfall during the last days of November.

Extra tips for your Annapurna Base Camp trek

  • The Annapurna Base Camp trek is an easier trail compared to the Everest Base Camp. This is in terms of altitude, duration, trail conditions, distance.
  • There are a lot of trekking trails to reach the Annapurna Base Camp. Get as much information about them and select one that suits you.
  • Weather up in the mountains, high altitude area, changes drastically. It is best to prepare your gear and equipment for your trek, even if you are going on a perfect best season.
  • Autumn is a peak season. The number of trekkers is quite high during these months. Make sure you book everything in advance to ensure you get your choice of rooms, tea houses, and flights.
  • In early September, chances of rain in the lower altitude is high. So, you should prepare yourself for a bit of muddy and slippery trails.
  • Make sure you pack the appropriate clothing depending on the conditions mentioned above.
  • Do not rush, rather maintain your trekking pace. Always stick to your own pace. This is not a competition. Enjoy it.
  • Always stay hydrated. This helps to keep most ailments at bay.
  • Learn as much as you can about altitude sickness. This is something that can and do happen.
  • Take your favorite light snacks to nibble on during your treks. They are great for boosting your energy and morale.
  • Get information about the weather in Pokhara and Kathmandu as well. You may end up staying overnight at these places.

Highlights of Annapurna Base Camp Trek in Autumn

  • Opportunity to visit two Base Camps in one trek. You will see both the Machapuchare Base Camp and Annapurna Base Camp on this trek.
  • Panoramic views of the whole Annapurna region and Dhaulagiri region. You can see mountains like Machhapuchhre, Annapurna I, II, III and South, Gangapurna, Hiunchuli, and Dhaulagiri.
  • Kaligandaki- the world’s deepest gorge lies on this trek.
  • Natural hot springs on the trails.
  • Opportunity to explore the diverse culture, tradition, and lifestyle of the remote regions of Nepal.
  • Flora and fauna of the regions including rhododendrons, subalpine flowers.
  • Rare opportunity to spot exotic wildlife in the Annapurna Sanctuary.

Final Say

Trekking never stops in Nepal. You can trek throughout the year in Nepal if you choose.

You can choose the season or month based on your preference. Do not choose something because it is ideal on the websites and for other people.

Autumn is a great choice for many reasons. Autumn season sees the dry and clear weather. Along with great visibility, autumn is the ideal time for trekking anywhere in Nepal including Annapurna Base Camp.

The weather in the mountains is unpredictable. Be prepared for the uncertainty regardless of the season you travel in.

title: Best Time to Trek Annapurna Base Camp
excerpt: Nepal is world famous for its many trekking destinations and adventurous trails. It offers treks for anyone and everyone. And you can choose to trek any time of the year, throughout the year. Some…
html:
Nepal is world famous for its many trekking destinations and adventurous trails. It offers treks for anyone and everyone. And you can choose to trek any time of the year, throughout the year.

Some popular trekking trails and destinations lie in the Annapurna and Everest region. Annapurna Base Camp is a popular trekking destination in the Annapurna region. And, Spring and Autumn are considered to be the best time to trek Annapurna Base Camp.

However, with the right preparation and equipment, Annapurna Base Camp trek is possible and doable throughout the year.

The most important thing to know before a trek is to get familiar with the weather conditions of the trails.

Nepal experiences four distinct seasons. The area of Annapurna Base Camp trek is no exception. Let us guide you on deciding the best season for your Annapurna Base Camp trek.

Seasons in and around Annapurna Base Camp

The four distinct season that Nepal experiences are Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter. Here is a brief introduction to these seasons in and around the Annapurna Base Camp area.

Spring

The local spring season is the second best season to trek in Nepal, Annapurna Base Camp included.

Spring falls in the months from March to May in Nepal. The winter ends around mid-February. The days start to get warmer. The weather, climate, and the temperature during spring are just perfect for treks here.

The temperature varies between 17-20 degrees Celsius during the day. The nights and early mornings are slightly colder. In the upper regions of the trek, the weather conditions and temperature do get colder.

The forests in the Annapurna regions start to come alive in spring. The forests and flowers in the lower regions start to bloom. Pink, white, and red blossoms of rhododendrons and wildflowers surround the lower regions of the trails. The surrounding forests of bamboo, pine on the trails are lush green.

You can enjoy the best of nature during this season.

It is also a great time to spot some wildlife like white Langurs, monkeys, Himalayan Tahr, musk deer. And the different species of birds in the forest will amaze you.

During the spring, you can see the beautiful, snow-capped mountains. The bright and dry days and nights make for great visibility. You can also enjoy incredible views of the surrounding landscapes, villages, rivers, and gorges.

This season sees a large number of trekkers and travelers on the trails. This season is great for climbing the high passes in and around the trails of Annapurna Base Camp.

Make sure you pre-book everything. Or else, you may have to struggle for your rooms and meals.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Summer

Nepal has a wet Summer. This season sees warm, humid days along with torrential rainfall and thunderstorms.

The months from June to August are the summer months in Nepal. The areas in and around Annapurna Base Camp are partially affected by this season.

The Annapurna Region lies in the rain-shadow area of the very mountain. This is a major reason why the monsoon does not affect largely in this region.

Most of the tea houses, cafes remain open during this season.

A great thing about the monsoons in Nepal is the timing. It mostly occurs during the late afternoons, evening and nights. The mornings to mid-day is usually dry and sunny.

The temperatures on clear days’ vary between 20-25 degrees Celsius. The lower regions of the treks see higher temperatures of 20 degrees Celsius. You can see the rivers, lakes, waterfalls, streams on the trails in their full glory.

You can enjoy the magnificence of mother nature on the trails during this season. But, if you do not enjoy the rain at all, there are some fantastic trekking trails in the rain-shadow areas of Nepal. Some of the most recommended ones are Upper Mustang trek, Lower Dolpo trek.

The trekking routes are not crowded by trekkers and travelers during this season. This leaves you to decide your own pace. You will have the freedom to explore the trails, choose the best tea houses and meals during your trek.

Autumn

Autumn is the best season to do treks in Nepal including the Annapurna Base Camp trek. Everything about this season is perfect for trekking.

The months of September, October and November is the local autumn season of Nepal. The clear weather makes for amazing visibility.

Awe-inspiring views of the surrounding mountains and landscapes during this season are spectacular. The temperature varies between a cool 15-17 degrees Celsius during the days. It drops slightly during the nights to 7-9 degrees Celsius.

The lower regions of the trails are less dusty. As the monsoon has just passed, the trails slowly start to dry up. The forest, flowers, and wildlife are all lovely and lush. It is a relaxing sight to behold on your treks.

You will also get to enjoy amazing sunrises and sunsets at your rest stops, tea houses, and early morning treks.

Autumn is ideal all around. The weather and temperature are more stable and you can enjoy the long, cool days at leisure.

Being the peak season for trekking, the trails, tea houses, cafes are busy with trekkers and travelers. Make sure you pre-book yours to be on a safer side.

The weather in the upper regions of the trek can change drastically. The clear weather can change into blizzards. So, prepare yourself with proper gear and equipment.

Winter

From December to February, Nepal enjoys winter. Due to the difference in altitude and landscapes, the temperature varies greatly. You can notice this within the same trek in the same season.

The starting part of your journey including Kathmandu and Pokhara sees a cool winter. The temperature ranges between 9-17 degrees Celsius during the days.

From the place where your actual trek on foot begins to your destination, the winter weather condition varies.

It gets colder on the trails leading to Annapurna Base Camp. The mornings and evenings are especially chilly. The temperatures drop to negative degrees Celsius during these times.

The days are slightly warmer with temperatures between 2-6 degrees Celsius. Some of the upper regions of the trek also witness snowfall. Some of the high passes in the region like Thorong La pass is closed for safety regions.

The Annapurna region wears a deserted snowy look in winter. Most of the locals migrate to the lower regions for the season.

But, if you like the cold and the snow, this can be a perfect season for you to trek to Annapurna Base Camp. And with the right preparation, equipment, and supplies, this trek should be spectacular.

You get magnificent views of snow-capped landscapes and mountain peaks. Along with these, you can also see the village houses in the upper regions covered by snow. It makes for wonderful, picturesque Christmas cards.

You will also have the trails for yourself. Most of the tea houses and cafes do close for the season. There are some that remain open throughout the year. Be sure to confirm your booking with your tea houses, cafes in advance.

The tea houses offer you warm fireplaces, blankets, hot water, soup to help combat the cold. Some alpine or mountain climbing experience would be great if you want to climb the smaller peaks or passes in this region during this season.

Shoulder Months

Shoulder months refer to months that fall in-between seasons. February, September, December, and June are shoulder months in Nepal.

You are in for a surprise trek during these months, you may experience some difficult weather conditions. But you will enjoy the best weather conditions within the same trek.

Early February still sees some signs of winter. You may get to enjoy the occasional snowfall in the upper regions of the trek. The temperatures are just starting to rise. So, you may be in for a chilly morning or night during early February.

By Mid-February, spring sets in and you get the full benefits of the spring season.

Some traces of monsoon can be felt during early September. You may encounter the occasional rainfall and thunderstorms.

Autumn finally settles from Mid-September. The temperature and weather conditions start to cool and become more stable. The weather becomes cool, warm and dry.

You can still enjoy the last traces of autumn during early December. Winter has not yet settled. So, the temperature has not reached negative degrees. You can enjoy the trails freely and comfortably during early December.

Early June still sees the lingering spring season weather conditions and temperature.

By May, most trekkers will have left. You can enjoy the quiet and peaceful trails at your own pace in early June. By mid-June, the summer (monsoon) season will have settled.

These months are an adventure in itself. You may see the best and worst of what the season has to offer. The trails to ABC (Annapurna Base Camp) see lesser number of trekkers during these months. If you are up for it, these are great months to do you trek as well.

Festivals

Nepal is a country of diverse culture. Numerous ethnic groups and people of different religious beliefs live here in harmony. This makes a good reason for Nepal to enjoy many festivals throughout the year.

Festivals give you a unique opportunity to explore and indulge in the culture and lifestyle of the locals.

You can witness the local culture to its full glory. The local people come in their finest clothes and jewellery. They celebrate the festivals with songs, prayers, drama, and dance.

The bright and beautiful season of Spring sees the festivals of color ‘Holi’. Nepali New year also takes place during this season.

Some colorful and enjoyable festivals like Gai Jatra, Janai Purnima, and Teej takes place during summer.

  • Gai Jatra is celebrated in memory of their loved ones lost during the year. In modern times, it is also celebrated with parades from the LGBT community of Nepal.
  • Teej is the festival for the women. They dance and fast for a day. They also pray to Lord Shiva for blessings. Single women pray to find a suitable match for themselves.

Autumn is the season of the biggest and grandest festivals in Nepal. Majority of Hindus in the lower regions of the trek celebrate their biggest festivals of the year- Dashain, Tihar during this season. Tihar is the festival of lights. You can see the entire nation in colorful lights.

In winter, you have the opportunity to enjoy a snowy Christmas and New Year in some of the remotest parts of Nepal.

The locals in the Annapurna region also celebrate Tamu Loshar, Gyalpo Losar, Christmas, and Mageshangrati. Losar means New year in the local dialect.

The local Gurung community in different parts of Nepal celebrates Tamu Loshar. the upper regions of the trek like Jomsom, Mustang, Manang celebrate Gyalpo Losar. You can witness the locals decked in their cultural dresses. They visit monasteries and celebrate at their homes, community places.

Highlights of Annapurna Base Camp

  • Immaculate 360 degrees view of spectacular mountain peaks. These include the majestic Annapurna mastiff, Mt. Machhapuchhre (6,993 m), Hiunchuli (6,441 m), Tukuche (6,920 m) and Dhaulagiri (8,167 m).
  • Two base camps in one trek- Machhapuchhre Base Camp and Annapurna Base Camp
  • Beautiful lush green forests of rhododendron, pine, bamboo
  • Opportunity to explore and indulge in the diverse local culture, tradition, and lifestyle of the region
  • One of the more easily accessible treks of Nepal.
  • An easy to moderate level trek- doable and possible for anyone regardless of age, gender, budget.
  • Natural, hot springs- great for relaxing your tired muscles after the trek.
  • Can be modified to include other trekking destinations near the area like Ghorepani, Poon Hill.

Some Extra Tips to Annapurna Base Camp Trek

  • The best season for treks to Nepal including Annapurna Base Camp Trek is autumn and spring. The best month to do this trek is in October.
  • Do not choose a season or month because of its listing on famous trekking websites and blogs. Make your decision based on your own preference and strength.
  • The cool and stable weather conditions are recommended for beginners.
  • Make sure you pack everything essential for a high altitude trek during your ABC trek. The weather conditions are unpredictable on the higher regions of the trek.
  • It is always recommended to trek with guide and porters throughout the year. They will have experience of doing the trek in all seasons. They can help enhance your overall trekking experience.
  • Do not rush your trek. Always maintain your own pace. Relax and enjoy the surroundings and the experience. You are on holiday.
  • It is recommended to pre-book everything if you are trekking during the peak seasons. This ensures that you get the tea houses and rooms of your choice.
  • Learn as much as you can about high altitude sickness. This will be helpful for you as well as your fellow trekkers.
  • Remember to stay hydrated. Staying hydrated is one of the keys for a comfortable and safe trek.
  • The weather conditions of Pokhara and Kathmandu are different from the trekking trails of Annapurna Base Camp. Do not plan your trek to Annapurna Base Camp based on information about the weather conditions of Pokhara and Kathmandu.
  • Make sure to check your trekking gear and equipment before your trek. They will come handy on the trails.
  • Make sure you take a bug repellent in summer. You will come across mosquitoes, flies, and other bugs during this season.
  • Do consult with your doctor before undertaking this high altitude trek.
  • Take some aqua-tabs, gels or steripen. This is a safety precaution against water contamination.
  • Make sure you have a day or two extra for any delays in flight, need to explore the beautiful villages, culture in and around the trails.
  • If possible and for beginners, do put in some physical training before your actual trek.

Final Say,

Annapurna Base Camp trek is an adventurous and exciting trek. Trekking to the base of one of the highest mountains in the world, Mt. Annapurna is absolutely blissful.

It is possible to trek in all the four seasons. You will need proper preparation, training, and equipment for winters and summers. Each season offers its own unique flavor to your overall trekking experience.

The weather in the higher regions of the trek is unpredictable and can change anytime. It is best to be well prepared for it.

Trekkers from all around the world visit Nepal for treks, tours, adventure sports. With some of the most diverse trekking destinations and trails, Nepal will spoil you with its choices.
