title: Best Time to go Trekking in Nepal
excerpt: In this article, we are going to discuss the Best Time to go Trekking in Nepal in a detailed manner. Trekking is an adventure you choose to take. It can be both a short or long trip, usually on foot…
html:
In this article, we are going to discuss the Best Time to go Trekking in Nepal in a detailed manner.

Trekking is an adventure you choose to take. It can be both a short or long trip, usually on foot. It is an opportunity for you to get closer to nature and its beauties. Going for a trek is one of the best ways to forget all your troubles and stress for a while and refresh your mind.

Nepal is well known for its natural beauty, it’s beautiful hills, and magnificent mountains. It is one of the best destinations in the world for traveling and trekking. Thousands of trekkers and mountaineers come to visit Nepal every year especially to trek in the Himalayas.

Numerous trekking routes in Nepal gives you a taste of its cultural and natural diversity. Most of the trekking packages follow an ancient walking route that passes through lovely river-banks, daring suspension bridges, terraced fields, dense forests. The trails connect with several small villages where you can meet people of different ethnic tribes, cultures, religions, etc.

Due to the diverse landscape, you can choose from an assortment of trekking trails, from easy to difficult trails. For the first-timers, the easy trails would be perfect for trekking. The mountainous trails would be the most courageous for those who seek adventure during their trekking trip.

The rough ascending or descending hilly path, the green hills, and the blue snow-capped mountains, will be your friend on your whole trekking period. The forest in the hills always will welcome you with seasonal blossoms. So, trekking is a wonderful opportunity to both observe and experience the lifestyle and the natural and geographical conditions of remote areas.

Trekking in Nepal is popular throughout the year. The trails are busy every season. However, the most recommended time to trek is in the autumn season or spring season.

Autumn season in Nepal falls on the months from September to December and spring falls in March, April, and May. In winter trekking in high altitudes is not possible and in summer due to monsoon rain, it is not always possible to trek in the trails at this time.

To make sure you know the best time and place to go trekking in Nepal, here is a full description of its four, major climatic seasons. But each of the seasons has its own popular attraction to offer.

1. Trekking in Nepal in Spring

Spring season is one of the Best Time to go Trekking in Nepal. In Nepal, the Spring season falls in the months of March, April, and May. After autumn, spring is the best season to go trekking as the temperature in this season will not be as cold like winter and not as hot as summer. It is warmer at lower altitudes and as the altitude increases temperature decreases.

In spring, all the trails will be available due to clear trails as the heavy snow of winter would have melted by these months. There are a few and rare occasions where you might still experience light to moderate snowfall on the higher altitudes in early spring.

The perfect examples of forest beauty can be experienced in this season. You can witness the full blossoms of the beautiful rhododendrons, orchids, and other species of flowers. Blossoming of the plants occurs in spring and the forest surrounding the trekking trails is full of greenery.

You can spot different species of birds and animals on the way as this season attracts many migratory birds and animals. You may get to view some exotic animals in spring.

The spring season is dry and windy with the dust blocking the mountain views from the hills. There is less possibility of downpour in spring which makes it one of the Best Times to go Trekking in Nepal.

Spring will welcome you with its calm nature. You can prepare to trek in this season without any hesitation. However all the trekking routes in Nepal are suitable to trek in this spring season, there are some of the recommended treks in this season. They are Everest Base Camp with Island peak climbing, Everest three pass trek, Langtang Gosaikunda Helambu trek, Gokyo and Cho la Pass Trek, Annapurna Circuit Trek and many more.

Just to be safe, be prepared with your rain gear and warm clothes always with you while trekking as the weather in the mountains is unpredictable.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

2. Trekking in Nepal in Summer

Summer falls on the months of June July and August in Nepal. In Nepal, summer not only includes the hot weather but also monsoon rain. You can trek with less difficulty in early summer, but after the monsoon starts, your trekking journey will be harder.

Monsoon brings heavy rainfall with thunderstorms. In this season, the temperature will be hot during dry days and moderate during cloudy or rainy days. Due to these reasons, Summer isn’t regarded as the Best Time to go Trekking in Nepal.

This season is not suitable for trekking for many reasons. The trails become muddy and slippery. The hilly areas become prone to mudslides and landslides during this season.

This season also attracts lots of pests like mosquitoes, leeches. The wet sensation of your clothes and shoes will just add to the troubles.

However, if you do choose on going during this season, you might just be rewarded with some of the best views of the mountains and the hills as the rain washes out much of the dust. You can witness the farmers around the trekking trails enjoying the rainy season. It is also quite an adventure to try and climb the muddy and slippery trails and you get to choose the best restaurants and guest houses as there will be fewer trekkers.

This season is best to visit rain shadowed areas of Nepal like upper Mustang and Dolpa. These places are barren and known as the desert of Nepal as it is rain shadowy area. There is very less possibility of rainfall in these areas throughout the year.

Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek, Annapurna Panorama Trek, Annapurna Circuit Trek, Mustang Trek, etc. are some of the recommended trekking trails in the season, summer.

Insect repellent and mosquito nets are a must for trekking in this season. Strong grip waterproof shoes and using leech repellent will also help to make this trek a more forgiving one if you trek in this season.
Be prepared with every kind of rain gear if you plan to trek during this season. Comfortable hiking wears with full sleeves is also recommended in this season to keep your body away from direct contact with sun and insect.

3. Trekking in Nepal in Autumn

The Autumn season is unarguably the Best Time to go Trekking in Nepal. Autumn falls in the months of September, October, and November. It is the best trekking season in Nepal. Almost all the trekking trails will be full of travelers as this is considered a peak trekking season.

The clear weather in this season will give you a pristine view of mountain vistas. Hardly any traces of clouds will be seen in the sky. The early autumn brings glorious and pleasant days with fresh air after the monsoon rain; however, late autumn is a bit colder.

The forest is full of green vegetation in the early autumn season. The winter is right around the corner and the temperature gradually declines. Trekking this season will give you a wonderful and thrilling experience while you walk on trails covered with fallen dry leaves.

Autumn, at the higher altitude, is colder compared to the lower altitudes. The temperature at daytime is moderate and feels good while during nighttime, the temperature may gradually dip down to freezing and below freezing at times.

Two of the most popular festivals, Dashain, and Tihar are celebrated across the country during this season. So you can get to experience multiple festivities in Nepal. You will get to learn different types of rituals, customs, traditions, and cultures of the different local ethnic groups in Nepal. You will get an extra quality time celebrating the festivals with them while trekking which makes autumn the Best Time to go Trekking in Nepal.

The trekking trails will be full of trekkers from all around the world, so you will need to pre-book everything, from flights to accommodations. You will have to start your trek early in the morning so that you can reach your destination before other trekkers to reserve a good place to stay. There will be a queue for getting your meals in order early.

Since the weather in autumn is clear and calm, you will feel privileged to trek the higher altitudes at this time so that you can observe the majestic view of the mountain vistas so clearly and closely making it the Best Time to go Trekking in Nepal.

Some of the recommended treks for this season are, Everest Base Camp Trek, Everest Three Pass Trek, Gokyo and Cho La Pass Trek, Amphu Lapcha Pass with Mera Peak Climb, Annapurna Base Camp Trek, Langtang Gosainkunda Helambu Trek, Ganesh Himal Trekking
And many more

4. Trekking in Nepal in Winter

Winter season in Nepal falls from December to February. The weather and the climate are super cold at this time. The Winter season is also the least recommendable season to trek in Nepal due to the freezing temperatures. In higher altitudes, some of the trekking routes will not be open due to winds and heavy snowfall.

Trekking in lower elevations below 3,000 to 4,000 m would be comfortable in winter. You should be ready with all the winter clothes and accessories so that the cold will not hit you if you do decide to go higher or trek during this season.

The best part of trekking in winter is the view of white, snow-covered mountain ranges. Your journey will be full of adventures as the cold weather challenges you and makes it harder to trek with all the heavy snowfalls. In the mountains, many tea houses will be not functioning, with only one or two open ones.

The weather is windy during the winter season so it is impossible for you to ascend towards some trekking peaks. During early winter, as the wind condition remains stable at this time, trekking over Everest, Langtang, Annapurna is popular and possible.

Everest view trek, Tengboche Monastery Trek, Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek, Langtang Circuit Trek, Annapurna Base Camp Trek are the recommended treks for wintertime. 

Celebrating Christmas and new year in the heart of the Himalayas would be a great, lifetime experience. It is also good if you do not want more traffic on your trekking trails. As there will be much fewer trekkers during this season.

Best Time to go Trekking in Nepal – Conclusion

It would be awesome to visit Nepal in any season. You have loads of choices of trekking routes and trekking destinations in Nepal. First of all, make sure to read the above article about Best Time to go Trekking in Nepal. Thereafter,  pick a month that you know will be great for you to come here. After deciding the month, inquire about the trekking route that you wish to trek. Gather as much information as you can. This will help you on your trip.

You should pack your bags according to the season and duration. While traveling to Nepal as your necessity may change accordingly.

title: 10 Days Trek in Nepal
excerpt: In this article, we are going to discuss 10 Days Trek in Nepal. Nepal, the land of the Himalayas, is famous for having the most diverse trekking trails in the world. These diverse trekking trails…
html:
In this article, we are going to discuss 10 Days Trek in Nepal.

Nepal, the land of the Himalayas, is famous for having the most diverse trekking trails in the world. These diverse trekking trails offer routes that are suitable for every age group, every budget, and can be done throughout the year.

These diverse trekking trails not only offers diverse terrains, natural beauty but also houses people from different ethnic tribes who have their own unique culture and follow a different religion. Trekking in Nepal thus offers you a unique opportunity to trek around some of the highest peaks in the world along with the opportunity to experience Nepal’s unique culture, tradition, customs and it’s numerous festivals.

The varied geographical structure is one of the best features of Nepal. Besides, there are plenty of trekking routes available in Nepal. You can choose the right package according to your vacation period. Also, the 10 days trek in Nepal is neither too short nor too long and is just perfect for adventure seekers.

Moreover, the 10 days trek in Nepal is designed in such a way that any age group can join the package and are budget-friendly. Similarly, Nepal is one of the most affordable trekking destinations. In fact, it is suitable and can be done by anyone who can walk around 5-6 hours a day.

Similarly, some of the trekking trails will be closed during the monsoon and winter seasons in Nepal to reduce the risk of accidents due to landslides and avalanches. But luckily none of the given 10 days trek packages falls in this category and hence, all the routes are open throughout the year. Moreover, these short packages will not lead you to the higher altitudes and you will be safe in any season you plan to start your trekking trip.

Some recommended trekking Packages

Listed below are some of the best packages available in Nepal if you wish to trek but cannot give more than 10 days. All of these trekking packages can be modified as per your need and time constraints.

Panchase Trek

If you opt to do 10 Days trek in Nepal, this can be one of the best choices for you. Panchase is a beautiful village situated on the south of Annapurna II and Lamjung Himal. Panchase Trek is an ideal trek for those who want to get the experience of trekking in Nepal without spending much time doing it. It is a short hilly homestay trek with a dazzling series of mountain views.

Starting from Pokhara, the city of lakes, your trek leads you to Panchase. You have the option of choosing to fly or drive from and to Pokhara from Kathmandu.

The trails of Panchase Trek passes through different terrains, beautiful, traditional villages with people from diverse ethnic groups, and terrace rice farms. This trek offers you spectacular views of mountains like Mount Annapurna, Mount Dhaulagiri, Mount Manaslu, Mount Machhapuchhre, Ganesh Himal, Himchuli, and many more.

The trip will take you to an altitude of about 3,000 m It is a comfortable trek for people of all ages. The ascending and descending paths of this trek will take you through lush green forests, grasslands, paddy fields, and finally to Panchase Bhanjyang, the highest point of this trek. Here, you will be rewarded with an awe-inspiring view of the mountains and a picturesque view of lower lands as well.

This trek provides you with spectacular sceneries and can make great postcards and photographs for your family or friends back home.
The best season for this particular trek is Autumn, Spring, and winter. This 10-day trek allows you to experience trekking in hills. This trek is great for beginners and for those wishing to get some experience for trekking on higher lands.

Trip Itinerary

Day 01: Arrive in Kathmandu.
Day 02: Kathmandu Sight Seeing
Day 03: Kathmandu-Pokhara.Fly or drive
Day 04: Drive to Khade Khola, trek to Bhumdi
Day 05: Bhumdi-Panchase Bhanjyang
Day 06: Panchase-Bhadure
Day 07: Bhadure-Dhampus via Kare
Day 08: Dhampus-Kirakhore
Day 09: Kirakhor-Hangja-Pokhara
Day 10: Pokhara-Kathmandu

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek

Another trek on the list of 10 Days trek in Nepal is Ghorepani and Poonhill Trek. An ideal short trek lies in the Annapurna Region and it is none other than the popular 10 days trek Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek. It is really appropriate for those who do not have enough time yet wish to experience the Himalaya trek. Every age group can trek here due to its lower elevation and easy trail.

You will be starting your journey with a short drive from Pokhara, the city of lakes. Your actual trek starts by crossing the suspension bridge of Modi Khola. Khola means river in the local language. You will be hiking along the banks of Modi Khola. The trail leads you through several villages of various ethnic communities.

The stone-paved trails that join one village to another are one of the attractions of this trek. You might get a glimpse of Mount Machhapuchhre/Fishtail along the trail which will refresh you and encourage you to follow the route. Then, you trek to Ghorepani, from here you trek to your final destination, Poon hill

Poon hill is the highest point of this trek and from its viewpoint, you will get a 360-degree panoramic views of mountain peaks like Mount Machhapuchhre (6,998 m), Annapurna I (8,091 m), Annapurna II (7,939 m), Annapurna III (7,555 m), Mount Dhaulagiri (8,167 m), Nilgiri (7,041 m), and Tukuche (6,920 m).

If you do choose to get up early, you will be rewarded with one of the most beautiful sunrises in the world from Poon Hill. It is the best part of this trek. Poon Hill (3,210 m) is listed as one of the top 100 places to visit in your lifetime and is known as the “Photographer’s Paradise”.

This short trek will definitely make you fall in love with the natural beauty of the Mountains. Likewise, this trek provides you with opportunities to mix together with the locals of the nearby villages to better grasp their way of living, traditions, culture. Moreover, you will definitely be left with memories of the amazing diversity of landscape and ethnicities. So, be ready to experience the best trek with Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek.

Trip Itinerary

Day 01: Your arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport and transfer to the hotel in Kathmandu
Day 02: Pre-trip Meeting and Sightseeing around Kathmandu valley
Day 03: Drive from Kathmandu to Pokhara
Day 04: One hour drive to Nayapul and trek to Tikhedhunga
Day 05: Trek to Ghorepani.
Day 06: Trek to Ghandruk.
Day 07: Trek down to Birethanti, Nayapul, and drive back to Pokhara
Day 08: Drive back to Kathmandu
Day 09: Full day sightseeing tour of Kathmandu valley (Pashupatinath Temple, Boudhanath, Swayambhu, and Kathmandu durbar square).
Day 10: Transfer to Airport

Gosaikunda Helambu Trek

The classical and exciting trekking destination, Gosaikunda Helambu trek is the destination for adventure seekers. This 10 day trek lies in the Helambu region and is less crowded than the other trekking destinations in Nepal.

Your trekking journey begins from Sundarijal in Kathmandu, the capital city of Nepal. The final destination of this trek is Gosaikunda, a sacred lake revered by both Hindus and Buddhists lies at the altitude of 4,380 m

You will get to explores the ancient villages on the way. The majority of the people in the Helambu region are Sherpas who follow Buddhism. Hence, you will get to see different Buddhist monasteries, prayer flags, chortens along the way.

The trails along the forest will provide you the opportunity to observe exotic animals like Red Panda, Musk Deer, Himalayan Thar, and Black Bear. You will also get to enjoy the picturesque scenery of Langtang Lirung, Gaurishankar, Yala Peak, and others during this trek.

The mesmerizing view of tiny lakes will make your trek more exciting. During winter, all the lakes will be frozen which makes for an interesting and unique view of this region. Helambu is well-known for its sweet apples and so you will find apple farms along this trek as well.

This 10 day trek in Nepal follows through diverse terrain giving you a unique opportunity to experience hiking in the hilly or temperate region and trekking up in the mountains or alpine regions of Nepal. Therefore, you will get opportunities to climb some small peaks on this trek.

If you are a person who loves to embrace nature and is always enthusiastic to achieve new knowledge and experience, then Gosaikunda Helambu 10 Days Trek in Nepal is the best option for you.

Trip Itinerary

Day 01: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA), Kathmandu and transfer to hotel.
Day 02: Drive from Kathmandu to Dhunche
Day 03: Trek from Dhunche to Syabru Gaon
Day 04: Trek from Thulo Syabru to Sing Gompa or Chandan Bari
Day 05: Trek from Sing Gompa to Gosaikunda via Lauribinayak La
Day 06: Trek from Gosaikunda to Ghopte
Day 07: Trek from Ghopte to Kutumsang
Day 08: Trek from Kutumsang to Chisapani
Day 09: Conclude trek at Sundarijal and drive to Kathmandu
Day 10: Transfer to Airport for your onward destination.

Tengboche Monastery Trek

Another option for the 10 days trek in Nepal is Tengboche Monastery Trek. In fact, it is a popular short trek in the Everest Region and the halfway trek of Everest Base Camp Trek.

Besides, experiencing the adventures of the Himalayan lifestyle and the mesmerizing views of some of the world’s highest peaks are the main highlights of this trek.

Your journey begins with a short but adventurous 35 minutes flight from Kathmandu to Lukla. Lukla is the starting point of your actual trek. Also, the trekking trail from Lukla will lead you to Namche Bazar. Moreover, on the way, you cross through different settlements, lush forests of birch and rhododendron, Dudh Koshi River, and many more scenic views

Due to the high altitude, there will be an acclimatization day at Namche Bazar. In fact, this is to prevent any unnecessary exhaustion and also as a precaution against High Altitude Sickness. Therefore, you will have the option to take a day hike on this day to Kunde and Khumjung. Similarly, exploring the periphery of Namche Bazaar will give you the experience of Sherpa lifestyle, culture, and tradition.

In sum, you will reach your final destination Tengboche Monastery (3,870 m), the largest monastery in the Everest region, on the other day of acclimatization. Likewise, a stunning panoramic view of about 20 snow-covered mountains like Mount Everest, Mount Tawache, Mount Nuptse, Mount Lhotse, Mount Ama Dablam, and Mount Thamserku is what you will be rewarded with when you reach here. Moreover, the overwhelming scenery of downhills, full of green forest can be observed from the viewpoint of the monastery. Overall, in the spring season, the forest in the downhill will be covered with flowers of rhododendron.

In particular, the Everest region is one of the best places to trek. Besides, it is full of natural beauty and gives you the experience of a mountain lifestyle and the unique culture and warm hospitality of Sherpa people.

Trip Itinerary

Day 01: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu, and transfer to the hotel.
Day 02: Trek Preparation and Kathmandu Valley Sightseeing Tour.
Day 03: Fly from Kathmandu to Lukla and then Trek to Phakding
Day 04: Trek to Namche Bazaar
Day 05: Acclimatization day at Namche Bazaar or day hike to Kunde and Khumjung villages.
Day 06: Trek to Thyangboche monastery
Day 07: Trek to Namche and continue to Monjo
Day 08: Trek back to Lukla airport.
Day 09: Fly from Lukla to Kathmandu.
Day 10: Transfer to International Airport for the next destination.

Tips for 10 Days Trek in Nepal

10-days trek in Nepal is the most reliable trek for those who want to spend 10 days of their holiday trekking in Nepal. Also, you should be prepared and plan according to the weather condition of the time you decide to do your trek.

Here are some tips that you should know before starting your trek.

Advance Booking
Booking your trekking package in advance will make everything easier to prepare and increase the chances of getting the most service from travel agencies.

Starting your trek early in the morning
Every day, you should start your trek early in the morning to avoid the midday sun and windy environment of the mountains. In addition, starting your trek late may make you late for arrival at your next destination which may be problematic.

Hiring a Professional Guide and Getting a Porter

It is always better to trek with a guide than trekking on your own. A professional and experienced guide will improve your overall experience of the trek as she/he can give you in-depth information on the trails, local community, local fauna, climate, weather, tea houses, rest stops. Overall, there is also a very low chance of you getting lost on the trails.

In fact, hiring a porter to carry your luggage is also recommended. Also, it is an entire 10 days package so you have to pack for the 10 days and your backpack may get heavy to carry it on your own. Overall, this also allows you to travel lightly so that you can comfortably enjoy the path that you are on.

Hydrating your body
While trekking, hydrating your body continuously will make you walk more. Staying hydrated prevents you from being fatigued and energizes your body. Likewise, it is necessary to drink plenty of water as you get to higher altitudes as you will be getting dehydrated at a faster pace.

Packing backpack with all the necessary items
Your backpack is the home for you on your trekking journey. Hence, all the things that you need in your 10 days trek should be included in your backpack. Besides, your backpack should include clothing, toiletries, and other important accessories.

Clothing

  • Hiking t-shirts or shirts
  • Fleece, Windproof Jacket
  • Waterproof Jacket
  • Hiking underwears
  • Lightweight hiking pants
  • Warm Trousers
  • Waterproof pants of breathable fabric

Head, Foot, and Handwear

  • UV Sunglasses
  • Sun hat or scarf
  • Thin, lightweight socks
  • Hiking shoes
  • Hiking slippers
  • Lightweight gloves

Personal Hygienic Products and Toiletries

  • Moisturizer
  • Sunscreen cream
  • Hairbrush/comb
  • lip balm
  • Toothbrush and toothpaste
  • Shampoo and conditioner
  • Quick-dry hand towel
  • Toilet paper and tissues
  • Antibacterial handwash
  • Wet wipes
  • Soap
  • Female hygiene products ( in case you get a period)

Other accessories

  • Trekking Poles
  • Daypack
  • Sleeping bag
  • Rucksack Bag
  • Basic First Aid Kit
  • Water bottles
  • Headlamp
  • Some plastic bags (to keep your things dry)
  • Camera and extra batteries
  • Trail map and trekking guidebook

10 Days Trek in Nepal – Conclusion

Trekking will be interesting if you have preplanning. Choosing the best trekking package is one of the key tasks while you plan for your trek. If you are trekking for the first time, the 10 days trek package will definitely be suitable for you. Likewise, the trails in this package are not tough and you can modify your trekking experience while you are on the trek by adding up hikes nearby your trekking trails.

Above mentioned 10 days trekking packages of the different regions of Nepal gives you different experiences of trekking. Also, you will be mesmerized by the natural beauty as well as the unique lifestyle, culture, and tradition of the different regions of Nepal.

Nepal has good weather conditions for trekking and traveling. Hence, you don’t need to synchronize your holidays with the perfect weather conditions of the country. Moreover, the above mentioned 10 days trekking packages are available in every season. In particular, the best recommended months are autumn (September, October, and November) and spring (March, April, and May). Therefore, these are the best season to explore nature in its full glory and beauty.

The 10 days trekking packages are waiting for you to come and grab them to make lifelong memories.

title: Nepal Tea House Trek
excerpt: In this article, we are going to discuss the Nepal Tea House Trek in a detailed manner. With great and audacious Himalayan trails, Nepal has set itself as a go-to land for trekkers. Trekking in Nepal…
html:
In this article, we are going to discuss the Nepal Tea House Trek in a detailed manner.

With great and audacious Himalayan trails, Nepal has set itself as a go-to land for trekkers.

Trekking in Nepal is generally categorized in terms of the level of difficulty as easy and tough treks. But you may have also heard about the other type of trek based on the availability of accommodations. These are typical of two types, wiz. Teahouse and Camping.

In Nepal, people use a local name for Teahouses. It is called ‘Bhatti’ in the native language. And Bhattis are quite popular in the well-known trek routes in Nepal.

It might be a bit confusing for tourists as the word ‘Hotel’ is generally used by the locals as a reference to a place where they can eat but not sleep. A better word that you can use can be ‘Lodge’. They will understand that you want a place to accommodate.

You will also find boards that clarify your confusion by mentioning the available services as ‘Hotel and Lodge’ or ‘Hotel, Lodge and Teahouse’ at many places throughout the trek route. These boards help trekkers coming from around the world to understand where to go for their required needs.

Tea Houses are basically referred to as the local lodges where you can eat and accommodate during your trek.

If are wondering about how a teahouse trek would be like, it is a trek where you halt at these teahouses for rest during your trek journey. They will provide you with food and bedding facilities. There are certain categories of teahouse based on quality, but you should not expect them to be exotic or full-fledged. Since the trekking routes are usually not connected to roads for transportation, the services can be quite basic only.

Nepal Tea House Trek vs Camping

Trekking at high altitude areas can be quite challenging due to weather and limited facilities. Therefore, camping alone or when with a large group may not be suitable. This is where the need for the tea house emerges. Since the popular trek routes attract many visitors on a regular basis, there are multiple tea houses every few hours distance of the trekking trail. These places help you ease your luggage load while you halt for some rest.

A backpack with all the essential items including tents, towels, snacks, water bottles, and so on, can be quite heavy for your body, making you want to release it and stretch out your muscles.

Therefore, teahouse treks add enough flexibility to your trekking schedule so that you can listen to your body’s desire for rest, unlike the camping treks where you need to rush with a fear of being left out in the group.

In addition, you will also be able to experience the richness of the ethnic culture and tradition if you choose to stay with the locals at their tea houses. It is the best way to showcase the pseudo-culture of the locals.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Nepal Tea house Trek Recommendations

Nepal Tea House Trek is quite popular as you can choose this trek in most of the regions of the country. You are likely to find tea houses at distinct milestones in these trek routes.

The quality of services they provide has improved quite a lot in the past few years. As these trek trails have been flooded with both local and international tourists in the last couple of years. Certainly, because of the competition, there is a drastic improvement in the aesthetic ambiance and quality of services.

Everest Base Camp Trek

Nepal and Everest are synonymous. People from around the world come here to explore the beauty of the highest peak in the world. Therefore, making the Everest Base Camp Trek the most popular trek route in Nepal. Nevertheless, there are a lot of other treks in the Everest region.

There are about 30000 visitors yearly for the Everest Base Camp Trek. Therefore, to facilitate the emerging rate of tourists, there are many tea houses made available throughout the trail. You can find many tea houses with basic facilities in between Jiri and Lukla. While for Lukla to Everest Base Camp, you can get better quality tea houses.

A well-equipped tea house may cost you around USD 5 to 10 per night. If you pre-booked your trip, the agency usually takes care of all the basic accommodation.

Usually, you get a twin room offering two single beds with a pillow, sheets, and bed cover. If you are conscious about hygiene, you can use a pillow liner or your sleeping bag.

They also offer you internet service based on the area of connectivity. It can be difficult to get a hot water supply at a higher altitude. However, some tea houses will provide you a bucket of hot water with some additional charges.

And yes, if you are a meat-lover, you should understand that you will not get fresh meat at this altitude. All the goods are carried to this place by porters and mountain yaks. And it takes a few days to travel. So avoiding meat during your trek days will lower your risk of ill health. Rather, you should opt for food made out of flour and cereals to provide you with the required nutrition.

Nepalese traditional meal – Dal Bhat will make the best meal during the trek. It will treat your taste buds and at the same time provide you with the required nutrients.

Also, the vegetables are organic and locally grown.

Annapurna Base Camp Trek

Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) Trek is a fine 2 weeks tea house trek in the Annapurna region. The Annapurna base camp is surrounded by a range of magnificent mountains including the Annapurna range, Machhapuchhre, and Dhaulagiri.

The tea houses found in this region is the major business and source of income for local families residing here. They have a big kitchen to prepare a meal for every guest. The rooms are also cheap and affordable, costing you around USD 2 to 3 per room per night.

If you take your meal in the same teahouse where you reside, the charges can be negotiated to USD 1-2 per night.

However, the meal can get a bit more expensive than the bedding as the cost of food supply increases with the altitude. The rate of meals can be around USD 3-5 per person. At this rate, you will get 3 typical Nepali meals a day.

While there is an adequate number of teahouses available on this route, it can be difficult to find a room to accommodate during the peak seasons. Therefore, pre-booking your trips to secure good accommodation can save you from possible difficulties during your trip.

It is essential to communicate with a travel agency or a local guide who can provide you with all the information you will need.

ABC trek will give you the privilege to also closely observe the different ethnic communities and their typical lifestyle. This trip will allow you to learn more about the unique culture of tribal Gurungs, Magars, Tamangs, and Chettris of this region. There are a lot more treks that are possible in the Annapurna Region.

Langtang Circuit Trek

Langtang circuit trek is another amazing adventure for trek enthusiasts around the world. Though listed as a short and easy trek route, it is one of the popular trekking spots in Nepal.

This trek will give you exposure to the beauty of Mother Nature. Besides, you can find diverging landscapes and ample green forests and waterfalls in this trek route. Langtang is home to spectacular mountain ranges like Langtang Lirung, Gang Chhenpo, Lenpo Gang, and Dorje Lakpa.

Tea house trek is also possible in the Langtang Region. There are a variety of options to choose from.

The charges for night stay may range from USD 2 to 4 per night. The cost of a dish varies from USD 2-6. Therefore, for a group of two people, an average per day charge can range between USD 20 to 30.

The tea houses will provide you with a basic accommodation of twin beds along with blankets and pillows. You can find two types of rooms – one with an attached toilet and another with a common (shared) toilet. The price of the room will vary accordingly.

You can find a hot water shower in some tea houses while the lack of solar panels in some teahouse will limit you from acquiring this facility. However, they can provide you with a bucket of hot water with some additional charges.

For obvious reasons, the facilities that you can expect decreases with the increase in altitude.

It is difficult to find a proper internet connection in this region. Moreover, reliable internet access can be found only in a town called Syabrubesi. However, you’ll find landline phones at multiple tea houses that will give you the facility to make phone calls at a defined rate.

Manaslu Circuit Trek

Manaslu Circuit is another amazing Nepal Tea House Trek destination and a very good alternative to Annapurna Circuit Trek. The astonishing sceneries, diverse culture, and tribal villages of Midwest Himalaya are definitely worth exploring.

This region is slowly growing as the next go-to place for passionate trekkers. With an increasing number of annual visitors, this region has been growing as a tourist destination. Many comfortable and quality tea houses have been established since then.

This circuit trek will give you the opportunity to closely examine the enchanting view of Mt. Manaslu, Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Gangapurna, and Annapurna III.

The cost of your teahouse stay depends on two things, the altitude of the place (measured by the difficulty in bringing the required goods to this altitude without any means of transportation) and the standard of the services they are providing.

Basically, the average cost per day can vary from USD 10 to USD 30 per person depending on the quality of services.

Nepal Tea House Trek – Final words

The concept of Tea houses began keeping comfort and convenience in mind. And availability and local culture play a major role in the continuity and popularity of this emerging concept in the Himalayas.

The main objective of the tea houses is to provide the trekkers with basic facilities for food and shelter. Some additional services for hot water, electricity, internet, and others add-in, in making the journey of the trekkers a bit more comfortable.

Why not, right?

Nepal Tea House Trek will make you more comfortable with the people and the landscape. It is a great way to understand their culture, traditions, and some local language. Living in the mountains in a native way is a must-try experience.

Though there are adequate places to stay in the teahouse trek routes, it is always recommended to be prepared for the worst case. If you are planning to travel during the peak seasons, it is wise to pre-book your trips.

Some guides from the trekking agencies could know some teahouses. This could mean discounts, better rooms with better views.

Well, why stay behind?

Trekking in rural parts of Nepal is always adventurous so you should keep yourself prepared for everything that can come to your way.

title: Nepal Luxury Trekking

html:
In this article, we are going to discuss and guide you about Nepal Luxury Trekking.

Nepal is a country of diverse culture, tradition, and landscape. The high mountains, flora and fauna, rich culture, historical monuments, art, tradition, savorous local delicacies, and warm hospitality of people never fail to amuse the sense of the visitors. Moreover, if you are a passionate traveler, Nepal offers you everything you would want to see and experience.

However, there’s a fallacy that trekking in the hills and mountains of Nepal is all about adventure and no luxury. But this isn’t true. If you have a good budget, then trekking in Nepal can be a blissful and memorable traveling. You can explore the beautiful Himalayas with utmost comfort. Yes, this is possible!

Adventure and luxury can go side by side when you consider choosing a tour package that assures comfort. Also, you can enjoy the glorious views of enchanting mountains throughout your entire days of traveling.

The travel routes are generally the same as that of the normal trek route. The accommodation will be in a different place though. With a luxury package, you’ll get a well-furnished room that is nicely carpeted with large comfy beds. Besides, these rooms are facilitated with an attached bathroom that includes a western-style toilet and provides 24-hour hot water service.

You will also get a good variety of food served in a spacious and comfortable dining room with a warm ambiance. Flight service is also provided to every place within the trek-route where flights are possible.

In particular, Nepal has something for every kind of traveler – either comfort or adventure-oriented. Also, you can experience a wide range of adventures like trekking, peak climbing, paragliding, skydiving, bungee jumping, rafting, and others.

Generally, if you are more inclined towards exploring the magnificent mountain ranges you can get a package to get a close view of different mountains. And, if you are more fascinated by art, culture, and diversity you can choose to explore the culturally diverse cities of Kathmandu, Lalitpur, and Bhaktapur.

In addition, places like Pokhara and Lumbini (birthplace of Gautam Buddha) are areas of tourist attraction where most of the tourists go for recreation and to spend quality time. So no matter what, you will definitely be fascinated with the beauty of nature, art, and the heart-warming hospitality of the locals.

Depending on your need, you can select one of the many luxury packages that are made available.

Popular Nepal Luxury Trekking Routes

Luxury trekking allows you to experience the magnificent snow-caps of the mountains with ease and relaxation. Likewise, the luxury trip ensures that you’re well supplied with food and equipment without you having to carry them through the hills and mountains.

title: Nepal Tea House Trekking Packing List
excerpt: In this article, we are going to discuss the Nepal Tea House Trekking Packing List. Trekking in the endearing land of the Himalayas, filled with scenic beauty, is a fantasy for every travel bug. With…
html:
In this article, we are going to discuss the Nepal Tea House Trekking Packing List.

Trekking in the endearing land of the Himalayas, filled with scenic beauty, is a fantasy for every travel bug. With the power of the internet, the captivating images that reflect a beautiful sight at one part of the world can reach many of its admirers in no time.

The enchanting views portrayed by the pictures definitely do draw the attention of a lot of people. If you have not yet traveled to Nepal, it’s about time.

Had you chose a luxury trip to Nepal, there wouldn’t have been any problem with the checklist because you could easily get the left-over items in the city areas. Since you are setting off for an exciting adventure – trekking in the rural parts of Nepal, you must be mindful of what can be essential and what unnecessary.

It is possible to leave your unnecessary goods at your hotel/lodge room at Kathmandu or Pokhara or even with the travel agency you choose. You are in fact suggested to carry only the things that you will require. Shed the baggage right from home.

Nepal teahouse trekking packing list

The main idea behind this list is to share the list of items that you’d possibly need while you’re trekking in Nepal. But, this is just a tentative list of items, please feel free to personalize it.

Clothes

T-shirts (non-cotton) – 5

As cotton clothes take much time to dry, it is not a recommended fabric for travel. You’d possibly be sweating all your way through the trek. So in that case as well, a non-cotton t-shirt will easily dry and prevent your body from longer exposure to humidity.

As for the number, you will not need a new shirt for every day. There are places where you can give your shirts a quick wash if you feel they are sweaty and smelly.

Polyester is light-weighted, breathable, and dries quickly. You can opt for other similar fabric too.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Long-sleeve shirts – 2

It is always intelligent to back up for any possible situation. The long-sleeve shirts will keep you warm if the atmosphere is quite cold. These are also good for the cold chilling nights near the Himalayas. On the other hand, long-sleeved shirts will also protect you from direct sunlight, if the rays are scorching in the daytime. You can also buy them in the store of Kathmandu for some $ 3 per piece. These are the must include items in the Nepal Tea House Trekking Packing List.

Waterproof hiking boots – 1 pair

The trekking trails are filled with adventures. You will be climbing up and down the stairs, through the steep hills, crossing the water streams, walking through the meadows and the forests.

Therefore, it is important that you have a pair of reliable hiking boots that is water-resistant. It is important to keep your feet dry and moving. Wet feet can cause numbness and difficulty in walking.

Pants or convertible trekking pants – 1 pair

For me, shorts are more comfortable while trekking as the body will be heating up naturally. A pair of trekking pants is more than enough as you can use them multiple times, even without washing – they will ultimately get dirty anyway.

Convertible trekking pants are a great option. A waterproof one is also another wise option.

Hiking Undergarment – 3

These are some of the essential items in the packing. Hiking undergarments are usually made of breathable fabric. They are light to carry and goes well in both cold and warm weather.

Boardshorts – 1 pair

It can be surprising to know that you’ll need a swimsuit on your trek to freezing altitudes but let me tell you, there’s more than what you can expect. While on your trek route, you’ll come across many natural water spots – both hot and cold.

Therefore, backing up one extra boardshorts will keep you favored. Or jump in in your undergarments.

Sandals – 1 pair

After the day-long trek, you might not desire to get into those shoes. They will want to breathe. So once you reach your destination tea house, you’d probably want to take them off and aid them with a pair of easy slippers/sandals. These are easy to carry you anywhere within the lodge, or even along the riverside. Therefore, these are the must include items in the Nepal Tea House Trekking Packing List.

Rain jacket – 1

A good quality rain jacket with a hood is essential to keep you away from the rain. Weather in the Himalayas can be unpredictable. Therefore, it is better to keep yourself safe from possible obligations throughout your trek journey.

You can add a light fleece to the list for extra warmth but do not opt for a 2-in-1 fleece and rain jacket as it will not be feasible for trekking in the woods.

Waterproof pants – 1 pair

Waterproof pants can take a huge space in your packing but they are very essential to keep you dry if you are trekking at higher altitudes where rain is unpredictable. It is better to update yourself with the environment and possible weather conditions on your expected travel dates.

Do this with your travel agency. They’ll give you the most genuine suggestions.

Trekking socks – 2-3 pairs

It is obvious that walking throughout the day will cause your feet to sweat more than normal. But you simply can’t let your feet be greasy and wet with your sweat. It can cause difficulty in walking and also cause a problem to your travel partners once you take off your shoes at the destination.

So you must choose good quality trekking socks that will prevent you from all the possible consequences.

Gears -Nepal Tea House Trekking Packing List

Backpack

If you’re not hiring a travel agency service, then you’ll have to make sure the backpack you’re carrying is comfortable and easy enough.

Make sure the bag offers an evenly distributed weight throughout its body so that it provides you a much easy uphill trek. Depending upon your days of the trek, you can choose a 50 to 70 liters bag.

Water bottle

Water bottles are the must carry in the list. You are sure to get thirsty. Also, keeping yourself hydrated is a must. This will prevent altitude sickness too.

You can refill them at many places in the trek route. These are the must include items in the Nepal Tea House Trekking Packing List.

Headlamp

In the trekking route, there can be places where there’s no electricity, or if you’re walking through a hill, early in the morning for the sunrise, you’ll definitely need it. You can also opt for a torch but headlamps are more comfortable while walking.

Sunglasses/ Caps

If you do not want to get a suntan, equip yourself with caps and sunscreen lotions. Also, sunglasses are great for the day when you are in snow. And back up a UV lip balm to keep your lips moisturized.

Sleeping Bags

Though not much required for tea-house trekking in Nepal, you can get one in for emergency cases. While purchasing a sleeping bag, choose wisely. If you are trekking and love to spend time outdoors, get a zero-degree sleeping bag that can handle the cold.

Electronics – Nepal Tea House Trekking Packing List

Cell phone with a Nepalese sim

You are definitely not forgetting your mobile phone because you will have to make calls to the travel agency, the travel guide/potters and the hotel where you’ll be staying. Make sure you get a Nepali sim card so that you can make local calls with ease.

Camera, chargers, and extra batteries

You’re going to travel because of the photos you’ve seen from some source. And you’d definitely want to capture them for yourself too – either for sharing or storing for memories. So a good camera is a must on the list. Extra batteries, just in case.

In Nepal, you’ll find a two-prong, 220-volt plug. Make sure you have a good surge protector integrated into them, because the electricity supply may not be stable at times.

First Aid kit

It is wise to keep your requirements updated. If you’re trekking with a travel agency, they may provide you with a first-aid safety kit but it is always better to become self-sufficient.

Add all your daily supplement dosages along with a bandage for possible sprains, iodine wipes, electrolyte powder, anti-allergy pills, anti-diarrheal tablets, band-aids, and if you have high altitude sickness problem, take medication such as Diamox with you. These are the must include items in the Nepal Tea House Trekking Packing List.

Nepalese Currency

You won’t find any ATMs or credit card vendors once you start trekking. Tea houses prefer cash. So carry enough money for your trek days.

You’ll require about 1500 – 2000 NPR ($15-$20) for food and 2000 – 3000 NPR ($20-$30) for accommodation on per day basis if you are trekking on your own.

Extras

Besides the major requirements, there are other things that you can carry in your backpack that will aid your journey. Things like toiletries, tents, reading books, trekking poles, additional battery/memory cards, zip lock bags, microfiber towel, ear plugs should add in to your comfort.

You’re also suggested to carry snacks like energy bars, chocolates, peanuts, and nuts. These will supply you with required energy during your trek.

Nepal Tea House Trekking Packing List – Conclusion

The tea house trekking routes in Nepal is filled with adequate resting houses for relaxation and will provide you with food and accommodation service at regular trekking intervals. But you may not find some essentials that you will probably require on a personal basis. Therefore, this travel checklist is created for your ease in packing the right thing.

You can either bring them on your own or buy them once you arrive at Kathmandu. You also have a choice to rent certain clothing and gears for few dollars per day in Kathmandu and Pokhara. Renting a sleeping bag will cost you some USD 2 per day.

If you have any queries or doubts regarding trekking in Nepal, feel free to contact us.

html:
In this article, we are going to discuss the doable as well as Best Treks In Nepal.

Nepal is a country of the Himalayas. And undoubtedly, a utopia for trekking adventures.

The type of landscape that you find in Nepal can be rarely found in other parts of the world. In particular, the hills and mountains of Nepal give a rich trekking experience.

Not one, not two, but there are many trails that takes you to the glorious Himalayas with stunning routes filled with beautiful sightseeing and adventure. Likewise, this provides the best experience throughout the journey.

So, it would be unfair to name the best trek in Nepal. And one visit to Nepal is not enough.

Everyone has their own taste and preferences for trekking too. So depending upon what you are seeking from the tour will make a difference in categorizing the trek as best. Moreover, if your expectations are met with the offerings of a trek, then you find it ideal else otherwise.

When you are talking about trekking, there are a number of factors that will make a difference in your experience. Similarly, the level of difficulty, number of days involved, the budget of the trek, type of package you choose, etc. can highly influence your expectations with the trek.

Best Trekking Routes in Nepal

Some of the amazing and popular treks in Nepal based on adventure, natural beauty, ethnic diversity, and cost are discussed below.

The added details will help you find your next ideal trek destination in Nepal.

1. Everest Base Camp Trek

One of the most popular choices of trekkers from around the world, Everest Base Camp Trek is a great option for those who are willing to relish the stunning views of the world’s highest peak – Mount Everest.

This trek will give you an exclusive trekking experience. Also, it is very achievable, unlike climbing Everest.

Furthermore, the trek gives you the opportunity to explore the rich local culture and festivals, diverse landscape, flora and fauna, breathtaking scenery, peaceful ambiance, and everything you can expect from ideal trekking in rustic Nepal.

Besides, trekking in the Everest Region or the Khumbu Region gives you an opportunity to walk through the trails traversed by legendary mountaineers.

The beautiful Everest High Passes, rowdy Dudh Koshi River, the renowned gateway of Namche Bazaar, peaceful Imja Tse valley, and a number of Buddhist Monasteries en route are remarkable sites you shouldn’t miss out to capture.

Summary:

Highest Elevation 5,600 m at Kala Patthar
Average Time in Days 12 Days
Difficulty Level Medium
Remoteness Not Isolated. Is visited by huge crowd every year.
Cost Medium (Will not be heavy to your wallet)
Best Season To Travel March to May and October to November.
Accommodation Type Teahouse
Restricted Permits No
Required Permits TIMS

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

2. Annapurna Circuit Trek

Another most popular trekking routes in Nepal is the Annapurna Circuit Trek. You will find a variety of terrain to explore, in addition to the richly diverse cultural and natural aspects of this region.

Generally, this trek will definitely allure you with stunning views of Mount Annapurna, Mount Machhapuchhre, Mount Dhaulagiri, Mount Manaslu, and Langtang Himal.

In fact, Annapurna Circuit Trek is one of Nepal’s greatest adventurous treks offering cultural and natural beauty to overwhelm the visitors in this region.

Furthermore, the trail allows the natural acclimatization process.

You will find a variety of landscapes throughout your way, ranging from jungle to high alpine, the green valley, and the dry peaks, and from hospitable villages to the world’s deepest gorge.

Summary:

Highest Elevation 5,416 m at Thorong La Pass
Average Time in Days 14
Difficulty Level Moderate
Remoteness Not Isolated
Cost Cheap
Best Season To Travel March to May and October to November.
Accommodation Type Teahouse
Restricted Permits No
Required Permits ACAP, TIMS

3. Manaslu Circuit Trek

The Manaslu Circuit Trek gives you an extremely remarkable trek experience by flaunting the remarkable panoramas of the peaks lying on the Nepal-Tibet border.

In sum, the trek takes you around the stunning Mount Manaslu, the 8th highest mountain in the world. Moreover, it reaches the highest altitude at Larkya Pass that offers a breathtaking view of Manaslu.

Manaslu Circuit Trek trails lead to fabulous scenes of the mountain range, hybrid Nepalese-Tibetan style villages. In addition, the presence of ancient Buddhist monasteries and surely challenging and adventurous Mountain Passes bejewels the route.

This topographically remote trekking route offers a fabulous experience for trekkers looking for adventure with opportunities to explore natural beauty – one of the many reasons why it is considered one of the best treks in Nepal.

Restrictions:

As a result of the remoteness, there’s a permit restriction that says that a minimum of two trekkers must be accompanied by a Nepali guide or Porter to trek the Manaslu Circuit. Hence, it is better to consult with a trekking agency to provide you with your trekking partner for this trek.

Summary:

Highest Elevation 5,115 m at Larkya Pass
Average Time in Days 15 Days
Difficulty Level Hard
Remoteness Isolated
Cost Medium
Best Season To Travel March to May and October to November.
Accommodation Type Guesthouses & Lodges
Restricted Permits Yes
Required Permits ACAP, MCAP, RAP

4. Ghorepani-Poonhill Trek

Comparatively easy and short in distance, Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek gives you a beautiful trekking experience through the terraced farmlands, eye-pleasing rhododendron forest, and warm welcoming Gurung Villages.

Likewise, the trek offers exceptional scenes during the spring season when the Rhododendrons are blooming everywhere along with the panorama of the high mountains.

In fact, the spectacular view of the sunrise over the Annapurna range is the major highlight of the trek.

Ghorepani- Poonhill is the best trek in Nepal if you want to enjoy the beauty and hospitality of the Annapurna Region in a short period of time.

Summary:

Highest Elevation 3,210 m at Poonhill
Average Time in Days 5
Difficulty level Easy to Moderate
Remoteness Not Isolated
Cost Cheap
Best Season To Travel March to May and October to November.
Accommodation Type Teahouse
Restricted Permits No
Required Permits ACAP, TIMS

5. Langtang Valley Trek

Renowned for its diverse culture and vegetation, the Langtang Valley Trek offers a great view of Langtang Ri and the amazing sight of Mount Annapurna and Mount Makalu.

Moreover, if you check the proximity of this place to Kathmandu it is very near to civilization but still offers a trekking experience as wild as any other Tibetan highlands. Likewise, it offers a tranquil rural landscape and is ideal for someone seeking one such experience.

Besides, this trek route supports exposure to the unique Tamang culture residing in the area along with the opportunity to relish the stunning glaciers at a relatively low altitude.

Also, the Langtang Valley provides you the advantage of sightseeing the exceptionally beautiful view of mountain panorama.

Summary:

Highest Elevation 4,984 m at Tserko Ri
Average Time in Days 10
Difficulty Level Moderate
Remoteness Not Isolated
Cost Cheap
Best Season To Travel March to May and October to November.
Accommodation Type Teahouse
Restricted Permits No
Required Permits TIMS

6. Upper Mustang Trek

In particular, Upper Mustang is a geographically sensitive area of Nepal that was not open for trekking until 1992. Besides, bordering with Tibet in the North, the culture here resembles that behind the borders.

The culture and landscape of the region have close proximity to that of Tibet.

Because of isolation from the remaining world, people here are able to retain their ancient culture and beliefs. Also, it is shocking to know that the Buddhist monasteries and caves carved into cliff walls in Mustang are there from the 16th century. Therefore, it easily draws the attention of many trekkers visiting the region.

Moreover, the landscape of Mustang is peculiar and is a kind of semi-dry desert with rocky structures covered with snow. Also, Mustang is a paradise behind the range of majestic Himalayas. Similarly, this trek can give an amazing experience to those seeking to explore a different than usual terrain and also the rich Nepalese- Tibetan culture.

Restrictions:

In fact, the permit restriction says that a minimum of two trekkers must be accompanied by a Nepali guide or Porter to trek the Upper Mustang. Hence, you can consult with a trekking agency for further details.

Summary:

Highest Elevation 3,810 m at Dhakmar
Average Time in Days 14
Difficulty Level Moderate to Hard
Remoteness Very Isolated
Cost High
Best Season To Travel March to May and October to November.
Accommodation Type Teahouse
Restricted Permits Yes
Required Permits ACAP, RAP

7. Kanchenjunga Base Camp Trek

Mount Kanchenjunga is the second highest peak in the world. In fact, the journey to its base camp gives you the opportunity to explore the natural and cultural beauty of eastern Nepal.

Generally, the journey takes you through the wilderness of high mountain terrain, along the mountain ranges standing on Nepal’s border with Sikkim and Tibet. Likewise, this area is home to some of the exotic wildlife found in Asia.

Moreover, this incredible trek allows you to make the most out of the unspoiled exposure to the local culture and virgin nature. Overall, it is indeed a rewarding adventure.

Restrictions:

A minimum of two trekkers must be accompanied by a Nepali guide or Porter to trek the Kanchenjunga Base Camp. So consult a trekking agency before you plan your trip.

Summary:

Highest Elevation 5,160 m at Lapsang Pass
Average Time in Days 20
Difficulty Level Difficult
Remoteness Very Isolated
Cost High
Best Season To Travel March to May and October to November.
Accommodation Type Camping
Restricted Permits Yes
Required Permits KCA, RAP

8. Annapurna Base Camp Trek

Under the list of best treks in Nepal comes the ABC trek. In particular, the scenic trek to Annapurna Base Camp takes you through the hospitable Gurung villages, via the high passes, walking past the picturesque valleys, before you reach the destined base of the mighty Mount Annapurna.

While in the trek, you will encounter a number of different landscapes and as you move forward through each new kind brings you closer to the base of 8,000 m high peaks in such a small time.

Moreover, if you are a nature admirer then this trek is definitely for you as you get to experience perfect natural sceneries along with the rich cultural diversity of the Annapurna Region. Besides, the trek to Annapurna Base Camp is a marvelous walk towards tranquility and a joyous experience for trekkers in many ways.

Summary:

Highest Elevation 4,320 m at Annapurna Base Camp
Average Time in Days 10
Difficulty Level Moderate
Remoteness Not Isolated
Cost Cheap
Best Season To Travel March to May and October to November.
Accommodation Type Teahouse
Restricted Permits No
Required Permits ACAP, TIMS

9. Trek to Gokyo Ri

Gokyo Valley Trek offers one of the most attractive trekking in the Khumbu region. Similarly, it comes under the list of one of the best treks in Nepal. Likewise, the major attraction includes side glens, turquoise lakes, the biggest glacier in the country, and the arc of the snow mountain.

In sum, the Gokyo Ri Trek takes you to the exceptional Gokyo valley via the wild forests and through numerous suspension bridges and beautiful ridges with shrines on top, not to forget the charming little hamlets, the alpine valleys, and the glacial moraines.

Furthermore, the breathtaking view of the five lakes together under the shadow of the tall mountain peaks in the Gokyo Valley leaves every visitor spellbound.

Summary:

Highest Elevation 5,357 m at Gokyo Ri
Average Time in Days 12
Difficulty Level Moderate
Remoteness Isolated
Cost Medium
Best Season To Travel March to May and October to November.
Accommodation Type Teahouse
Restricted Permits No
Required Permits TIMS

10. Upper Dolpo Trek

Upper Dolpo is truly a hidden gem of Nepal that has not been much in highlight. Very few trekkers know about this place and what it has to offer. Also, the stunning barren landscapes, picture-perfect mountain peaks, and Tibetan style villages give a unique flavor to your regular trek-buds.

Similar to the Upper Mustang region, this region also holds century-old cultures that are not affected by modern civilization.

The trail in this trek route requires you to cross three high passes of Magdalo La (5,350 m), Shey La (5,000 m), and Jeng La (5,110 m) requiring you to climb and drop a decently long walk. Furthermore, trekking in this region is accompanied by challenges, but at the same time, is rewarded with adventures and spectacular views of mountains.

Restriction:

As a result of the remoteness, a minimum of two trekkers must be accompanied by a Nepali guide or Porter to trek the Upper Dolpo.

Summary:

Highest Elevation 5,250 m at Kang La Pass
Average Time in Days 22
Difficulty Level Moderate
Remoteness Very Isolated
Cost High
Best Season To Travel March to May and October to November.
Accommodation Type Camping
Restricted Permits Yes
Required Permits RAP

Conclusion – Best Treks in Nepal

In sum, the diverse terrain of Nepal offers a rare experience in each of the treks. Similarly, the exceptionally beautiful trek routes will leave you stunned in amusement and remain in your senses for a lifetime.

You will definitely cherish the moments as you go through the photographs.

Generally, there are many other trek routes in Nepal but it is not possible to list them all at once.

If you think, we may have forgotten to list your favorite ones, do write to us about it in the comment section below.

In conclusion, we would also like to know which of these treks have you checked out from your list. Share your experiences and let everyone know which one has been the best for you. Also, if you are looking to taking a trip, contact us for further details.

title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek Packing List
excerpt: In this article, you are going to get a lot of ideas about the Annapurna Base Camp Trek Packing List. Annapurna Base Camp Trek has one of the amazing trekking trails that gives you an opportunity to…
html:
In this article, you are going to get a lot of ideas about the Annapurna Base Camp Trek Packing List.

Annapurna Base Camp Trek has one of the amazing trekking trails that gives you an opportunity to walk through the diverse landscape and a variety of cultures. In addition, it offers you enticing views of mountain vistas, beautiful terraced fields, a unique Gurung community, and quite a range of flora and fauna.

In fact, Mt. Annapurna (8,091 m) is the 10th highest mountain in the world and Annapurna Base Camp lies at an altitude of 4,130 m above sea level. Similarly, the weather at this height can be expected to be unpredictable, making it difficult to decide what to carry and what not.

Generally, the base camp is reached via the trails through Mt. Machhapuchhre, also known as Fishtail. Moreover, it is admired by people all over the world for its unique identity and beauty.

Furthermore, the well organized standard itinerary of the Annapurna Base Camp trekking package is very achievable and can be flexible as per the requirement.

The trek to Annapurna Base Camp is a highly-visited and popular choice among enthusiasts from diverse outdoor. You can see different types of fellow trekkers ranging from solo female travelers to trekkers traveling in groups to Nepal.

The base camp trek may range from 11 to 25 days depending on the type of package chosen and also based on custom packages as per the need of the traveler or traveling group. Besides, Basecamp Adventure provides services for custom trek itineraries based on your scheduled time frame and ease of access.

Despite the itinerary, there are things that you need to consider before you actually start packing bags for the trip. If you are not a local trekker, then trekking in another country can come with a fair share of nuances.

In addition, things that you generally neglect such as clean drinking water, toilet papers, running faucets, and electricity can come as an obstacle too.

But luckily, the main course of the trek is highly dominated by food, the strength of walking, adequate and comfortable sleep, and repeating everything over again. And all these are fairly available in the teahouse trekking routes of Nepal.

In particular, the minor challenges in the trek can be annoying but the real taste of adventure comes with overcoming the hurdles and creating a journey that would be memorable for a lifetime.

However, it is always healthy to take all the essentials with you that are necessary for the trip. As rightly quoted, “It is better to be safe than to be sorry”, being prepared before starting the trek can help you enjoy every bit of the adventure.

Planning for the checklist will help in removing the possible stress due to inadequacy and no means to buy them at that altitude. Therefore, let us share with you the list of things that you should consider taking with you while on your trek to Annapurna Circuit and Annapurna Base Camp.

In sum, you may optimize your backpack based on your specific needs.

What to take on Annapurna Base Camp Trek?

The list below is fairly a guideline to help trekkers pack for an adventurous trek to the rural uphills of Nepal. Also, it is also equally important to understand that the items listed here can vary according to the season, current climate, and the duration of the trek.

Furthermore, there is a weight limit for luggage per person while flying to Pokhara – the last city you will encounter before your trekking starts. Likewise, the weight limit is 33 pounds or 15 kg. On guided trekking, you will get a porter to carry your luggage from your hired trip advisors’ agency.

Also, it is very important to pack only what is necessary – nothing more, nothing less.

Please submit your inquiry using the form below. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible.

Essentials

Backpack:

You will need a sturdy hiking backpack that can include all your checklist items.

Map

There is hardly any chance of getting lost but it is a good idea to have a map to track the distances and plan accordingly.

Trekking Permits

Trekking permits will be required for your trek journey. You can get the trekking permits in Pokhara or Kathmandu.

A sleeping bag

You can go with a standard 3-seasons sleeping bag. Besides, it will make a good choice for your trekking adventures.

A bottle of water

You will need a bottle which you can refill with filtered or pre-boiled water at the lodges where you halt for taking some rest. Moreover, a standard 1-liter water bottle is a good size.

Cash

You may not find any ATM once you start trekking. So it is a good idea to carry sufficient local currency.

A small medical kit

Carrying a small medical kit in your travel bag will be very helpful in case of an emergency.

Clothes Annapurna Base Camp Trek Packing List

A comfortable pair of hiking boots

To ensure comfort while walking, you can choose either class B or C.

2 to 4 pairs of trekking socks

They soak the sweat better and stink less. In addition, they are also easy to wash and dry as compared to normal socks.

3 sets of underwear

It is a better idea to wash and dry them than to add further weight to your backpack.

A couple of lightweight & fast-drying (Non-Cotton) T-Shirts

Fabric-like cotton will easily soak up all the sweat but will not dry soon, persisting the cold that might cause pneumonia. Moreover, you don’t want to get sick while you’re on such an amazing trek. Also, fast-drying fabrics light to your bag and are easy for laundry.

1 pair of easy-drying long trousers

You don’t need trousers specifically for mountaineering. Likewise, the standard outdoor ones will be fine. And yes, choose thin ones as it can get hot as you walk.

1 set of skiing underwear

Usually, you might find some natural water sources, or hot water springs (in Jinhu) to dive in or even get opportunities for skiing on the ice.

A lightweight, fast-drying pullover or fleece

A hat

It will help you protect yourself from the sun.

Gloves

Gloves are necessary for protection against snow and ice.

A scarf or balaclava

The roads can get dusty, so you will need one to cover your face at times.

A lightweight waterproof jacket

A waterproof jacket will protect you from unpredictable wind and rain.

An insulating jacket or vest

The nights and early mornings can get cooler, so to safeguard your body from possible chances of illness, take a lightweight insulating jacket.

Sandals or flip-flops

After the long tiring walk, you will want to get off your shoes and give some fresh air to pass through your toes.

Waterproof trousers

In fact, the weather can be unpredictable so better be safe with a pair of these.

Others

Toothbrush

You will be needing it twice every day.

A towel

A lightweight outdoor towel would be a great choice.

Traveler’s size shampoo and shower gel or soap

Some lodges/ tea houses may provide you with these but not everyone will.

Toilet paper

You’ll generally find the Indian style toilet with water supply but backup with the toilet papers for worse case.

Sunscreen

The sun may be scorching and harsh to your skin if you forget to apply a protective sunscreen cream/lotion.

Trekking poles

These provide you with good support to walk both uphill and downhill, especially if you are a novice trekker.

Sunglasses

Here, a good pair of sunglasses will give you better vision against the sun rays.

Camera

In fact, you will definitely want to capture all the best sights you get along the trek route.

Battery Charge/ Power bank and a spare battery for your camera

Electricity can be unpredictable in rural areas of Nepal, so it is a better idea to carry a backup.

Snickers or energy bars

Something to munch in or for instant energy. Also as a mid-meal snack.

Something to read

In order to save you from boredom in case of flight delays or during road trips, based on your package type.

A smartphone or watch

You will want to track time, distance covered, and maybe some calories you burnt along the way.

A torch

A headlight will be the best choice, you may need it to go to the bathroom at night which are mostly shared and occasionally within your room.

A whistle

Carry a whistle to draw attention in case of an emergency.

Conclusion -Annapurna Base Camp Trek Packing List

In particular, the Annapurna Base Camp trek can give you one of the most exciting trekking experience you can possibly get in rustic Nepal.

The countryside of Nepal is a wonderland for explorers around the world as it is blessed with unique culture, tradition, people, temples/ monasteries, cuisines, festivals. In addition, enthralling sights of tall, glorious mountains, varying landscapes, breathtaking views of sunrise and sunset are some in the list one should not miss out on.

In fact, every trek, including Annapurna Base Camp Trek, can turn out to be either a blessing or a misery based on your knowledge of requirements and the list of things you make for your backpack.

Furthermore, missing out on some major essentials can be a reason for unexpected disappointment. Therefore, it is a good idea to study and plan for the requirements before you actually set off for the journey.

Note: Generally, the packing list will equally differ based on the season in which you’re planning to travel.

In short, if you need any suggestions or details regarding the trek, routes, best seasons to travel, accommodation, or anything, feel free to contact us. Also, we will be more than happy to assist in your trek journey.

Make every moment of your trip memorable and worthwhile. Collect reminiscences that you can cherish for a lifetime. Think smart, pack smarter!
